papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques transform large, costly models into smaller, faster, or more private models while retaining much of the original performance. Across modalities and tasks, distillation has been applied to compress vision and language models, transfer cross-modal or privileged information, enable deployment under latency and memory constraints, and preserve privacy in distributed settings. Key directions include distillation of logits (soft labels), feature- or attention-level distillation, self-distillation, data-free or zero-shot approaches, and architecture-aware compression. Empirical results show that when carefully designed—often combining distillation with pruning or architecture search—student models can approach teacher accuracy, gain robustness, or enable capabilities (e.g., multimodal generation) previously unavailable to the smaller model. Important open problems remain in data heterogeneity, robustness transfer, and principled teacher-student design for diverse deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Zuniga
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Flexible Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable ones across modalities. When combined with complementary techniques—such as self-supervised teacher-to-student transfer, data-aware augmentation, progressive module replacement, architecture search, pruning, quantization, curriculum strategies, and teacher optimization—KD delivers strong accuracy/efficiency trade-offs while addressing constraints like privacy and data unavailability. This paper argues that KD should be treated not as a single recipe but as a composable framework that can be adapted to task, data, and hardware requirements to maximize utility in real-world NLP and deep-learning deployments.

papers_seen.author: Spears
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and essential technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher networks to students through various mechanisms, addressing critical deployment constraints including latency, memory, privacy, and computational efficiency. Knowledge distillation has become a foundational methodology across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, and multimodal learning, enabling practical deployment of state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices. While KD encompasses multiple complementary strategies and demonstrates consistent empirical effectiveness, realizing optimal gains requires careful attention to design choices, teacher quality, data availability, and task-specific adaptation.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used paradigm to compress large models into smaller, more efficient students by transferring information from teacher models. Research has explored multiple transfer mechanisms (soft labels, intermediate feature matching, layer mappings), teacher and data strategies (student-friendly teachers, multi-teacher weighting, data-free distillation, and data augmentation), and applied KD to a variety of tasks including BERT compression, non-autoregressive translation, and lightweight NLP models. Progress shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while enabling substantial reductions in size and latency, but design choices about what to transfer, how teachers are trained, how data is constructed or augmented, and how multiple teachers are combined strongly affect outcomes. Remaining challenges include principled selection of transfer targets and data, robustness under domain shifts or heterogeneous deployments, and automating task-adaptive compression for downstream objectives.

papers_seen.author: Brennan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Evidence, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely applicable approach for compressing large deep learning and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. Empirical results across domains show KD preserves much of teacher performance while enabling dramatic reductions in model size and latency; however, KD is not a panacea — its success depends on choices about transferred signals, student capacity, data availability, privacy constraints, and heterogeneous deployment settings. A practically useful KD-centered compression strategy therefore combines targeted distillation objectives with complementary techniques (privacy-preserving mechanisms, data augmentation, ensemble teachers, and task-aware filtering) to meet specific deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from larger, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, efficient student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. The literature frames KD as a flexible toolbox rather than a single recipe: approaches include transferring output soft-labels, aligning intermediate representations or attention, using multi-teacher schedules, and combining distillation with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical work shows these choices — what to transfer, how to align student and teacher, and which data or augmentations to use — substantially affect whether a student approaches teacher performance. KD has been adapted across classification, sequence modeling, translation, retrieval, recommender systems, generative models, and many NLP tasks, with ongoing challenges around data-free distillation, representation alignment, and robustness in low-resource or privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and allied model-compression techniques provide practical ways to transfer predictive and representational knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models so compact systems can run under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. The literature shows a wide family of methods — matching softened logits, imitating intermediate features or attention, relational and task-specific mappings, self- and multi-teacher schemes, and data-side strategies such as augmentation, synthetic data, or pre-training compact architectures — that together enable strong trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy. Empirical successes span vision, speech, recommendation, and natural language tasks, but open issues remain, including teacher–student mismatch, robustness under distribution shift, limited or absent training data, and principled design of what to transfer for particular student capacities. Practical deployments benefit from combining complementary techniques (representation-level objectives, augmentation-aware distillation, pre-training of small models, and continual or task-adaptive strategies) and from careful tuning of teacher construction, data, and transfer objectives.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while maintaining competitive performance. Rather than a monolithic approach, knowledge distillation represents a flexible family of methods that transfer various forms of knowledge—from output distributions to intermediate representations—from teacher to student models. This technique enables the deployment of state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices and addresses critical challenges in reducing computational costs, latency, and memory requirements without significant accuracy loss. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, speech recognition, and federated learning settings.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: BAM! Born-Again Multi-Task Networks for Natural Language Understanding
papers_seen.abstract: It can be challenging to train multi-task neural networks that outperform or even match their single-task counterparts. To help address this, we propose using knowledge distillation where single-task models teach a multi-task model. We enhance this training with teacher annealing, a novel method that gradually transitions the model from distillation to supervised learning, helping the multi-task model surpass its single-task teachers. We evaluate our approach by multi-task fine-tuning BERT on the GLUE benchmark. Our method consistently improves over standard single-task and multi-task training.

papers_seen.author: Walls
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and widely-adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while preserving much of the original performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, KD enables deployment on edge devices, addresses privacy and data-availability constraints, and facilitates knowledge transfer across architectures and modalities. This synthesis examines the core methods of knowledge distillation, key applications across domains, practical effectiveness, and important limitations and open challenges in the field.

papers_seen.author: Murillo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become fundamental techniques for deploying large, high-performing deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, these methods enable substantial reductions in parameter count, memory consumption, and inference latency while maintaining competitive accuracy. These approaches have been successfully adapted across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, and graph neural networks, with emerging variants addressing specific challenges such as fairness, privacy preservation, and task-adaptive compression.

papers_seen.author: Novak
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a central technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while preserving performance. This method transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lower-capacity student models, enabling deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices. The approach has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech processing, and graph neural networks, with various methodological innovations continuously expanding its scope and effectiveness.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: R2L: Distilling Neural Radiance Field to Neural Light Field for Efficient Novel View Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Recent research explosion on Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) shows the encouraging potential to represent complex scenes with neural networks. One major drawback of NeRF is its prohibitive inference time: Rendering a single pixel requires querying the NeRF network hundreds of times. To resolve it, existing efforts mainly attempt to reduce the number of required sampled points. However, the problem of iterative sampling still exists. On the other hand, Neural Light Field (NeLF) presents a more straightforward representation over NeRF in novel view synthesis -- the rendering of a pixel amounts to one single forward pass without ray-marching. In this work, we present a deep residual MLP network (88 layers) to effectively learn the light field. We show the key to successfully learning such a deep NeLF network is to have sufficient data, for which we transfer the knowledge from a pre-trained NeRF model via data distillation. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world scenes show the merits of our method over other counterpart algorithms. On the synthetic scenes, we achieve 26-35x FLOPs reduction (per camera ray) and 28-31x runtime speedup, meanwhile delivering significantly better (1.4-2.8 dB average PSNR improvement) rendering quality than NeRF without any customized parallelism requirement.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Online Knowledge Distillation via Mutual Contrastive Learning for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: The teacher-free online Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to train an ensemble of multiple student models collaboratively and distill knowledge from each other. Although existing online KD methods achieve desirable performance, they often focus on class probabilities as the core knowledge type, ignoring the valuable feature representational information. We present a Mutual Contrastive Learning (MCL) framework for online KD. The core idea of MCL is to perform mutual interaction and transfer of contrastive distributions among a cohort of networks in an online manner. Our MCL can aggregate cross-network embedding information and maximize the lower bound to the mutual information between two networks. This enables each network to learn extra contrastive knowledge from others, leading to better feature representations, thus improving the performance of visual recognition tasks. Beyond the final layer, we extend MCL to intermediate layers and perform an adaptive layer-matching mechanism trained by meta-optimization. Experiments on image classification and transfer learning to visual recognition tasks show that layer-wise MCL can lead to consistent performance gains against state-of-the-art online KD approaches. The superiority demonstrates that layer-wise MCL can guide the network to generate better feature representations. Our code is publicly avaliable at https://github.com/winycg/L-MCL.

papers_seen.author: Rice
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: A Synthesis of Recent Advances
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying large neural networks on resource-constrained devices while maintaining predictive performance. These methods involve transferring knowledge from larger, more complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This synthesis examines the theoretical foundations, practical applications, and recent innovations in knowledge distillation across computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains like object detection and graph neural networks. The review highlights mechanisms that enable successful knowledge transfer, strategies for handling heterogeneous model architectures, data-free distillation approaches, and applications to federated learning and multi-modal learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: DE-RRD: A Knowledge Distillation Framework for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: Recent recommender systems have started to employ knowledge distillation, which is a model compression technique distilling knowledge from a cumbersome model (teacher) to a compact model (student), to reduce inference latency while maintaining performance. The state-of-the-art methods have only focused on making the student model accurately imitate the predictions of the teacher model. They have a limitation in that the prediction results incompletely reveal the teacher's knowledge. In this paper, we propose a novel knowledge distillation framework for recommender system, called DE-RRD, which enables the student model to learn from the latent knowledge encoded in the teacher model as well as from the teacher's predictions. Concretely, DE-RRD consists of two methods: 1) Distillation Experts (DE) that directly transfers the latent knowledge from the teacher model. DE exploits "experts" and a novel expert selection strategy for effectively distilling the vast teacher's knowledge to the student with limited capacity. 2) Relaxed Ranking Distillation (RRD) that transfers the knowledge revealed from the teacher's prediction with consideration of the relaxed ranking orders among items. Our extensive experiments show that DE-RRD outperforms the state-of-the-art competitors and achieves comparable or even better performance to that of the teacher model with faster inference time.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Vital Strategy for Efficient Deployment in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and practical technique for compressing large neural networks while preserving task performance. By transferring knowledge from larger, well-trained teacher models to compact student networks, this approach enables significant reductions in computational requirements and model size while maintaining or improving performance. Across natural language processing and computer vision, knowledge distillation addresses critical deployment challenges by enabling trade-offs among model size, latency, privacy, and accessibility for resource-constrained devices. Recent advances demonstrate that effective distillation requires careful attention to projector design, teacher quality, architectural choices, and task-specific formulations, making it essential for practical modern machine learning applications.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from a larger teacher model to a smaller student model, enabling efficient deployment of neural networks while maintaining competitive performance. This technique has become increasingly important across various domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications. The approach addresses the critical challenge of deploying complex, high-performing deep learning models on resource-constrained devices by enabling smaller models to achieve comparable results to their larger counterparts.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: On Representation Knowledge Distillation for Graph Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a learning paradigm for boosting resource-efficient graph neural networks (GNNs) using more expressive yet cumbersome teacher models. Past work on distillation for GNNs proposed the Local Structure Preserving loss (LSP), which matches local structural relationships defined over edges across the student and teacher's node embeddings. This paper studies whether preserving the global topology of how the teacher embeds graph data can be a more effective distillation objective for GNNs, as real-world graphs often contain latent interactions and noisy edges. We propose Graph Contrastive Representation Distillation (G-CRD), which uses contrastive learning to implicitly preserve global topology by aligning the student node embeddings to those of the teacher in a shared representation space. Additionally, we introduce an expanded set of benchmarks on large-scale real-world datasets where the performance gap between teacher and student GNNs is non-negligible. Experiments across 4 datasets and 14 heterogeneous GNN architectures show that G-CRD consistently boosts the performance and robustness of lightweight GNNs, outperforming LSP (and a global structure preserving variant of LSP) as well as baselines from 2D computer vision. An analysis of the representational similarity among teacher and student embedding spaces reveals that G-CRD balances preserving local and global relationships, while structure preserving approaches are best at preserving one or the other. Our code is available at https://github.com/chaitjo/efficient-gnns

papers_seen.author: Lin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become indispensable techniques for deploying large-scale deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, these approaches enable significant reductions in computational requirements and model size while preserving competitive performance. This paper argues that knowledge distillation, when carefully applied with attention to task-specific requirements and design choices, represents a vital strategy for enabling practical real-world deployment of neural networks across diverse domains and applications.

papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students across computer vision, language, graph, and federated settings. When applied thoughtfully—combining representational distillation, pre-training of compact architectures, and task- or system-aware protocols—KD can retain much of the teacher's accuracy while meeting constraints of latency, memory, privacy, and device heterogeneity. However, KD is not a panacea: its success depends on what is distilled (outputs vs. internal representations), how teachers and students are prepared, and additional concerns such as adversarial robustness and bias that may be transferred unless specifically addressed.

papers_seen.author: Hamilton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential Technique for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining or improving performance. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, this approach addresses the critical challenge of deploying sophisticated deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. The technique encompasses diverse methodologies and has demonstrated effectiveness across multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, making it a practical necessity for modern machine learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Cross-modal Knowledge Distillation for Vision-to-Sensor Action Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: Human activity recognition (HAR) based on multi-modal approach has been recently shown to improve the accuracy performance of HAR. However, restricted computational resources associated with wearable devices, i.e., smartwatch, failed to directly support such advanced methods. To tackle this issue, this study introduces an end-to-end Vision-to-Sensor Knowledge Distillation (VSKD) framework. In this VSKD framework, only time-series data, i.e., accelerometer data, is needed from wearable devices during the testing phase. Therefore, this framework will not only reduce the computational demands on edge devices, but also produce a learning model that closely matches the performance of the computational expensive multi-modal approach. In order to retain the local temporal relationship and facilitate visual deep learning models, we first convert time-series data to two-dimensional images by applying the Gramian Angular Field ( GAF) based encoding method. We adopted ResNet18 and multi-scale TRN with BN-Inception as teacher and student network in this study, respectively. A novel loss function, named Distance and Angle-wised Semantic Knowledge loss (DASK), is proposed to mitigate the modality variations between the vision and the sensor domain. Extensive experimental results on UTD-MHAD, MMAct, and Berkeley-MHAD datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and competitiveness of the proposed VSKD model which can deployed on wearable sensors.

papers_seen.author: Chapman
papers_seen.title: Why Knowledge Distillation Should Be the Default Strategy for Deploying Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile strategy for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster models that retain most of the original performance. When combined with targeted techniques—multi-teacher distillation, feature- and attention-level objectives, domain-aware adaptation, self-distillation, and privacy- or federation-aware protocols—KD enables deployment under tight latency, memory, and privacy constraints while often improving robustness and generalization. Despite these successes, careful teacher-student design, data availability, and principled evaluation remain important open problems for reliable production use.

papers_seen.author: Bass
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Findings, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher networks into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations, enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. A rich set of techniques—logit/soft-target matching, feature and layer alignment, multi-teacher and online schemes, adversarial or decision-boundary guided samples, and data-free synthesis—has been developed to address different practical constraints. Empirical work shows substantial efficiency gains are possible, but success depends on choices of distilled targets, data availability, teacher quality, and training curricula; theoretical analyses provide partial explanations and suggest when soft or hard targets are preferable. Ongoing challenges include handling domain shift, low-frequency phenomena, distributed training, and principled student architecture selection.

papers_seen.author: Arroyo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques have become central to deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Research spans practical recipes (logit matching, feature and layer-wise matching, projector modules), structural compression (architectural transforms, channel/filter reduction), and specialized strategies for NLP models (layer mapping for transformers and task-aware layer selection). Recent work also addresses learning dynamics and theory for wide networks, multi-teacher and meta-learned teaching, and scenarios with limited or no access to original training data. Empirical results show that careful choice of distillation targets, alignment mechanisms, and teacher-student curricula can yield compact models that retain strong performance on downstream tasks while enabling faster inference and smaller memory footprints. Open challenges include task-specific selection of distilled knowledge, robustness and generalization across distributions, and principled guidelines for architecture-aware distillation in transformers.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Rejuvenating Low-Frequency Words: Making the Most of Parallel Data in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly used to construct synthetic data for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models. However, there exists a discrepancy on low-frequency words between the distilled and the original data, leading to more errors on predicting low-frequency words. To alleviate the problem, we directly expose the raw data into NAT by leveraging pretraining. By analyzing directed alignments, we found that KD makes low-frequency source words aligned with targets more deterministically but fails to align sufficient low-frequency words from target to source. Accordingly, we propose reverse KD to rejuvenate more alignments for low-frequency target words. To make the most of authentic and synthetic data, we combine these complementary approaches as a new training strategy for further boosting NAT performance. We conduct experiments on five translation benchmarks over two advanced architectures. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach can significantly and universally improve translation quality by reducing translation errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach achieves 28.2 and 33.9 BLEU points on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets, respectively. Our code, data, and trained models are available at \url{https://github.com/alphadl/RLFW-NAT}.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are essential techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models, enabling substantial reductions in model size, computational cost, and inference time while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and question answering. The techniques address fundamental practical challenges in making state-of-the-art models viable for real-world deployment with limited latency, memory, and energy budgets.

papers_seen.author: Roman
papers_seen.title: Converging Strategies for Practical Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a heuristic for compressing classifiers into a versatile, modality-agnostic toolkit that enables deployment of large models in resource-constrained and privacy-sensitive settings. Advances span architectural strategies (progressive module replacement and feature mimicking), data-centric solutions (data-free and augmented distillation), teacher selection (ensembles and meta-learned teachers), and objectives that transfer robustness as well as accuracy. When combined thoughtfully — e.g., targeted feature-level objectives, careful data-generation or augmentation, and teacher optimization — KD enables small models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and deployment constraints. This article argues that best practice is not a single KD recipe but an integrated approach that matches the distillation technique to operational constraints (data availability, privacy, robustness requirements, and target hardware).

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models. When combined with careful design of student capacity, layer alignment, and complementary compression methods, KD enables substantial reductions in memory and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. However, distillation is not a universal remedy: its effectiveness depends on choices about what is transferred, available data, and how student and teacher internals align. Practical deployments benefit from treating KD as a multi-strategy engineering problem—selecting appropriate distillation targets, leveraging multi-teacher or data-free options when necessary, and addressing optimization gaps and low-frequency phenomena through task-aware interventions.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical and Versatile Core Technique for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and essential technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, more deployable versions while maintaining task performance. By transferring knowledge from teacher models to student models through diverse mechanisms—including soft logits, intermediate representations, and feature-level alignment—KD enables efficient deployment across resource-constrained environments. When strategically combined with complementary techniques such as quantization, pruning, and data-free methods, KD provides robust solutions to real-world deployment challenges in both computer vision and natural language processing. However, KD is not universally applicable; optimization challenges and architectural mismatches require careful design and evaluation protocols to achieve consistent results.

papers_seen.author: Ray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Task-Driven Toolkit: Benefits, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core method for compressing large models into deployable students while preserving much of teacher capability. KD’s strengths arise from multiple mechanisms — soft-target regularization, intermediate representation transfer, and self-distillation — and its best outcomes come when distillation objectives are matched to the task, data regime, and deployment constraints. However, KD is not a universal fix: teacher errors, domain shifts, architectural mismatch, and data heterogeneity can limit or bias students, so practitioners must combine KD with complementary compression steps and rigorous evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Velasquez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) consolidates a broad set of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger or differently-abled teacher models to smaller, faster, or capacity-constrained student models. Across logits, intermediate representations, layer mappings, and data-side strategies, KD enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art models under constraints of latency, memory, or device heterogeneity. While KD is empirically powerful and widely applicable across vision, language, speech, and specialized tasks, its effectiveness depends on method selection, data regimes, and careful handling of teacher–student alignment and optimization dynamics.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying large, powerful deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, these methods address the fundamental challenge of making state-of-the-art models practical for real-world applications while maintaining competitive performance. This position argues that knowledge distillation is not merely a complementary technique but a central and versatile strategy that, when carefully designed with complementary compression methods, enables effective deployment across diverse domains in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Tran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Theory, and Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for compressing large neural networks into smaller models that preserve predictive performance and desirable properties of the teacher. KD encompasses soft-label supervision, intermediate-feature matching, layer-wise alignment, multi-teacher fusion, online co-training, and teacher-free/self-distillation, and it is applied across modalities (vision, language, generation, recommendation) to meet deployment constraints such as latency, memory, low-precision arithmetic, privacy, and domain shift. Successful distillation requires task-aware choices of what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, how to generate or select data for transfer, and how to combine objectives to trade off fidelity and generalization. Remaining challenges include principled selection of distilled signals, data-free and privacy-preserving workflows, robustness under domain shift, and automated, task-adaptive compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Pacheco
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation with Adversarial Samples Supporting Decision Boundary
papers_seen.abstract: Many recent works on knowledge distillation have provided ways to transfer the knowledge of a trained network for improving the learning process of a new one, but finding a good technique for knowledge distillation is still an open problem. In this paper, we provide a new perspective based on a decision boundary, which is one of the most important component of a classifier. The generalization performance of a classifier is closely related to the adequacy of its decision boundary, so a good classifier bears a good decision boundary. Therefore, transferring information closely related to the decision boundary can be a good attempt for knowledge distillation. To realize this goal, we utilize an adversarial attack to discover samples supporting a decision boundary. Based on this idea, to transfer more accurate information about the decision boundary, the proposed algorithm trains a student classifier based on the adversarial samples supporting the decision boundary. Experiments show that the proposed method indeed improves knowledge distillation and achieves the state-of-the-arts performance.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) reduces the cost of large neural models by training smaller students to imitate higher-capacity teachers. The field has matured into a diverse toolkit that includes soft-label matching, feature- and layer-level imitation, data-free and federated variants, multi-teacher and ensemble strategies, and task-aware architecture design. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can recover much of a teacher's performance across vision, language, speech, and graph tasks while enabling deployment under compute, privacy, and device constraints; remaining challenges center on data absence, inductive-bias mismatch, automated student design, and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Zuniga
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Flexible Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable ones across modalities. When combined with complementary techniques—such as self-supervised teacher-to-student transfer, data-aware augmentation, progressive module replacement, architecture search, pruning, quantization, curriculum strategies, and teacher optimization—KD delivers strong accuracy/efficiency trade-offs while addressing constraints like privacy and data unavailability. This paper argues that KD should be treated not as a single recipe but as a composable framework that can be adapted to task, data, and hardware requirements to maximize utility in real-world NLP and deep-learning deployments.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and NLP. By training a lightweight student network to mimic a larger, well-trained teacher network, this approach enables the deployment of high-performance models on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive accuracy. Knowledge distillation operates through the transfer of soft targets and intermediate representations from teacher to student networks, providing implicit regularization and accelerating convergence. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, machine translation, information retrieval, and speech processing, offering substantial reductions in model size and computational cost with minimal performance degradation.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Findings, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal knowledge from teacher networks. Across computer vision, NLP, speech, and generative modeling, distillation methods have evolved from matching soft logits to aligning intermediate representations and adapting layer mappings for heterogeneous architectures. Practical results show large reductions in parameter counts and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance, but challenges remain in robustness, student-friendly teacher design, and reliably transferring rarer or structural knowledge.

papers_seen.author: Valdez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has evolved from a single training recipe into a versatile set of techniques that enable deployment of large neural models under constraints of compute, latency, privacy, and heterogeneity. When combined with complementary strategies such as architecture search, progressive compression, and task-aware signal selection, distillation routinely produces compact models that retain much of teacher performance across modalities and tasks. Practical success depends on choosing distillation variants that match deployment needs and on designing teacher–student pairs and objectives that transfer the right internal and output signals.

papers_seen.author: Parsons
papers_seen.title: Curriculum Learning for Dense Retrieval Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent work has shown that more effective dense retrieval models can be obtained by distilling ranking knowledge from an existing base re-ranking model. In this paper, we propose a generic curriculum learning based optimization framework called CL-DRD that controls the difficulty level of training data produced by the re-ranking (teacher) model. CL-DRD iteratively optimizes the dense retrieval (student) model by increasing the difficulty of the knowledge distillation data made available to it. In more detail, we initially provide the student model coarse-grained preference pairs between documents in the teacher's ranking and progressively move towards finer-grained pairwise document ordering requirements. In our experiments, we apply a simple implementation of the CL-DRD framework to enhance two state-of-the-art dense retrieval models. Experiments on three public passage retrieval datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed framework.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Deploying Deep Learning Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for enabling the deployment of large, powerful deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, these methods address the fundamental challenge of making state-of-the-art models practical for real-world applications that require fast inference and limited computational resources.

papers_seen.author: Jacobs
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational Technique for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a central and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from teacher models through various mechanisms—including soft logits, intermediate representations, and synthesized data—knowledge distillation addresses critical deployment challenges across deep learning and natural language processing. This technique represents a pragmatic solution for resource-constrained environments, offering substantial reductions in model size and inference latency without significant accuracy loss. However, realizing its full potential requires careful attention to optimization challenges, teacher-student alignment, and task-specific design considerations.

papers_seen.author: House
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques transform large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster, or more resource-efficient models for deployment. Work in this area spans methods that transfer teacher output distributions, match intermediate representations, perform layer- or module-level supervision, and combine compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) with distillation objectives. Recent advances emphasize task-aware selection of teacher signals, data-free or privacy-preserving distillation, the role of data augmentation and training heuristics, and hardware-aware pruning strategies. Empirical results show that careful distillation pipelines can retain most teacher performance while substantially reducing size and latency, but open challenges remain in handling mismatched teacher–student capacity, limited or absent training data, robustness on rare phenomena, and joint optimization for heterogeneous hardware.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach enables the deployment of state-of-the-art neural networks in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. KD has evolved significantly beyond simple logit matching to encompass diverse techniques including intermediate representation matching, layer-wise alignment, multi-teacher training, data-free approaches, and task-adaptive architecture search. The technique is now widely applied across multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, graph neural networks, and generative tasks, addressing critical challenges in bridging the gap between model performance and practical deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical and Multifaceted Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of the teachers' performance. KD encompasses many concrete mechanisms (logit-level supervision, feature/attention transfer, layer mapping, synthetic-data distillation, multi-teacher schedules) and can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture design to meet latency, memory, privacy, and interpretability constraints. When chosen and tuned for the deployment constraints and data regime at hand, KD routinely yields compact models that balance accuracy, robustness, and resource costs; however, careful attention to teacher–student capacity, data heterogeneity, fairness, and optimization dynamics is required to obtain reliable results.
