papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Tool for Compression, Generalization, and Responsible NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is more than a single recipe for shrinking models: it is a flexible framework that enables model compression, preserves or transfers useful behaviors (including inductive biases), supports domain adaptation and privacy-preserving deployment, and can be adapted to mitigate undesirable behaviors. Drawing on empirical and methodological work across NLP and other domains, KD should be considered a central technique for building smaller, faster models that retain or even improve important aspects of teacher behavior while meeting practical constraints.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Evidence, and Practical Guidelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring information beyond hard labels. KD encompasses multiple mechanisms (soft targets, feature imitation, contrastive alignment, multi-teacher pipelines, and data distillation) and is effective across domains including NLP, machine translation, recommendation, and graph and multimodal models. When combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture replacement), KD enables deployment on resource-constrained hardware while largely preserving performance. Success hinges on choices of distillation targets, teacher quality, data and augmentation strategies, and student capacity.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Towards Practical Lipreading with Distilled and Efficient Models
papers_seen.abstract: Lipreading has witnessed a lot of progress due to the resurgence of neural networks. Recent works have placed emphasis on aspects such as improving performance by finding the optimal architecture or improving generalization. However, there is still a significant gap between the current methodologies and the requirements for an effective deployment of lipreading in practical scenarios. In this work, we propose a series of innovations that significantly bridge that gap: first, we raise the state-of-the-art performance by a wide margin on LRW and LRW-1000 to 88.5% and 46.6%, respectively using self-distillation. Secondly, we propose a series of architectural changes, including a novel Depthwise Separable Temporal Convolutional Network (DS-TCN) head, that slashes the computational cost to a fraction of the (already quite efficient) original model. Thirdly, we show that knowledge distillation is a very effective tool for recovering performance of the lightweight models. This results in a range of models with different accuracy-efficiency trade-offs. However, our most promising lightweight models are on par with the current state-of-the-art while showing a reduction of 8.2x and 3.9x in terms of computational cost and number of parameters, respectively, which we hope will enable the deployment of lipreading models in practical applications.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central strategy for compressing large neural models into compact students that retain much of the teachers' performance. KD encompasses a family of techniques—matching softened logits, intermediate representations, attention maps, or synthesized data—that are applicable across modalities (vision, language, multimodal, graphs, and generative models). Practical KD workflows combine careful teacher selection, layer or token alignment, pre-training for the student, and complementary compression techniques (e.g., pruning or structured sparsity). While KD routinely yields favorable size–performance tradeoffs in production settings, its effectiveness depends on optimization choices, data availability, and mitigation of undesirable transferred behavior (bias, overconfidence, low-frequency errors). Current directions emphasize preserving internal representations, enabling data-free or privacy-preserving distillation, and carrying forward robustness and interpretability from teachers to students.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Preserving Privacy in Federated Learning with Ensemble Cross-Domain Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is a machine learning paradigm where local nodes collaboratively train a central model while the training data remains decentralized. Existing FL methods typically share model parameters or employ co-distillation to address the issue of unbalanced data distribution. However, they suffer from communication bottlenecks. More importantly, they risk privacy leakage. In this work, we develop a privacy preserving and communication efficient method in a FL framework with one-shot offline knowledge distillation using unlabeled, cross-domain public data. We propose a quantized and noisy ensemble of local predictions from completely trained local models for stronger privacy guarantees without sacrificing accuracy. Based on extensive experiments on image classification and text classification tasks, we show that our privacy-preserving method outperforms baseline FL algorithms with superior performance in both accuracy and communication efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical and Flexible Strategy for Compressing Deep and Pre-trained NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable approach for producing smaller, faster models that retain much of the performance of large teachers. Across NLP and related vision and multimodal tasks, KD enables substantial inference speedups, can be combined with complementary compression methods, and benefits from targeted algorithmic improvements — at the data, model, and teacher-selection levels — to close the gap to teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. I argue that KD should be a core component of real-world model-compression toolkits, used together with techniques such as careful pretraining of compact architectures, data augmentation, feature-level matching, and teacher-ensemble strategies to maximize accuracy-efficiency trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Alvarado
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while preserving performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to students, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices and reducing computational overhead. KD encompasses diverse methodologies including soft-target matching, feature-level mimicry, data-free approaches, and multi-teacher strategies, with applications spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks. The field continues to evolve with new insights into when and why distillation succeeds, addressing challenges such as data heterogeneity, privacy constraints, and the selection of appropriate student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Principles, Methods, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and model compression represent a broad set of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger, more complex neural networks to smaller, more efficient models. These approaches enable deployment of high-performing deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive accuracy. Applications span diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, speech recognition, and graph neural networks. Knowledge distillation has evolved from a heuristic compression technique to a versatile, modality-agnostic toolkit that addresses critical challenges in model efficiency, latency reduction, privacy preservation, and task-specific performance optimization.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: A Comprehensive Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile approach for both model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents a superior alternative to traditional compression methods because it enables effective compression while maintaining model performance, facilitates transfer of complex learned representations across architectures, and proves applicable across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, graph neural networks, and reinforcement learning. Unlike methods that simply reduce model parameters without guidance, knowledge distillation leverages teacher-student frameworks to encode valuable "dark knowledge" that improves generalization and produces more robust, efficient models.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, enabling practical deployment of state-of-the-art neural networks in resource-constrained environments. This approach addresses critical challenges in deep learning and natural language processing by reducing computational costs, memory requirements, and latency while maintaining competitive performance. Beyond basic compression, knowledge distillation encompasses diverse strategies including soft-target matching, intermediate representation transfer, multi-teacher approaches, and task-aware adaptations that extend its applicability across vision, language processing, speech recognition, and other domains.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: On Representation Knowledge Distillation for Graph Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a learning paradigm for boosting resource-efficient graph neural networks (GNNs) using more expressive yet cumbersome teacher models. Past work on distillation for GNNs proposed the Local Structure Preserving loss (LSP), which matches local structural relationships defined over edges across the student and teacher's node embeddings. This paper studies whether preserving the global topology of how the teacher embeds graph data can be a more effective distillation objective for GNNs, as real-world graphs often contain latent interactions and noisy edges. We propose Graph Contrastive Representation Distillation (G-CRD), which uses contrastive learning to implicitly preserve global topology by aligning the student node embeddings to those of the teacher in a shared representation space. Additionally, we introduce an expanded set of benchmarks on large-scale real-world datasets where the performance gap between teacher and student GNNs is non-negligible. Experiments across 4 datasets and 14 heterogeneous GNN architectures show that G-CRD consistently boosts the performance and robustness of lightweight GNNs, outperforming LSP (and a global structure preserving variant of LSP) as well as baselines from 2D computer vision. An analysis of the representational similarity among teacher and student embedding spaces reveals that G-CRD balances preserving local and global relationships, while structure preserving approaches are best at preserving one or the other. Our code is available at https://github.com/chaitjo/efficient-gnns

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Distilling portable Generative Adversarial Networks for Image Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been widely used in various image-to-image translation tasks, they can be hardly applied on mobile devices due to their heavy computation and storage cost. Traditional network compression methods focus on visually recognition tasks, but never deal with generation tasks. Inspired by knowledge distillation, a student generator of fewer parameters is trained by inheriting the low-level and high-level information from the original heavy teacher generator. To promote the capability of student generator, we include a student discriminator to measure the distances between real images, and images generated by student and teacher generators. An adversarial learning process is therefore established to optimize student generator and student discriminator. Qualitative and quantitative analysis by conducting experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method can learn portable generative models with strong performance.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: SEED: Self-supervised Distillation For Visual Representation
papers_seen.abstract: This paper is concerned with self-supervised learning for small models. The problem is motivated by our empirical studies that while the widely used contrastive self-supervised learning method has shown great progress on large model training, it does not work well for small models. To address this problem, we propose a new learning paradigm, named SElf-SupErvised Distillation (SEED), where we leverage a larger network (as Teacher) to transfer its representational knowledge into a smaller architecture (as Student) in a self-supervised fashion. Instead of directly learning from unlabeled data, we train a student encoder to mimic the similarity score distribution inferred by a teacher over a set of instances. We show that SEED dramatically boosts the performance of small networks on downstream tasks. Compared with self-supervised baselines, SEED improves the top-1 accuracy from 42.2% to 67.6% on EfficientNet-B0 and from 36.3% to 68.2% on MobileNet-v3-Large on the ImageNet-1k dataset.

papers_seen.author: Stevens
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models through various mechanisms, addressing the critical challenge of deploying state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices. The technique has proven effective across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, speech processing, and medical imaging, making it an essential paradigm for practical deep learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Framework for Efficient Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, knowledge distillation enables deployment in resource-constrained environments without significant accuracy loss. The approach has proven effective across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and multimodal learning, offering substantial performance improvements and computational efficiency gains. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should be considered a core and indispensable strategy for practical model compression, particularly when combined with complementary techniques and carefully tailored to specific task requirements and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Davidson
papers_seen.title: Robust Re-Identification by Multiple Views Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: To achieve robustness in Re-Identification, standard methods leverage tracking information in a Video-To-Video fashion. However, these solutions face a large drop in performance for single image queries (e.g., Image-To-Video setting). Recent works address this severe degradation by transferring temporal information from a Video-based network to an Image-based one. In this work, we devise a training strategy that allows the transfer of a superior knowledge, arising from a set of views depicting the target object. Our proposal - Views Knowledge Distillation (VKD) - pins this visual variety as a supervision signal within a teacher-student framework, where the teacher educates a student who observes fewer views. As a result, the student outperforms not only its teacher but also the current state-of-the-art in Image-To-Video by a wide margin (6.3% mAP on MARS, 8.6% on Duke-Video-ReId and 5% on VeRi-776). A thorough analysis - on Person, Vehicle and Animal Re-ID - investigates the properties of VKD from a qualitatively and quantitatively perspective. Code is available at https://github.com/aimagelab/VKD.

papers_seen.author: Ware
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational Strategy for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential and practical technique for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, this approach achieves significant reductions in model size, computational cost, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation encompasses diverse methodologies beyond simple logit matching, including feature-level alignment, attention transfer, and data-free approaches, enabling flexible adaptation to various deployment scenarios and constraints in domains spanning natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Flexible Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective framework for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. KD variants—ranging from logits matching to internal-feature alignment, adversarial/sample-synthesis methods, multi-teacher and online schemes, and privacy-aware protocols—enable practitioners to trade off model size, latency, privacy, and deployment constraints. Realizing these benefits in practice requires careful choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student representations, and how to handle data constraints such as privacy or unavailability. When integrated with complementary techniques (data synthesis, layer mapping, selective sampling, and curriculum designs) KD consistently yields practical compressed models across vision, language, graphs, and multimodal tasks.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: DE-RRD: A Knowledge Distillation Framework for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: Recent recommender systems have started to employ knowledge distillation, which is a model compression technique distilling knowledge from a cumbersome model (teacher) to a compact model (student), to reduce inference latency while maintaining performance. The state-of-the-art methods have only focused on making the student model accurately imitate the predictions of the teacher model. They have a limitation in that the prediction results incompletely reveal the teacher's knowledge. In this paper, we propose a novel knowledge distillation framework for recommender system, called DE-RRD, which enables the student model to learn from the latent knowledge encoded in the teacher model as well as from the teacher's predictions. Concretely, DE-RRD consists of two methods: 1) Distillation Experts (DE) that directly transfers the latent knowledge from the teacher model. DE exploits "experts" and a novel expert selection strategy for effectively distilling the vast teacher's knowledge to the student with limited capacity. 2) Relaxed Ranking Distillation (RRD) that transfers the knowledge revealed from the teacher's prediction with consideration of the relaxed ranking orders among items. Our extensive experiments show that DE-RRD outperforms the state-of-the-art competitors and achieves comparable or even better performance to that of the teacher model with faster inference time.

papers_seen.author: Rocha
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for compressing neural networks by transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach has become increasingly important for deploying sophisticated deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span multiple domains including computer vision, natural language processing, graph neural networks, and specialized tasks such as pose estimation and scene understanding. Recent advances have extended distillation beyond basic teacher-student frameworks to encompass data augmentation strategies, multi-teacher selection, and zero-shot learning scenarios where original training data is unavailable.

papers_seen.author: Green
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Variants, and Practical Patterns
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD methods include matching teacher output distributions, imitating intermediate feature representations, and using task- or architecture-aware adaptations. Across vision, language, graph, and sequential tasks, distillation enables practical deployment on resource-constrained devices by reducing parameter count, inference latency, and memory while often preserving most of the teacher's performance. However, effectiveness depends on optimization, data choice, and the match between teacher signals and student capacity; addressing these factors has motivated many specialized distillation variants and combined compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical and Necessary Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central framework for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from teachers to students. As deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy, heterogeneous devices) grow, KD’s flexibility — spanning soft-target matching, intermediate representation alignment, attention- and channel-wise transfer, multi-teacher schedules, and data-aware procedures — makes it uniquely suited to balance fidelity and efficiency. However, realizing KD’s promise in practice requires careful design choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student representations, and how to handle limited or private data. When combined with complementary compression techniques and representation-aware training practices, KD reliably produces compact models suitable for real-world NLP and multimodal systems.

papers_seen.author: Allison
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large models into efficient students that retain much of the teacher’s performance. KD techniques—spanning logits-based soft-target transfer, intermediate feature alignment, and data-free synthesis—enable deployment of high-performing models on resource-constrained devices while also offering benefits in robustness and interpretability. When paired with task-aware design and careful teacher selection, distillation can produce compact models that meet real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints without large sacrifices in accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Wong
papers_seen.title: Embracing the Dark Knowledge: Domain Generalization Using Regularized Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Though convolutional neural networks are widely used in different tasks, lack of generalization capability in the absence of sufficient and representative data is one of the challenges that hinder their practical application. In this paper, we propose a simple, effective, and plug-and-play training strategy named Knowledge Distillation for Domain Generalization (KDDG) which is built upon a knowledge distillation framework with the gradient filter as a novel regularization term. We find that both the ``richer dark knowledge" from the teacher network, as well as the gradient filter we proposed, can reduce the difficulty of learning the mapping which further improves the generalization ability of the model. We also conduct experiments extensively to show that our framework can significantly improve the generalization capability of deep neural networks in different tasks including image classification, segmentation, reinforcement learning by comparing our method with existing state-of-the-art domain generalization techniques. Last but not the least, we propose to adopt two metrics to analyze our proposed method in order to better understand how our proposed method benefits the generalization capability of deep neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from larger, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, efficient student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. The literature frames KD as a flexible toolbox rather than a single recipe: approaches include transferring output soft-labels, aligning intermediate representations or attention, using multi-teacher schedules, and combining distillation with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical work shows these choices — what to transfer, how to align student and teacher, and which data or augmentations to use — substantially affect whether a student approaches teacher performance. KD has been adapted across classification, sequence modeling, translation, retrieval, recommender systems, generative models, and many NLP tasks, with ongoing challenges around data-free distillation, representation alignment, and robustness in low-resource or privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Pham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are critical techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, these approaches enable significant reductions in model size and computational cost while maintaining competitive accuracy across diverse applications including computer vision, natural language processing, and machine translation. The field has evolved from basic teacher-student knowledge transfer to sophisticated multi-faceted approaches incorporating feature-level matching, data-free methods, and task-aware training protocols.

papers_seen.author: Ball
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical Framework for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, faster models suitable for resource-constrained deployment. By transferring knowledge from teacher models to student models, distillation enables practitioners to reduce inference latency and memory requirements while maintaining competitive performance. The approach spans diverse applications across computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and specialized domains, making it essential for practical deployment of state-of-the-art models.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Rejuvenating Low-Frequency Words: Making the Most of Parallel Data in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly used to construct synthetic data for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models. However, there exists a discrepancy on low-frequency words between the distilled and the original data, leading to more errors on predicting low-frequency words. To alleviate the problem, we directly expose the raw data into NAT by leveraging pretraining. By analyzing directed alignments, we found that KD makes low-frequency source words aligned with targets more deterministically but fails to align sufficient low-frequency words from target to source. Accordingly, we propose reverse KD to rejuvenate more alignments for low-frequency target words. To make the most of authentic and synthetic data, we combine these complementary approaches as a new training strategy for further boosting NAT performance. We conduct experiments on five translation benchmarks over two advanced architectures. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach can significantly and universally improve translation quality by reducing translation errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach achieves 28.2 and 33.9 BLEU points on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets, respectively. Our code, data, and trained models are available at \url{https://github.com/alphadl/RLFW-NAT}.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Methods, Adaptations, and Practical Insights
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques have become standard tools to transfer knowledge from large, high-capacity models to smaller, efficient models suitable for deployment. Research across modalities and tasks has developed variants that go beyond matching output logits, including feature mimicking, attention- and channel-wise transfers, layer alignment strategies, and task-adaptive or domain-aware schemes. These approaches aim to preserve predictive accuracy and representational structure while reducing storage, computation, and latency. Practical advances demonstrate that carefully designed distillation objectives and mapping strategies can yield compact models that approach teacher performance on classification, ranking, language, speech, graph, and generative tasks, and that adapting distillation to task or domain specifics improves real-world applicability.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Approaches
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, more efficient students while retaining much of the teachers' performance. Recent work expands the KD toolkit beyond matching soft logits to include feature- and layer-level mimicry, task-aware selection of teacher knowledge, data-free and multi-teacher strategies, and augmentation-driven improvements. Practical advances target domain-specific challenges in language models and cross-modal systems, emphasize efficient training and deployment on heterogeneous hardware, and reinterpret KD as a form of regularization that can sometimes be partially replaced or simulated. This review synthesizes these directions and highlights recurring design principles for effective distillation in both NLP and general deep learning settings.

papers_seen.author: Potter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Default for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP (with Caveats and Design Guidelines)
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically proven framework for compressing large teacher models into smaller student models that retain much of the teacher’s capabilities while meeting deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy). When combined with careful teacher–student alignment, multi-source supervision, privacy-preserving mechanisms, and task-aware data strategies, KD routinely produces favorable size–performance tradeoffs across vision, language, generative, and recommendation tasks. However, its practical success depends on matching distillation objectives to student capacity, addressing data availability and domain shift, and mitigating transferred errors or undesirable behaviors. KD should therefore be the default tool for model compression in production, used alongside complementary techniques and principled evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Roman
papers_seen.title: Fair Feature Distillation for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: Fairness is becoming an increasingly crucial issue for computer vision, especially in the human-related decision systems. However, achieving algorithmic fairness, which makes a model produce indiscriminative outcomes against protected groups, is still an unresolved problem. In this paper, we devise a systematic approach which reduces algorithmic biases via feature distillation for visual recognition tasks, dubbed as MMD-based Fair Distillation (MFD). While the distillation technique has been widely used in general to improve the prediction accuracy, to the best of our knowledge, there has been no explicit work that also tries to improve fairness via distillation. Furthermore, We give a theoretical justification of our MFD on the effect of knowledge distillation and fairness. Throughout the extensive experiments, we show our MFD significantly mitigates the bias against specific minorities without any loss of the accuracy on both synthetic and real-world face datasets.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Collaborative Distillation for Ultra-Resolution Universal Style Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Universal style transfer methods typically leverage rich representations from deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models (e.g., VGG-19) pre-trained on large collections of images. Despite the effectiveness, its application is heavily constrained by the large model size to handle ultra-resolution images given limited memory. In this work, we present a new knowledge distillation method (named Collaborative Distillation) for encoder-decoder based neural style transfer to reduce the convolutional filters. The main idea is underpinned by a finding that the encoder-decoder pairs construct an exclusive collaborative relationship, which is regarded as a new kind of knowledge for style transfer models. Moreover, to overcome the feature size mismatch when applying collaborative distillation, a linear embedding loss is introduced to drive the student network to learn a linear embedding of the teacher's features. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness of our method when applied to different universal style transfer approaches (WCT and AdaIN), even if the model size is reduced by 15.5 times. Especially, on WCT with the compressed models, we achieve ultra-resolution (over 40 megapixels) universal style transfer on a 12GB GPU for the first time. Further experiments on optimization-based stylization scheme show the generality of our algorithm on different stylization paradigms. Our code and trained models are available at https://github.com/mingsun-tse/collaborative-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Current Approaches and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and natural language processing. By training smaller student models to learn from larger teacher models, distillation enables the development of efficient yet accurate neural networks suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices. This synthesis examines the current landscape of knowledge distillation methods, their theoretical foundations, and diverse applications across computer vision, NLP, and specialized domains.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a practical, flexible set of techniques that enable deploying compact models while retaining much of the performance of larger teachers. When applied with attention to what is distilled (logits versus internal representations), how teachers and students are matched, and how scarce or private data are handled, KD routinely produces deployable models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a universal remedy: teacher–student capacity mismatches, data limitations, optimization dynamics, and task-specific phenomena (e.g., low-frequency tokens) can limit or bias results. A principled KD pipeline—layer-aware representation transfer, data-aware augmentation or synthesis, multi-source supervision, and careful evaluation on rare phenomena and fairness—yields the best practical outcomes.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Robust Cross-Modal Representation Learning with Progressive Self-Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The learning objective of vision-language approach of CLIP does not effectively account for the noisy many-to-many correspondences found in web-harvested image captioning datasets, which contributes to its compute and data inefficiency. To address this challenge, we introduce a novel training framework based on cross-modal contrastive learning that uses progressive self-distillation and soft image-text alignments to more efficiently learn robust representations from noisy data. Our model distills its own knowledge to dynamically generate soft-alignment targets for a subset of images and captions in every minibatch, which are then used to update its parameters. Extensive evaluation across 14 benchmark datasets shows that our method consistently outperforms its CLIP counterpart in multiple settings, including: (a) zero-shot classification, (b) linear probe transfer, and (c) image-text retrieval, without incurring added computational cost. Analysis using an ImageNet-based robustness test-bed reveals that our method offers better effective robustness to natural distribution shifts compared to both ImageNet-trained models and CLIP itself. Lastly, pretraining with datasets spanning two orders of magnitude in size shows that our improvements over CLIP tend to scale with number of training examples.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: Compressing Deep Graph Neural Networks via Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep graph neural networks (GNNs) have been shown to be expressive for modeling graph-structured data. Nevertheless, the over-stacked architecture of deep graph models makes it difficult to deploy and rapidly test on mobile or embedded systems. To compress over-stacked GNNs, knowledge distillation via a teacher-student architecture turns out to be an effective technique, where the key step is to measure the discrepancy between teacher and student networks with predefined distance functions. However, using the same distance for graphs of various structures may be unfit, and the optimal distance formulation is hard to determine. To tackle these problems, we propose a novel Adversarial Knowledge Distillation framework for graph models named GraphAKD, which adversarially trains a discriminator and a generator to adaptively detect and decrease the discrepancy. Specifically, noticing that the well-captured inter-node and inter-class correlations favor the success of deep GNNs, we propose to criticize the inherited knowledge from node-level and class-level views with a trainable discriminator. The discriminator distinguishes between teacher knowledge and what the student inherits, while the student GNN works as a generator and aims to fool the discriminator. To our best knowledge, GraphAKD is the first to introduce adversarial training to knowledge distillation in graph domains. Experiments on node-level and graph-level classification benchmarks demonstrate that GraphAKD improves the student performance by a large margin. The results imply that GraphAKD can precisely transfer knowledge from a complicated teacher GNN to a compact student GNN.

papers_seen.author: Hawkins
papers_seen.title: A Fast Knowledge Distillation Framework for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: While Knowledge Distillation (KD) has been recognized as a useful tool in many visual tasks, such as supervised classification and self-supervised representation learning, the main drawback of a vanilla KD framework is its mechanism, which consumes the majority of the computational overhead on forwarding through the giant teacher networks, making the entire learning procedure inefficient and costly. ReLabel, a recently proposed solution, suggests creating a label map for the entire image. During training, it receives the cropped region-level label by RoI aligning on a pre-generated entire label map, allowing for efficient supervision generation without having to pass through the teachers many times. However, as the KD teachers are from conventional multi-crop training, there are various mismatches between the global label-map and region-level label in this technique, resulting in performance deterioration. In this study, we present a Fast Knowledge Distillation (FKD) framework that replicates the distillation training phase and generates soft labels using the multi-crop KD approach, while training faster than ReLabel since no post-processes such as RoI align and softmax operations are used. When conducting multi-crop in the same image for data loading, our FKD is even more efficient than the traditional image classification framework. On ImageNet-1K, we obtain 79.8% with ResNet-50, outperforming ReLabel by ~1.0% while being faster. On the self-supervised learning task, we also show that FKD has an efficiency advantage. Our project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/FKD/index.html, source code and models are available at: https://github.com/szq0214/FKD.

papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster models by transferring behavior or representations from a teacher to a student. It is widely used to enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints across modalities (vision, language, speech, multimodal) and tasks (classification, retrieval, generation, segmentation). Effective distillation combines multiple signals (soft targets, intermediate-feature matching, layer-wise supervision, adversarial training, and ensemble guidance) and is commonly paired with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Practical pipelines must balance teacher selection, data regimes, and student capacity to approach teacher performance while meeting resource constraints.

papers_seen.author: Allen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Critical Technology for Efficient Neural Network Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has become an indispensable technique for deploying high-performing deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to compact student models, distillation enables significant reductions in computational requirements and model size while maintaining competitive performance. This position argues that knowledge distillation, when properly designed and combined with complementary compression strategies, represents the most practical and versatile approach to achieving efficient neural networks across diverse applications in computer vision, natural language processing, and beyond.

papers_seen.author: Cohen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Powerful Tool for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for training efficient student models by transferring knowledge from larger teacher networks. This paper argues that knowledge distillation is uniquely valuable not only for model compression and deployment on resource-constrained devices, but also for enabling knowledge transfer across diverse model architectures, improving model robustness, and facilitating collaborative learning in distributed and federated settings. The evidence demonstrates that distillation succeeds through multiple mechanisms beyond traditional soft label matching, making it an indispensable method for practical deep learning applications.

papers_seen.author: Cowan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of their performance. KD techniques range from classic soft-logit matching to feature- and layer-wise transfer, and they enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, realizing KD's benefits requires task- and architecture-aware choices: what to distill (logits, features, internal layers), how to handle limited or private data, and how to align teacher-student capacities. When combined with principled practices, KD is indispensable for translating research-scale models into robust, efficient production systems.

papers_seen.author: Osborne
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely-adopted technique for training compact and efficient models by transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models. This approach has become instrumental across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications like graph neural networks and recommender systems. The technique addresses the fundamental challenge of deploying sophisticated deep learning models in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance levels. Recent advances have expanded the methodology beyond simple output probability matching to include intermediate representations, multi-teacher frameworks, and integration with complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Distilled Semantics for Comprehensive Scene Understanding from Videos
papers_seen.abstract: Whole understanding of the surroundings is paramount to autonomous systems. Recent works have shown that deep neural networks can learn geometry (depth) and motion (optical flow) from a monocular video without any explicit supervision from ground truth annotations, particularly hard to source for these two tasks. In this paper, we take an additional step toward holistic scene understanding with monocular cameras by learning depth and motion alongside with semantics, with supervision for the latter provided by a pre-trained network distilling proxy ground truth images. We address the three tasks jointly by a) a novel training protocol based on knowledge distillation and self-supervision and b) a compact network architecture which enables efficient scene understanding on both power hungry GPUs and low-power embedded platforms. We thoroughly assess the performance of our framework and show that it yields state-of-the-art results for monocular depth estimation, optical flow and motion segmentation.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and allied model-compression techniques transform large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster, or more specialized models while retaining much of the original performance. The approaches span matching teacher soft outputs, imitating intermediate representations, many-to-many layer mapping, data augmentation during transfer, data-free distillation, and architecture-aware compression. Practical systems combine distillation with neural architecture search, federated or privacy-preserving protocols, and multimodal adaptation to meet deployment constraints such as latency, memory, heterogeneity of devices, and absence of original training data. This synthesis summarizes key methods, empirical insights, and deployment-oriented strategies developed to date.

papers_seen.author: Wise
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression methods create smaller, faster models by transferring useful information from large teacher networks to compact student networks. In practice, KD reduces inference latency and memory use while preserving much of teacher performance; it is implemented through a spectrum of techniques (soft-target matching, intermediate representation alignment, multi-teacher fusion, and data-side strategies) and is applied across domains from pretrained language models to domain adaptation and privacy-sensitive releases. Effectiveness depends on what signals are transferred, data available for distillation, alignment between teacher and student architectures, and deployment constraints; open challenges include robustness under distribution shift, few-shot or data-free distillation, principled teacher design for constrained students, and privacy-aware protocols.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Vital Strategy for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile technique for model compression and efficient deployment of deep neural networks. By transferring knowledge from larger, well-trained teacher models to compact student networks, this approach enables significant reductions in computational requirements while maintaining or even improving performance. This paper argues that knowledge distillation is indispensable for modern machine learning applications, particularly in NLP and computer vision, where the trade-off between model complexity and efficiency remains critical for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Mcclain
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: Powerful, Practical, but Not a Panacea
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a core technique for compressing large models, transferring knowledge across architectures, enabling private or federated workflows, and improving efficiency for deployment in resource-constrained settings. While KD often yields substantial practical gains—reducing model size and inference cost with limited loss in performance—it has important theoretical and empirical limitations related to optimization, data dependence, model and domain heterogeneity, and teacher–student mismatch. A pragmatic stance recognizes KD as a versatile toolset whose effectiveness depends on how it is applied: the choice of distilled targets (logits, features, or relations), the availability or synthesis of data, the use of multiple teachers or staged procedures, and awareness of when distillation can harm or help generalization. This paper argues that KD should be used as part of a broader compression and adaptation strategy guided by empirical diagnostics and appropriate extensions (multi-teacher, zero-shot/data-free, federated/distilled protocols, or self-supervised distillation) rather than as an off-the-shelf cure-all.

papers_seen.author: Pacheco
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation with Adversarial Samples Supporting Decision Boundary
papers_seen.abstract: Many recent works on knowledge distillation have provided ways to transfer the knowledge of a trained network for improving the learning process of a new one, but finding a good technique for knowledge distillation is still an open problem. In this paper, we provide a new perspective based on a decision boundary, which is one of the most important component of a classifier. The generalization performance of a classifier is closely related to the adequacy of its decision boundary, so a good classifier bears a good decision boundary. Therefore, transferring information closely related to the decision boundary can be a good attempt for knowledge distillation. To realize this goal, we utilize an adversarial attack to discover samples supporting a decision boundary. Based on this idea, to transfer more accurate information about the decision boundary, the proposed algorithm trains a student classifier based on the adversarial samples supporting the decision boundary. Experiments show that the proposed method indeed improves knowledge distillation and achieves the state-of-the-arts performance.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Fundamental Approach to Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a transformative technique for compressing neural networks while maintaining predictive performance. By enabling knowledge transfer from large teacher models to compact student networks, distillation addresses the critical challenge of deploying sophisticated deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents an essential methodology for practical machine learning deployment, offering significant advantages in model size reduction, computational efficiency, and accessibility across diverse application domains from natural language processing to computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Maddox
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Strategy for Compression, Regularization and Privacy-Preserving Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach for compressing high-capacity models into lightweight students while preserving or even improving generalization. Beyond simple teacher–student logits matching, KD can transfer architectural inductive biases, act as an effective regularizer, enable compression without access to original training data, and be adapted to low-data and multi-teacher settings. The choice of distillation objective, the availability of data, and the reliability of teacher signals determine success; consequently, a portfolio of techniques (data synthesis, augmentation, calibrated divergences, and confidence-aware aggregation) is needed to make KD robust and widely applicable in deep learning and NLP deployments.

papers_seen.author: Kim
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Strategic Approach for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a central and versatile technique for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing, enabling the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, deployable student networks. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should be considered a foundational tool in modern machine learning compression strategies, particularly when combined with strategic design choices and awareness of its limitations. The technique demonstrates broad applicability across diverse domains and problem settings, from vision and language tasks to graph neural networks and generative models, while supporting critical deployment requirements such as privacy preservation, data-free compression, and resource-constrained inference.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses information from larger or more complex models into smaller, faster models by transferring soft targets, intermediate representations, or relational structure. In deep learning and NLP, KD is used both to reduce inference cost and to adapt large pretrained models to new domains or resource-constrained settings. Practical KD pipelines balance fidelity to the teacher with student capacity, employ selective or curriculum-driven training data, and can combine with quantization or low-precision methods to meet latency and memory constraints. While KD frequently yields strong empirical gains, its effectiveness depends on data complexity, teacher quality, and how teacher knowledge is exposed to the student; these dependencies produce both opportunities (e.g., domain-specific distilled models) and risks (e.g., propagation of teacher errors). Current work advances theoretical understanding, proposes methods for student- and task-aware teacher design, and extends KD to robustness, large-scale distributed training, and low-precision deployment.

papers_seen.author: Valdez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has evolved from a single training recipe into a versatile set of techniques that enable deployment of large neural models under constraints of compute, latency, privacy, and heterogeneity. When combined with complementary strategies such as architecture search, progressive compression, and task-aware signal selection, distillation routinely produces compact models that retain much of teacher performance across modalities and tasks. Practical success depends on choosing distillation variants that match deployment needs and on designing teacher–student pairs and objectives that transfer the right internal and output signals.

papers_seen.author: Higgins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that enables the efficient deployment of large neural networks by training smaller student models to mimic the behavior of larger teacher models. This approach has become fundamental across computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains, addressing the critical challenge of reducing computational overhead and memory requirements while maintaining competitive performance. The technique encompasses diverse strategies ranging from soft label guidance to intermediate layer alignment and operates through the transfer of learned knowledge from teacher to student networks.

papers_seen.author: Conner
papers_seen.title: Distilling Task-Specific Knowledge from BERT into Simple Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: In the natural language processing literature, neural networks are becoming increasingly deeper and complex. The recent poster child of this trend is the deep language representation model, which includes BERT, ELMo, and GPT. These developments have led to the conviction that previous-generation, shallower neural networks for language understanding are obsolete. In this paper, however, we demonstrate that rudimentary, lightweight neural networks can still be made competitive without architecture changes, external training data, or additional input features. We propose to distill knowledge from BERT, a state-of-the-art language representation model, into a single-layer BiLSTM, as well as its siamese counterpart for sentence-pair tasks. Across multiple datasets in paraphrasing, natural language inference, and sentiment classification, we achieve comparable results with ELMo, while using roughly 100 times fewer parameters and 15 times less inference time.

papers_seen.author: Powers
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central strategy for compressing large, high-performing neural networks into smaller, more efficient models by transferring knowledge from a teacher to a student. Research over the past decade has produced a diverse set of distillation objectives (soft-target/logit matching, feature- and attention-level imitation, contrastive and adversarial formulations), integration with complementary compression techniques (pruning, layer skipping, architecture search, quantization), and methods for operating under deployment constraints (domain adaptation, data-free distillation, ensemble teachers). Empirical studies across vision, language, multimodal, and industrial prediction tasks demonstrate that carefully chosen distillation formulations and teacher-student pairings yield substantial gains in efficiency with limited accuracy loss, while ongoing challenges remain in handling domain shift, teacher errors, and task-specific desiderata.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical and Versatile Framework for Efficient Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a practical and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while preserving competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks, knowledge distillation enables the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. The technique encompasses multiple methodologies—including soft-target matching, feature mimicking, layer-wise alignment, and data-free synthesis—and has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and reinforcement learning. Recent research demonstrates that knowledge distillation is not merely a compression heuristic but a flexible toolkit that, when carefully designed and integrated with complementary techniques, can achieve student models that approach teacher performance while meeting practical deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Methods, Adaptations, and Practical Insights
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques have become standard tools to transfer knowledge from large, high-capacity models to smaller, efficient models suitable for deployment. Research across modalities and tasks has developed variants that go beyond matching output logits, including feature mimicking, attention- and channel-wise transfers, layer alignment strategies, and task-adaptive or domain-aware schemes. These approaches aim to preserve predictive accuracy and representational structure while reducing storage, computation, and latency. Practical advances demonstrate that carefully designed distillation objectives and mapping strategies can yield compact models that approach teacher performance on classification, ranking, language, speech, graph, and generative tasks, and that adapting distillation to task or domain specifics improves real-world applicability.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or other internal signals. Across vision and language, practitioners use a toolbox of techniques—soft-target/logit matching, feature- and attention-level alignment, layer-wise mapping or progressive replacement, multi/online-teacher schedules, and data-free synthesis—to reduce parameter counts and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. Empirical work shows substantial efficiency gains are possible when distillation is combined with complementary methods (pre-training, pruning, quantization, architecture design), but open problems remain in robustness transfer, domain shift, low-frequency and structural knowledge, and principled teacher-student selection for varied deployment constraints.
