papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Methods and Practices for Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible set of techniques to transfer knowledge from a high-capacity teacher model to a smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student. Work across modalities and tasks has shown KD can yield compact models that approach teacher performance, enable deployment on resource-limited devices, help mitigate data-availability or privacy constraints, and act as a vehicle for transferring ensemble or multi-teacher knowledge into a single model. Practical KD methods vary in what they transfer (logits, intermediate features, or rankings), whether they require original training data, and how they structure training (offline, online, adversarial, or curriculum-based). Empirical and methodological work highlights (1) the effectiveness of feature-level supervision in many settings, (2) the value of synthetic or replayed data when real data are unavailable, (3) that ensemble and online schemes can speed training and improve robustness, and (4) that augmentation, sample selection, and task-specific losses materially affect distilled-student outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Explaining Knowledge Distillation by Quantifying the Knowledge
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a method to interpret the success of knowledge distillation by quantifying and analyzing task-relevant and task-irrelevant visual concepts that are encoded in intermediate layers of a deep neural network (DNN). More specifically, three hypotheses are proposed as follows. 1. Knowledge distillation makes the DNN learn more visual concepts than learning from raw data. 2. Knowledge distillation ensures that the DNN is prone to learning various visual concepts simultaneously. Whereas, in the scenario of learning from raw data, the DNN learns visual concepts sequentially. 3. Knowledge distillation yields more stable optimization directions than learning from raw data. Accordingly, we design three types of mathematical metrics to evaluate feature representations of the DNN. In experiments, we diagnosed various DNNs, and above hypotheses were verified.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: AutoGAN-Distiller: Searching to Compress Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: The compression of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has lately drawn attention, due to the increasing demand for deploying GANs into mobile devices for numerous applications such as image translation, enhancement and editing. However, compared to the substantial efforts to compressing other deep models, the research on compressing GANs (usually the generators) remains at its infancy stage. Existing GAN compression algorithms are limited to handling specific GAN architectures and losses. Inspired by the recent success of AutoML in deep compression, we introduce AutoML to GAN compression and develop an AutoGAN-Distiller (AGD) framework. Starting with a specifically designed efficient search space, AGD performs an end-to-end discovery for new efficient generators, given the target computational resource constraints. The search is guided by the original GAN model via knowledge distillation, therefore fulfilling the compression. AGD is fully automatic, standalone (i.e., needing no trained discriminators), and generically applicable to various GAN models. We evaluate AGD in two representative GAN tasks: image translation and super resolution. Without bells and whistles, AGD yields remarkably lightweight yet more competitive compressed models, that largely outperform existing alternatives. Our codes and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/TAMU-VITA/AGD.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Knowledge Distillation for CTR Prediction
papers_seen.abstract: Recently, deep learning-based models have been widely studied for click-through rate (CTR) prediction and lead to improved prediction accuracy in many industrial applications. However, current research focuses primarily on building complex network architectures to better capture sophisticated feature interactions and dynamic user behaviors. The increased model complexity may slow down online inference and hinder its adoption in real-time applications. Instead, our work targets at a new model training strategy based on knowledge distillation (KD). KD is a teacher-student learning framework to transfer knowledge learned from a teacher model to a student model. The KD strategy not only allows us to simplify the student model as a vanilla DNN model but also achieves significant accuracy improvements over the state-of-the-art teacher models. The benefits thus motivate us to further explore the use of a powerful ensemble of teachers for more accurate student model training. We also propose some novel techniques to facilitate ensembled CTR prediction, including teacher gating and early stopping by distillation loss. We conduct comprehensive experiments against 12 existing models and across three industrial datasets. Both offline and online A/B testing results show the effectiveness of our KD-based training strategy.

papers_seen.author: Bush
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Techniques, and Caveats
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a niche compression trick into a broad set of methods that enable deploying high-performing but compact models across vision, language, and other domains. KD techniques operate at different levels (logits, feature maps, intermediate layers) and can be combined with pruning, quantization, or domain adaptation strategies to meet latency, memory, privacy, and cross-domain generalization constraints. When applied with task-aware design and attention to optimization and data constraints, KD yields substantial practical gains for real-world systems; however, mismatches between teacher and student capacities, data availability, and optimization dynamics require careful method selection and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical and Necessary Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central framework for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from teachers to students. As deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy, heterogeneous devices) grow, KD’s flexibility — spanning soft-target matching, intermediate representation alignment, attention- and channel-wise transfer, multi-teacher schedules, and data-aware procedures — makes it uniquely suited to balance fidelity and efficiency. However, realizing KD’s promise in practice requires careful design choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student representations, and how to handle limited or private data. When combined with complementary compression techniques and representation-aware training practices, KD reliably produces compact models suitable for real-world NLP and multimodal systems.

papers_seen.author: Waller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a model compression technique that enables the transfer of knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach has become increasingly essential for deploying state-of-the-art neural networks in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation encompasses a diverse set of theoretical and practical approaches, ranging from simple logit matching to sophisticated intermediate representation alignment and task-aware compression strategies. The technique has been successfully applied across multiple domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, speech recognition, and specialized applications such as recommendation systems and graph neural networks. By addressing critical deployment constraints such as latency, memory, computational cost, and privacy, knowledge distillation has emerged as a foundational technique in modern machine learning.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Learning Compact Metrics for MT
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in machine translation and multilingual text generation have led researchers to adopt trained metrics such as COMET or BLEURT, which treat evaluation as a regression problem and use representations from multilingual pre-trained models such as XLM-RoBERTa or mBERT. Yet studies on related tasks suggest that these models are most efficient when they are large, which is costly and impractical for evaluation. We investigate the trade-off between multilinguality and model capacity with RemBERT, a state-of-the-art multilingual language model, using data from the WMT Metrics Shared Task. We present a series of experiments which show that model size is indeed a bottleneck for cross-lingual transfer, then demonstrate how distillation can help addressing this bottleneck, by leveraging synthetic data generation and transferring knowledge from one teacher to multiple students trained on related languages. Our method yields up to 10.5% improvement over vanilla fine-tuning and reaches 92.6% of RemBERT's performance using only a third of its parameters.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: PKD: General Distillation Framework for Object Detectors via Pearson Correlation Coefficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation(KD) is a widely-used technique to train compact models in object detection. However, there is still a lack of study on how to distill between heterogeneous detectors. In this paper, we empirically find that better FPN features from a heterogeneous teacher detector can help the student although their detection heads and label assignments are different. However, directly aligning the feature maps to distill detectors suffers from two problems. First, the difference in feature magnitude between the teacher and the student could enforce overly strict constraints on the student. Second, the FPN stages and channels with large feature magnitude from the teacher model could dominate the gradient of distillation loss, which will overwhelm the effects of other features in KD and introduce much noise. To address the above issues, we propose to imitate features with Pearson Correlation Coefficient to focus on the relational information from the teacher and relax constraints on the magnitude of the features. Our method consistently outperforms the existing detection KD methods and works for both homogeneous and heterogeneous student-teacher pairs. Furthermore, it converges faster. With a powerful MaskRCNN-Swin detector as the teacher, ResNet-50 based RetinaNet and FCOS achieve 41.5% and 43.9% mAP on COCO2017, which are 4.1\% and 4.8\% higher than the baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Novak
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a central technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while preserving performance. This method transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lower-capacity student models, enabling deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices. The approach has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech processing, and graph neural networks, with various methodological innovations continuously expanding its scope and effectiveness.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-adopted model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large, complex teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach enables the deployment of high-performing deep learning models on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive accuracy. Knowledge distillation has been applied across multiple domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, graph neural networks, and recommendation systems, with variants adapted to different architectures and task-specific requirements. The technique addresses the critical challenge of deploying sophisticated neural models in resource-constrained environments while managing computational efficiency, latency, and storage constraints.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential Framework for Model Compression and Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers learned representations from complex teacher networks to simpler student networks, enabling efficient deployment across resource-constrained environments in natural language processing, computer vision, and other domains. The method addresses critical practical challenges in model deployment including computational efficiency, memory constraints, and latency reduction without sacrificing accuracy. Beyond compression, knowledge distillation facilitates knowledge transfer across architectures, improves model robustness, and supports learning from ensembles, making it an indispensable tool in modern deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Rios
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a technique for transferring knowledge from a large, complex teacher model to a smaller, more efficient student model. This approach enables model compression while maintaining performance, making it valuable for deployment on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across various domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and federated learning, addressing both computational efficiency and interpretability challenges in deep neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression approaches transfer information from larger or differently-abled models to smaller, faster, or modality-restricted models. Methods vary from matching final soft logits to mimicking intermediate representations, mapping layers across architectures, adversarially synthesizing training data, and adapting distillation to distributed or heterogeneous-device settings. Empirical and theoretical work highlights trade-offs between simplicity, effectiveness, data availability, and task-specificity, and suggests design patterns for effective compression across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Private Model Compression via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The soaring demand for intelligent mobile applications calls for deploying powerful deep neural networks (DNNs) on mobile devices. However, the outstanding performance of DNNs notoriously relies on increasingly complex models, which in turn is associated with an increase in computational expense far surpassing mobile devices' capacity. What is worse, app service providers need to collect and utilize a large volume of users' data, which contain sensitive information, to build the sophisticated DNN models. Directly deploying these models on public mobile devices presents prohibitive privacy risk. To benefit from the on-device deep learning without the capacity and privacy concerns, we design a private model compression framework RONA. Following the knowledge distillation paradigm, we jointly use hint learning, distillation learning, and self learning to train a compact and fast neural network. The knowledge distilled from the cumbersome model is adaptively bounded and carefully perturbed to enforce differential privacy. We further propose an elegant query sample selection method to reduce the number of queries and control the privacy loss. A series of empirical evaluations as well as the implementation on an Android mobile device show that RONA can not only compress cumbersome models efficiently but also provide a strong privacy guarantee. For example, on SVHN, when a meaningful $(9.83,10^{-6})$-differential privacy is guaranteed, the compact model trained by RONA can obtain 20$\times$ compression ratio and 19$\times$ speed-up with merely 0.97% accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from well-trained teacher models to student networks, this approach enables practical deployment of sophisticated deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. The methodology encompasses diverse approaches ranging from soft target matching to intermediate representation alignment, and has demonstrated effectiveness across multiple domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and recommender systems. Recent advances have expanded knowledge distillation beyond simple output probability matching to include multi-teacher frameworks, task-aware layer-wise distillation, and integration with complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Larson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical Approach to Deploying Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Systems
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing. By transferring knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, knowledge distillation enables the deployment of sophisticated neural networks on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive performance. This approach has proven effective across multiple domains and has evolved beyond basic teacher-student frameworks to encompass diverse methodologies including feature-level distillation, multi-teacher selection, zero-shot learning, and adversarial sample selection. Despite challenges in optimization and teacher-student capacity mismatches, knowledge distillation remains essential for practical deployment scenarios requiring efficient inference without substantial accuracy degradation.

papers_seen.author: Harrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques transform large, costly models into smaller, faster, or more private models while retaining much of the original performance. Across modalities and tasks, distillation has been applied to compress vision and language models, transfer cross-modal or privileged information, enable deployment under latency and memory constraints, and preserve privacy in distributed settings. Key directions include distillation of logits (soft labels), feature- or attention-level distillation, self-distillation, data-free or zero-shot approaches, and architecture-aware compression. Empirical results show that when carefully designed—often combining distillation with pruning or architecture search—student models can approach teacher accuracy, gain robustness, or enable capabilities (e.g., multimodal generation) previously unavailable to the smaller model. Important open problems remain in data heterogeneity, robustness transfer, and principled teacher-student design for diverse deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Bush
papers_seen.title: Multi-Label Image Classification via Knowledge Distillation from Weakly-Supervised Detection
papers_seen.abstract: Multi-label image classification is a fundamental but challenging task towards general visual understanding. Existing methods found the region-level cues (e.g., features from RoIs) can facilitate multi-label classification. Nevertheless, such methods usually require laborious object-level annotations (i.e., object labels and bounding boxes) for effective learning of the object-level visual features. In this paper, we propose a novel and efficient deep framework to boost multi-label classification by distilling knowledge from weakly-supervised detection task without bounding box annotations. Specifically, given the image-level annotations, (1) we first develop a weakly-supervised detection (WSD) model, and then (2) construct an end-to-end multi-label image classification framework augmented by a knowledge distillation module that guides the classification model by the WSD model according to the class-level predictions for the whole image and the object-level visual features for object RoIs. The WSD model is the teacher model and the classification model is the student model. After this cross-task knowledge distillation, the performance of the classification model is significantly improved and the efficiency is maintained since the WSD model can be safely discarded in the test phase. Extensive experiments on two large-scale datasets (MS-COCO and NUS-WIDE) show that our framework achieves superior performances over the state-of-the-art methods on both performance and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become fundamental techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, enabling practical deployment while maintaining competitive performance. The techniques address critical challenges in modern deep learning, including reducing inference latency, memory requirements, and computational costs across diverse domains including computer vision and natural language processing.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Reassessing Knowledge Distillation: Regularization, Teacher Quality, and Task-Driven Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile tool for compressing models and transferring capabilities from large teachers to smaller students across vision, graph, 3D, and NLP tasks. Its effectiveness arises not only from transmitting teacher class similarities but also from the regularizing properties of soft targets and from mimicking intermediate representations. Recent advances demonstrate that KD can be applied without direct access to a strong pretrained teacher or original training data, and that task-specific distillation objectives (contrastive, adversarial, feature-level) often outperform naive logit matching. At the same time, optimization barriers, teacher errors, and domain shifts can limit or bias distilled students, so practitioners should choose distillation formulations and teacher-student pairings that align with the target task and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Techniques and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing, enabling the creation of efficient student models that learn from larger, more complex teacher networks. This approach addresses the fundamental challenge of deploying sophisticated neural models in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. The methodology spans multiple domains including computer vision, NLP tasks, and graph neural networks, demonstrating its versatility and effectiveness across different problem spaces. Beyond basic compression, knowledge distillation has been extended to address important concerns such as adversarial robustness, privacy preservation, fairness mitigation, and domain generalization, establishing it as a foundational technique in modern machine learning.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Keystone for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically essential family of techniques for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable ones without sacrificing much task performance. Across supervised, self-supervised, federated, and data-constrained settings, KD enables latency- and memory-efficient deployment, supports domain adaptation, and can be adapted to privacy-sensitive and distributed workflows. Advances in KD emphasize not only learning from teacher logits but also mimicking intermediate features, designing student-friendly teacher objectives, and automating student architectures for specific tasks—yielding a spectrum of methods that together make model compression tractable in real-world NLP and vision systems.

papers_seen.author: Allen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Critical Technology for Efficient Neural Network Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has become an indispensable technique for deploying high-performing deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to compact student models, distillation enables significant reductions in computational requirements and model size while maintaining competitive performance. This position argues that knowledge distillation, when properly designed and combined with complementary compression strategies, represents the most practical and versatile approach to achieving efficient neural networks across diverse applications in computer vision, natural language processing, and beyond.

papers_seen.author: Pena
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practical family of methods for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information from a high-capacity teacher to a compact student using a range of signals (soft logits, intermediate representations, layer-wise supervision, or synthesized data). Across vision and language tasks, KD enables substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance, and it composes effectively with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical success requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to handle limited or private data, and how to evaluate robustness and rare-case behavior.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Towards Practical Lipreading with Distilled and Efficient Models
papers_seen.abstract: Lipreading has witnessed a lot of progress due to the resurgence of neural networks. Recent works have placed emphasis on aspects such as improving performance by finding the optimal architecture or improving generalization. However, there is still a significant gap between the current methodologies and the requirements for an effective deployment of lipreading in practical scenarios. In this work, we propose a series of innovations that significantly bridge that gap: first, we raise the state-of-the-art performance by a wide margin on LRW and LRW-1000 to 88.5% and 46.6%, respectively using self-distillation. Secondly, we propose a series of architectural changes, including a novel Depthwise Separable Temporal Convolutional Network (DS-TCN) head, that slashes the computational cost to a fraction of the (already quite efficient) original model. Thirdly, we show that knowledge distillation is a very effective tool for recovering performance of the lightweight models. This results in a range of models with different accuracy-efficiency trade-offs. However, our most promising lightweight models are on par with the current state-of-the-art while showing a reduction of 8.2x and 3.9x in terms of computational cost and number of parameters, respectively, which we hope will enable the deployment of lipreading models in practical applications.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Beyond Soft Labels: A Multi-Objective View of Knowledge Distillation for Robust, Efficient Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical route to compress large neural models for deployment, but treating distillation as merely matching teacher output probabilities limits what can be transferred and how reliably the student will generalize. This paper argues that effective distillation should combine representation-level transfer, channel- and feature-aware objectives, confidence-weighted multi-teacher signals, domain adaptation, and training-time efficiency techniques, while explicitly attending to optimization gaps and fairness concerns. We synthesize evidence across methods and propose a prioritized, pragmatic pipeline for producing compact models that better retain teacher knowledge, scale in production, and reduce unintended harms.

papers_seen.author: Arroyo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques have become central to deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Research spans practical recipes (logit matching, feature and layer-wise matching, projector modules), structural compression (architectural transforms, channel/filter reduction), and specialized strategies for NLP models (layer mapping for transformers and task-aware layer selection). Recent work also addresses learning dynamics and theory for wide networks, multi-teacher and meta-learned teaching, and scenarios with limited or no access to original training data. Empirical results show that careful choice of distillation targets, alignment mechanisms, and teacher-student curricula can yield compact models that retain strong performance on downstream tasks while enabling faster inference and smaller memory footprints. Open challenges include task-specific selection of distilled knowledge, robustness and generalization across distributions, and principled guidelines for architecture-aware distillation in transformers.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Understanding BERT Rankers Under Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep language models such as BERT pre-trained on large corpus have given a huge performance boost to the state-of-the-art information retrieval ranking systems. Knowledge embedded in such models allows them to pick up complex matching signals between passages and queries. However, the high computation cost during inference limits their deployment in real-world search scenarios. In this paper, we study if and how the knowledge for search within BERT can be transferred to a smaller ranker through distillation. Our experiments demonstrate that it is crucial to use a proper distillation procedure, which produces up to nine times speedup while preserving the state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: Powerful, Practical, but Context-Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, empirically effective route to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students in deep learning and NLP. KD encompasses a range of techniques (soft-label matching, representation mimicry, intermediate-layer alignment, multi-teacher/ensemble strategies, and data-free or online variants). While KD often yields substantial gains in model size, latency, and memory with modest performance loss, its success depends on data characteristics, teacher–student capacity relationships, and deployment constraints. Best practice treats KD as a toolkit to be combined with targeted data strategies, representation-level objectives, and teacher selection or synthesis, rather than a single off-the-shelf solution.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to compact student models while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in deploying deep learning systems across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, machine translation, and speech recognition, providing a practical pathway for creating efficient models without substantial accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Rocha
papers_seen.title: Few Shot Network Compression via Cross Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Model compression has been widely adopted to obtain light-weighted deep neural networks. Most prevalent methods, however, require fine-tuning with sufficient training data to ensure accuracy, which could be challenged by privacy and security issues. As a compromise between privacy and performance, in this paper we investigate few shot network compression: given few samples per class, how can we effectively compress the network with negligible performance drop? The core challenge of few shot network compression lies in high estimation errors from the original network during inference, since the compressed network can easily over-fits on the few training instances. The estimation errors could propagate and accumulate layer-wisely and finally deteriorate the network output. To address the problem, we propose cross distillation, a novel layer-wise knowledge distillation approach. By interweaving hidden layers of teacher and student network, layer-wisely accumulated estimation errors can be effectively reduced.The proposed method offers a general framework compatible with prevalent network compression techniques such as pruning. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that cross distillation can significantly improve the student network's accuracy when only a few training instances are available.

papers_seen.author: Owens
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD methods span logit matching, feature- and layer-level mimicry, ensemble and online schemes, and augmentation-driven strategies. When applied thoughtfully — choosing appropriate distillation targets, considering teacher-student capacity and data availability, and employing methods such as projector layers or data augmentation — KD can deliver compact models that approach teacher accuracy across vision and language tasks. However, realizing these gains requires attention to optimization dynamics and task-specific constraints.

papers_seen.author: Mckay
papers_seen.title: MixKD: Towards Efficient Distillation of Large-scale Language Models
papers_seen.abstract: Large-scale language models have recently demonstrated impressive empirical performance. Nevertheless, the improved results are attained at the price of bigger models, more power consumption, and slower inference, which hinder their applicability to low-resource (both memory and computation) platforms. Knowledge distillation (KD) has been demonstrated as an effective framework for compressing such big models. However, large-scale neural network systems are prone to memorize training instances, and thus tend to make inconsistent predictions when the data distribution is altered slightly. Moreover, the student model has few opportunities to request useful information from the teacher model when there is limited task-specific data available. To address these issues, we propose MixKD, a data-agnostic distillation framework that leverages mixup, a simple yet efficient data augmentation approach, to endow the resulting model with stronger generalization ability. Concretely, in addition to the original training examples, the student model is encouraged to mimic the teacher's behavior on the linear interpolation of example pairs as well. We prove from a theoretical perspective that under reasonable conditions MixKD gives rise to a smaller gap between the generalization error and the empirical error. To verify its effectiveness, we conduct experiments on the GLUE benchmark, where MixKD consistently leads to significant gains over the standard KD training, and outperforms several competitive baselines. Experiments under a limited-data setting and ablation studies further demonstrate the advantages of the proposed approach.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Apprentice: Using Knowledge Distillation Techniques To Improve Low-Precision Network Accuracy
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning networks have achieved state-of-the-art accuracies on computer vision workloads like image classification and object detection. The performant systems, however, typically involve big models with numerous parameters. Once trained, a challenging aspect for such top performing models is deployment on resource constrained inference systems - the models (often deep networks or wide networks or both) are compute and memory intensive. Low-precision numerics and model compression using knowledge distillation are popular techniques to lower both the compute requirements and memory footprint of these deployed models. In this paper, we study the combination of these two techniques and show that the performance of low-precision networks can be significantly improved by using knowledge distillation techniques. Our approach, Apprentice, achieves state-of-the-art accuracies using ternary precision and 4-bit precision for variants of ResNet architecture on ImageNet dataset. We present three schemes using which one can apply knowledge distillation techniques to various stages of the train-and-deploy pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Zamora
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression and efficient deployment of neural networks. This approach involves transferring knowledge from larger, more capable teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, enabling their deployment in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. The technique has been extensively applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications, addressing critical challenges in practical deployment of state-of-the-art neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: An Essential Strategy for Deploying Deep Learning and NLP Systems
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while transferring valuable learned knowledge. This approach enables the practical deployment of high-performing deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and machine translation. By transferring knowledge beyond simple class labels to encompass soft targets, intermediate representations, and structural behaviors, knowledge distillation addresses the critical challenge of balancing model capacity with computational efficiency while maintaining competitive performance.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation in Efficient and Robust NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a unifying approach for producing smaller, faster, and often more robust models for NLP and deep learning broadly. When combined with architecture search, layer-wise matching, data-centric techniques, and privacy-aware protocols, distillation enables task-adaptive compression, domain adaptation, and practical deployment under latency, memory, and regulatory constraints. However, the benefits of distillation depend on how knowledge is represented, which data and augmentations are used during transfer, and whether the distillation procedure is aligned with downstream tasks; careful method design—rather than blind teacher-student pairing—is therefore required to realize its full promise.

papers_seen.author: Wheeler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Flexible Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a foundational technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while maintaining competitive performance. Rather than a single monolithic approach, KD functions best as a flexible, composable framework that can be adapted to specific task, data, and hardware constraints. When combined with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, and data-aware strategies, KD enables practical deployment of high-performing models on resource-constrained devices while addressing real-world challenges including privacy concerns, data unavailability, and computational limitations.

papers_seen.author: Alvarado
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while preserving performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to students, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices and reducing computational overhead. KD encompasses diverse methodologies including soft-target matching, feature-level mimicry, data-free approaches, and multi-teacher strategies, with applications spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks. The field continues to evolve with new insights into when and why distillation succeeds, addressing challenges such as data heterogeneity, privacy constraints, and the selection of appropriate student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Comprehensive Framework for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and practical approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This technique enables the transfer of knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, making deployment in resource-constrained environments feasible without sacrificing accuracy. The method has proven successful across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and multimodal learning, offering substantial performance improvements and computational efficiency gains with minimal accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Maldonado
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge by Mimicking Features
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a popular method to train efficient networks ("student") with the help of high-capacity networks ("teacher"). Traditional methods use the teacher's soft logits as extra supervision to train the student network. In this paper, we argue that it is more advantageous to make the student mimic the teacher's features in the penultimate layer. Not only the student can directly learn more effective information from the teacher feature, feature mimicking can also be applied for teachers trained without a softmax layer. Experiments show that it can achieve higher accuracy than traditional KD. To further facilitate feature mimicking, we decompose a feature vector into the magnitude and the direction. We argue that the teacher should give more freedom to the student feature's magnitude, and let the student pay more attention on mimicking the feature direction. To meet this requirement, we propose a loss term based on locality-sensitive hashing (LSH). With the help of this new loss, our method indeed mimics feature directions more accurately, relaxes constraints on feature magnitudes, and achieves state-of-the-art distillation accuracy. We provide theoretical analyses of how LSH facilitates feature direction mimicking, and further extend feature mimicking to multi-label recognition and object detection.

papers_seen.author: Freeman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Strategic Approach to Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lightweight student models while maintaining competitive performance across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and speech processing. By employing multiple mechanisms such as soft-label matching, intermediate representation transfer, and task-adaptive strategies, knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in model size, inference latency, and computational resource requirements while enabling practical deployment of state-of-the-art models.

papers_seen.author: Hurst
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques have matured into a diverse set of methods for producing smaller, faster, and sometimes more robust models from larger teachers. Approaches span from soft-label and internal-representation transfer to data-free distillation, federated/distilled training for privacy and communication efficiency, and task-adaptive architecture search for large pretrained language models. Empirical work shows KD can improve inference efficiency with limited accuracy loss, transfer adversarial robustness, and enable effective low-precision and task-specific compressed models, while theoretical analyses and algorithmic variants clarify when and why distillation helps.

papers_seen.author: Callahan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring useful information from teacher models. Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple soft-label matching to a rich toolkit that includes representation- and layer-level transfer, architecture-aware transformations, data- and teacher-selection strategies, and domain-adaptive procedures. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can yield large efficiency gains while retaining most teacher performance, but practical success depends on careful choices about what is distilled, how teachers and students are prepared, and how data or synthetic examples are used.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential, Practically Flexible Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical strategy for compressing large neural models into deployable students while preserving much of the teacher’s capabilities. KD techniques span matching teacher logits, aligning internal features, and using multi-teacher or teacher-free schedules; they enable large speedups and memory reductions, adapt to privacy- and data-limited settings, and have been successfully applied across retrieval, graph learning, generative models, and pretrained NLP transformers. The choice of what to transfer (outputs vs. intermediate representations), how to weight multiple sources, and whether to rely on original data fundamentally shapes outcomes. I argue that KD is indispensable for real-world deep learning deployment, but progress will require tighter practices for representation alignment, student-friendly teacher design, and handling heterogeneous or private data.

papers_seen.author: Moran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Insights
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying large, powerful deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, enabling practical deployment with reduced computational requirements and memory footprint while maintaining competitive performance across diverse applications in computer vision and natural language processing.

papers_seen.author: May
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Strategic Framework for Deploying Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a foundational and practical approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while maintaining competitive performance. Rather than a single monolithic technique, knowledge distillation functions as a flexible, composable framework that can be adapted to specific task, data, and hardware constraints. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should be treated as the default strategy for model compression across deep learning and NLP applications, particularly when combined with complementary compression techniques and careful consideration of optimization and data constraints.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Composable Core for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a versatile foundation for compressing large neural models into efficient students suitable for real-world deployment. As models grow in size and application contexts diversify, distillation provides a set of interoperable mechanisms — from soft-target transfer to intermediate feature matching, self-distillation, and teacher-ensemble consolidation — that can be combined with architecture search, quantization, and task-aware filtering to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. While distillation often preserves much of teacher performance, careful choices about what to transfer, which data to use, and how to adapt the student architecture are necessary to avoid failure modes such as degraded handling of low-frequency phenomena or overfitting teacher artifacts. A composable, task- and data-aware distillation strategy that integrates representation-level objectives, selective data curation, and architecture adaptation yields the best practical trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Riley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Frameworks, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while transferring valuable learned knowledge. This approach enables the deployment of high-performing deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments across multiple domains including computer vision and natural language processing. Knowledge distillation operates through teacher-student learning frameworks that transfer knowledge beyond simple class labels to encompass soft targets, intermediate representations, and structural behaviors. The technique addresses critical challenges in balancing model capacity with computational efficiency while maintaining competitive performance and enabling practical deployment of state-of-the-art models.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Towards Practical Lipreading with Distilled and Efficient Models
papers_seen.abstract: Lipreading has witnessed a lot of progress due to the resurgence of neural networks. Recent works have placed emphasis on aspects such as improving performance by finding the optimal architecture or improving generalization. However, there is still a significant gap between the current methodologies and the requirements for an effective deployment of lipreading in practical scenarios. In this work, we propose a series of innovations that significantly bridge that gap: first, we raise the state-of-the-art performance by a wide margin on LRW and LRW-1000 to 88.5% and 46.6%, respectively using self-distillation. Secondly, we propose a series of architectural changes, including a novel Depthwise Separable Temporal Convolutional Network (DS-TCN) head, that slashes the computational cost to a fraction of the (already quite efficient) original model. Thirdly, we show that knowledge distillation is a very effective tool for recovering performance of the lightweight models. This results in a range of models with different accuracy-efficiency trade-offs. However, our most promising lightweight models are on par with the current state-of-the-art while showing a reduction of 8.2x and 3.9x in terms of computational cost and number of parameters, respectively, which we hope will enable the deployment of lipreading models in practical applications.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Bridging the Gap Between Performance and Efficiency in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful paradigm for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing, enabling the transfer of knowledge from larger, well-trained teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student networks. This technique addresses the critical challenge of deploying sophisticated neural networks on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive performance. Through various methodological innovations ranging from attention-based mechanisms to adversarial approaches, knowledge distillation has demonstrated its effectiveness across multiple domains including computer vision, machine translation, and NLP tasks. The field continues to evolve with advances in online distillation, multi-modal approaches, and task-aware compression strategies that optimize the knowledge transfer process.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Unifying Heterogeneous Classifiers with Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we study the problem of unifying knowledge from a set of classifiers with different architectures and target classes into a single classifier, given only a generic set of unlabelled data. We call this problem Unifying Heterogeneous Classifiers (UHC). This problem is motivated by scenarios where data is collected from multiple sources, but the sources cannot share their data, e.g., due to privacy concerns, and only privately trained models can be shared. In addition, each source may not be able to gather data to train all classes due to data availability at each source, and may not be able to train the same classification model due to different computational resources. To tackle this problem, we propose a generalisation of knowledge distillation to merge HCs. We derive a probabilistic relation between the outputs of HCs and the probability over all classes. Based on this relation, we propose two classes of methods based on cross-entropy minimisation and matrix factorisation, which allow us to estimate soft labels over all classes from unlabelled samples and use them in lieu of ground truth labels to train a unified classifier. Our extensive experiments on ImageNet, LSUN, and Places365 datasets show that our approaches significantly outperform a naive extension of distillation and can achieve almost the same accuracy as classifiers that are trained in a centralised, supervised manner.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from a larger teacher model to a smaller student model, enabling efficient deployment of neural networks while maintaining competitive performance. This technique has become increasingly important across various domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications. The approach addresses the critical challenge of deploying complex, high-performing deep learning models on resource-constrained devices by enabling smaller models to achieve comparable results to their larger counterparts.

papers_seen.author: Shields
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Review
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a foundational model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large teacher networks to smaller student networks, enabling efficient deployment of neural models in resource-constrained environments. This synthesis examines the evolution of knowledge distillation from early soft-label matching approaches to sophisticated multi-level knowledge transfer strategies, exploring its applications across natural language processing, computer vision, and multimodal tasks. The review highlights how knowledge distillation addresses critical practical constraints in model deployment while revealing emerging challenges and best practices for effective compression.

papers_seen.author: Osborne
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely-adopted technique for training compact and efficient models by transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models. This approach has become instrumental across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications like graph neural networks and recommender systems. The technique addresses the fundamental challenge of deploying sophisticated deep learning models in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance levels. Recent advances have expanded the methodology beyond simple output probability matching to include intermediate representations, multi-teacher frameworks, and integration with complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and NLP applications. By enabling the transfer of knowledge from large teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges of inference speed, memory consumption, and computational resource requirements. This approach has been successfully applied across diverse domains including NLP tasks, computer vision, federated learning, and various specialized applications, offering practical solutions for deploying complex models in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Channel Distillation: Channel-Wise Attention for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is to transfer the knowledge from the data learned by the teacher network to the student network, so that the student has the advantage of less parameters and less calculations, and the accuracy is close to the teacher. In this paper, we propose a new distillation method, which contains two transfer distillation strategies and a loss decay strategy. The first transfer strategy is based on channel-wise attention, called Channel Distillation (CD). CD transfers the channel information from the teacher to the student. The second is Guided Knowledge Distillation (GKD). Unlike Knowledge Distillation (KD), which allows the student to mimic each sample's prediction distribution of the teacher, GKD only enables the student to mimic the correct output of the teacher. The last part is Early Decay Teacher (EDT). During the training process, we gradually decay the weight of the distillation loss. The purpose is to enable the student to gradually control the optimization rather than the teacher. Our proposed method is evaluated on ImageNet and CIFAR100. On ImageNet, we achieve 27.68% of top-1 error with ResNet18, which outperforms state-of-the-art methods. On CIFAR100, we achieve surprising result that the student outperforms the teacher. Code is available at https://github.com/zhouzaida/channel-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques transfer information from larger, high-capacity models into smaller, more efficient models to enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Practitioners use a variety of objectives and architectures—logit matching, intermediate-feature imitation, layer-wise supervision, and adversarial or ensemble-based transfers—often combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Applications span vision, speech, recommender systems, machine translation, reading comprehension and multi-modal medical imaging. Key challenges include mismatches between teacher and student capacity, reliance on teacher training data, maintaining performance on rare or low-frequency phenomena, and the runtime cost of using large teachers during distillation. Recent work addresses these with task-aware layer selection, student-aware teacher training, data-free or privacy-preserving distillation, and joint optimization of compression with distillation losses.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Linkless Link Prediction via Relational Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown exceptional performance in the task of link prediction. Despite their effectiveness, the high latency brought by non-trivial neighborhood data dependency limits GNNs in practical deployments. Conversely, the known efficient MLPs are much less effective than GNNs due to the lack of relational knowledge. In this work, to combine the advantages of GNNs and MLPs, we start with exploring direct knowledge distillation (KD) methods for link prediction, i.e., predicted logit-based matching and node representation-based matching. Upon observing direct KD analogs do not perform well for link prediction, we propose a relational KD framework, Linkless Link Prediction (LLP), to distill knowledge for link prediction with MLPs. Unlike simple KD methods that match independent link logits or node representations, LLP distills relational knowledge that is centered around each (anchor) node to the student MLP. Specifically, we propose rank-based matching and distribution-based matching strategies that complement each other. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LLP boosts the link prediction performance of MLPs with significant margins, and even outperforms the teacher GNNs on 7 out of 8 benchmarks. LLP also achieves a 70.68x speedup in link prediction inference compared to GNNs on the large-scale OGB dataset.
