papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach enables the deployment of state-of-the-art neural networks in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. KD has evolved significantly beyond simple logit matching to encompass diverse techniques including intermediate representation matching, layer-wise alignment, multi-teacher training, data-free approaches, and task-adaptive architecture search. The technique is now widely applied across multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, graph neural networks, and generative tasks, addressing critical challenges in bridging the gap between model performance and practical deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Cowan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of their performance. KD techniques range from classic soft-logit matching to feature- and layer-wise transfer, and they enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, realizing KD's benefits requires task- and architecture-aware choices: what to distill (logits, features, internal layers), how to handle limited or private data, and how to align teacher-student capacities. When combined with principled practices, KD is indispensable for translating research-scale models into robust, efficient production systems.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Private Model Compression via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The soaring demand for intelligent mobile applications calls for deploying powerful deep neural networks (DNNs) on mobile devices. However, the outstanding performance of DNNs notoriously relies on increasingly complex models, which in turn is associated with an increase in computational expense far surpassing mobile devices' capacity. What is worse, app service providers need to collect and utilize a large volume of users' data, which contain sensitive information, to build the sophisticated DNN models. Directly deploying these models on public mobile devices presents prohibitive privacy risk. To benefit from the on-device deep learning without the capacity and privacy concerns, we design a private model compression framework RONA. Following the knowledge distillation paradigm, we jointly use hint learning, distillation learning, and self learning to train a compact and fast neural network. The knowledge distilled from the cumbersome model is adaptively bounded and carefully perturbed to enforce differential privacy. We further propose an elegant query sample selection method to reduce the number of queries and control the privacy loss. A series of empirical evaluations as well as the implementation on an Android mobile device show that RONA can not only compress cumbersome models efficiently but also provide a strong privacy guarantee. For example, on SVHN, when a meaningful $(9.83,10^{-6})$-differential privacy is guaranteed, the compact model trained by RONA can obtain 20$\times$ compression ratio and 19$\times$ speed-up with merely 0.97% accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Effective Practices and Limits of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students. When combined with complementary strategies—such as pre-training compact architectures, layer-wise or representation-level transfer, task-aware selection of distilled signals, quantization, and federated or data-free techniques—KD can preserve much of teacher performance while meeting resource constraints. However, distillation is not a silver bullet: optimization challenges, mismatch between teacher and student internals, and mismatches between teacher predictions and task needs can limit gains. Careful design choices and evaluation protocols are therefore necessary to obtain robust, privacy-preserving, and task-appropriate compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: DE-RRD: A Knowledge Distillation Framework for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: Recent recommender systems have started to employ knowledge distillation, which is a model compression technique distilling knowledge from a cumbersome model (teacher) to a compact model (student), to reduce inference latency while maintaining performance. The state-of-the-art methods have only focused on making the student model accurately imitate the predictions of the teacher model. They have a limitation in that the prediction results incompletely reveal the teacher's knowledge. In this paper, we propose a novel knowledge distillation framework for recommender system, called DE-RRD, which enables the student model to learn from the latent knowledge encoded in the teacher model as well as from the teacher's predictions. Concretely, DE-RRD consists of two methods: 1) Distillation Experts (DE) that directly transfers the latent knowledge from the teacher model. DE exploits "experts" and a novel expert selection strategy for effectively distilling the vast teacher's knowledge to the student with limited capacity. 2) Relaxed Ranking Distillation (RRD) that transfers the knowledge revealed from the teacher's prediction with consideration of the relaxed ranking orders among items. Our extensive experiments show that DE-RRD outperforms the state-of-the-art competitors and achieves comparable or even better performance to that of the teacher model with faster inference time.

papers_seen.author: Archer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental training paradigm in which a large, well-trained teacher model transfers learned knowledge to a smaller, more efficient student model. This technique has emerged as essential for model compression, enabling the deployment of high-performing neural networks in resource-constrained environments without sacrificing accuracy. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and speech recognition, serving as a versatile solution for reducing computational costs and storage requirements while maintaining competitive performance levels.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) trains compact student models to mimic larger teacher models to reduce size, latency, and resource use while retaining much of the teacher's performance. KD encompasses several transfer mechanisms (soft-target/logit transfer, intermediate feature and layer matching, attention-based mapping, and data- or model-aware curricula) and extensions (ensemble distillation, data-free or privacy-preserving workflows, and adversarial sample selection). Applied widely in NLP (including compressing large pretrained transformers), computer vision, and multimodal systems, KD is most effective when combined with complementary techniques—task-aware layer alignment, careful teacher selection or ensembling, and data strategies—to meet deployment constraints. Remaining open problems include principled choices of transfer targets, robustness under domain and data heterogeneity, and automated, task-adaptive compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Freeman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Strategic Approach to Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lightweight student models while maintaining competitive performance across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and speech processing. By employing multiple mechanisms such as soft-label matching, intermediate representation transfer, and task-adaptive strategies, knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in model size, inference latency, and computational resource requirements while enabling practical deployment of state-of-the-art models.

papers_seen.author: Richards
papers_seen.title: TextKD-GAN: Text Generation using KnowledgeDistillation and Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Text generation is of particular interest in many NLP applications such as machine translation, language modeling, and text summarization. Generative adversarial networks (GANs) achieved a remarkable success in high quality image generation in computer vision,and recently, GANs have gained lots of interest from the NLP community as well. However, achieving similar success in NLP would be more challenging due to the discrete nature of text. In this work, we introduce a method using knowledge distillation to effectively exploit GAN setup for text generation. We demonstrate how autoencoders (AEs) can be used for providing a continuous representation of sentences, which is a smooth representation that assign non-zero probabilities to more than one word. We distill this representation to train the generator to synthesize similar smooth representations. We perform a number of experiments to validate our idea using different datasets and show that our proposed approach yields better performance in terms of the BLEU score and Jensen-Shannon distance (JSD) measure compared to traditional GAN-based text generation approaches without pre-training.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential, Practically Flexible Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical strategy for compressing large neural models into deployable students while preserving much of the teacher’s capabilities. KD techniques span matching teacher logits, aligning internal features, and using multi-teacher or teacher-free schedules; they enable large speedups and memory reductions, adapt to privacy- and data-limited settings, and have been successfully applied across retrieval, graph learning, generative models, and pretrained NLP transformers. The choice of what to transfer (outputs vs. intermediate representations), how to weight multiple sources, and whether to rely on original data fundamentally shapes outcomes. I argue that KD is indispensable for real-world deep learning deployment, but progress will require tighter practices for representation alignment, student-friendly teacher design, and handling heterogeneous or private data.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: BAM! Born-Again Multi-Task Networks for Natural Language Understanding
papers_seen.abstract: It can be challenging to train multi-task neural networks that outperform or even match their single-task counterparts. To help address this, we propose using knowledge distillation where single-task models teach a multi-task model. We enhance this training with teacher annealing, a novel method that gradually transitions the model from distillation to supervised learning, helping the multi-task model surpass its single-task teachers. We evaluate our approach by multi-task fine-tuning BERT on the GLUE benchmark. Our method consistently improves over standard single-task and multi-task training.

papers_seen.author: Rocha
papers_seen.title: Few Shot Network Compression via Cross Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Model compression has been widely adopted to obtain light-weighted deep neural networks. Most prevalent methods, however, require fine-tuning with sufficient training data to ensure accuracy, which could be challenged by privacy and security issues. As a compromise between privacy and performance, in this paper we investigate few shot network compression: given few samples per class, how can we effectively compress the network with negligible performance drop? The core challenge of few shot network compression lies in high estimation errors from the original network during inference, since the compressed network can easily over-fits on the few training instances. The estimation errors could propagate and accumulate layer-wisely and finally deteriorate the network output. To address the problem, we propose cross distillation, a novel layer-wise knowledge distillation approach. By interweaving hidden layers of teacher and student network, layer-wisely accumulated estimation errors can be effectively reduced.The proposed method offers a general framework compatible with prevalent network compression techniques such as pruning. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that cross distillation can significantly improve the student network's accuracy when only a few training instances are available.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Critical Technique for Deep Learning Model Compression and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large deep learning models while maintaining performance. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student models, enabling efficient deployment across diverse applications. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents an essential strategy for addressing the trade-off between model complexity and practical deployment requirements in both computer vision and natural language processing domains.

papers_seen.author: Kidd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential, Task-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, efficient students suitable for deployment in resource-constrained settings. When applied thoughtfully—selecting which teacher signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student representations, and adapting procedures to task and data constraints—KD can preserve most of a teacher's performance while dramatically reducing model size and inference cost. However, its effectiveness depends on design choices (targets, intermediate supervision, data selection) and on awareness of task-specific failure modes; KD is powerful but not universally automatic, and it should be integrated with complementary compression and adaptation techniques to achieve reliable, production-ready results.

papers_seen.author: Ware
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational Strategy for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential and practical technique for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, this approach achieves significant reductions in model size, computational cost, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation encompasses diverse methodologies beyond simple logit matching, including feature-level alignment, attention transfer, and data-free approaches, enabling flexible adaptation to various deployment scenarios and constraints in domains spanning natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Shaffer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful paradigm for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and natural language processing. This survey synthesizes current approaches to distillation, covering compression of diverse architectures including transformers, vision models, and generative models. Key developments include data-free distillation methods, multi-teacher frameworks, and task-aware approaches. Applications span NLP tasks, computer vision, and specialized domains such as medical imaging and fake media detection. The field demonstrates that compact student models can achieve performance comparable to or exceeding their non-compressed counterparts while significantly reducing computational and memory requirements.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation in Deep Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation deals with the problem of training a smaller model (Student) from a high capacity source model (Teacher) so as to retain most of its performance. Existing approaches use either the training data or meta-data extracted from it in order to train the Student. However, accessing the dataset on which the Teacher has been trained may not always be feasible if the dataset is very large or it poses privacy or safety concerns (e.g., bio-metric or medical data). Hence, in this paper, we propose a novel data-free method to train the Student from the Teacher. Without even using any meta-data, we synthesize the Data Impressions from the complex Teacher model and utilize these as surrogates for the original training data samples to transfer its learning to Student via knowledge distillation. We, therefore, dub our method "Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation" and demonstrate that our framework results in competitive generalization performance as achieved by distillation using the actual training data samples on multiple benchmark datasets.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and practical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and speech recognition. Through various mechanisms and strategic design choices, knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in balancing model capacity with computational efficiency without substantial accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Green
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Variants, and Practical Patterns
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD methods include matching teacher output distributions, imitating intermediate feature representations, and using task- or architecture-aware adaptations. Across vision, language, graph, and sequential tasks, distillation enables practical deployment on resource-constrained devices by reducing parameter count, inference latency, and memory while often preserving most of the teacher's performance. However, effectiveness depends on optimization, data choice, and the match between teacher signals and student capacity; addressing these factors has motivated many specialized distillation variants and combined compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Silva
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Strategy for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and broadly applicable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while preserving predictive performance. By transferring knowledge from large teacher models to compact student networks, knowledge distillation enables efficient deployment across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and recommendation systems. This approach addresses critical practical constraints of modern machine learning by reducing storage requirements, computational costs, and inference latency, making sophisticated deep learning systems accessible for resource-constrained environments and real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Task-Aware Approach to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a flexible framework to transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from large, costly models (teachers) to smaller, faster models (students). Across modalities and tasks, KD can both preserve or even improve accuracy while enabling deployment constraints such as lower latency, reduced memory, quantized arithmetic, and multi-task or privacy-aware settings. Realizing these benefits requires matching the distillation strategy to task structure and student capacity: approaches that exploit multi-teacher signals, task-aware layer alignment, teacher adaptation, or self-distillation consistently produce better compressed models. I argue that distillation is not a single recipe but a family of practical, complementary techniques that — when chosen and combined thoughtfully — make state-of-the-art models usable in resource-constrained and application-specific scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Robbins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques transfer information from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory, and latency while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. The toolkit includes soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate feature and layer mimicry, layer-wise or task-aware filtering, multi- and online-teacher schemes, data-free and synthetic-data approaches, and combinations with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Practical success depends on aligning what is distilled to student capacity and task needs, designing efficient training protocols, and mitigating limits such as teacher–student mismatch, optimization barriers, and degraded performance on low-frequency phenomena. This synthesis summarizes core mechanisms, empirical patterns, practical design choices, domain adaptations (including NLP and generative models), and open challenges for robust, deployment-ready compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Keith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a central technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while preserving much of the original performance. This approach transfers knowledge from teacher models to student models, enabling practical deployment on resource-constrained devices and reducing computational overhead. Knowledge distillation encompasses diverse methodologies including soft-target matching, feature-level mimicry, data-free approaches, and multi-teacher strategies, with wide application across natural language processing, computer vision, and other domains. The field continues to evolve with new insights into when and why distillation succeeds, addressing challenges such as data heterogeneity, privacy constraints, and low-frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression methods form a broad set of techniques for transferring information from larger models (or ensembles) to smaller, faster, or more deployable models. Approaches range from using teacher soft labels to transfer logits, to aligning intermediate representations, to teacher-free and online schemes, and to task- or domain-aware compression for pretrained language models. Applications span image and object recognition, speech and spoken-language tasks, machine translation, continual/federated settings, and specialized domains where latency, memory, or privacy constraints are critical. Empirical work shows that carefully designed distillation—sometimes combined with data augmentation, representation alignment, or multi-teacher selection—can produce compact models that retain a large fraction of teacher performance while improving generalization, calibration, and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from larger, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, efficient student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. The literature frames KD as a flexible toolbox rather than a single recipe: approaches include transferring output soft-labels, aligning intermediate representations or attention, using multi-teacher schedules, and combining distillation with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical work shows these choices — what to transfer, how to align student and teacher, and which data or augmentations to use — substantially affect whether a student approaches teacher performance. KD has been adapted across classification, sequence modeling, translation, retrieval, recommender systems, generative models, and many NLP tasks, with ongoing challenges around data-free distillation, representation alignment, and robustness in low-resource or privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression represent critical techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, these approaches enable significant reductions in model size and computational cost while maintaining competitive accuracy across diverse applications including computer vision, natural language processing, and machine translation. The field has evolved from basic teacher-student knowledge transfer to sophisticated multi-faceted approaches incorporating feature-level matching, data-free methods, sample selection strategies, and robustness-aware training protocols.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Bridging the Gap Between Performance and Efficiency in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful paradigm for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing, enabling the transfer of knowledge from larger, well-trained teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student networks. This technique addresses the critical challenge of deploying sophisticated neural networks on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive performance. Through various methodological innovations ranging from attention-based mechanisms to adversarial approaches, knowledge distillation has demonstrated its effectiveness across multiple domains including computer vision, machine translation, and NLP tasks. The field continues to evolve with advances in online distillation, multi-modal approaches, and task-aware compression strategies that optimize the knowledge transfer process.

papers_seen.author: Jacobs
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational Technique for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a central and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from teacher models through various mechanisms—including soft logits, intermediate representations, and synthesized data—knowledge distillation addresses critical deployment challenges across deep learning and natural language processing. This technique represents a pragmatic solution for resource-constrained environments, offering substantial reductions in model size and inference latency without significant accuracy loss. However, realizing its full potential requires careful attention to optimization challenges, teacher-student alignment, and task-specific design considerations.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Tool for Compression, Generalization, and Responsible NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is more than a single recipe for shrinking models: it is a flexible framework that enables model compression, preserves or transfers useful behaviors (including inductive biases), supports domain adaptation and privacy-preserving deployment, and can be adapted to mitigate undesirable behaviors. Drawing on empirical and methodological work across NLP and other domains, KD should be considered a central technique for building smaller, faster models that retain or even improve important aspects of teacher behavior while meeting practical constraints.

papers_seen.author: Rice
papers_seen.title: CoReD: Generalizing Fake Media Detection with Continual Representation using Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Over the last few decades, artificial intelligence research has made tremendous strides, but it still heavily relies on fixed datasets in stationary environments. Continual learning is a growing field of research that examines how AI systems can learn sequentially from a continuous stream of linked data in the same way that biological systems do. Simultaneously, fake media such as deepfakes and synthetic face images have emerged as significant to current multimedia technologies. Recently, numerous method has been proposed which can detect deepfakes with high accuracy. However, they suffer significantly due to their reliance on fixed datasets in limited evaluation settings. Therefore, in this work, we apply continuous learning to neural networks' learning dynamics, emphasizing its potential to increase data efficiency significantly. We propose Continual Representation using Distillation (CoReD) method that employs the concept of Continual Learning (CL), Representation Learning (RL), and Knowledge Distillation (KD). We design CoReD to perform sequential domain adaptation tasks on new deepfake and GAN-generated synthetic face datasets, while effectively minimizing the catastrophic forgetting in a teacher-student model setting. Our extensive experimental results demonstrate that our method is efficient at domain adaptation to detect low-quality deepfakes videos and GAN-generated images from several datasets, outperforming the-state-of-art baseline methods.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Findings, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal knowledge from teacher networks. Across computer vision, NLP, speech, and generative modeling, distillation methods have evolved from matching soft logits to aligning intermediate representations and adapting layer mappings for heterogeneous architectures. Practical results show large reductions in parameter counts and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance, but challenges remain in robustness, student-friendly teacher design, and reliably transferring rarer or structural knowledge.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Current Methods, Findings, and Challenges in Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques have become central to deploying high-performing deep models under resource constraints. Approaches range from transferring teacher soft targets to students, to mimicking intermediate representations, to automated architecture search for task-adaptive compact models. Distillation has been applied broadly across modalities and tasks (language understanding, question answering, ranking, multimodal models, and detection), and can improve efficiency while preserving accuracy or robustness. However, distillation can introduce artifacts (e.g., degraded handling of low-frequency phenomena), create dependence on teacher/data availability, and interact nontrivially with pretraining; recent work explores multi-teacher schemes, teacher-free variants, feature-level objectives, and task-specific compression to mitigate these limitations. Open directions include principled choices of student architectures, dealing with data-free or privacy-constrained scenarios, and understanding when distillation helps generalization versus when it transfers undesirable biases.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Approaches
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques provide practical paths to deploy large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Recent work spans strategies that (1) compress by transferring softened outputs or intermediate representations from large teachers to smaller students, (2) pre-train compact architectures instead of only compressing post-hoc, (3) adapt distillation to task specifics (e.g., detection, generation, ranking), (4) enable distillation without access to original training data, and (5) combine KD with quantization, pruning, and data augmentation to improve robustness and efficiency. Empirical evidence shows that carefully designed distillation losses, data strategies, and teacher-student curricula can preserve much of teacher performance while greatly reducing model size, latency, and memory footprint. Practical trade-offs include the need for task-specific treatment (feature imitation, permutation-invariant alignment), sensitivity to the teacher’s training regime, and opportunities where teacher-free or self-distillation variants can match or exceed classic teacher-student pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Transferring Knowledge for Efficient Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining performance. This approach transfers knowledge from a larger teacher model to a smaller student model, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices. Model compression through distillation has proven effective across diverse applications including natural language processing, computer vision, and multimodal learning. This paper surveys the principles, methods, and applications of knowledge distillation and related compression techniques in deep learning.

papers_seen.author: Walls
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and widely-adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while preserving much of the original performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, KD enables deployment on edge devices, addresses privacy and data-availability constraints, and facilitates knowledge transfer across architectures and modalities. This synthesis examines the core methods of knowledge distillation, key applications across domains, practical effectiveness, and important limitations and open challenges in the field.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. The approach spans matching softened logits, mimicking intermediate features, adversarial and generative teacher-student games, and data- or architecture-aware pipelines. Empirical work shows distillation preserves much teacher performance while reducing inference cost, but effectiveness depends on student capacity, data availability, and the design of transfer signals. Ongoing directions include theory for when distillation improves generalization, task- and modality-specific objectives (including generation and multimodal transfer), and practical strategies for data-free or privacy-preserving compression.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational, Multi-Strategy Approach for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most effective when treated not as a single algorithmic trick but as an engineering paradigm that integrates teacher design, student capacity, data strategy, representation objectives, and deployment constraints. When combined with complementary compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and deployment-aware practices (privacy, federated protocols, pre-training of small architectures), KD routinely enables compact models that meet latency, memory, and robustness requirements while preserving most of a teacher's performance. However, KD has limits: teacher–student mismatch, data heterogeneity in federated settings, and fairness or distribution-shift failures demand careful, task-aware design and evaluation. The practical position advocated here is that KD should be adopted as a core, configurable component of compression pipelines, with choice of techniques driven by operational constraints and empirical validation.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis from Provided Studies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) trains compact student models to capture the predictive behavior or internal representations of larger teacher networks, enabling deployment under latency, memory, and compute constraints. Across domains, KD strategies range from matching softened output distributions to transferring intermediate features or relational structure, and they are commonly combined with complementary compression techniques such as quantization or architecture search. Empirical evidence shows KD can substantially reduce model size and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance, but effectiveness depends on choices about distillation targets, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability, and task-aware training protocols. Practical pipelines emphasize careful design of objectives, selective use of training examples, and efficiency-aware engineering to make KD viable in production systems.

papers_seen.author: Murphy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: Powerful, Context-Dependent, and Best Deployed as an Integrated Strategy
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically essential approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD methods range from soft-target matching to representation alignment and staged or multi-teacher procedures. Their empirical success across vision and language tasks makes KD a central tool for production deployment on resource-constrained hardware, but its effectiveness depends on careful matching of objectives, data, and student capacity. I argue that KD should be treated as a toolkit to be combined with privacy, robustness, and fairness-aware practices rather than a one-size-fits-all solution.

papers_seen.author: Moreno
papers_seen.title: Learning Perception-Aware Agile Flight in Cluttered Environments
papers_seen.abstract: Recently, neural control policies have outperformed existing model-based planning-and-control methods for autonomously navigating quadrotors through cluttered environments in minimum time. However, they are not perception aware, a crucial requirement in vision-based navigation due to the camera's limited field of view and the underactuated nature of a quadrotor. We propose a learning-based system that achieves perception-aware, agile flight in cluttered environments. Our method combines imitation learning with reinforcement learning (RL) by leveraging a privileged learning-by-cheating framework. Using RL, we first train a perception-aware teacher policy with full-state information to fly in minimum time through cluttered environments. Then, we use imitation learning to distill its knowledge into a vision-based student policy that only perceives the environment via a camera. Our approach tightly couples perception and control, showing a significant advantage in computation speed (10 times faster) and success rate. We demonstrate the closed-loop control performance using hardware-in-the-loop simulation.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques have matured into a diverse set of theoretical and practical approaches for producing smaller, faster, or more specialized models from larger ones. Work in this area ranges from formal analyses of when and why distillation helps, to engineering advances that reduce runtime cost, enable training without original data, transfer across modalities, improve robustness and privacy, and tailor distilled models for downstream tasks or heterogeneous deployment environments. Practical methods include mimicking logits, matching intermediate representations or attention, progressively replacing modules, using student-focused filtering of teacher signals, and leveraging data augmentation or online collaboration between models. Emerging directions emphasize theoretical understanding, task-aware selection of distilled information, privacy-preserving or data-free pipelines, and retaining adversarial robustness while reducing model size.

papers_seen.author: Harvey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Targeted Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses larger teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. Across vision and NLP, KD supports latency- and memory-constrained deployment by combining soft-target matching, feature-level alignment, online and ensemble strategies, and data- or privacy-aware variants. Practical pipelines increasingly blend multiple techniques (representation distillation, architecture-aware mappings, data synthesis, and training-time teacher adaptation) to balance accuracy, efficiency, and deployment constraints. Open challenges remain in teacher–student mismatch, data unavailability, distribution shift, and fairness/privacy trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Ball
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical Framework for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, faster models suitable for resource-constrained deployment. By transferring knowledge from teacher models to student models, distillation enables practitioners to reduce inference latency and memory requirements while maintaining competitive performance. The approach spans diverse applications across computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and specialized domains, making it essential for practical deployment of state-of-the-art models.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Compressing Visual-linguistic Model via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite exciting progress in pre-training for visual-linguistic (VL) representations, very few aspire to a small VL model. In this paper, we study knowledge distillation (KD) to effectively compress a transformer-based large VL model into a small VL model. The major challenge arises from the inconsistent regional visual tokens extracted from different detectors of Teacher and Student, resulting in the misalignment of hidden representations and attention distributions. To address the problem, we retrain and adapt the Teacher by using the same region proposals from Student's detector while the features are from Teacher's own object detector. With aligned network inputs, the adapted Teacher is capable of transferring the knowledge through the intermediate representations. Specifically, we use the mean square error loss to mimic the attention distribution inside the transformer block and present a token-wise noise contrastive loss to align the hidden state by contrasting with negative representations stored in a sample queue. To this end, we show that our proposed distillation significantly improves the performance of small VL models on image captioning and visual question answering tasks. It reaches 120.8 in CIDEr score on COCO captioning, an improvement of 5.1 over its non-distilled counterpart; and an accuracy of 69.8 on VQA 2.0, a 0.8 gain from the baseline. Our extensive experiments and ablations confirm the effectiveness of VL distillation in both pre-training and fine-tuning stages.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Compression, Transfer, and Robustification in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile technique that not only enables compressing large models into efficient students but also serves as a mechanism for domain adaptation, multi-task transfer, self-supervised representation transfer, and improved generalization. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can reproduce state-of-the-art performance with far fewer resources in NLP and vision, but success depends on design choices such as which teacher signals to transfer (logits, intermediate representations, or adversarial/support samples), how to align teacher and student layers, whether to select or weight training samples, and how to handle heterogeneous data sources. KD can be extended via multi-teacher, teacher-free, black-box, and adversarial formulations, yet practical limits remain under data heterogeneity and some optimization/regulatization interactions. Thoughtful integration of KD with layer mapping, sample selection, data augmentation, and domain-aware trust metrics yields the greatest practical benefit.

papers_seen.author: Spears
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and essential technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher networks to students through various mechanisms, addressing critical deployment constraints including latency, memory, privacy, and computational efficiency. Knowledge distillation has become a foundational methodology across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, and multimodal learning, enabling practical deployment of state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices. While KD encompasses multiple complementary strategies and demonstrates consistent empirical effectiveness, realizing optimal gains requires careful attention to design choices, teacher quality, data availability, and task-specific adaptation.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Vital Technique for Practical Deep Learning and NLP Model Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach is particularly valuable for enabling deployment of state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments. This paper argues that knowledge distillation, whether applied to computer vision, reinforcement learning, or natural language processing tasks, represents an essential tool for bridging the gap between model performance and practical deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Dixon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for turning large, high-performing models into compact, deployable students. When combined with complementary strategies (data augmentation, task-aware pre-training, multi-teacher signals, architecture search, and divergence choices), KD enables substantial reductions in parameter count and inference latency while preserving much of teacher performance. Best practice is not a single recipe but an integrated, constraint-aware pipeline that selects distilled signals, data strategies, and student architectures to meet deployment objectives.

papers_seen.author: Reid
papers_seen.title: Moonshine: Distilling with Cheap Convolutions
papers_seen.abstract: Many engineers wish to deploy modern neural networks in memory-limited settings; but the development of flexible methods for reducing memory use is in its infancy, and there is little knowledge of the resulting cost-benefit. We propose structural model distillation for memory reduction using a strategy that produces a student architecture that is a simple transformation of the teacher architecture: no redesign is needed, and the same hyperparameters can be used. Using attention transfer, we provide Pareto curves/tables for distillation of residual networks with four benchmark datasets, indicating the memory versus accuracy payoff. We show that substantial memory savings are possible with very little loss of accuracy, and confirm that distillation provides student network performance that is better than training that student architecture directly on data.

papers_seen.author: Wheeler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Flexible Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a foundational technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while maintaining competitive performance. Rather than a single monolithic approach, KD functions best as a flexible, composable framework that can be adapted to specific task, data, and hardware constraints. When combined with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, and data-aware strategies, KD enables practical deployment of high-performing models on resource-constrained devices while addressing real-world challenges including privacy concerns, data unavailability, and computational limitations.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: DINE: Domain Adaptation from Single and Multiple Black-box Predictors
papers_seen.abstract: To ease the burden of labeling, unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) aims to transfer knowledge in previous and related labeled datasets (sources) to a new unlabeled dataset (target). Despite impressive progress, prior methods always need to access the raw source data and develop data-dependent alignment approaches to recognize the target samples in a transductive learning manner, which may raise privacy concerns from source individuals. Several recent studies resort to an alternative solution by exploiting the well-trained white-box model from the source domain, yet, it may still leak the raw data through generative adversarial learning. This paper studies a practical and interesting setting for UDA, where only black-box source models (i.e., only network predictions are available) are provided during adaptation in the target domain. To solve this problem, we propose a new two-step knowledge adaptation framework called DIstill and fine-tuNE (DINE). Taking into consideration the target data structure, DINE first distills the knowledge from the source predictor to a customized target model, then fine-tunes the distilled model to further fit the target domain. Besides, neural networks are not required to be identical across domains in DINE, even allowing effective adaptation on a low-resource device. Empirical results on three UDA scenarios (i.e., single-source, multi-source, and partial-set) confirm that DINE achieves highly competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art data-dependent approaches. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/tim-learn/DINE/}.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Linkless Link Prediction via Relational Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown exceptional performance in the task of link prediction. Despite their effectiveness, the high latency brought by non-trivial neighborhood data dependency limits GNNs in practical deployments. Conversely, the known efficient MLPs are much less effective than GNNs due to the lack of relational knowledge. In this work, to combine the advantages of GNNs and MLPs, we start with exploring direct knowledge distillation (KD) methods for link prediction, i.e., predicted logit-based matching and node representation-based matching. Upon observing direct KD analogs do not perform well for link prediction, we propose a relational KD framework, Linkless Link Prediction (LLP), to distill knowledge for link prediction with MLPs. Unlike simple KD methods that match independent link logits or node representations, LLP distills relational knowledge that is centered around each (anchor) node to the student MLP. Specifically, we propose rank-based matching and distribution-based matching strategies that complement each other. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LLP boosts the link prediction performance of MLPs with significant margins, and even outperforms the teacher GNNs on 7 out of 8 benchmarks. LLP also achieves a 70.68x speedup in link prediction inference compared to GNNs on the large-scale OGB dataset.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from well-trained teacher models to student networks, this approach enables practical deployment of sophisticated deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. The methodology encompasses diverse approaches ranging from soft target matching to intermediate representation alignment, and has demonstrated effectiveness across multiple domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and recommender systems. Recent advances have expanded knowledge distillation beyond simple output probability matching to include multi-teacher frameworks, task-aware layer-wise distillation, and integration with complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are fundamental techniques for enabling the deployment of large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, addressing the critical challenge of reducing model size while maintaining predictive performance. This review synthesizes recent advances in distillation techniques, compression methodologies, and their applications across various deep learning domains.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Model Compression with Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation for Web Question Answering System
papers_seen.abstract: Deep pre-training and fine-tuning models (such as BERT and OpenAI GPT) have demonstrated excellent results in question answering areas. However, due to the sheer amount of model parameters, the inference speed of these models is very slow. How to apply these complex models to real business scenarios becomes a challenging but practical problem. Previous model compression methods usually suffer from information loss during the model compression procedure, leading to inferior models compared with the original one. To tackle this challenge, we propose a Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (TMKD for short) method for web Question Answering system. We first develop a general Q\&A distillation task for student model pre-training, and further fine-tune this pre-trained student model with multi-teacher knowledge distillation on downstream tasks (like Web Q\&A task, MNLI, SNLI, RTE tasks from GLUE), which effectively reduces the overfitting bias in individual teacher models, and transfers more general knowledge to the student model. The experiment results show that our method can significantly outperform the baseline methods and even achieve comparable results with the original teacher models, along with substantial speedup of model inference.

papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Adaptation: Teaching to Adapt
papers_seen.abstract: Domain adaptation is crucial in many real-world applications where the distribution of the training data differs from the distribution of the test data. Previous Deep Learning-based approaches to domain adaptation need to be trained jointly on source and target domain data and are therefore unappealing in scenarios where models need to be adapted to a large number of domains or where a domain is evolving, e.g. spam detection where attackers continuously change their tactics.   To fill this gap, we propose Knowledge Adaptation, an extension of Knowledge Distillation (Bucilua et al., 2006; Hinton et al., 2015) to the domain adaptation scenario. We show how a student model achieves state-of-the-art results on unsupervised domain adaptation from multiple sources on a standard sentiment analysis benchmark by taking into account the domain-specific expertise of multiple teachers and the similarities between their domains.   When learning from a single teacher, using domain similarity to gauge trustworthiness is inadequate. To this end, we propose a simple metric that correlates well with the teacher's accuracy in the target domain. We demonstrate that incorporating high-confidence examples selected by this metric enables the student model to achieve state-of-the-art performance in the single-source scenario.

papers_seen.author: Allison
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large models into efficient students that retain much of the teacher’s performance. KD techniques—spanning logits-based soft-target transfer, intermediate feature alignment, and data-free synthesis—enable deployment of high-performing models on resource-constrained devices while also offering benefits in robustness and interpretability. When paired with task-aware design and careful teacher selection, distillation can produce compact models that meet real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints without large sacrifices in accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Blair
papers_seen.title: Distilling Policy Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The transfer of knowledge from one policy to another is an important tool in Deep Reinforcement Learning. This process, referred to as distillation, has been used to great success, for example, by enhancing the optimisation of agents, leading to stronger performance faster, on harder domains [26, 32, 5, 8]. Despite the widespread use and conceptual simplicity of distillation, many different formulations are used in practice, and the subtle variations between them can often drastically change the performance and the resulting objective that is being optimised. In this work, we rigorously explore the entire landscape of policy distillation, comparing the motivations and strengths of each variant through theoretical and empirical analysis. Our results point to three distillation techniques, that are preferred depending on specifics of the task. Specifically a newly proposed expected entropy regularised distillation allows for quicker learning in a wide range of situations, while still guaranteeing convergence.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: FedZKT: Zero-Shot Knowledge Transfer towards Resource-Constrained Federated Learning with Heterogeneous On-Device Models
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning enables multiple distributed devices to collaboratively learn a shared prediction model without centralizing their on-device data. Most of the current algorithms require comparable individual efforts for local training with the same structure and size of on-device models, which, however, impedes participation from resource-constrained devices. Given the widespread yet heterogeneous devices nowadays, in this paper, we propose an innovative federated learning framework with heterogeneous on-device models through Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer, named by FedZKT. Specifically, FedZKT allows devices to independently determine the on-device models upon their local resources. To achieve knowledge transfer across these heterogeneous on-device models, a zero-shot distillation approach is designed without any prerequisites for private on-device data, which is contrary to certain prior research based on a public dataset or a pre-trained data generator. Moreover, this compute-intensive distillation task is assigned to the server to allow the participation of resource-constrained devices, where a generator is adversarially learned with the ensemble of collected on-device models. The distilled central knowledge is then sent back in the form of the corresponding on-device model parameters, which can be easily absorbed on the device side. Extensive experimental studies demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of FedZKT towards on-device knowledge agnostic, on-device model heterogeneity, and other challenging federated learning scenarios, such as heterogeneous on-device data and straggler effects.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context-Dependent Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated framework for producing compact models that preserve much of the performance of larger teachers. KD spans a range of mechanisms—from softened-output matching to intermediate-feature and layer-wise alignment—and can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. While KD often enables deployable students that approach teacher performance, success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to handle data availability or privacy constraints, and how to pair distillation with complementary compression techniques.
