papers_seen.author: West
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining or even improving predictive performance. This approach enables the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP models on resource-constrained devices by transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student models. The method addresses critical challenges in practical machine learning deployment, including reducing computational costs, memory requirements, inference latency, and addressing privacy concerns. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and specialized tasks, demonstrating its versatility and importance for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Chambers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a versatile and practical family of techniques for compressing large deep neural models into smaller, deployable ones without substantial loss of performance. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks, addressing critical deployment constraints including computational cost, memory requirements, inference latency, and privacy concerns. KD has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and specialized applications, with continuous methodological innovations expanding its scope and effectiveness.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical, Multi-Domain Imperative
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and widely applicable strategy for compressing deep models and enabling their deployment in resource-constrained settings. By transferring predictive and representational knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller students, KD reduces inference costs while often preserving — and sometimes improving — accuracy and robustness. Across computer vision, speech, NLP, and large-scale distributed training, KD enables designers to balance performance and efficiency, but realizing its full potential requires careful choices about what is distilled (logits, features, relations), which data or surrogates are used, and how multi-teacher or online protocols are organized.

papers_seen.author: Pope
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a compact, flexible, and empirically effective route to compress large neural models into deployable students. When treated as a design-first tool rather than a single loss term, KD can be combined with pre-training of compact architectures, representation-level objectives, data-efficient and data-free techniques, and architecture- or task-aware adjustments to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Adopting KD as the default strategy requires engineering practices that explicitly address teacher–student alignment, domain shift, rare-token behavior, and evaluation protocols, but doing so yields a practical, composable pipeline for converting research-scale models into production-ready systems.

papers_seen.author: Cortez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central, flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, speech, and natural language tasks. Over the past decade KD evolved from matching soft logits into a broad set of techniques—feature-level and attention alignment, multi-teacher and online schemes, data- and privacy-aware variants, curriculum and architecture-aware strategies—that collectively enable substantial reductions in model size and latency while preserving much of teacher performance. Practical success depends on matching distillation objectives, data regimes, and student architectures to deployment constraints; open issues include teacher–student mismatch, robustness and fairness transfer, and distillation under limited or private data.

papers_seen.author: Rhodes
papers_seen.title: Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: It is challenging to perform lifelong language learning (LLL) on a stream of different tasks without any performance degradation comparing to the multi-task counterparts. To address this issue, we present Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation (L2KD), a simple but efficient method that can be easily applied to existing LLL architectures in order to mitigate the degradation. Specifically, when the LLL model is trained on a new task, we assign a teacher model to first learn the new task, and pass the knowledge to the LLL model via knowledge distillation. Therefore, the LLL model can better adapt to the new task while keeping the previously learned knowledge. Experiments show that the proposed L2KD consistently improves previous state-of-the-art models, and the degradation comparing to multi-task models in LLL tasks is well mitigated for both sequence generation and text classification tasks.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-used technique for compressing neural networks and transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models. This approach has been successfully applied across multiple domains including neural machine translation, language models, graph neural networks, and speech processing. The technique enables deployment of high-performing models on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive accuracy through various knowledge transfer mechanisms and distillation strategies.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: Powerful, Practical, but Context-Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, empirically effective route to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students in deep learning and NLP. KD encompasses a range of techniques (soft-label matching, representation mimicry, intermediate-layer alignment, multi-teacher/ensemble strategies, and data-free or online variants). While KD often yields substantial gains in model size, latency, and memory with modest performance loss, its success depends on data characteristics, teacher–student capacity relationships, and deployment constraints. Best practice treats KD as a toolkit to be combined with targeted data strategies, representation-level objectives, and teacher selection or synthesis, rather than a single off-the-shelf solution.

papers_seen.author: Heath
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Essential Strategy for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Systems
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and practical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from large teacher models to compact student models, knowledge distillation enables deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP systems on resource-constrained devices without significant accuracy loss. The approach addresses critical challenges in balancing model capacity with computational efficiency across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Overview
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while transferring valuable knowledge from teacher models. This approach enables the practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and speech recognition. By leveraging various distillation methodologies and combining them with complementary compression techniques, practitioners can achieve substantial reductions in model size and latency while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation has become an essential toolkit for building efficient, deployable neural networks that meet real-world computational constraints without sacrificing accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Patterson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher networks into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD enables deployment of high-performing models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints across domains such as natural language processing, computer vision, generative modeling, and federated settings. Practical success depends on what is distilled (logits, features, or relational signals), how teacher and student are coupled, access to data, and task-specific adaptations. While KD frequently yields strong efficiency-accuracy tradeoffs, remaining challenges include teacher–student mismatch, data scarcity, robustness, and principled guidelines for transformer-based architectures and specialized models like GANs.

papers_seen.author: Walter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation from A Stronger Teacher
papers_seen.abstract: Unlike existing knowledge distillation methods focus on the baseline settings, where the teacher models and training strategies are not that strong and competing as state-of-the-art approaches, this paper presents a method dubbed DIST to distill better from a stronger teacher. We empirically find that the discrepancy of predictions between the student and a stronger teacher may tend to be fairly severer. As a result, the exact match of predictions in KL divergence would disturb the training and make existing methods perform poorly. In this paper, we show that simply preserving the relations between the predictions of teacher and student would suffice, and propose a correlation-based loss to capture the intrinsic inter-class relations from the teacher explicitly. Besides, considering that different instances have different semantic similarities to each class, we also extend this relational match to the intra-class level. Our method is simple yet practical, and extensive experiments demonstrate that it adapts well to various architectures, model sizes and training strategies, and can achieve state-of-the-art performance consistently on image classification, object detection, and semantic segmentation tasks. Code is available at: https://github.com/hunto/DIST_KD .

papers_seen.author: Blair
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful, flexible approach for turning large models into compact, deployable students. KD techniques range from simple soft-label matching to sophisticated intermediate-representation alignment, meta-learned teachers, and self-supervised or adversarially aware objectives. These methods have been shown to preserve much of teacher performance across vision and language tasks while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. At the same time, practical success depends on choices about what information to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to handle limited or private data—areas where principled guidelines and automated strategies remain active opportunities for research and engineering.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from teacher models. Across vision, language, graph, and generative settings, distillation methods range from matching softened logits to aligning intermediate features, using data-centric strategies (e.g., synthetic data or teacher-generated targets), selective sample weighting, and meta-learning of teacher behaviors. Distillation functions both as a compression tool and as a mechanism for regularization, domain adaptation, and privacy-aware transfer; however, practical success depends on teacher quality, data availability and complexity, optimization dynamics, and careful choice of distillation targets and sample selection. Domain-specific adaptations (e.g., for non-autoregressive translation, machine reading comprehension, and graph neural networks) show significant gains but highlight open problems in reliably preserving rare/low-frequency phenomena and in formalizing when distillation is most effective.

papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster models by transferring behavior or representations from a teacher to a student. It is widely used to enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints across modalities (vision, language, speech, multimodal) and tasks (classification, retrieval, generation, segmentation). Effective distillation combines multiple signals (soft targets, intermediate-feature matching, layer-wise supervision, adversarial training, and ensemble guidance) and is commonly paired with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Practical pipelines must balance teacher selection, data regimes, and student capacity to approach teacher performance while meeting resource constraints.

papers_seen.author: Carr
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Composable, Practical Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models by transferring useful behavior from teacher models to students. Across vision, speech, and NLP, KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while often preserving much of the teacher's performance. The technique encompasses multiple operational modalities — logits matching, feature mimicking, multi-teacher fusion, data-free synthesis, and distributed/federated protocols — and is best applied as an adaptable toolkit whose components are selected to match data availability, privacy constraints, robustness needs, and target hardware.

papers_seen.author: Byrd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical Tool for Model Compression: Strengths, Mechanisms, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. KD methods—ranging from soft-target matching to representation-level imitation, self-distillation, and adversarial teacher–student games—enable substantial efficiency gains while often improving generalization. However, distillation's benefits depend on careful design choices (what signals to transfer, how to align layers, and how to handle data or privacy constraints) and it is not a universal panacea: issues such as teacher–student mismatch, scarce or unavailable data, and task-specific optimization barriers require specialized strategies and evaluation. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a flexible, composable framework that is essential for practical compression but must be applied with task-aware techniques and awareness of its limitations.

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: Practical Strengths and Limits of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible framework for compressing large models into efficient students suitable for deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. When combined with complementary techniques—data augmentation, representation-level matching, online or collaborative training, and data-free strategies—KD yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance across vision and language tasks. However, achieving reliable gains requires task-aware choices about teacher signals, student capacity, and data availability; mismatches in inputs or internal structure and concerns about robustness and privacy remain important practical limitations.

papers_seen.author: Mcmillan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression transfer predictive behavior or internal structure from large teacher models to smaller student models so that compact models can run under latency, memory, and privacy constraints while retaining much of the original performance. A spectrum of techniques—matching teacher output distributions, aligning intermediate representations, attention- or correlation-based feature imitation, task-adaptive architecture search, and data-side methods such as augmentation or synthetic example generation—have been developed and combined in practice. Success depends on choices about what signal to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to prepare or augment the data used for distillation; open problems include robust transfer under distribution shift, privacy-preserving and data-free distillation, and principled teacher design for specific student architectures and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Parsons
papers_seen.title: Curriculum Learning for Dense Retrieval Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent work has shown that more effective dense retrieval models can be obtained by distilling ranking knowledge from an existing base re-ranking model. In this paper, we propose a generic curriculum learning based optimization framework called CL-DRD that controls the difficulty level of training data produced by the re-ranking (teacher) model. CL-DRD iteratively optimizes the dense retrieval (student) model by increasing the difficulty of the knowledge distillation data made available to it. In more detail, we initially provide the student model coarse-grained preference pairs between documents in the teacher's ranking and progressively move towards finer-grained pairwise document ordering requirements. In our experiments, we apply a simple implementation of the CL-DRD framework to enhance two state-of-the-art dense retrieval models. Experiments on three public passage retrieval datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed framework.

papers_seen.author: Davidson
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large models into smaller, faster models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from a teacher to a student. Across vision, language, graph, generative, and neural-architecture-search settings, methods vary from matching soft labels to aligning intermediate features, using attention-based layer projection, contrastive alignment, and optimization-aware divergences. Practical adaptations address data availability, privacy, and efficiency constraints, while empirical and theoretical analyses reveal optimization limits, dataset and heterogeneity sensitivities, and opportunities from meta-learning teachers and task-specific design. Despite broad success, key open problems remain in reliably preserving teacher knowledge, designing data- and privacy-aware protocols, and tailoring distillation to domain-specific structures.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Improved Accuracy in Spoken Question Answering
papers_seen.abstract: Spoken question answering (SQA) is a challenging task that requires the machine to fully understand the complex spoken documents. Automatic speech recognition (ASR) plays a significant role in the development of QA systems. However, the recent work shows that ASR systems generate highly noisy transcripts, which critically limit the capability of machine comprehension on the SQA task. To address the issue, we present a novel distillation framework. Specifically, we devise a training strategy to perform knowledge distillation (KD) from spoken documents and written counterparts. Our work makes a step towards distilling knowledge from the language model as a supervision signal to lead to better student accuracy by reducing the misalignment between automatic and manual transcriptions. Experiments demonstrate that our approach outperforms several state-of-the-art language models on the Spoken-SQuAD dataset.

papers_seen.author: Farrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for compressing large, complex neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from teacher to student models, this approach enables the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices and accelerates inference across diverse domains. Recent advances have expanded knowledge distillation beyond simple output matching to include intermediate representation alignment, data-free approaches, and integration with complementary compression methods, making it an essential methodology for practical machine learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Le
papers_seen.title: VPN++: Rethinking Video-Pose embeddings for understanding Activities of Daily Living
papers_seen.abstract: Many attempts have been made towards combining RGB and 3D poses for the recognition of Activities of Daily Living (ADL). ADL may look very similar and often necessitate to model fine-grained details to distinguish them. Because the recent 3D ConvNets are too rigid to capture the subtle visual patterns across an action, this research direction is dominated by methods combining RGB and 3D Poses. But the cost of computing 3D poses from RGB stream is high in the absence of appropriate sensors. This limits the usage of aforementioned approaches in real-world applications requiring low latency. Then, how to best take advantage of 3D Poses for recognizing ADL? To this end, we propose an extension of a pose driven attention mechanism: Video-Pose Network (VPN), exploring two distinct directions. One is to transfer the Pose knowledge into RGB through a feature-level distillation and the other towards mimicking pose driven attention through an attention-level distillation. Finally, these two approaches are integrated into a single model, we call VPN++. We show that VPN++ is not only effective but also provides a high speed up and high resilience to noisy Poses. VPN++, with or without 3D Poses, outperforms the representative baselines on 4 public datasets. Code is available at https://github.com/srijandas07/vpnplusplus.

papers_seen.author: Santana
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from large teacher models to compact student models, addressing the critical challenge of deploying state-of-the-art deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices. The technique encompasses diverse methodologies spanning logits-based distillation, feature and intermediate-layer matching, data-free approaches, multi-teacher strategies, and task-aware compression methods. Knowledge distillation has proven effective across multiple domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and specialized applications, making it an essential methodology for practical deep learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Powerful, Practical — but Not a Panacea
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. KD is broadly effective across domains and scales — enabling efficient inference, reducing memory and latency, and supporting applications from pre-trained language models to distributed training — but its success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data and robustness concerns. I argue that KD is an essential, versatile tool for real-world deployment, while also identifying key limitations and concrete practices that improve reliability and performance.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical and Versatile Framework for Efficient Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a practical and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while preserving competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks, knowledge distillation enables the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. The technique encompasses multiple methodologies—including soft-target matching, feature mimicking, layer-wise alignment, and data-free synthesis—and has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and reinforcement learning. Recent research demonstrates that knowledge distillation is not merely a compression heuristic but a flexible toolkit that, when carefully designed and integrated with complementary techniques, can achieve student models that approach teacher performance while meeting practical deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: BERT Learns to Teach: Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We present Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning (MetaDistil), a simple yet effective alternative to traditional knowledge distillation (KD) methods where the teacher model is fixed during training. We show the teacher network can learn to better transfer knowledge to the student network (i.e., learning to teach) with the feedback from the performance of the distilled student network in a meta learning framework. Moreover, we introduce a pilot update mechanism to improve the alignment between the inner-learner and meta-learner in meta learning algorithms that focus on an improved inner-learner. Experiments on various benchmarks show that MetaDistil can yield significant improvements compared with traditional KD algorithms and is less sensitive to the choice of different student capacity and hyperparameters, facilitating the use of KD on different tasks and models.

papers_seen.author: Freeman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Strategic Approach to Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lightweight student models while maintaining competitive performance across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and speech processing. By employing multiple mechanisms such as soft-label matching, intermediate representation transfer, and task-adaptive strategies, knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in model size, inference latency, and computational resource requirements while enabling practical deployment of state-of-the-art models.

papers_seen.author: Tran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Theory, and Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for compressing large neural networks into smaller models that preserve predictive performance and desirable properties of the teacher. KD encompasses soft-label supervision, intermediate-feature matching, layer-wise alignment, multi-teacher fusion, online co-training, and teacher-free/self-distillation, and it is applied across modalities (vision, language, generation, recommendation) to meet deployment constraints such as latency, memory, low-precision arithmetic, privacy, and domain shift. Successful distillation requires task-aware choices of what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, how to generate or select data for transfer, and how to combine objectives to trade off fidelity and generalization. Remaining challenges include principled selection of distilled signals, data-free and privacy-preserving workflows, robustness under domain shift, and automated, task-adaptive compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Framework for Efficient Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, knowledge distillation enables deployment in resource-constrained environments without significant accuracy loss. The approach has proven effective across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and multimodal learning, offering substantial performance improvements and computational efficiency gains. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should be considered a core and indispensable strategy for practical model compression, particularly when combined with complementary techniques and carefully tailored to specific task requirements and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Enhancing Student Model Performance Through Teacher-Guided Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining or even improving performance. This approach transfers knowledge from a well-trained teacher model to a lightweight student model through various mechanisms including soft target matching, intermediate layer alignment, and task-aware filtering. Applications span across natural language processing, computer vision, and domain-specific tasks, addressing critical deployment challenges related to latency, computational resources, and model size constraints in real-world production environments.

papers_seen.author: Mcclain
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: Powerful, Practical, but Not a Panacea
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a core technique for compressing large models, transferring knowledge across architectures, enabling private or federated workflows, and improving efficiency for deployment in resource-constrained settings. While KD often yields substantial practical gains—reducing model size and inference cost with limited loss in performance—it has important theoretical and empirical limitations related to optimization, data dependence, model and domain heterogeneity, and teacher–student mismatch. A pragmatic stance recognizes KD as a versatile toolset whose effectiveness depends on how it is applied: the choice of distilled targets (logits, features, or relations), the availability or synthesis of data, the use of multiple teachers or staged procedures, and awareness of when distillation can harm or help generalization. This paper argues that KD should be used as part of a broader compression and adaptation strategy guided by empirical diagnostics and appropriate extensions (multi-teacher, zero-shot/data-free, federated/distilled protocols, or self-supervised distillation) rather than as an off-the-shelf cure-all.

papers_seen.author: Davenport
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Paradigm for Model Compression and Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to smaller student models, knowledge distillation addresses the critical challenge of deploying state-of-the-art deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains. This approach extends beyond basic model compression to enable practical deployment scenarios, privacy-preserving learning, and knowledge transfer across heterogeneous architectures. The technique has proven effective across natural language processing, computer vision, graph neural networks, and multimodal learning, establishing it as an indispensable tool for modern deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods and Practice in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across deep learning and NLP, KD techniques range from matching teacher logits to aligning intermediate representations and relational structures, and they are routinely combined with complementary compression strategies (pruning, quantization, architecture search, etc.) to meet practical constraints. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while enabling large reductions in model size and inference cost, but success depends on choices about teacher design, student capacity, the distillation objective, and data availability. Extensions such as federated and data-free distillation broaden applicability to privacy-sensitive and low-data settings; task-aware and layer-wise adaptations help align what is transferred to student capacity and task needs. Remaining challenges include representation alignment, optimization gaps between teachers and students, and principled guarantees for fairness and generalization, pointing toward composable, task-adaptive KD systems for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Schultz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Methods, Applications, and Practical Constraints
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger teacher models into smaller student models to reduce model size, latency, and resource use while preserving task performance. Distillation mechanisms include transferring softened output distributions, matching intermediate representations, ensembling or online teacher strategies, and data- or task-aware adaptations. KD has been applied across domains — from recommendation and ranking to object detection, non-autoregressive machine translation, and federated settings — and is often combined with complementary compression methods. Its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, the choice of distilled targets, student capacity, and the match between training data and deployment conditions; these dependencies motivate pragmatic design choices and ongoing research into robust, data-efficient, and privacy-aware distillation pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and widely-adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, enabling practical deployment while maintaining competitive performance across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and machine translation. While knowledge distillation offers substantial practical benefits in reducing model size, computational cost, and inference latency, recent research reveals important limitations and nuances in how knowledge transfer occurs, and highlights the importance of careful design choices and methodical application rather than treating distillation as a universal solution.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical and Essential Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from well-trained teacher models to compact student networks, distillation enables significant reductions in computational requirements, memory footprint, and inference latency while maintaining competitive predictive performance. This approach has demonstrated broad applicability across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and specialized applications, making it an indispensable method for modern machine learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Aguirre
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster students by transferring information beyond hard labels. Across modalities and tasks, distillation reduces memory and compute requirements while often preserving most of the teacher’s performance. Techniques vary from matching output distributions to aligning intermediate representations, and are combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, low-precision numerics, architecture search) to meet deployment constraints. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, which data or augmentations to use, how to select or adapt teachers, and how to align teacher-student capacities. This synthesis summarizes common mechanisms, practical methods, domain-specific adaptations (including privacy- or data-limited scenarios), and recurring challenges for applying distillation in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Carr
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Composable, Practical Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models by transferring useful behavior from teacher models to students. Across vision, speech, and NLP, KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while often preserving much of the teacher's performance. The technique encompasses multiple operational modalities — logits matching, feature mimicking, multi-teacher fusion, data-free synthesis, and distributed/federated protocols — and is best applied as an adaptable toolkit whose components are selected to match data availability, privacy constraints, robustness needs, and target hardware.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression represent critical techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, these approaches enable significant reductions in model size and computational cost while maintaining competitive accuracy across diverse applications including computer vision, natural language processing, and machine translation. The field has evolved from basic teacher-student knowledge transfer to sophisticated multi-faceted approaches incorporating feature-level matching, data-free methods, sample selection strategies, and robustness-aware training protocols.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Understanding Knowledge Distillation in Non-autoregressive Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Non-autoregressive machine translation (NAT) systems predict a sequence of output tokens in parallel, achieving substantial improvements in generation speed compared to autoregressive models. Existing NAT models usually rely on the technique of knowledge distillation, which creates the training data from a pretrained autoregressive model for better performance. Knowledge distillation is empirically useful, leading to large gains in accuracy for NAT models, but the reason for this success has, as of yet, been unclear. In this paper, we first design systematic experiments to investigate why knowledge distillation is crucial to NAT training. We find that knowledge distillation can reduce the complexity of data sets and help NAT to model the variations in the output data. Furthermore, a strong correlation is observed between the capacity of an NAT model and the optimal complexity of the distilled data for the best translation quality. Based on these findings, we further propose several approaches that can alter the complexity of data sets to improve the performance of NAT models. We achieve the state-of-the-art performance for the NAT-based models, and close the gap with the autoregressive baseline on WMT14 En-De benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Daniels
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a single compression trick into a broad, practical toolkit that enables deployment of high-performing models under real-world constraints. KD techniques transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller students, and they can be adapted to address deployment constraints such as device heterogeneity, privacy, domain shift, fairness, and limited or missing training data. When combined with task-aware design choices and complementary compression methods, KD routinely produces compact models suitable for latency-, memory-, and privacy-constrained applications across vision, speech, and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Decker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Practical Effectiveness, Theoretical Trade-offs, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and flexible approach to compressing large neural networks while retaining much of their predictive power. Across modalities and tasks—NLP, vision, recommendation, graph learning, and generative modeling—KD-based methods enable faster inference and lower resource use with modest accuracy loss. However, realizing these gains requires attention to teacher quality, the form of supervisory signal (soft vs. hard labels), data augmentation and curriculum, and task-adaptive design. KD can be combined with other compression techniques (pruning, architecture search) and adapted for privacy-preserving or distributed settings. This paper argues that KD is a broadly applicable core strategy for model compression, outlines the mechanisms that make it effective, and provides practical recommendations grounded in empirical and theoretical findings.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Extract the Knowledge of Graph Neural Networks and Go Beyond it: An Effective Knowledge Distillation Framework
papers_seen.abstract: Semi-supervised learning on graphs is an important problem in the machine learning area. In recent years, state-of-the-art classification methods based on graph neural networks (GNNs) have shown their superiority over traditional ones such as label propagation. However, the sophisticated architectures of these neural models will lead to a complex prediction mechanism, which could not make full use of valuable prior knowledge lying in the data, e.g., structurally correlated nodes tend to have the same class. In this paper, we propose a framework based on knowledge distillation to address the above issues. Our framework extracts the knowledge of an arbitrary learned GNN model (teacher model), and injects it into a well-designed student model. The student model is built with two simple prediction mechanisms, i.e., label propagation and feature transformation, which naturally preserves structure-based and feature-based prior knowledge, respectively. In specific, we design the student model as a trainable combination of parameterized label propagation and feature transformation modules. As a result, the learned student can benefit from both prior knowledge and the knowledge in GNN teachers for more effective predictions. Moreover, the learned student model has a more interpretable prediction process than GNNs. We conduct experiments on five public benchmark datasets and employ seven GNN models including GCN, GAT, APPNP, SAGE, SGC, GCNII and GLP as the teacher models. Experimental results show that the learned student model can consistently outperform its corresponding teacher model by 1.4% - 4.7% on average. Code and data are available at https://github.com/BUPT-GAMMA/CPF

papers_seen.author: Suarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Evidence, and Open Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses and adapts large teacher models into smaller, more deployable students by transferring predictive distributions, intermediate representations, or structural behavior. Across vision, language, speech, and graph domains, distillation variants enable latency- and memory-constrained deployment, improve transfer and robustness, and can be combined with architecture search or progressive module replacement to balance fidelity and efficiency. Practical success depends on choices about distillation targets, data availability (including data-free approaches), teacher–student capacity alignment, and task-aware training; these considerations frame ongoing research toward automated, privacy-aware, and domain-adaptive compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Effective yet Context-Dependent Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and widely-adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while preserving performance. By enabling knowledge transfer through soft targets and intermediate representations, distillation addresses the critical challenge of deploying sophisticated deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices. However, distillation is not universally applicable and requires careful design choices regarding teacher-student alignment, data availability, and task-specific constraints to realize optimal compression benefits.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational, Multi-Strategy Approach for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most effective when treated not as a single algorithmic trick but as an engineering paradigm that integrates teacher design, student capacity, data strategy, representation objectives, and deployment constraints. When combined with complementary compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and deployment-aware practices (privacy, federated protocols, pre-training of small architectures), KD routinely enables compact models that meet latency, memory, and robustness requirements while preserving most of a teacher's performance. However, KD has limits: teacher–student mismatch, data heterogeneity in federated settings, and fairness or distribution-shift failures demand careful, task-aware design and evaluation. The practical position advocated here is that KD should be adopted as a core, configurable component of compression pipelines, with choice of techniques driven by operational constraints and empirical validation.

papers_seen.author: Russell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Composable Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a foundational, composable technique for compressing deep and NLP models: it reliably transfers predictive behavior and representations from high-capacity teachers into smaller students, and when combined with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search, data synthesis or adversarial training) it enables practical deployment on resource-constrained hardware. Realizing KD's benefits requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to handle data and teacher quality, and how to integrate KD into an end-to-end compression pipeline; when used with these considerations it yields compact, robust models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, size, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: The Case for Responsible, Task-Adaptive Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an indispensable tool for compressing large neural models into compact, deployable students. When combined with representation transfer, architecture search, and data-aware synthesis, KD enables substantial reductions in latency and memory while retaining much of the teacher's performance. However, distillation must be applied carefully: mismatches between teacher and student internals, scarce or private training data, and distributional or low-frequency phenomena can limit gains or introduce undesirable artifacts. I argue that KD should be treated as a system-level design choice that pairs multi-objective distillation objectives with task-adaptive student architectures and privacy- or robustness-aware synthesis methods to realize reliable, production-ready compression.

papers_seen.author: Pena
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practical family of methods for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information from a high-capacity teacher to a compact student using a range of signals (soft logits, intermediate representations, layer-wise supervision, or synthesized data). Across vision and language tasks, KD enables substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance, and it composes effectively with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical success requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to handle limited or private data, and how to evaluate robustness and rare-case behavior.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge distillation from multi-modal to mono-modal segmentation networks
papers_seen.abstract: The joint use of multiple imaging modalities for medical image segmentation has been widely studied in recent years. The fusion of information from different modalities has demonstrated to improve the segmentation accuracy, with respect to mono-modal segmentations, in several applications. However, acquiring multiple modalities is usually not possible in a clinical setting due to a limited number of physicians and scanners, and to limit costs and scan time. Most of the time, only one modality is acquired. In this paper, we propose KD-Net, a framework to transfer knowledge from a trained multi-modal network (teacher) to a mono-modal one (student). The proposed method is an adaptation of the generalized distillation framework where the student network is trained on a subset (1 modality) of the teacher's inputs (n modalities). We illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in brain tumor segmentation with the BraTS 2018 dataset. Using different architectures, we show that the student network effectively learns from the teacher and always outperforms the baseline mono-modal network in terms of segmentation accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Graph-less Neural Networks: Teaching Old MLPs New Tricks via Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are popular for graph machine learning and have shown great results on wide node classification tasks. Yet, they are less popular for practical deployments in the industry owing to their scalability challenges incurred by data dependency. Namely, GNN inference depends on neighbor nodes multiple hops away from the target, and fetching them burdens latency-constrained applications. Existing inference acceleration methods like pruning and quantization can speed up GNNs by reducing Multiplication-and-ACcumulation (MAC) operations, but the improvements are limited given the data dependency is not resolved. Conversely, multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) have no graph dependency and infer much faster than GNNs, even though they are less accurate than GNNs for node classification in general. Motivated by these complementary strengths and weaknesses, we bring GNNs and MLPs together via knowledge distillation (KD). Our work shows that the performance of MLPs can be improved by large margins with GNN KD. We call the distilled MLPs Graph-less Neural Networks (GLNNs) as they have no inference graph dependency. We show that GLNNs with competitive accuracy infer faster than GNNs by 146X-273X and faster than other acceleration methods by 14X-27X. Under a production setting involving both transductive and inductive predictions across 7 datasets, GLNN accuracies improve over stand-alone MLPs by 12.36% on average and match GNNs on 6/7 datasets. Comprehensive analysis shows when and why GLNNs can achieve competitive accuracies to GNNs and suggests GLNN as a handy choice for latency-constrained applications.

papers_seen.author: Bush
papers_seen.title: Multi-Label Image Classification via Knowledge Distillation from Weakly-Supervised Detection
papers_seen.abstract: Multi-label image classification is a fundamental but challenging task towards general visual understanding. Existing methods found the region-level cues (e.g., features from RoIs) can facilitate multi-label classification. Nevertheless, such methods usually require laborious object-level annotations (i.e., object labels and bounding boxes) for effective learning of the object-level visual features. In this paper, we propose a novel and efficient deep framework to boost multi-label classification by distilling knowledge from weakly-supervised detection task without bounding box annotations. Specifically, given the image-level annotations, (1) we first develop a weakly-supervised detection (WSD) model, and then (2) construct an end-to-end multi-label image classification framework augmented by a knowledge distillation module that guides the classification model by the WSD model according to the class-level predictions for the whole image and the object-level visual features for object RoIs. The WSD model is the teacher model and the classification model is the student model. After this cross-task knowledge distillation, the performance of the classification model is significantly improved and the efficiency is maintained since the WSD model can be safely discarded in the test phase. Extensive experiments on two large-scale datasets (MS-COCO and NUS-WIDE) show that our framework achieves superior performances over the state-of-the-art methods on both performance and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while preserving predictive performance. This approach enables the deployment of deep learning and NLP models on resource-constrained devices by transferring knowledge from large teacher models to compact student models. The method has been successfully applied across various domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized tasks like object detection and speech recognition, demonstrating consistent improvements in model efficiency without substantial accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Chandler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Multifaceted Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, adaptable approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while often preserving or even improving generalization. KD operates at multiple levels—soft logits, intermediate representations, relational signals, and architectural guidance—and can be combined with data, augmentation, and architecture-design techniques to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. While KD delivers strong empirical gains across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks, its success depends on careful matching of teacher signals, student capacity, data strategies, and task-specific objectives; outstanding problems include robustness transfer, teacher imperfections, heterogeneous architecture alignment, and data-free distillation strategies.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: PKD: General Distillation Framework for Object Detectors via Pearson Correlation Coefficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation(KD) is a widely-used technique to train compact models in object detection. However, there is still a lack of study on how to distill between heterogeneous detectors. In this paper, we empirically find that better FPN features from a heterogeneous teacher detector can help the student although their detection heads and label assignments are different. However, directly aligning the feature maps to distill detectors suffers from two problems. First, the difference in feature magnitude between the teacher and the student could enforce overly strict constraints on the student. Second, the FPN stages and channels with large feature magnitude from the teacher model could dominate the gradient of distillation loss, which will overwhelm the effects of other features in KD and introduce much noise. To address the above issues, we propose to imitate features with Pearson Correlation Coefficient to focus on the relational information from the teacher and relax constraints on the magnitude of the features. Our method consistently outperforms the existing detection KD methods and works for both homogeneous and heterogeneous student-teacher pairs. Furthermore, it converges faster. With a powerful MaskRCNN-Swin detector as the teacher, ResNet-50 based RetinaNet and FCOS achieve 41.5% and 43.9% mAP on COCO2017, which are 4.1\% and 4.8\% higher than the baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster models by transferring behavior or representations from a teacher to a student. It is widely used to enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints across modalities (vision, language, speech, multimodal) and tasks (classification, retrieval, generation, segmentation). Effective distillation combines multiple signals (soft targets, intermediate-feature matching, layer-wise supervision, adversarial training, and ensemble guidance) and is commonly paired with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Practical pipelines must balance teacher selection, data regimes, and student capacity to approach teacher performance while meeting resource constraints.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a prominent technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and natural language processing. This approach involves training a smaller student network to mimic the output of a larger, more capable teacher network. The method addresses critical challenges in deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments while maintaining performance quality. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, machine translation, and information retrieval systems.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: Compressing Deep Graph Neural Networks via Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep graph neural networks (GNNs) have been shown to be expressive for modeling graph-structured data. Nevertheless, the over-stacked architecture of deep graph models makes it difficult to deploy and rapidly test on mobile or embedded systems. To compress over-stacked GNNs, knowledge distillation via a teacher-student architecture turns out to be an effective technique, where the key step is to measure the discrepancy between teacher and student networks with predefined distance functions. However, using the same distance for graphs of various structures may be unfit, and the optimal distance formulation is hard to determine. To tackle these problems, we propose a novel Adversarial Knowledge Distillation framework for graph models named GraphAKD, which adversarially trains a discriminator and a generator to adaptively detect and decrease the discrepancy. Specifically, noticing that the well-captured inter-node and inter-class correlations favor the success of deep GNNs, we propose to criticize the inherited knowledge from node-level and class-level views with a trainable discriminator. The discriminator distinguishes between teacher knowledge and what the student inherits, while the student GNN works as a generator and aims to fool the discriminator. To our best knowledge, GraphAKD is the first to introduce adversarial training to knowledge distillation in graph domains. Experiments on node-level and graph-level classification benchmarks demonstrate that GraphAKD improves the student performance by a large margin. The results imply that GraphAKD can precisely transfer knowledge from a complicated teacher GNN to a compact student GNN.
