papers_seen.author: Flynn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a foundational technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring learned representations from complex teacher networks to simpler student networks, this approach enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices across diverse applications in computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains. The technique encompasses multiple concrete mechanisms including logit-level supervision, feature and layer-level matching, ensemble guidance, and data-free synthesis. When combined with complementary compression strategies and adapted to task-specific constraints, knowledge distillation routinely produces compact models that preserve much of the teacher's performance while substantially reducing computational requirements, memory footprint, and inference latency.

papers_seen.author: Russell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Composable Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a foundational, composable technique for compressing deep and NLP models: it reliably transfers predictive behavior and representations from high-capacity teachers into smaller students, and when combined with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search, data synthesis or adversarial training) it enables practical deployment on resource-constrained hardware. Realizing KD's benefits requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to handle data and teacher quality, and how to integrate KD into an end-to-end compression pipeline; when used with these considerations it yields compact, robust models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, size, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Task-Aware Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical core technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving task performance. KD mechanisms—ranging from soft-target/logit matching to intermediate representation and layer-wise supervision—support deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints across NLP and other domains. However, KD is not a universal, plug-and-play solution: its success depends on task- and architecture-aware choices, data availability and distribution, and complementary compression techniques. Viewed as part of an integrated compression strategy, KD routinely yields compact models that are suitable for real-world systems, provided practitioners attend to known failure modes and adapt distillation objectives and pipelines to deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational, Multi-Strategy Approach for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most effective when treated not as a single algorithmic trick but as an engineering paradigm that integrates teacher design, student capacity, data strategy, representation objectives, and deployment constraints. When combined with complementary compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and deployment-aware practices (privacy, federated protocols, pre-training of small architectures), KD routinely enables compact models that meet latency, memory, and robustness requirements while preserving most of a teacher's performance. However, KD has limits: teacher–student mismatch, data heterogeneity in federated settings, and fairness or distribution-shift failures demand careful, task-aware design and evaluation. The practical position advocated here is that KD should be adopted as a core, configurable component of compression pipelines, with choice of techniques driven by operational constraints and empirical validation.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Beyond Soft Labels: A Multi-Objective View of Knowledge Distillation for Robust, Efficient Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical route to compress large neural models for deployment, but treating distillation as merely matching teacher output probabilities limits what can be transferred and how reliably the student will generalize. This paper argues that effective distillation should combine representation-level transfer, channel- and feature-aware objectives, confidence-weighted multi-teacher signals, domain adaptation, and training-time efficiency techniques, while explicitly attending to optimization gaps and fairness concerns. We synthesize evidence across methods and propose a prioritized, pragmatic pipeline for producing compact models that better retain teacher knowledge, scale in production, and reduce unintended harms.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become indispensable techniques for deploying large, powerful deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, these methods address the fundamental challenge of making state-of-the-art models practical for real-world applications that require fast inference and limited computational resources. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents a mature, multifaceted framework with broad applicability across diverse domains, supported by both strong empirical results and emerging theoretical understanding of how and why these techniques enable effective knowledge transfer.

papers_seen.author: Green
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Variants, and Practical Patterns
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD methods include matching teacher output distributions, imitating intermediate feature representations, and using task- or architecture-aware adaptations. Across vision, language, graph, and sequential tasks, distillation enables practical deployment on resource-constrained devices by reducing parameter count, inference latency, and memory while often preserving most of the teacher's performance. However, effectiveness depends on optimization, data choice, and the match between teacher signals and student capacity; addressing these factors has motivated many specialized distillation variants and combined compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis from Provided Studies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) trains compact student models to capture the predictive behavior or internal representations of larger teacher networks, enabling deployment under latency, memory, and compute constraints. Across domains, KD strategies range from matching softened output distributions to transferring intermediate features or relational structure, and they are commonly combined with complementary compression techniques such as quantization or architecture search. Empirical evidence shows KD can substantially reduce model size and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance, but effectiveness depends on choices about distillation targets, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability, and task-aware training protocols. Practical pipelines emphasize careful design of objectives, selective use of training examples, and efficiency-aware engineering to make KD viable in production systems.

papers_seen.author: Aguilar
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical and Versatile Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential and widely-adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while preserving much of their performance. The approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students through multiple complementary mechanisms, enabling efficient inference and reduced computational requirements across diverse domains. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents a core practical strategy for model compression, supported by diverse methodologies, empirical validation across multiple applications, and a growing body of research addressing both effectiveness and limitations.

papers_seen.author: Obrien
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental model compression technique that transfers knowledge from larger, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach enables the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a versatile, broadly applicable strategy across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech processing, and specialized applications, addressing critical challenges in computational efficiency, memory constraints, and latency requirements. The technique supports various compression objectives and has been extended to address privacy preservation, domain adaptation, and robust deployment in practical settings.

papers_seen.author: Zavala
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring task-relevant information. Across deep learning and NLP, KD encompasses output-level soft-label matching, feature- and layer-level supervision, architecture-aware procedures, and data-centric strategies (including pretraining and synthetic data). These techniques enable deployment in resource-constrained settings, often preserving much of a teacher’s performance while reducing latency, memory, and energy use. Practical success depends on choices about what teacher signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student components, whether to pretrain students, and how to handle limited or private data. Current advances broaden KD’s role beyond compression to include regularization, robustness, fairness-aware transfer, and privacy-preserving forms of model adaptation, while open challenges remain in principled selection of transfer targets, handling distribution shift, and automating task-adaptive compression.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and NLP. This approach involves training a lightweight student network to mimic a more powerful teacher network, enabling the creation of efficient models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and multimodal learning, addressing the challenge of maintaining high performance while significantly reducing computational requirements and model size.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Towards Model Agnostic Federated Learning Using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Is it possible to design an universal API for federated learning using which an ad-hoc group of data-holders (agents) collaborate with each other and perform federated learning? Such an API would necessarily need to be model-agnostic i.e. make no assumption about the model architecture being used by the agents, and also cannot rely on having representative public data at hand. Knowledge distillation (KD) is the obvious tool of choice to design such protocols. However, surprisingly, we show that most natural KD-based federated learning protocols have poor performance.   To investigate this, we propose a new theoretical framework, Federated Kernel ridge regression, which can capture both model heterogeneity as well as data heterogeneity. Our analysis shows that the degradation is largely due to a fundamental limitation of knowledge distillation under data heterogeneity. We further validate our framework by analyzing and designing new protocols based on KD. Their performance on real world experiments using neural networks, though still unsatisfactory, closely matches our theoretical predictions.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Distilling the Knowledge of BERT for Sequence-to-Sequence ASR
papers_seen.abstract: Attention-based sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) models have achieved promising results in automatic speech recognition (ASR). However, as these models decode in a left-to-right way, they do not have access to context on the right. We leverage both left and right context by applying BERT as an external language model to seq2seq ASR through knowledge distillation. In our proposed method, BERT generates soft labels to guide the training of seq2seq ASR. Furthermore, we leverage context beyond the current utterance as input to BERT. Experimental evaluations show that our method significantly improves the ASR performance from the seq2seq baseline on the Corpus of Spontaneous Japanese (CSJ). Knowledge distillation from BERT outperforms that from a transformer LM that only looks at left context. We also show the effectiveness of leveraging context beyond the current utterance. Our method outperforms other LM application approaches such as n-best rescoring and shallow fusion, while it does not require extra inference cost.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Adversarial Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) has made remarkable progress in the last few years and become a popular paradigm for model compression and knowledge transfer. However, almost all existing KD algorithms are data-driven, i.e., relying on a large amount of original training data or alternative data, which is usually unavailable in real-world scenarios. In this paper, we devote ourselves to this challenging problem and propose a novel adversarial distillation mechanism to craft a compact student model without any real-world data. We introduce a model discrepancy to quantificationally measure the difference between student and teacher models and construct an optimizable upper bound. In our work, the student and the teacher jointly act the role of the discriminator to reduce this discrepancy, when a generator adversarially produces some "hard samples" to enlarge it. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed data-free method yields comparable performance to existing data-driven methods. More strikingly, our approach can be directly extended to semantic segmentation, which is more complicated than classification, and our approach achieves state-of-the-art results. Code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/VainF/Data-Free-Adversarial-Distillation.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lightweight student networks, KD enables practical deployment of sophisticated deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. The approach encompasses multiple methodologies including soft-target matching, feature-level imitation, and attention-based transfers, with applications spanning computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and specialized domains. While KD delivers substantial practical gains in model size, latency, and memory requirements, its effectiveness depends critically on careful design choices regarding what knowledge is transferred, data availability, teacher-student alignment, and task-specific optimization strategies.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation in Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Since deep learning became a key player in natural language processing (NLP), many deep learning models have been showing remarkable performances in a variety of NLP tasks, and in some cases, they are even outperforming humans. Such high performance can be explained by efficient knowledge representation of deep learning models. While many methods have been proposed to learn more efficient representation, knowledge distillation from pretrained deep networks suggest that we can use more information from the soft target probability to train other neural networks. In this paper, we propose a new knowledge distillation method self-knowledge distillation, based on the soft target probabilities of the training model itself, where multimode information is distilled from the word embedding space right below the softmax layer. Due to the time complexity, our method approximates the soft target probabilities. In experiments, we applied the proposed method to two different and fundamental NLP tasks: language model and neural machine translation. The experiment results show that our proposed method improves performance on the tasks.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: BAM! Born-Again Multi-Task Networks for Natural Language Understanding
papers_seen.abstract: It can be challenging to train multi-task neural networks that outperform or even match their single-task counterparts. To help address this, we propose using knowledge distillation where single-task models teach a multi-task model. We enhance this training with teacher annealing, a novel method that gradually transitions the model from distillation to supervised learning, helping the multi-task model surpass its single-task teachers. We evaluate our approach by multi-task fine-tuning BERT on the GLUE benchmark. Our method consistently improves over standard single-task and multi-task training.

papers_seen.author: Richards
papers_seen.title: TextKD-GAN: Text Generation using KnowledgeDistillation and Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Text generation is of particular interest in many NLP applications such as machine translation, language modeling, and text summarization. Generative adversarial networks (GANs) achieved a remarkable success in high quality image generation in computer vision,and recently, GANs have gained lots of interest from the NLP community as well. However, achieving similar success in NLP would be more challenging due to the discrete nature of text. In this work, we introduce a method using knowledge distillation to effectively exploit GAN setup for text generation. We demonstrate how autoencoders (AEs) can be used for providing a continuous representation of sentences, which is a smooth representation that assign non-zero probabilities to more than one word. We distill this representation to train the generator to synthesize similar smooth representations. We perform a number of experiments to validate our idea using different datasets and show that our proposed approach yields better performance in terms of the BLEU score and Jensen-Shannon distance (JSD) measure compared to traditional GAN-based text generation approaches without pre-training.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Enhancing Student Model Performance Through Teacher-Guided Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining or even improving performance. This approach transfers knowledge from a well-trained teacher model to a lightweight student model through various mechanisms including soft target matching, intermediate layer alignment, and task-aware filtering. Applications span across natural language processing, computer vision, and domain-specific tasks, addressing critical deployment challenges related to latency, computational resources, and model size constraints in real-world production environments.

papers_seen.author: Mcclain
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation from Internal Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is typically conducted by training a small model (the student) to mimic a large and cumbersome model (the teacher). The idea is to compress the knowledge from the teacher by using its output probabilities as soft-labels to optimize the student. However, when the teacher is considerably large, there is no guarantee that the internal knowledge of the teacher will be transferred into the student; even if the student closely matches the soft-labels, its internal representations may be considerably different. This internal mismatch can undermine the generalization capabilities originally intended to be transferred from the teacher to the student. In this paper, we propose to distill the internal representations of a large model such as BERT into a simplified version of it. We formulate two ways to distill such representations and various algorithms to conduct the distillation. We experiment with datasets from the GLUE benchmark and consistently show that adding knowledge distillation from internal representations is a more powerful method than only using soft-label distillation.

papers_seen.author: Oliver
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Practical, Responsible Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core technique for reducing the size and inference cost of high‑capacity models while retaining much of their predictive power. KD extends beyond simple teacher→student soft‑label matching to include representation‑level transfer, contrastive alignment, data‑free synthesis, and privacy‑aware schemes that make compression feasible when original training data are unavailable or sensitive. When combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and guided by task‑aware choices about what and when to transfer, KD enables deployable models for resource‑constrained and safety‑sensitive settings. However, realizing these benefits requires attention to teacher–student capacity gaps, the form of transferred knowledge, and domain or token‑frequency effects; principled design and evaluation are therefore essential for reliable compression in practice.

papers_seen.author: Carr
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Composable, Practical Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models by transferring useful behavior from teacher models to students. Across vision, speech, and NLP, KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while often preserving much of the teacher's performance. The technique encompasses multiple operational modalities — logits matching, feature mimicking, multi-teacher fusion, data-free synthesis, and distributed/federated protocols — and is best applied as an adaptable toolkit whose components are selected to match data availability, privacy constraints, robustness needs, and target hardware.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Methods and Practices for Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible set of techniques to transfer knowledge from a high-capacity teacher model to a smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student. Work across modalities and tasks has shown KD can yield compact models that approach teacher performance, enable deployment on resource-limited devices, help mitigate data-availability or privacy constraints, and act as a vehicle for transferring ensemble or multi-teacher knowledge into a single model. Practical KD methods vary in what they transfer (logits, intermediate features, or rankings), whether they require original training data, and how they structure training (offline, online, adversarial, or curriculum-based). Empirical and methodological work highlights (1) the effectiveness of feature-level supervision in many settings, (2) the value of synthetic or replayed data when real data are unavailable, (3) that ensemble and online schemes can speed training and improve robustness, and (4) that augmentation, sample selection, and task-specific losses materially affect distilled-student outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: Compressing Deep Graph Neural Networks via Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep graph neural networks (GNNs) have been shown to be expressive for modeling graph-structured data. Nevertheless, the over-stacked architecture of deep graph models makes it difficult to deploy and rapidly test on mobile or embedded systems. To compress over-stacked GNNs, knowledge distillation via a teacher-student architecture turns out to be an effective technique, where the key step is to measure the discrepancy between teacher and student networks with predefined distance functions. However, using the same distance for graphs of various structures may be unfit, and the optimal distance formulation is hard to determine. To tackle these problems, we propose a novel Adversarial Knowledge Distillation framework for graph models named GraphAKD, which adversarially trains a discriminator and a generator to adaptively detect and decrease the discrepancy. Specifically, noticing that the well-captured inter-node and inter-class correlations favor the success of deep GNNs, we propose to criticize the inherited knowledge from node-level and class-level views with a trainable discriminator. The discriminator distinguishes between teacher knowledge and what the student inherits, while the student GNN works as a generator and aims to fool the discriminator. To our best knowledge, GraphAKD is the first to introduce adversarial training to knowledge distillation in graph domains. Experiments on node-level and graph-level classification benchmarks demonstrate that GraphAKD improves the student performance by a large margin. The results imply that GraphAKD can precisely transfer knowledge from a complicated teacher GNN to a compact student GNN.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from larger, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, efficient student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. The literature frames KD as a flexible toolbox rather than a single recipe: approaches include transferring output soft-labels, aligning intermediate representations or attention, using multi-teacher schedules, and combining distillation with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical work shows these choices — what to transfer, how to align student and teacher, and which data or augmentations to use — substantially affect whether a student approaches teacher performance. KD has been adapted across classification, sequence modeling, translation, retrieval, recommender systems, generative models, and many NLP tasks, with ongoing challenges around data-free distillation, representation alignment, and robustness in low-resource or privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Crosby
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Overview
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, achieving substantial reductions in parameter count, memory consumption, and inference latency while maintaining competitive accuracy. The field encompasses diverse approaches including logit-level distillation, feature-based imitation, data-free methods, and multi-teacher frameworks, with successful applications across computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and recommendation systems.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-adopted technique for compressing neural networks by transferring knowledge from a larger teacher model to a smaller student model. This approach enables the development of efficient models with reduced parameters and computational requirements while maintaining high performance across various domains including computer vision and natural language processing. The field has evolved to encompass diverse methodologies, from basic logit matching to advanced layer-wise and feature-level distillation approaches, with applications spanning machine translation, question answering, sentiment analysis, and multi-modal learning.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Transferring Knowledge for Efficient Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining performance. This approach transfers knowledge from a larger teacher model to a smaller student model, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices. Model compression through distillation has proven effective across diverse applications including natural language processing, computer vision, and multimodal learning. This paper surveys the principles, methods, and applications of knowledge distillation and related compression techniques in deep learning.

papers_seen.author: Higgins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that enables the efficient deployment of large neural networks by training smaller student models to mimic the behavior of larger teacher models. This approach has become fundamental across computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains, addressing the critical challenge of reducing computational overhead and memory requirements while maintaining competitive performance. The technique encompasses diverse strategies ranging from soft label guidance to intermediate layer alignment and operates through the transfer of learned knowledge from teacher to student networks.

papers_seen.author: Osborne
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely-adopted technique for training compact and efficient models by transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models. This approach has become instrumental across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications like graph neural networks and recommender systems. The technique addresses the fundamental challenge of deploying sophisticated deep learning models in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance levels. Recent advances have expanded the methodology beyond simple output probability matching to include intermediate representations, multi-teacher frameworks, and integration with complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Blair
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful, flexible approach for turning large models into compact, deployable students. KD techniques range from simple soft-label matching to sophisticated intermediate-representation alignment, meta-learned teachers, and self-supervised or adversarially aware objectives. These methods have been shown to preserve much of teacher performance across vision and language tasks while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. At the same time, practical success depends on choices about what information to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to handle limited or private data—areas where principled guidelines and automated strategies remain active opportunities for research and engineering.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a single teacher-student recipe into a flexible family of techniques that enable deployment of high-performing, resource-efficient models across domains including NLP, vision, and federated settings. KD can compress large pretrained models into lightweight architectures, transfer task-specific behavior, enable data-free or zero-shot transfers when original data are unavailable, and improve interpretability or domain generalization when adapted appropriately. However, distillation is not universally sufficient: optimization barriers, dataset artifacts, and bias transfer can limit gains unless addressed by careful method design. I argue that KD is a necessary part of any practical compression toolbox for modern deep learning, but must be combined with task-adaptive search, careful teacher selection, privacy-aware synthesis, and bias mitigation to realize reliable, production-ready compressed models.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models by transferring knowledge from teacher models. This approach has become increasingly important as deep learning models grow larger and more computationally demanding, yet deployment requirements necessitate efficient, lightweight alternatives. Model compression through knowledge distillation encompasses diverse methodologies across computer vision, NLP, and multimodal domains, enabling practical deployment on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive performance.

papers_seen.author: Carney
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the deployment of state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models. Applications span diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, machine translation, and speech recognition, making it a versatile solution for reducing computational costs and storage requirements.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Understanding BERT Rankers Under Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep language models such as BERT pre-trained on large corpus have given a huge performance boost to the state-of-the-art information retrieval ranking systems. Knowledge embedded in such models allows them to pick up complex matching signals between passages and queries. However, the high computation cost during inference limits their deployment in real-world search scenarios. In this paper, we study if and how the knowledge for search within BERT can be transferred to a smaller ranker through distillation. Our experiments demonstrate that it is crucial to use a proper distillation procedure, which produces up to nine times speedup while preserving the state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Deleon
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a versatile, empirically proven approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teacher networks. Across computer vision, natural language processing, graph learning, and multimodal tasks, KD techniques transfer different forms of teacher knowledge — from soft output distributions to intermediate representations — and combine with data-centric strategies (e.g., selective sampling, data synthesis, and curriculum design) to meet deployment constraints such as latency, memory, and privacy. Practical use of KD requires careful matching of teacher signals to student capacity, handling of limited or private data, and often integration with other compression or architecture-aware methods to realize robust, efficient models in production settings.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Transferring Knowledge for Efficient Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining performance. This approach transfers knowledge from a larger teacher model to a smaller student model, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices. Model compression through distillation has proven effective across diverse applications including natural language processing, computer vision, and multimodal learning. This paper surveys the principles, methods, and applications of knowledge distillation and related compression techniques in deep learning.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques transfer information from larger, high-capacity models into smaller, more efficient models to enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Practitioners use a variety of objectives and architectures—logit matching, intermediate-feature imitation, layer-wise supervision, and adversarial or ensemble-based transfers—often combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Applications span vision, speech, recommender systems, machine translation, reading comprehension and multi-modal medical imaging. Key challenges include mismatches between teacher and student capacity, reliance on teacher training data, maintaining performance on rare or low-frequency phenomena, and the runtime cost of using large teachers during distillation. Recent work addresses these with task-aware layer selection, student-aware teacher training, data-free or privacy-preserving distillation, and joint optimization of compression with distillation losses.

Beyond simple compression, knowledge distillation has evolved into a versatile framework applicable across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and reinforcement learning, addressing critical challenges in practical model deployment.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Unifying Heterogeneous Classifiers with Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we study the problem of unifying knowledge from a set of classifiers with different architectures and target classes into a single classifier, given only a generic set of unlabelled data. We call this problem Unifying Heterogeneous Classifiers (UHC). This problem is motivated by scenarios where data is collected from multiple sources, but the sources cannot share their data, e.g., due to privacy concerns, and only privately trained models can be shared. In addition, each source may not be able to gather data to train all classes due to data availability at each source, and may not be able to train the same classification model due to different computational resources. To tackle this problem, we propose a generalisation of knowledge distillation to merge HCs. We derive a probabilistic relation between the outputs of HCs and the probability over all classes. Based on this relation, we propose two classes of methods based on cross-entropy minimisation and matrix factorisation, which allow us to estimate soft labels over all classes from unlabelled samples and use them in lieu of ground truth labels to train a unified classifier. Our extensive experiments on ImageNet, LSUN, and Places365 datasets show that our approaches significantly outperform a naive extension of distillation and can achieve almost the same accuracy as classifiers that are trained in a centralised, supervised manner.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from well-trained teacher models to student networks, this approach enables practical deployment of sophisticated deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. The methodology encompasses diverse approaches ranging from soft target matching to intermediate representation alignment, and has demonstrated effectiveness across multiple domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and recommender systems. Recent advances have expanded knowledge distillation beyond simple output probability matching to include multi-teacher frameworks, task-aware layer-wise distillation, and integration with complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Composable Core for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a versatile foundation for compressing large neural models into efficient students suitable for real-world deployment. As models grow in size and application contexts diversify, distillation provides a set of interoperable mechanisms — from soft-target transfer to intermediate feature matching, self-distillation, and teacher-ensemble consolidation — that can be combined with architecture search, quantization, and task-aware filtering to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. While distillation often preserves much of teacher performance, careful choices about what to transfer, which data to use, and how to adapt the student architecture are necessary to avoid failure modes such as degraded handling of low-frequency phenomena or overfitting teacher artifacts. A composable, task- and data-aware distillation strategy that integrates representation-level objectives, selective data curation, and architecture adaptation yields the best practical trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Compression of Deep Learning Models for Text: A Survey
papers_seen.abstract: In recent years, the fields of natural language processing (NLP) and information retrieval (IR) have made tremendous progress thanksto deep learning models like Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTMs)networks, and Transformer [120] based models like Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) [24], GenerativePre-training Transformer (GPT-2) [94], Multi-task Deep Neural Network (MT-DNN) [73], Extra-Long Network (XLNet) [134], Text-to-text transfer transformer (T5) [95], T-NLG [98] and GShard [63]. But these models are humongous in size. On the other hand,real world applications demand small model size, low response times and low computational power wattage. In this survey, wediscuss six different types of methods (Pruning, Quantization, Knowledge Distillation, Parameter Sharing, Tensor Decomposition, andSub-quadratic Transformer based methods) for compression of such models to enable their deployment in real industry NLP projects.Given the critical need of building applications with efficient and small models, and the large amount of recently published work inthis area, we believe that this survey organizes the plethora of work done by the 'deep learning for NLP' community in the past fewyears and presents it as a coherent story.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression methods form a broad set of techniques for transferring information from larger models (or ensembles) to smaller, faster, or more deployable models. Approaches range from using teacher soft labels to transfer logits, to aligning intermediate representations, to teacher-free and online schemes, and to task- or domain-aware compression for pretrained language models. Applications span image and object recognition, speech and spoken-language tasks, machine translation, continual/federated settings, and specialized domains where latency, memory, or privacy constraints are critical. Empirical work shows that carefully designed distillation—sometimes combined with data augmentation, representation alignment, or multi-teacher selection—can produce compact models that retain a large fraction of teacher performance while improving generalization, calibration, and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques have become central to deploying high-performing deep models under computational, memory, privacy, and latency constraints. Work in this area spans traditional teacher→student soft-target distillation, distillation of internal representations, data-free or zero-shot approaches for when training data are unavailable, online and mutual distillation among peers, multi-teacher and ensemble-based strategies, and adaptations for domain shifts and task-specific requirements (e.g., non-autoregressive translation). Empirical findings emphasize that distillation often reduces training data complexity and transfers information most effectively when methods account for representation mismatch, data generation or augmentation, teacher–student capacity differences, and the distributional specifics of the task. Practical trends favor hybrid pipelines that combine soft-targets with representation matching, selective use of raw or synthesized data, and scalable online/ensemble procedures to support large datasets and heterogeneous deployment scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Oliver
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Practical, Responsible Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core technique for reducing the size and inference cost of high‑capacity models while retaining much of their predictive power. KD extends beyond simple teacher→student soft‑label matching to include representation‑level transfer, contrastive alignment, data‑free synthesis, and privacy‑aware schemes that make compression feasible when original training data are unavailable or sensitive. When combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and guided by task‑aware choices about what and when to transfer, KD enables deployable models for resource‑constrained and safety‑sensitive settings. However, realizing these benefits requires attention to teacher–student capacity gaps, the form of transferred knowledge, and domain or token‑frequency effects; principled design and evaluation are therefore essential for reliable compression in practice.

papers_seen.author: Mayo
papers_seen.title: Rethinking Soft Labels for Knowledge Distillation: A Bias-Variance Tradeoff Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective approach to leverage a well-trained network or an ensemble of them, named as the teacher, to guide the training of a student network. The outputs from the teacher network are used as soft labels for supervising the training of a new network. Recent studies \citep{muller2019does,yuan2020revisiting} revealed an intriguing property of the soft labels that making labels soft serves as a good regularization to the student network. From the perspective of statistical learning, regularization aims to reduce the variance, however how bias and variance change is not clear for training with soft labels. In this paper, we investigate the bias-variance tradeoff brought by distillation with soft labels. Specifically, we observe that during training the bias-variance tradeoff varies sample-wisely. Further, under the same distillation temperature setting, we observe that the distillation performance is negatively associated with the number of some specific samples, which are named as regularization samples since these samples lead to bias increasing and variance decreasing. Nevertheless, we empirically find that completely filtering out regularization samples also deteriorates distillation performance. Our discoveries inspired us to propose the novel weighted soft labels to help the network adaptively handle the sample-wise bias-variance tradeoff. Experiments on standard evaluation benchmarks validate the effectiveness of our method. Our code is available at \url{https://github.com/bellymonster/Weighted-Soft-Label-Distillation}.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Versatile Core Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an adaptable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teacher performance. KD encompasses multiple families of techniques — soft-target matching, intermediate-representation matching, module replacement, online/peer distillation, and ensemble-to-single-model transfer — and has been applied successfully across NLP tasks (including large transformer compression and machine translation), graph and recommender systems, and large-scale distributed training. Realizing KD’s benefits in practice requires matching the distillation objective to student capacity and deployment constraints, choosing appropriate data or surrogate data strategies, and addressing interactions with training regularizers and teacher quality.

papers_seen.author: Pacheco
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Powerful Framework for Model Compression and Transfer Learning in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a highly effective approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This technique enables the transfer of knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, making it particularly valuable for deploying models in resource-constrained environments. The method has proven successful across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and multimodal learning. By leveraging various distillation strategies and loss functions, researchers have demonstrated that knowledge distillation can achieve substantial performance improvements and computational efficiency gains with minimal accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers learned representations from complex teacher networks to simpler student networks, enabling efficient deployment of state-of-the-art models across diverse applications in deep learning and natural language processing. Beyond simple model compression, knowledge distillation facilitates knowledge transfer across different architectures, improves robustness, and supports learning from ensemble models. The technique has proven particularly valuable in addressing computational constraints that limit practical deployment while preserving the performance gains achieved through large-scale pre-training.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: A Multi-Strategy Prescription for Effective Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are most effective when treated as a multi-objective engineering problem rather than a single loss-matching task. Practical, robust compression for NLP and other deep models requires coordinated decisions about teacher construction, data and augmentation strategies, what to transfer (logits, features, or modules), and how to handle limited or absent training data. Combining dynamic multi-teacher selection, representation-level objectives, augmentation-aware distillation, and adversarial or meta-learned teacher paradigms yields students that retain more of the teacher's strengths while addressing common failure modes such as rare-token degradation and domain shift.

papers_seen.author: May
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Strategic Framework for Deploying Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a foundational and practical approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while maintaining competitive performance. Rather than a single monolithic technique, knowledge distillation functions as a flexible, composable framework that can be adapted to specific task, data, and hardware constraints. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should be treated as the default strategy for model compression across deep learning and NLP applications, particularly when combined with complementary compression techniques and careful consideration of optimization and data constraints.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Releasing Graph Neural Networks with Differential Privacy Guarantees
papers_seen.abstract: With the increasing popularity of graph neural networks (GNNs) in several sensitive applications like healthcare and medicine, concerns have been raised over the privacy aspects of trained GNNs. More notably, GNNs are vulnerable to privacy attacks, such as membership inference attacks, even if only black-box access to the trained model is granted. We propose PrivGNN, a privacy-preserving framework for releasing GNN models in a centralized setting. Assuming an access to a public unlabeled graph, PrivGNN provides a framework to release GNN models trained explicitly on public data along with knowledge obtained from the private data in a privacy preserving manner. PrivGNN combines the knowledge-distillation framework with the two noise mechanisms, random subsampling, and noisy labeling, to ensure rigorous privacy guarantees. We theoretically analyze our approach in the Renyi differential privacy framework. Besides, we show the solid experimental performance of our method compared to several baselines adapted for graph-structured data. Our code is available at https://github.com/iyempissy/privGnn.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a practical, flexible set of techniques that enable deploying compact models while retaining much of the performance of larger teachers. When applied with attention to what is distilled (logits versus internal representations), how teachers and students are matched, and how scarce or private data are handled, KD routinely produces deployable models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a universal remedy: teacher–student capacity mismatches, data limitations, optimization dynamics, and task-specific phenomena (e.g., low-frequency tokens) can limit or bias results. A principled KD pipeline—layer-aware representation transfer, data-aware augmentation or synthesis, multi-source supervision, and careful evaluation on rare phenomena and fairness—yields the best practical outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Jacobs
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational Technique for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a central and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from teacher models through various mechanisms—including soft logits, intermediate representations, and synthesized data—knowledge distillation addresses critical deployment challenges across deep learning and natural language processing. This technique represents a pragmatic solution for resource-constrained environments, offering substantial reductions in model size and inference latency without significant accuracy loss. However, realizing its full potential requires careful attention to optimization challenges, teacher-student alignment, and task-specific design considerations.

papers_seen.author: Cook
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the primary tool for compressing large models into efficient students for deployment in deep learning and NLP. KD offers flexible mechanisms to transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from teachers to students, enabling substantial reductions in model size and latency while preserving much of the original performance. However, KD is not a one-size-fits-all recipe: its success depends on careful, task-aware design choices (e.g., which signals to transfer, teacher selection, data regimes, and complementary compression techniques) and on explicit strategies to detect and mitigate teacher error propagation. When applied thoughtfully and combined with other compression and deployment-aware methods, KD yields practical, high-fidelity compressed models across modalities and tasks.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while preserving task performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, enabling deployment across diverse domains including natural language processing and computer vision. By operating beyond simple class labels to encompass soft targets, intermediate representations, and structural behaviors, knowledge distillation addresses critical practical constraints including latency, memory efficiency, privacy, and device heterogeneity. Recent advances have extended KD beyond basic teacher-student frameworks to include multi-teacher schemes, feature-level and attention-based objectives, data-free distillation, and combinations with complementary compression techniques, making it indispensable for real-world neural network deployment.

papers_seen.author: Wong
papers_seen.title: Embracing the Dark Knowledge: Domain Generalization Using Regularized Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Though convolutional neural networks are widely used in different tasks, lack of generalization capability in the absence of sufficient and representative data is one of the challenges that hinder their practical application. In this paper, we propose a simple, effective, and plug-and-play training strategy named Knowledge Distillation for Domain Generalization (KDDG) which is built upon a knowledge distillation framework with the gradient filter as a novel regularization term. We find that both the ``richer dark knowledge" from the teacher network, as well as the gradient filter we proposed, can reduce the difficulty of learning the mapping which further improves the generalization ability of the model. We also conduct experiments extensively to show that our framework can significantly improve the generalization capability of deep neural networks in different tasks including image classification, segmentation, reinforcement learning by comparing our method with existing state-of-the-art domain generalization techniques. Last but not the least, we propose to adopt two metrics to analyze our proposed method in order to better understand how our proposed method benefits the generalization capability of deep neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Findings, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal knowledge from teacher networks. Across computer vision, NLP, speech, and generative modeling, distillation methods have evolved from matching soft logits to aligning intermediate representations and adapting layer mappings for heterogeneous architectures. Practical results show large reductions in parameter counts and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance, but challenges remain in robustness, student-friendly teacher design, and reliably transferring rarer or structural knowledge.
