papers_seen.author: Liu
papers_seen.title: Enabling Multimodal Generation on CLIP via Vision-Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The recent large-scale vision-language pre-training (VLP) of dual-stream architectures (e.g., CLIP) with a tremendous amount of image-text pair data, has shown its superiority on various multimodal alignment tasks. Despite its success, the resulting models are not capable of multimodal generative tasks due to the weak text encoder. To tackle this problem, we propose to augment the dual-stream VLP model with a textual pre-trained language model (PLM) via vision-language knowledge distillation (VLKD), enabling the capability for multimodal generation. VLKD is pretty data- and computation-efficient compared to the pre-training from scratch. Experimental results show that the resulting model has strong zero-shot performance on multimodal generation tasks, such as open-ended visual question answering and image captioning. For example, it achieves 44.5% zero-shot accuracy on the VQAv2 dataset, surpassing the previous state-of-the-art zero-shot model with $7\times$ fewer parameters. Furthermore, the original textual language understanding and generation ability of the PLM is maintained after VLKD, which makes our model versatile for both multimodal and unimodal tasks.

papers_seen.author: Maddox
papers_seen.title: BERT-EMD: Many-to-Many Layer Mapping for BERT Compression with Earth Mover's Distance
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained language models (e.g., BERT) have achieved significant success in various natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, high storage and computational costs obstruct pre-trained language models to be effectively deployed on resource-constrained devices. In this paper, we propose a novel BERT distillation method based on many-to-many layer mapping, which allows each intermediate student layer to learn from any intermediate teacher layers. In this way, our model can learn from different teacher layers adaptively for various NLP tasks. %motivated by the intuition that different NLP tasks require different levels of linguistic knowledge contained in the intermediate layers of BERT. In addition, we leverage Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) to compute the minimum cumulative cost that must be paid to transform knowledge from teacher network to student network. EMD enables the effective matching for many-to-many layer mapping. %EMD can be applied to network layers with different sizes and effectively measures semantic distance between the teacher network and student network. Furthermore, we propose a cost attention mechanism to learn the layer weights used in EMD automatically, which is supposed to further improve the model's performance and accelerate convergence time. Extensive experiments on GLUE benchmark demonstrate that our model achieves competitive performance compared to strong competitors in terms of both accuracy and model compression.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Mitigating Gender Bias in Distilled Language Models via Counterfactual Role Reversal
papers_seen.abstract: Language models excel at generating coherent text, and model compression techniques such as knowledge distillation have enabled their use in resource-constrained settings. However, these models can be biased in multiple ways, including the unfounded association of male and female genders with gender-neutral professions. Therefore, knowledge distillation without any fairness constraints may preserve or exaggerate the teacher model's biases onto the distilled model. To this end, we present a novel approach to mitigate gender disparity in text generation by learning a fair model during knowledge distillation. We propose two modifications to the base knowledge distillation based on counterfactual role reversal$\unicode{x2014}$modifying teacher probabilities and augmenting the training set. We evaluate gender polarity across professions in open-ended text generated from the resulting distilled and finetuned GPT$\unicode{x2012}$2 models and demonstrate a substantial reduction in gender disparity with only a minor compromise in utility. Finally, we observe that language models that reduce gender polarity in language generation do not improve embedding fairness or downstream classification fairness.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation describes a method for training a student network to perform better by learning from a stronger teacher network. Translating a sentence with an Neural Machine Translation (NMT) engine is time expensive and having a smaller model speeds up this process. We demonstrate how to transfer the translation quality of an ensemble and an oracle BLEU teacher network into a single NMT system. Further, we present translation improvements from a teacher network that has the same architecture and dimensions of the student network. As the training of the student model is still expensive, we introduce a data filtering method based on the knowledge of the teacher model that not only speeds up the training, but also leads to better translation quality. Our techniques need no code change and can be easily reproduced with any NMT architecture to speed up the decoding process.

papers_seen.author: Novak
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical Necessity for Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential technique for deploying high-performing deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. By enabling the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in model size, inference latency, and computational resource requirements. This approach has proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and specialized medical applications, demonstrating its versatility and practical importance for modern machine learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: SEED: Self-supervised Distillation For Visual Representation
papers_seen.abstract: This paper is concerned with self-supervised learning for small models. The problem is motivated by our empirical studies that while the widely used contrastive self-supervised learning method has shown great progress on large model training, it does not work well for small models. To address this problem, we propose a new learning paradigm, named SElf-SupErvised Distillation (SEED), where we leverage a larger network (as Teacher) to transfer its representational knowledge into a smaller architecture (as Student) in a self-supervised fashion. Instead of directly learning from unlabeled data, we train a student encoder to mimic the similarity score distribution inferred by a teacher over a set of instances. We show that SEED dramatically boosts the performance of small networks on downstream tasks. Compared with self-supervised baselines, SEED improves the top-1 accuracy from 42.2% to 67.6% on EfficientNet-B0 and from 36.3% to 68.2% on MobileNet-v3-Large on the ImageNet-1k dataset.

papers_seen.author: Cowan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of their performance. KD techniques range from classic soft-logit matching to feature- and layer-wise transfer, and they enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, realizing KD's benefits requires task- and architecture-aware choices: what to distill (logits, features, internal layers), how to handle limited or private data, and how to align teacher-student capacities. When combined with principled practices, KD is indispensable for translating research-scale models into robust, efficient production systems.

papers_seen.author: Alvarado
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while preserving performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to students, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices and reducing computational overhead. KD encompasses diverse methodologies including soft-target matching, feature-level mimicry, data-free approaches, and multi-teacher strategies, with applications spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks. The field continues to evolve with new insights into when and why distillation succeeds, addressing challenges such as data heterogeneity, privacy constraints, and the selection of appropriate student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: DE-RRD: A Knowledge Distillation Framework for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: Recent recommender systems have started to employ knowledge distillation, which is a model compression technique distilling knowledge from a cumbersome model (teacher) to a compact model (student), to reduce inference latency while maintaining performance. The state-of-the-art methods have only focused on making the student model accurately imitate the predictions of the teacher model. They have a limitation in that the prediction results incompletely reveal the teacher's knowledge. In this paper, we propose a novel knowledge distillation framework for recommender system, called DE-RRD, which enables the student model to learn from the latent knowledge encoded in the teacher model as well as from the teacher's predictions. Concretely, DE-RRD consists of two methods: 1) Distillation Experts (DE) that directly transfers the latent knowledge from the teacher model. DE exploits "experts" and a novel expert selection strategy for effectively distilling the vast teacher's knowledge to the student with limited capacity. 2) Relaxed Ranking Distillation (RRD) that transfers the knowledge revealed from the teacher's prediction with consideration of the relaxed ranking orders among items. Our extensive experiments show that DE-RRD outperforms the state-of-the-art competitors and achieves comparable or even better performance to that of the teacher model with faster inference time.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical and Essential Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from well-trained teacher models to compact student networks, distillation enables significant reductions in computational requirements, memory footprint, and inference latency while maintaining competitive predictive performance. This approach has demonstrated broad applicability across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and specialized applications, making it an indispensable method for modern machine learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Chambers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a versatile and practical family of techniques for compressing large deep neural models into smaller, deployable ones without substantial loss of performance. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks, addressing critical deployment constraints including computational cost, memory requirements, inference latency, and privacy concerns. KD has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and specialized applications, with continuous methodological innovations expanding its scope and effectiveness.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher networks to smaller, efficient student networks, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. This approach has become a foundational strategy in deep learning and natural language processing, addressing critical challenges such as reducing computational costs, memory footprint, and inference latency. Knowledge distillation supports diverse applications across computer vision, NLP, speech recognition, and specialized domains, and can be combined with complementary compression techniques to achieve practical, production-ready compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) trains compact student models to mimic larger teacher models to reduce size, latency, and resource use while retaining much of the teacher's performance. KD encompasses several transfer mechanisms (soft-target/logit transfer, intermediate feature and layer matching, attention-based mapping, and data- or model-aware curricula) and extensions (ensemble distillation, data-free or privacy-preserving workflows, and adversarial sample selection). Applied widely in NLP (including compressing large pretrained transformers), computer vision, and multimodal systems, KD is most effective when combined with complementary techniques—task-aware layer alignment, careful teacher selection or ensembling, and data strategies—to meet deployment constraints. Remaining open problems include principled choices of transfer targets, robustness under domain and data heterogeneity, and automated, task-adaptive compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Arroyo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques have become central to deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Research spans practical recipes (logit matching, feature and layer-wise matching, projector modules), structural compression (architectural transforms, channel/filter reduction), and specialized strategies for NLP models (layer mapping for transformers and task-aware layer selection). Recent work also addresses learning dynamics and theory for wide networks, multi-teacher and meta-learned teaching, and scenarios with limited or no access to original training data. Empirical results show that careful choice of distillation targets, alignment mechanisms, and teacher-student curricula can yield compact models that retain strong performance on downstream tasks while enabling faster inference and smaller memory footprints. Open challenges include task-specific selection of distilled knowledge, robustness and generalization across distributions, and principled guidelines for architecture-aware distillation in transformers.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Findings, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal knowledge from teacher networks. Across computer vision, NLP, speech, and generative modeling, distillation methods have evolved from matching soft logits to aligning intermediate representations and adapting layer mappings for heterogeneous architectures. Practical results show large reductions in parameter counts and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance, but challenges remain in robustness, student-friendly teacher design, and reliably transferring rarer or structural knowledge.

papers_seen.author: Robbins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques transfer information from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory, and latency while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. The toolkit includes soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate feature and layer mimicry, layer-wise or task-aware filtering, multi- and online-teacher schemes, data-free and synthetic-data approaches, and combinations with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Practical success depends on aligning what is distilled to student capacity and task needs, designing efficient training protocols, and mitigating limits such as teacher–student mismatch, optimization barriers, and degraded performance on low-frequency phenomena. This synthesis summarizes core mechanisms, empirical patterns, practical design choices, domain adaptations (including NLP and generative models), and open challenges for robust, deployment-ready compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a simple technique for matching teacher logits into a broad, practical framework for compressing large models and adapting them to deployment constraints. Contemporary KD encompasses soft-output matching, intermediate feature and layer imitation, online mutual distillation, data-free and zero-shot procedures, and combinations with pruning or low-precision quantization. Empirical evidence shows that when distillation choices (targets, data, teacher selection, and training curriculum) are matched to operational constraints, student models can retain much of teacher performance while achieving significant reductions in size, latency, and memory. Remaining challenges include teacher–student capacity mismatch, distilling robustness and rare phenomena, privacy-preserving distillation, and automating design choices across heterogeneous hardware and tasks. Practical success typically arises from integrated pipelines that combine multiple distillation signals with complementary compression techniques and data strategies.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: The Case for Responsible, Task-Adaptive Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an indispensable tool for compressing large neural models into compact, deployable students. When combined with representation transfer, architecture search, and data-aware synthesis, KD enables substantial reductions in latency and memory while retaining much of the teacher's performance. However, distillation must be applied carefully: mismatches between teacher and student internals, scarce or private training data, and distributional or low-frequency phenomena can limit gains or introduce undesirable artifacts. I argue that KD should be treated as a system-level design choice that pairs multi-objective distillation objectives with task-adaptive student architectures and privacy- or robustness-aware synthesis methods to realize reliable, production-ready compression.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Effective Practices and Limits of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students. When combined with complementary strategies—such as pre-training compact architectures, layer-wise or representation-level transfer, task-aware selection of distilled signals, quantization, and federated or data-free techniques—KD can preserve much of teacher performance while meeting resource constraints. However, distillation is not a silver bullet: optimization challenges, mismatch between teacher and student internals, and mismatches between teacher predictions and task needs can limit gains. Careful design choices and evaluation protocols are therefore necessary to obtain robust, privacy-preserving, and task-appropriate compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Unifying Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, flexible toolkit for compressing large neural models while preserving task performance. Across NLP and other domains, KD enables trade-offs among model size, latency, privacy, interpretability, and cross-device heterogeneity. Effective application requires choosing or designing KD variants that match the deployment constraint (e.g., layer matching for transformers, meta-learning teachers, data-free generation, or federated output sharing). When combined with complementary compression practices (progressive replacement, architectural search, or attention-based feature matching), KD routinely yields compact models suitable for real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Fletcher
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Composable, but Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. KD provides a flexible toolkit—matching logits, aligning features or intermediate layers, ensembling teachers, and integrating with pruning/quantization—that often yields strong accuracy/efficiency trade-offs for vision, NLP, and other domains. However, KD’s effectiveness depends on data availability, teacher-student capacity alignment, optimization dynamics, and the potential transfer of teacher biases; addressing these requires task-aware design, careful augmentation or data synthesis, and privacy-preserving or multi-teacher protocols when needed.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Cross-modal Knowledge Distillation for Vision-to-Sensor Action Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: Human activity recognition (HAR) based on multi-modal approach has been recently shown to improve the accuracy performance of HAR. However, restricted computational resources associated with wearable devices, i.e., smartwatch, failed to directly support such advanced methods. To tackle this issue, this study introduces an end-to-end Vision-to-Sensor Knowledge Distillation (VSKD) framework. In this VSKD framework, only time-series data, i.e., accelerometer data, is needed from wearable devices during the testing phase. Therefore, this framework will not only reduce the computational demands on edge devices, but also produce a learning model that closely matches the performance of the computational expensive multi-modal approach. In order to retain the local temporal relationship and facilitate visual deep learning models, we first convert time-series data to two-dimensional images by applying the Gramian Angular Field ( GAF) based encoding method. We adopted ResNet18 and multi-scale TRN with BN-Inception as teacher and student network in this study, respectively. A novel loss function, named Distance and Angle-wised Semantic Knowledge loss (DASK), is proposed to mitigate the modality variations between the vision and the sensor domain. Extensive experimental results on UTD-MHAD, MMAct, and Berkeley-MHAD datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and competitiveness of the proposed VSKD model which can deployed on wearable sensors.

papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students across computer vision, language, graph, and federated settings. When applied thoughtfully—combining representational distillation, pre-training of compact architectures, and task- or system-aware protocols—KD can retain much of the teacher's accuracy while meeting constraints of latency, memory, privacy, and device heterogeneity. However, KD is not a panacea: its success depends on what is distilled (outputs vs. internal representations), how teachers and students are prepared, and additional concerns such as adversarial robustness and bias that may be transferred unless specifically addressed.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation in Efficient and Robust NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a unifying approach for producing smaller, faster, and often more robust models for NLP and deep learning broadly. When combined with architecture search, layer-wise matching, data-centric techniques, and privacy-aware protocols, distillation enables task-adaptive compression, domain adaptation, and practical deployment under latency, memory, and regulatory constraints. However, the benefits of distillation depend on how knowledge is represented, which data and augmentations are used during transfer, and whether the distillation procedure is aligned with downstream tasks; careful method design—rather than blind teacher-student pairing—is therefore required to realize its full promise.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-adopted model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large, complex teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach enables the deployment of high-performing deep learning models on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive accuracy. Knowledge distillation has been applied across multiple domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, graph neural networks, and recommendation systems, with variants adapted to different architectures and task-specific requirements. The technique addresses the critical challenge of deploying sophisticated neural models in resource-constrained environments while managing computational efficiency, latency, and storage constraints.

papers_seen.author: Hawkins
papers_seen.title: A Fast Knowledge Distillation Framework for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: While Knowledge Distillation (KD) has been recognized as a useful tool in many visual tasks, such as supervised classification and self-supervised representation learning, the main drawback of a vanilla KD framework is its mechanism, which consumes the majority of the computational overhead on forwarding through the giant teacher networks, making the entire learning procedure inefficient and costly. ReLabel, a recently proposed solution, suggests creating a label map for the entire image. During training, it receives the cropped region-level label by RoI aligning on a pre-generated entire label map, allowing for efficient supervision generation without having to pass through the teachers many times. However, as the KD teachers are from conventional multi-crop training, there are various mismatches between the global label-map and region-level label in this technique, resulting in performance deterioration. In this study, we present a Fast Knowledge Distillation (FKD) framework that replicates the distillation training phase and generates soft labels using the multi-crop KD approach, while training faster than ReLabel since no post-processes such as RoI align and softmax operations are used. When conducting multi-crop in the same image for data loading, our FKD is even more efficient than the traditional image classification framework. On ImageNet-1K, we obtain 79.8% with ResNet-50, outperforming ReLabel by ~1.0% while being faster. On the self-supervised learning task, we also show that FKD has an efficiency advantage. Our project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/FKD/index.html, source code and models are available at: https://github.com/szq0214/FKD.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Efficient Transformer-based Large Scale Language Representations using Hardware-friendly Block Structured Pruning
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained large-scale language models have increasingly demonstrated high accuracy on many natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, the limited weight storage and computational speed on hardware platforms have impeded the popularity of pre-trained models, especially in the era of edge computing. In this work, we propose an efficient transformer-based large-scale language representation using hardware-friendly block structure pruning. We incorporate the reweighted group Lasso into block-structured pruning for optimization. Besides the significantly reduced weight storage and computation, the proposed approach achieves high compression rates. Experimental results on different models (BERT, RoBERTa, and DistilBERT) on the General Language Understanding Evaluation (GLUE) benchmark tasks show that we achieve up to 5.0x with zero or minor accuracy degradation on certain task(s). Our proposed method is also orthogonal to existing compact pre-trained language models such as DistilBERT using knowledge distillation, since a further 1.79x average compression rate can be achieved on top of DistilBERT with zero or minor accuracy degradation. It is suitable to deploy the final compressed model on resource-constrained edge devices.

papers_seen.author: Farmer
papers_seen.title: Towards Efficient 3D Object Detection with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite substantial progress in 3D object detection, advanced 3D detectors often suffer from heavy computation overheads. To this end, we explore the potential of knowledge distillation (KD) for developing efficient 3D object detectors, focusing on popular pillar- and voxel-based detectors.In the absence of well-developed teacher-student pairs, we first study how to obtain student models with good trade offs between accuracy and efficiency from the perspectives of model compression and input resolution reduction. Then, we build a benchmark to assess existing KD methods developed in the 2D domain for 3D object detection upon six well-constructed teacher-student pairs. Further, we propose an improved KD pipeline incorporating an enhanced logit KD method that performs KD on only a few pivotal positions determined by teacher classification response, and a teacher-guided student model initialization to facilitate transferring teacher model's feature extraction ability to students through weight inheritance. Finally, we conduct extensive experiments on the Waymo dataset. Our best performing model achieves $65.75\%$ LEVEL 2 mAPH, surpassing its teacher model and requiring only $44\%$ of teacher flops. Our most efficient model runs 51 FPS on an NVIDIA A100, which is $2.2\times$ faster than PointPillar with even higher accuracy. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/CVMI-Lab/SparseKD}.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Reinforced Multi-Teacher Selection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In natural language processing (NLP) tasks, slow inference speed and huge footprints in GPU usage remain the bottleneck of applying pre-trained deep models in production. As a popular method for model compression, knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from one or multiple large (teacher) models to a small (student) model. When multiple teacher models are available in distillation, the state-of-the-art methods assign a fixed weight to a teacher model in the whole distillation. Furthermore, most of the existing methods allocate an equal weight to every teacher model. In this paper, we observe that, due to the complexity of training examples and the differences in student model capability, learning differentially from teacher models can lead to better performance of student models distilled. We systematically develop a reinforced method to dynamically assign weights to teacher models for different training instances and optimize the performance of student model. Our extensive experimental results on several NLP tasks clearly verify the feasibility and effectiveness of our approach.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying large deep neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while preserving predictive performance. Applications span computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and other domains, with diverse approaches adapted to specific task requirements and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: A Comprehensive Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile approach for both model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents a superior alternative to traditional compression methods because it enables effective compression while maintaining model performance, facilitates transfer of complex learned representations across architectures, and proves applicable across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, graph neural networks, and reinforcement learning. Unlike methods that simply reduce model parameters without guidance, knowledge distillation leverages teacher-student frameworks to encode valuable "dark knowledge" that improves generalization and produces more robust, efficient models.

papers_seen.author: Wolfe
papers_seen.title: Robust and Resource-Efficient Data-Free Knowledge Distillation by Generative Pseudo Replay
papers_seen.abstract: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation (KD) allows knowledge transfer from a trained neural network (teacher) to a more compact one (student) in the absence of original training data. Existing works use a validation set to monitor the accuracy of the student over real data and report the highest performance throughout the entire process. However, validation data may not be available at distillation time either, making it infeasible to record the student snapshot that achieved the peak accuracy. Therefore, a practical data-free KD method should be robust and ideally provide monotonically increasing student accuracy during distillation. This is challenging because the student experiences knowledge degradation due to the distribution shift of the synthetic data. A straightforward approach to overcome this issue is to store and rehearse the generated samples periodically, which increases the memory footprint and creates privacy concerns. We propose to model the distribution of the previously observed synthetic samples with a generative network. In particular, we design a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) with a training objective that is customized to learn the synthetic data representations optimally. The student is rehearsed by the generative pseudo replay technique, with samples produced by the VAE. Hence knowledge degradation can be prevented without storing any samples. Experiments on image classification benchmarks show that our method optimizes the expected value of the distilled model accuracy while eliminating the large memory overhead incurred by the sample-storing methods.

papers_seen.author: Silva
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Strategy for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and broadly applicable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while preserving predictive performance. By transferring knowledge from large teacher models to compact student networks, knowledge distillation enables efficient deployment across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and recommendation systems. This approach addresses critical practical constraints of modern machine learning by reducing storage requirements, computational costs, and inference latency, making sophisticated deep learning systems accessible for resource-constrained environments and real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Rejuvenating Low-Frequency Words: Making the Most of Parallel Data in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly used to construct synthetic data for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models. However, there exists a discrepancy on low-frequency words between the distilled and the original data, leading to more errors on predicting low-frequency words. To alleviate the problem, we directly expose the raw data into NAT by leveraging pretraining. By analyzing directed alignments, we found that KD makes low-frequency source words aligned with targets more deterministically but fails to align sufficient low-frequency words from target to source. Accordingly, we propose reverse KD to rejuvenate more alignments for low-frequency target words. To make the most of authentic and synthetic data, we combine these complementary approaches as a new training strategy for further boosting NAT performance. We conduct experiments on five translation benchmarks over two advanced architectures. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach can significantly and universally improve translation quality by reducing translation errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach achieves 28.2 and 33.9 BLEU points on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets, respectively. Our code, data, and trained models are available at \url{https://github.com/alphadl/RLFW-NAT}.

papers_seen.author: Fisher
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach involves transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to resource-constrained student networks through various mechanisms including soft logits, intermediate representations, and feature-level alignment. Knowledge distillation has become essential for deploying state-of-the-art deep learning systems across diverse domains including computer vision and natural language processing, addressing critical challenges in model size, inference latency, and computational efficiency while enabling deployment on resource-limited devices without sacrificing accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression approaches transfer information from larger or differently-abled models to smaller, faster, or modality-restricted models. Methods vary from matching final soft logits to mimicking intermediate representations, mapping layers across architectures, adversarially synthesizing training data, and adapting distillation to distributed or heterogeneous-device settings. Empirical and theoretical work highlights trade-offs between simplicity, effectiveness, data availability, and task-specificity, and suggests design patterns for effective compression across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks.

papers_seen.author: Potter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Default for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP (with Caveats and Design Guidelines)
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically proven framework for compressing large teacher models into smaller student models that retain much of the teacher’s capabilities while meeting deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy). When combined with careful teacher–student alignment, multi-source supervision, privacy-preserving mechanisms, and task-aware data strategies, KD routinely produces favorable size–performance tradeoffs across vision, language, generative, and recommendation tasks. However, its practical success depends on matching distillation objectives to student capacity, addressing data availability and domain shift, and mitigating transferred errors or undesirable behaviors. KD should therefore be the default tool for model compression in production, used alongside complementary techniques and principled evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: PKD: General Distillation Framework for Object Detectors via Pearson Correlation Coefficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation(KD) is a widely-used technique to train compact models in object detection. However, there is still a lack of study on how to distill between heterogeneous detectors. In this paper, we empirically find that better FPN features from a heterogeneous teacher detector can help the student although their detection heads and label assignments are different. However, directly aligning the feature maps to distill detectors suffers from two problems. First, the difference in feature magnitude between the teacher and the student could enforce overly strict constraints on the student. Second, the FPN stages and channels with large feature magnitude from the teacher model could dominate the gradient of distillation loss, which will overwhelm the effects of other features in KD and introduce much noise. To address the above issues, we propose to imitate features with Pearson Correlation Coefficient to focus on the relational information from the teacher and relax constraints on the magnitude of the features. Our method consistently outperforms the existing detection KD methods and works for both homogeneous and heterogeneous student-teacher pairs. Furthermore, it converges faster. With a powerful MaskRCNN-Swin detector as the teacher, ResNet-50 based RetinaNet and FCOS achieve 41.5% and 43.9% mAP on COCO2017, which are 4.1\% and 4.8\% higher than the baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Settings, and Insights
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving task performance. Research over the past decade has extended the basic KD idea (teacher soft targets guiding a student) into a diverse set of methods and problem settings: data-free and zero-shot distillation when original data are unavailable, privacy- and communication-aware distillation for on-device or federated deployments, architecture-aware and layer-mapping strategies for large pretrained models, self-distillation and task-adaptive compression, and representational or contrastive objectives tailored for structured domains. Empirical work shows KD enables large speedups and size reductions across vision, speech, graph, and NLP tasks; theoretical and empirical analyses clarify when soft labels help, how dataset complexity interacts with student capacity, and how distillation objectives should be chosen for different architectures and downstream constraints.

papers_seen.author: Cortez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central, flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, speech, and natural language tasks. Over the past decade KD evolved from matching soft logits into a broad set of techniques—feature-level and attention alignment, multi-teacher and online schemes, data- and privacy-aware variants, curriculum and architecture-aware strategies—that collectively enable substantial reductions in model size and latency while preserving much of teacher performance. Practical success depends on matching distillation objectives, data regimes, and student architectures to deployment constraints; open issues include teacher–student mismatch, robustness and fairness transfer, and distillation under limited or private data.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher networks to smaller, efficient student networks, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. This approach has become a foundational strategy in deep learning and natural language processing, addressing critical challenges such as reducing computational costs, memory footprint, and inference latency. Knowledge distillation supports diverse applications across computer vision, NLP, speech recognition, and specialized domains, and can be combined with complementary compression techniques to achieve practical, production-ready compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: Compressing Deep Graph Neural Networks via Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep graph neural networks (GNNs) have been shown to be expressive for modeling graph-structured data. Nevertheless, the over-stacked architecture of deep graph models makes it difficult to deploy and rapidly test on mobile or embedded systems. To compress over-stacked GNNs, knowledge distillation via a teacher-student architecture turns out to be an effective technique, where the key step is to measure the discrepancy between teacher and student networks with predefined distance functions. However, using the same distance for graphs of various structures may be unfit, and the optimal distance formulation is hard to determine. To tackle these problems, we propose a novel Adversarial Knowledge Distillation framework for graph models named GraphAKD, which adversarially trains a discriminator and a generator to adaptively detect and decrease the discrepancy. Specifically, noticing that the well-captured inter-node and inter-class correlations favor the success of deep GNNs, we propose to criticize the inherited knowledge from node-level and class-level views with a trainable discriminator. The discriminator distinguishes between teacher knowledge and what the student inherits, while the student GNN works as a generator and aims to fool the discriminator. To our best knowledge, GraphAKD is the first to introduce adversarial training to knowledge distillation in graph domains. Experiments on node-level and graph-level classification benchmarks demonstrate that GraphAKD improves the student performance by a large margin. The results imply that GraphAKD can precisely transfer knowledge from a complicated teacher GNN to a compact student GNN.

papers_seen.author: Mills
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Enabling Efficient Deep Learning Through Strategic Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental paradigm for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while preserving competitive performance. This technique enables the transfer of knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students through various mechanisms including soft target matching, intermediate feature alignment, and self-distillation approaches. By addressing the critical challenge of deploying computationally intensive models on memory and latency-limited devices, knowledge distillation has become indispensable across diverse domains in deep learning and natural language processing, offering practical solutions for real-world applications where efficiency is paramount.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression methods form a broad set of techniques for transferring information from larger models (or ensembles) to smaller, faster, or more deployable models. Approaches range from using teacher soft labels to transfer logits, to aligning intermediate representations, to teacher-free and online schemes, and to task- or domain-aware compression for pretrained language models. Applications span image and object recognition, speech and spoken-language tasks, machine translation, continual/federated settings, and specialized domains where latency, memory, or privacy constraints are critical. Empirical work shows that carefully designed distillation—sometimes combined with data augmentation, representation alignment, or multi-teacher selection—can produce compact models that retain a large fraction of teacher performance while improving generalization, calibration, and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and widely-adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, enabling practical deployment while maintaining competitive performance across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and machine translation. While knowledge distillation offers substantial practical benefits in reducing model size, computational cost, and inference latency, recent research reveals important limitations and nuances in how knowledge transfer occurs, and highlights the importance of careful design choices and methodical application rather than treating distillation as a universal solution.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Distilling portable Generative Adversarial Networks for Image Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been widely used in various image-to-image translation tasks, they can be hardly applied on mobile devices due to their heavy computation and storage cost. Traditional network compression methods focus on visually recognition tasks, but never deal with generation tasks. Inspired by knowledge distillation, a student generator of fewer parameters is trained by inheriting the low-level and high-level information from the original heavy teacher generator. To promote the capability of student generator, we include a student discriminator to measure the distances between real images, and images generated by student and teacher generators. An adversarial learning process is therefore established to optimize student generator and student discriminator. Qualitative and quantitative analysis by conducting experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method can learn portable generative models with strong performance.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying large deep neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while preserving predictive performance. Applications span computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and other domains, with diverse approaches adapted to specific task requirements and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Bowman
papers_seen.title: TRILLsson: Distilled Universal Paralinguistic Speech Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in self-supervision have dramatically improved the quality of speech representations. However, deployment of state-of-the-art embedding models on devices has been restricted due to their limited public availability and large resource footprint. Our work addresses these issues by publicly releasing a collection of paralinguistic speech models that are small and near state-of-the-art performance. Our approach is based on knowledge distillation, and our models are distilled on public data only. We explore different architectures and thoroughly evaluate our models on the Non-Semantic Speech (NOSS) benchmark. Our largest distilled model is less than 15% the size of the original model (314MB vs 2.2GB), achieves over 96% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks, and is trained on 6.5% the data. The smallest model is 1% in size (22MB) and achieves over 90% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks. Our models outperform the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 model on 6 of 7 tasks, and our smallest model outperforms the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 on both emotion recognition tasks despite being 7% the size.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Less is More: Task-aware Layer-wise Distillation for Language Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Layer-wise distillation is a powerful tool to compress large models (i.e. teacher models) into small ones (i.e., student models). The student distills knowledge from the teacher by mimicking the hidden representations of the teacher at every intermediate layer. However, layer-wise distillation is difficult. Since the student has a smaller model capacity than the teacher, it is often under-fitted. Furthermore, the hidden representations of the teacher contain redundant information that the student does not necessarily need for the target task's learning. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Task-aware layEr-wise Distillation (TED). TED designs task-aware filters to align the hidden representations of the student and the teacher at each layer. The filters select the knowledge that is useful for the target task from the hidden representations. As such, TED reduces the knowledge gap between the two models and helps the student to fit better on the target task. We evaluate TED in two scenarios: continual pre-training and fine-tuning. TED demonstrates significant and consistent improvements over existing distillation methods in both scenarios. Code is available at https://github.com/cliang1453/task-aware-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Allen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Critical Technology for Efficient Neural Network Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has become an indispensable technique for deploying high-performing deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to compact student models, distillation enables significant reductions in computational requirements and model size while maintaining competitive performance. This position argues that knowledge distillation, when properly designed and combined with complementary compression strategies, represents the most practical and versatile approach to achieving efficient neural networks across diverse applications in computer vision, natural language processing, and beyond.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression Across Modalities
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a flexible, domain-agnostic strategy that enables deployment of high-performing deep models in resource-constrained settings. By transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or distilled data between teacher and student, KD supports compression of generators, discriminative models, and multimodal systems, while enabling privacy-preserving and data-free workflows. When combined with careful pre-training, many-to-many layer alignment, or generative replay, KD allows compact architectures to approach the performance of large teachers and, in some cases, inherit desirable properties such as robustness or interpretability. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a foundational method in model compression toolkits and proposes practical emphases for future work: preserving internal representations, supporting data-free distillation, leveraging pre-training for small models, and distilling robustness.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical and Multifaceted Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of the teachers' performance. KD encompasses many concrete mechanisms (logit-level supervision, feature/attention transfer, layer mapping, synthetic-data distillation, multi-teacher schedules) and can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture design to meet latency, memory, privacy, and interpretability constraints. When chosen and tuned for the deployment constraints and data regime at hand, KD routinely yields compact models that balance accuracy, robustness, and resource costs; however, careful attention to teacher–student capacity, data heterogeneity, fairness, and optimization dynamics is required to obtain reliable results.

papers_seen.author: Riley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Frameworks, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while transferring valuable learned knowledge. This approach enables the deployment of high-performing deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments across multiple domains including computer vision and natural language processing. Knowledge distillation operates through teacher-student learning frameworks that transfer knowledge beyond simple class labels to encompass soft targets, intermediate representations, and structural behaviors. The technique addresses critical challenges in balancing model capacity with computational efficiency while maintaining competitive performance and enabling practical deployment of state-of-the-art models.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning, enabling the training of smaller, more efficient student models to mimic the behavior of larger teacher models. This approach has become increasingly important for deploying neural networks on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive accuracy. The technique has been extensively studied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, federated learning, and generative models, with various architectural innovations and theoretical frameworks developed to improve its effectiveness and applicability.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Methods, Applications, and Empirical Insights
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models by transferring knowledge from a teacher network to a student network. This approach has become increasingly important for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments such as mobile and edge devices. The field encompasses diverse methodologies ranging from feature-level distillation to cross-modal approaches, with applications spanning computer vision, natural language processing, and multimodal learning. Recent research has advanced both theoretical understanding and practical implementations of knowledge distillation, demonstrating significant improvements in model compression while maintaining predictive performance.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Understanding BERT Rankers Under Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep language models such as BERT pre-trained on large corpus have given a huge performance boost to the state-of-the-art information retrieval ranking systems. Knowledge embedded in such models allows them to pick up complex matching signals between passages and queries. However, the high computation cost during inference limits their deployment in real-world search scenarios. In this paper, we study if and how the knowledge for search within BERT can be transferred to a smaller ranker through distillation. Our experiments demonstrate that it is crucial to use a proper distillation procedure, which produces up to nine times speedup while preserving the state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Jacobs
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational Technique for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a central and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from teacher models through various mechanisms—including soft logits, intermediate representations, and synthesized data—knowledge distillation addresses critical deployment challenges across deep learning and natural language processing. This technique represents a pragmatic solution for resource-constrained environments, offering substantial reductions in model size and inference latency without significant accuracy loss. However, realizing its full potential requires careful attention to optimization challenges, teacher-student alignment, and task-specific design considerations.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become fundamental techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, enabling practical deployment while maintaining competitive performance. The techniques address critical challenges in modern deep learning, including reducing inference latency, memory requirements, and computational costs across diverse domains including computer vision and natural language processing.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Comprehensive Framework for Efficient Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying deep neural networks efficiently across diverse applications. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student networks while maintaining performance. This survey examines the fundamental principles, applications, and recent advances in knowledge distillation across multiple domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized tasks. The techniques address critical challenges in model deployment including computational efficiency, memory constraints, and privacy preservation while maintaining state-of-the-art performance levels.

papers_seen.author: Wise
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression methods create smaller, faster models by transferring useful information from large teacher networks to compact student networks. In practice, KD reduces inference latency and memory use while preserving much of teacher performance; it is implemented through a spectrum of techniques (soft-target matching, intermediate representation alignment, multi-teacher fusion, and data-side strategies) and is applied across domains from pretrained language models to domain adaptation and privacy-sensitive releases. Effectiveness depends on what signals are transferred, data available for distillation, alignment between teacher and student architectures, and deployment constraints; open challenges include robustness under distribution shift, few-shot or data-free distillation, principled teacher design for constrained students, and privacy-aware protocols.
