papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: AutoGAN-Distiller: Searching to Compress Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: The compression of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has lately drawn attention, due to the increasing demand for deploying GANs into mobile devices for numerous applications such as image translation, enhancement and editing. However, compared to the substantial efforts to compressing other deep models, the research on compressing GANs (usually the generators) remains at its infancy stage. Existing GAN compression algorithms are limited to handling specific GAN architectures and losses. Inspired by the recent success of AutoML in deep compression, we introduce AutoML to GAN compression and develop an AutoGAN-Distiller (AGD) framework. Starting with a specifically designed efficient search space, AGD performs an end-to-end discovery for new efficient generators, given the target computational resource constraints. The search is guided by the original GAN model via knowledge distillation, therefore fulfilling the compression. AGD is fully automatic, standalone (i.e., needing no trained discriminators), and generically applicable to various GAN models. We evaluate AGD in two representative GAN tasks: image translation and super resolution. Without bells and whistles, AGD yields remarkably lightweight yet more competitive compressed models, that largely outperform existing alternatives. Our codes and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/TAMU-VITA/AGD.

papers_seen.author: Huff
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are central for deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. By transferring information from larger teacher models to smaller student models, practitioners reduce inference cost while preserving performance. A diverse set of techniques—soft-target/logit transfer, intermediate-feature and attention-based matching, layer-wise/task-aware alignment, data-free and generative replay strategies, multi-teacher or teacher-friendly training, and automated architecture search—has been developed and adapted to domains such as vision, generative modeling, 3D/novel-view synthesis, recommendation, graphs, and language. Practical success depends on matching teacher signals to student capacity, combining distillation with complementary compression methods, handling limited or private data, and tailoring pipelines to task and architecture constraints.

papers_seen.author: Holmes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile, Practical Core Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a foundational technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models that maintain competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from a high-capacity teacher model to a lightweight student model, KD addresses critical practical constraints in modern deep learning deployment, including computational efficiency, memory constraints, and latency requirements. This approach has proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications, while remaining adaptable to various compression objectives and data availability scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from well-trained teacher models to student networks, this approach enables practical deployment of sophisticated deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. The methodology encompasses diverse approaches ranging from soft target matching to intermediate representation alignment, and has demonstrated effectiveness across multiple domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and recommender systems. Recent advances have expanded knowledge distillation beyond simple output probability matching to include multi-teacher frameworks, task-aware layer-wise distillation, and integration with complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: AlphaNet: Improved Training of Supernets with Alpha-Divergence
papers_seen.abstract: Weight-sharing neural architecture search (NAS) is an effective technique for automating efficient neural architecture design. Weight-sharing NAS builds a supernet that assembles all the architectures as its sub-networks and jointly trains the supernet with the sub-networks. The success of weight-sharing NAS heavily relies on distilling the knowledge of the supernet to the sub-networks. However, we find that the widely used distillation divergence, i.e., KL divergence, may lead to student sub-networks that over-estimate or under-estimate the uncertainty of the teacher supernet, leading to inferior performance of the sub-networks. In this work, we propose to improve the supernet training with a more generalized alpha-divergence. By adaptively selecting the alpha-divergence, we simultaneously prevent the over-estimation or under-estimation of the uncertainty of the teacher model. We apply the proposed alpha-divergence based supernets training to both slimmable neural networks and weight-sharing NAS, and demonstrate significant improvements. Specifically, our discovered model family, AlphaNet, outperforms prior-art models on a wide range of FLOPs regimes, including BigNAS, Once-for-All networks, and AttentiveNAS. We achieve ImageNet top-1 accuracy of 80.0% with only 444M FLOPs. Our code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/facebookresearch/AlphaNet.

papers_seen.author: Moran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Insights
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying large, powerful deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, enabling practical deployment with reduced computational requirements and memory footprint while maintaining competitive performance across diverse applications in computer vision and natural language processing.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models by transferring knowledge from teacher models. This approach has become increasingly important as deep learning models grow larger and more computationally demanding, yet deployment requirements necessitate efficient, lightweight alternatives. Model compression through knowledge distillation encompasses diverse methodologies across computer vision, NLP, and multimodal domains, enabling practical deployment on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive performance.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation in Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Since deep learning became a key player in natural language processing (NLP), many deep learning models have been showing remarkable performances in a variety of NLP tasks, and in some cases, they are even outperforming humans. Such high performance can be explained by efficient knowledge representation of deep learning models. While many methods have been proposed to learn more efficient representation, knowledge distillation from pretrained deep networks suggest that we can use more information from the soft target probability to train other neural networks. In this paper, we propose a new knowledge distillation method self-knowledge distillation, based on the soft target probabilities of the training model itself, where multimode information is distilled from the word embedding space right below the softmax layer. Due to the time complexity, our method approximates the soft target probabilities. In experiments, we applied the proposed method to two different and fundamental NLP tasks: language model and neural machine translation. The experiment results show that our proposed method improves performance on the tasks.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and NLP. By training a lightweight student network to mimic a larger, well-trained teacher network, this approach enables the deployment of high-performance models on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive accuracy. Knowledge distillation operates through the transfer of soft targets and intermediate representations from teacher to student networks, providing implicit regularization and accelerating convergence. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, machine translation, information retrieval, and speech processing, offering substantial reductions in model size and computational cost with minimal performance degradation.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Towards Practical Lipreading with Distilled and Efficient Models
papers_seen.abstract: Lipreading has witnessed a lot of progress due to the resurgence of neural networks. Recent works have placed emphasis on aspects such as improving performance by finding the optimal architecture or improving generalization. However, there is still a significant gap between the current methodologies and the requirements for an effective deployment of lipreading in practical scenarios. In this work, we propose a series of innovations that significantly bridge that gap: first, we raise the state-of-the-art performance by a wide margin on LRW and LRW-1000 to 88.5% and 46.6%, respectively using self-distillation. Secondly, we propose a series of architectural changes, including a novel Depthwise Separable Temporal Convolutional Network (DS-TCN) head, that slashes the computational cost to a fraction of the (already quite efficient) original model. Thirdly, we show that knowledge distillation is a very effective tool for recovering performance of the lightweight models. This results in a range of models with different accuracy-efficiency trade-offs. However, our most promising lightweight models are on par with the current state-of-the-art while showing a reduction of 8.2x and 3.9x in terms of computational cost and number of parameters, respectively, which we hope will enable the deployment of lipreading models in practical applications.

papers_seen.author: Bentley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Practical yet Limited Approach
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a widely adopted and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lightweight students, knowledge distillation reduces computational costs, memory requirements, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance across computer vision, natural language processing, and other domains. However, despite its substantial practical success, knowledge distillation is not a universal solution and faces important theoretical and empirical limitations including optimization difficulties, teacher-student misalignment, data availability constraints, and robustness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Unified Visual Transformer Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Vision transformers (ViTs) have gained popularity recently. Even without customized image operators such as convolutions, ViTs can yield competitive performance when properly trained on massive data. However, the computational overhead of ViTs remains prohibitive, due to stacking multi-head self-attention modules and else. Compared to the vast literature and prevailing success in compressing convolutional neural networks, the study of Vision Transformer compression has also just emerged, and existing works focused on one or two aspects of compression. This paper proposes a unified ViT compression framework that seamlessly assembles three effective techniques: pruning, layer skipping, and knowledge distillation. We formulate a budget-constrained, end-to-end optimization framework, targeting jointly learning model weights, layer-wise pruning ratios/masks, and skip configurations, under a distillation loss. The optimization problem is then solved using the primal-dual algorithm. Experiments are conducted with several ViT variants, e.g. DeiT and T2T-ViT backbones on the ImageNet dataset, and our approach consistently outperforms recent competitors. For example, DeiT-Tiny can be trimmed down to 50\% of the original FLOPs almost without losing accuracy. Codes are available online:~\url{https://github.com/VITA-Group/UVC}.

papers_seen.author: Rasmussen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Foundational Technique for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a central and versatile approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while maintaining competitive performance. This technique transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-efficient student networks through multiple mechanisms including soft output distributions, intermediate representation matching, and layer-level supervision. Evidence demonstrates that knowledge distillation is not merely a specialized compression trick, but rather a fundamental tool that enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art models across vision, language, and multimodal domains while addressing critical constraints such as latency, memory efficiency, and privacy preservation.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Effectiveness, Methods, and Practical Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for training efficient student models by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models, with particular relevance to natural language processing and deep learning applications. This paper examines the evidence for the effectiveness of knowledge distillation approaches, explores various distillation methodologies including feature-based and adaptive approaches, and discusses practical applications in NLP tasks. While knowledge distillation consistently provides parameter reduction and computational efficiency, recent findings suggest the mechanism of improvement involves both direct knowledge transfer and regularization effects. The technique has proven effective across diverse domains including machine translation, neural language models, and transformer compression, though careful consideration of teacher selection, optimization strategies, and hyperparameter tuning remains essential for achieving optimal results.

papers_seen.author: Archer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental training paradigm in which a large, well-trained teacher model transfers learned knowledge to a smaller, more efficient student model. This technique has emerged as essential for model compression, enabling the deployment of high-performing neural networks in resource-constrained environments without sacrificing accuracy. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and speech recognition, serving as a versatile solution for reducing computational costs and storage requirements while maintaining competitive performance levels.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression represent critical techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, these approaches enable significant reductions in model size and computational cost while maintaining competitive accuracy across diverse applications including computer vision, natural language processing, and machine translation. The field has evolved from basic teacher-student knowledge transfer to sophisticated multi-faceted approaches incorporating feature-level matching, data-free methods, sample selection strategies, and robustness-aware training protocols.

papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Object DGCNN: 3D Object Detection using Dynamic Graphs
papers_seen.abstract: 3D object detection often involves complicated training and testing pipelines, which require substantial domain knowledge about individual datasets. Inspired by recent non-maximum suppression-free 2D object detection models, we propose a 3D object detection architecture on point clouds. Our method models 3D object detection as message passing on a dynamic graph, generalizing the DGCNN framework to predict a set of objects. In our construction, we remove the necessity of post-processing via object confidence aggregation or non-maximum suppression. To facilitate object detection from sparse point clouds, we also propose a set-to-set distillation approach customized to 3D detection. This approach aligns the outputs of the teacher model and the student model in a permutation-invariant fashion, significantly simplifying knowledge distillation for the 3D detection task. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on autonomous driving benchmarks. We also provide abundant analysis of the detection model and distillation framework.

papers_seen.author: Rocha
papers_seen.title: Few Shot Network Compression via Cross Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Model compression has been widely adopted to obtain light-weighted deep neural networks. Most prevalent methods, however, require fine-tuning with sufficient training data to ensure accuracy, which could be challenged by privacy and security issues. As a compromise between privacy and performance, in this paper we investigate few shot network compression: given few samples per class, how can we effectively compress the network with negligible performance drop? The core challenge of few shot network compression lies in high estimation errors from the original network during inference, since the compressed network can easily over-fits on the few training instances. The estimation errors could propagate and accumulate layer-wisely and finally deteriorate the network output. To address the problem, we propose cross distillation, a novel layer-wise knowledge distillation approach. By interweaving hidden layers of teacher and student network, layer-wisely accumulated estimation errors can be effectively reduced.The proposed method offers a general framework compatible with prevalent network compression techniques such as pruning. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that cross distillation can significantly improve the student network's accuracy when only a few training instances are available.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Apprentice: Using Knowledge Distillation Techniques To Improve Low-Precision Network Accuracy
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning networks have achieved state-of-the-art accuracies on computer vision workloads like image classification and object detection. The performant systems, however, typically involve big models with numerous parameters. Once trained, a challenging aspect for such top performing models is deployment on resource constrained inference systems - the models (often deep networks or wide networks or both) are compute and memory intensive. Low-precision numerics and model compression using knowledge distillation are popular techniques to lower both the compute requirements and memory footprint of these deployed models. In this paper, we study the combination of these two techniques and show that the performance of low-precision networks can be significantly improved by using knowledge distillation techniques. Our approach, Apprentice, achieves state-of-the-art accuracies using ternary precision and 4-bit precision for variants of ResNet architecture on ImageNet dataset. We present three schemes using which one can apply knowledge distillation techniques to various stages of the train-and-deploy pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Approaches
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, more efficient students while retaining much of the teachers' performance. Recent work expands the KD toolkit beyond matching soft logits to include feature- and layer-level mimicry, task-aware selection of teacher knowledge, data-free and multi-teacher strategies, and augmentation-driven improvements. Practical advances target domain-specific challenges in language models and cross-modal systems, emphasize efficient training and deployment on heterogeneous hardware, and reinterpret KD as a form of regularization that can sometimes be partially replaced or simulated. This review synthesizes these directions and highlights recurring design principles for effective distillation in both NLP and general deep learning settings.

papers_seen.author: Mcclain
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: Powerful, Practical, but Not a Panacea
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a core technique for compressing large models, transferring knowledge across architectures, enabling private or federated workflows, and improving efficiency for deployment in resource-constrained settings. While KD often yields substantial practical gains—reducing model size and inference cost with limited loss in performance—it has important theoretical and empirical limitations related to optimization, data dependence, model and domain heterogeneity, and teacher–student mismatch. A pragmatic stance recognizes KD as a versatile toolset whose effectiveness depends on how it is applied: the choice of distilled targets (logits, features, or relations), the availability or synthesis of data, the use of multiple teachers or staged procedures, and awareness of when distillation can harm or help generalization. This paper argues that KD should be used as part of a broader compression and adaptation strategy guided by empirical diagnostics and appropriate extensions (multi-teacher, zero-shot/data-free, federated/distilled protocols, or self-supervised distillation) rather than as an off-the-shelf cure-all.

papers_seen.author: Humphrey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Deploying Deep Learning Models in Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile technique for compressing deep neural networks and improving their practical deployability. By enabling smaller "student" networks to learn from larger "teacher" models, knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in deploying deep learning systems across diverse domains and hardware constraints. This approach achieves significant model compression ratios while maintaining or even improving performance, making it invaluable for applications requiring efficient inference, interpretability, and resource-constrained deployment. The technique extends beyond simple model compression to encompass diverse applications including natural language processing, computer vision, reinforcement learning, and federated learning, demonstrating its fundamental importance in modern machine learning practice.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation transfers information from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory use, and latency while preserving task performance. A range of mechanisms — matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate features or attention maps, synthesizing surrogate data, and privacy-aware or multi-teacher schemes — enable practitioners to adapt distillation to domain- and task-specific constraints. Successful application depends on choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to handle data availability or privacy, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression methods. Remaining challenges include bridging large capacity gaps, preserving rare or safety-critical behavior, data-free distillation, and robust cross-domain transfer.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Comprehensive Framework for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and practical approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This technique enables the transfer of knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, making deployment in resource-constrained environments feasible without sacrificing accuracy. The method has proven successful across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and multimodal learning, offering substantial performance improvements and computational efficiency gains with minimal accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Vital Strategy for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile technique for model compression and efficient deployment of deep neural networks. By transferring knowledge from larger, well-trained teacher models to compact student networks, this approach enables significant reductions in computational requirements while maintaining or even improving performance. This paper argues that knowledge distillation is indispensable for modern machine learning applications, particularly in NLP and computer vision, where the trade-off between model complexity and efficiency remains critical for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Zuniga
papers_seen.title: Large scale distributed neural network training through online distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Techniques such as ensembling and distillation promise model quality improvements when paired with almost any base model. However, due to increased test-time cost (for ensembles) and increased complexity of the training pipeline (for distillation), these techniques are challenging to use in industrial settings. In this paper we explore a variant of distillation which is relatively straightforward to use as it does not require a complicated multi-stage setup or many new hyperparameters. Our first claim is that online distillation enables us to use extra parallelism to fit very large datasets about twice as fast. Crucially, we can still speed up training even after we have already reached the point at which additional parallelism provides no benefit for synchronous or asynchronous stochastic gradient descent. Two neural networks trained on disjoint subsets of the data can share knowledge by encouraging each model to agree with the predictions the other model would have made. These predictions can come from a stale version of the other model so they can be safely computed using weights that only rarely get transmitted. Our second claim is that online distillation is a cost-effective way to make the exact predictions of a model dramatically more reproducible. We support our claims using experiments on the Criteo Display Ad Challenge dataset, ImageNet, and the largest to-date dataset used for neural language modeling, containing $6\times 10^{11}$ tokens and based on the Common Crawl repository of web data.

papers_seen.author: Walsh
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Core Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, KD enables the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP systems on resource-constrained devices without substantial accuracy loss. This approach addresses critical challenges in balancing model capacity with computational efficiency across diverse domains while supporting practical constraints such as privacy preservation and data scarcity. While KD is not a universal solution, when combined with complementary compression strategies and careful design choices, it represents the most practical and broadly applicable approach to achieving efficient neural networks suitable for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Mueller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Effective Strategies for Deploying Deep Learning Models in Resource-Constrained Environments
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and practical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices and edge computing systems. By leveraging various distillation methodologies—from soft target matching to feature-level alignment—this technique addresses fundamental challenges in deep learning deployment without sacrificing model capability. Knowledge distillation has proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and graph neural networks, making it a foundational technique in modern machine learning.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Preserving Privacy in Federated Learning with Ensemble Cross-Domain Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is a machine learning paradigm where local nodes collaboratively train a central model while the training data remains decentralized. Existing FL methods typically share model parameters or employ co-distillation to address the issue of unbalanced data distribution. However, they suffer from communication bottlenecks. More importantly, they risk privacy leakage. In this work, we develop a privacy preserving and communication efficient method in a FL framework with one-shot offline knowledge distillation using unlabeled, cross-domain public data. We propose a quantized and noisy ensemble of local predictions from completely trained local models for stronger privacy guarantees without sacrificing accuracy. Based on extensive experiments on image classification and text classification tasks, we show that our privacy-preserving method outperforms baseline FL algorithms with superior performance in both accuracy and communication efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Figueroa
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a set of methods that compress large, high-performing neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. Across modalities and tasks, distillation operates as a flexible toolkit—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations or attentions, and adapting training data or objectives—to achieve favorable tradeoffs between model size, latency, and performance. Practical deployments combine KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture changes) and task-aware design choices. While KD routinely yields strong size–performance gains, its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, the choice of distilled targets, data and augmentation strategies, and attention to distributional and low-frequency phenomena; these factors also expose open problems in representation alignment, robustness, and principled teacher design.

papers_seen.author: Novak
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a central technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while preserving performance. This method transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lower-capacity student models, enabling deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices. The approach has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech processing, and graph neural networks, with various methodological innovations continuously expanding its scope and effectiveness.

papers_seen.author: Zuniga
papers_seen.title: Large scale distributed neural network training through online distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Techniques such as ensembling and distillation promise model quality improvements when paired with almost any base model. However, due to increased test-time cost (for ensembles) and increased complexity of the training pipeline (for distillation), these techniques are challenging to use in industrial settings. In this paper we explore a variant of distillation which is relatively straightforward to use as it does not require a complicated multi-stage setup or many new hyperparameters. Our first claim is that online distillation enables us to use extra parallelism to fit very large datasets about twice as fast. Crucially, we can still speed up training even after we have already reached the point at which additional parallelism provides no benefit for synchronous or asynchronous stochastic gradient descent. Two neural networks trained on disjoint subsets of the data can share knowledge by encouraging each model to agree with the predictions the other model would have made. These predictions can come from a stale version of the other model so they can be safely computed using weights that only rarely get transmitted. Our second claim is that online distillation is a cost-effective way to make the exact predictions of a model dramatically more reproducible. We support our claims using experiments on the Criteo Display Ad Challenge dataset, ImageNet, and the largest to-date dataset used for neural language modeling, containing $6\times 10^{11}$ tokens and based on the Common Crawl repository of web data.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Critical Technique for Deep Learning Model Compression and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large deep learning models while maintaining performance. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student models, enabling efficient deployment across diverse applications. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents an essential strategy for addressing the trade-off between model complexity and practical deployment requirements in both computer vision and natural language processing domains.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques have become central tools for shrinking large neural networks while retaining much of their predictive performance. Researchers have adapted KD beyond classification to tasks such as object detection, generative modeling, machine translation, and sequence-to-sequence systems, and have explored many variants including feature imitation, teacher ensembles, sample selection, communication-efficient distributed protocols, and robustness-aware distillation. Empirical work shows KD can yield substantial savings in parameter count, memory, and runtime while often preserving accuracy; however, task-specific challenges, teacher-student mismatches, and distributional or adversarial vulnerabilities require modified objectives, architectures, or training curricula to transfer the right form of “dark” knowledge. The field is moving toward methods that (a) shape teacher outputs or training so distilled information is student-friendly, (b) target intermediate features and decision boundaries rather than only logits, and (c) adapt to resource- and privacy-constrained settings such as federated or few-shot compression.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation in Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Since deep learning became a key player in natural language processing (NLP), many deep learning models have been showing remarkable performances in a variety of NLP tasks, and in some cases, they are even outperforming humans. Such high performance can be explained by efficient knowledge representation of deep learning models. While many methods have been proposed to learn more efficient representation, knowledge distillation from pretrained deep networks suggest that we can use more information from the soft target probability to train other neural networks. In this paper, we propose a new knowledge distillation method self-knowledge distillation, based on the soft target probabilities of the training model itself, where multimode information is distilled from the word embedding space right below the softmax layer. Due to the time complexity, our method approximates the soft target probabilities. In experiments, we applied the proposed method to two different and fundamental NLP tasks: language model and neural machine translation. The experiment results show that our proposed method improves performance on the tasks.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Distilling the Knowledge of BERT for Sequence-to-Sequence ASR
papers_seen.abstract: Attention-based sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) models have achieved promising results in automatic speech recognition (ASR). However, as these models decode in a left-to-right way, they do not have access to context on the right. We leverage both left and right context by applying BERT as an external language model to seq2seq ASR through knowledge distillation. In our proposed method, BERT generates soft labels to guide the training of seq2seq ASR. Furthermore, we leverage context beyond the current utterance as input to BERT. Experimental evaluations show that our method significantly improves the ASR performance from the seq2seq baseline on the Corpus of Spontaneous Japanese (CSJ). Knowledge distillation from BERT outperforms that from a transformer LM that only looks at left context. We also show the effectiveness of leveraging context beyond the current utterance. Our method outperforms other LM application approaches such as n-best rescoring and shallow fusion, while it does not require extra inference cost.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying large, powerful deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, these methods address the fundamental challenge of making state-of-the-art models practical for real-world applications while maintaining competitive performance. This position argues that knowledge distillation is not merely a complementary technique but a central and versatile strategy that, when carefully designed with complementary compression methods, enables effective deployment across diverse domains in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Mcclain
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation from Internal Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is typically conducted by training a small model (the student) to mimic a large and cumbersome model (the teacher). The idea is to compress the knowledge from the teacher by using its output probabilities as soft-labels to optimize the student. However, when the teacher is considerably large, there is no guarantee that the internal knowledge of the teacher will be transferred into the student; even if the student closely matches the soft-labels, its internal representations may be considerably different. This internal mismatch can undermine the generalization capabilities originally intended to be transferred from the teacher to the student. In this paper, we propose to distill the internal representations of a large model such as BERT into a simplified version of it. We formulate two ways to distill such representations and various algorithms to conduct the distillation. We experiment with datasets from the GLUE benchmark and consistently show that adding knowledge distillation from internal representations is a more powerful method than only using soft-label distillation.

papers_seen.author: Henson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Versatile Framework for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to constrained student networks, knowledge distillation enables practical deployment of sophisticated deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and multimodal applications. The approach encompasses multiple complementary strategies ranging from soft-label matching and feature-level transfer to data-free variants and integration with other compression techniques, establishing itself as a core practical framework for modern machine learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Powerful, Practical — but Not a Panacea
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. KD is broadly effective across domains and scales — enabling efficient inference, reducing memory and latency, and supporting applications from pre-trained language models to distributed training — but its success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data and robustness concerns. I argue that KD is an essential, versatile tool for real-world deployment, while also identifying key limitations and concrete practices that improve reliability and performance.

papers_seen.author: Donovan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Pragmatic, Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically essential approach for compressing large models into efficient students that can run under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. When matched to task demands—through choices about targets (logits, features, or relations), data availability (real, synthetic, or none), and architectural strategies (progressive replacement, module design, or self-distillation)—KD reliably yields compact models suitable for real-world deployment. However, its effectiveness depends on careful teacher-student design, appropriate distillation objectives, and complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and allied model-compression techniques provide practical ways to transfer predictive and representational knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models so compact systems can run under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. The literature shows a wide family of methods — matching softened logits, imitating intermediate features or attention, relational and task-specific mappings, self- and multi-teacher schemes, and data-side strategies such as augmentation, synthetic data, or pre-training compact architectures — that together enable strong trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy. Empirical successes span vision, speech, recommendation, and natural language tasks, but open issues remain, including teacher–student mismatch, robustness under distribution shift, limited or absent training data, and principled design of what to transfer for particular student capacities. Practical deployments benefit from combining complementary techniques (representation-level objectives, augmentation-aware distillation, pre-training of small models, and continual or task-adaptive strategies) and from careful tuning of teacher construction, data, and transfer objectives.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Show, Attend and Distill:Knowledge Distillation via Attention-based Feature Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation extracts general knowledge from a pre-trained teacher network and provides guidance to a target student network. Most studies manually tie intermediate features of the teacher and student, and transfer knowledge through pre-defined links. However, manual selection often constructs ineffective links that limit the improvement from the distillation. There has been an attempt to address the problem, but it is still challenging to identify effective links under practical scenarios. In this paper, we introduce an effective and efficient feature distillation method utilizing all the feature levels of the teacher without manually selecting the links. Specifically, our method utilizes an attention-based meta-network that learns relative similarities between features, and applies identified similarities to control distillation intensities of all possible pairs. As a result, our method determines competent links more efficiently than the previous approach and provides better performance on model compression and transfer learning tasks. Further qualitative analyses and ablative studies describe how our method contributes to better distillation. The implementation code is available at github.com/clovaai/attention-feature-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Towards Model Agnostic Federated Learning Using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Is it possible to design an universal API for federated learning using which an ad-hoc group of data-holders (agents) collaborate with each other and perform federated learning? Such an API would necessarily need to be model-agnostic i.e. make no assumption about the model architecture being used by the agents, and also cannot rely on having representative public data at hand. Knowledge distillation (KD) is the obvious tool of choice to design such protocols. However, surprisingly, we show that most natural KD-based federated learning protocols have poor performance.   To investigate this, we propose a new theoretical framework, Federated Kernel ridge regression, which can capture both model heterogeneity as well as data heterogeneity. Our analysis shows that the degradation is largely due to a fundamental limitation of knowledge distillation under data heterogeneity. We further validate our framework by analyzing and designing new protocols based on KD. Their performance on real world experiments using neural networks, though still unsatisfactory, closely matches our theoretical predictions.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression methods form a broad set of techniques for transferring information from larger models (or ensembles) to smaller, faster, or more deployable models. Approaches range from using teacher soft labels to transfer logits, to aligning intermediate representations, to teacher-free and online schemes, and to task- or domain-aware compression for pretrained language models. Applications span image and object recognition, speech and spoken-language tasks, machine translation, continual/federated settings, and specialized domains where latency, memory, or privacy constraints are critical. Empirical work shows that carefully designed distillation—sometimes combined with data augmentation, representation alignment, or multi-teacher selection—can produce compact models that retain a large fraction of teacher performance while improving generalization, calibration, and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Spears
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and essential technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher networks to students through various mechanisms, addressing critical deployment constraints including latency, memory, privacy, and computational efficiency. Knowledge distillation has become a foundational methodology across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, and multimodal learning, enabling practical deployment of state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices. While KD encompasses multiple complementary strategies and demonstrates consistent empirical effectiveness, realizing optimal gains requires careful attention to design choices, teacher quality, data availability, and task-specific adaptation.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Understanding BERT Rankers Under Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep language models such as BERT pre-trained on large corpus have given a huge performance boost to the state-of-the-art information retrieval ranking systems. Knowledge embedded in such models allows them to pick up complex matching signals between passages and queries. However, the high computation cost during inference limits their deployment in real-world search scenarios. In this paper, we study if and how the knowledge for search within BERT can be transferred to a smaller ranker through distillation. Our experiments demonstrate that it is crucial to use a proper distillation procedure, which produces up to nine times speedup while preserving the state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation in Efficient and Robust NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a unifying approach for producing smaller, faster, and often more robust models for NLP and deep learning broadly. When combined with architecture search, layer-wise matching, data-centric techniques, and privacy-aware protocols, distillation enables task-adaptive compression, domain adaptation, and practical deployment under latency, memory, and regulatory constraints. However, the benefits of distillation depend on how knowledge is represented, which data and augmentations are used during transfer, and whether the distillation procedure is aligned with downstream tasks; careful method design—rather than blind teacher-student pairing—is therefore required to realize its full promise.

papers_seen.author: Rocha
papers_seen.title: Few Shot Network Compression via Cross Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Model compression has been widely adopted to obtain light-weighted deep neural networks. Most prevalent methods, however, require fine-tuning with sufficient training data to ensure accuracy, which could be challenged by privacy and security issues. As a compromise between privacy and performance, in this paper we investigate few shot network compression: given few samples per class, how can we effectively compress the network with negligible performance drop? The core challenge of few shot network compression lies in high estimation errors from the original network during inference, since the compressed network can easily over-fits on the few training instances. The estimation errors could propagate and accumulate layer-wisely and finally deteriorate the network output. To address the problem, we propose cross distillation, a novel layer-wise knowledge distillation approach. By interweaving hidden layers of teacher and student network, layer-wisely accumulated estimation errors can be effectively reduced.The proposed method offers a general framework compatible with prevalent network compression techniques such as pruning. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that cross distillation can significantly improve the student network's accuracy when only a few training instances are available.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and allied model-compression techniques transform large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster, or more specialized models while retaining much of the original performance. The approaches span matching teacher soft outputs, imitating intermediate representations, many-to-many layer mapping, data augmentation during transfer, data-free distillation, and architecture-aware compression. Practical systems combine distillation with neural architecture search, federated or privacy-preserving protocols, and multimodal adaptation to meet deployment constraints such as latency, memory, heterogeneity of devices, and absence of original training data. This synthesis summarizes key methods, empirical insights, and deployment-oriented strategies developed to date.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are essential techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models, enabling substantial reductions in model size, computational cost, and inference time while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and question answering. The techniques address fundamental practical challenges in making state-of-the-art models viable for real-world deployment with limited latency, memory, and energy budgets.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lightweight student networks, KD enables practical deployment of sophisticated deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. The approach encompasses multiple methodologies including soft-target matching, feature-level imitation, and attention-based transfers, with applications spanning computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and specialized domains. While KD delivers substantial practical gains in model size, latency, and memory requirements, its effectiveness depends critically on careful design choices regarding what knowledge is transferred, data availability, teacher-student alignment, and task-specific optimization strategies.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: DE-RRD: A Knowledge Distillation Framework for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: Recent recommender systems have started to employ knowledge distillation, which is a model compression technique distilling knowledge from a cumbersome model (teacher) to a compact model (student), to reduce inference latency while maintaining performance. The state-of-the-art methods have only focused on making the student model accurately imitate the predictions of the teacher model. They have a limitation in that the prediction results incompletely reveal the teacher's knowledge. In this paper, we propose a novel knowledge distillation framework for recommender system, called DE-RRD, which enables the student model to learn from the latent knowledge encoded in the teacher model as well as from the teacher's predictions. Concretely, DE-RRD consists of two methods: 1) Distillation Experts (DE) that directly transfers the latent knowledge from the teacher model. DE exploits "experts" and a novel expert selection strategy for effectively distilling the vast teacher's knowledge to the student with limited capacity. 2) Relaxed Ranking Distillation (RRD) that transfers the knowledge revealed from the teacher's prediction with consideration of the relaxed ranking orders among items. Our extensive experiments show that DE-RRD outperforms the state-of-the-art competitors and achieves comparable or even better performance to that of the teacher model with faster inference time.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Online Knowledge Distillation via Mutual Contrastive Learning for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: The teacher-free online Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to train an ensemble of multiple student models collaboratively and distill knowledge from each other. Although existing online KD methods achieve desirable performance, they often focus on class probabilities as the core knowledge type, ignoring the valuable feature representational information. We present a Mutual Contrastive Learning (MCL) framework for online KD. The core idea of MCL is to perform mutual interaction and transfer of contrastive distributions among a cohort of networks in an online manner. Our MCL can aggregate cross-network embedding information and maximize the lower bound to the mutual information between two networks. This enables each network to learn extra contrastive knowledge from others, leading to better feature representations, thus improving the performance of visual recognition tasks. Beyond the final layer, we extend MCL to intermediate layers and perform an adaptive layer-matching mechanism trained by meta-optimization. Experiments on image classification and transfer learning to visual recognition tasks show that layer-wise MCL can lead to consistent performance gains against state-of-the-art online KD approaches. The superiority demonstrates that layer-wise MCL can guide the network to generate better feature representations. Our code is publicly avaliable at https://github.com/winycg/L-MCL.

papers_seen.author: Joyce
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or ensemble models into smaller, faster students by transferring information beyond hard labels. Methods include matching teacher output distributions, aligning internal representations, adversarial/generative teacher-student games, multi-teacher fusion, and data- or augmentation-driven pipelines. Distillation is widely used to reduce inference cost, enable deployment on constrained hardware, and adapt models when training data is limited or sensitive. Practical deployments require careful choices about what to transfer, how to prepare data and augmentations, and whether to combine distillation with complementary compression methods such as pruning and quantization. Open problems include data-free distillation, principled teacher design for student friendliness, robust multi-teacher aggregation, and aligning representations across heterogeneous architectures.

papers_seen.author: Ware
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational Strategy for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential and practical technique for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, this approach achieves significant reductions in model size, computational cost, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation encompasses diverse methodologies beyond simple logit matching, including feature-level alignment, attention transfer, and data-free approaches, enabling flexible adaptation to various deployment scenarios and constraints in domains spanning natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Rasmussen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Foundational Technique for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a central and versatile approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while maintaining competitive performance. This technique transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-efficient student networks through multiple mechanisms including soft output distributions, intermediate representation matching, and layer-level supervision. Evidence demonstrates that knowledge distillation is not merely a specialized compression trick, but rather a fundamental tool that enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art models across vision, language, and multimodal domains while addressing critical constraints such as latency, memory efficiency, and privacy preservation.

papers_seen.author: Cohen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Powerful Tool for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for training efficient student models by transferring knowledge from larger teacher networks. This paper argues that knowledge distillation is uniquely valuable not only for model compression and deployment on resource-constrained devices, but also for enabling knowledge transfer across diverse model architectures, improving model robustness, and facilitating collaborative learning in distributed and federated settings. The evidence demonstrates that distillation succeeds through multiple mechanisms beyond traditional soft label matching, making it an indispensable method for practical deep learning applications.

papers_seen.author: Fletcher
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Composable, but Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. KD provides a flexible toolkit—matching logits, aligning features or intermediate layers, ensembling teachers, and integrating with pruning/quantization—that often yields strong accuracy/efficiency trade-offs for vision, NLP, and other domains. However, KD’s effectiveness depends on data availability, teacher-student capacity alignment, optimization dynamics, and the potential transfer of teacher biases; addressing these requires task-aware design, careful augmentation or data synthesis, and privacy-preserving or multi-teacher protocols when needed.

papers_seen.author: Robbins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques transfer information from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory, and latency while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. The toolkit includes soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate feature and layer mimicry, layer-wise or task-aware filtering, multi- and online-teacher schemes, data-free and synthetic-data approaches, and combinations with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Practical success depends on aligning what is distilled to student capacity and task needs, designing efficient training protocols, and mitigating limits such as teacher–student mismatch, optimization barriers, and degraded performance on low-frequency phenomena. This synthesis summarizes core mechanisms, empirical patterns, practical design choices, domain adaptations (including NLP and generative models), and open challenges for robust, deployment-ready compressed models.
