papers_seen.author: Walter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-adopted training paradigm that enables the compression of large neural networks by transferring knowledge from a high-capacity teacher model to a more efficient student model. This approach has proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and recommendation systems. By leveraging teacher guidance during training, knowledge distillation achieves significant reductions in model size and computational cost while maintaining or even improving student model performance, making it essential for deploying neural networks on resource-constrained devices and enabling practical real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Flynn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Critical Strategy for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential technique for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments by transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach enables substantial reductions in model size, computational cost, and inference latency while maintaining competitive predictive performance. While knowledge distillation is not a universal solution, when carefully combined with complementary strategies such as representation-level transfer, task-specific optimization, and data-aware techniques, it becomes an indispensable tool for bringing state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP models into practical systems across diverse domains.

papers_seen.author: Montoya
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from complex teacher models to lightweight student models, addressing the critical challenge of deploying state-of-the-art deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices. By leveraging various mechanisms including soft target matching, intermediate layer alignment, and feature imitation, knowledge distillation achieves significant reductions in model size and computational cost across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and multimodal learning, making it essential for practical deployment scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Novak
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical Necessity for Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential technique for deploying high-performing deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. By enabling the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in model size, inference latency, and computational resource requirements. This approach has proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and specialized medical applications, demonstrating its versatility and practical importance for modern machine learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and NLP. This approach involves training a lightweight student network to mimic a more powerful teacher network, enabling the creation of efficient models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and multimodal learning, addressing the challenge of maintaining high performance while significantly reducing computational requirements and model size.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and widely-adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, enabling practical deployment while maintaining competitive performance across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and machine translation. While knowledge distillation offers substantial practical benefits in reducing model size, computational cost, and inference latency, recent research reveals important limitations and nuances in how knowledge transfer occurs, and highlights the importance of careful design choices and methodical application rather than treating distillation as a universal solution.

papers_seen.author: Rhodes
papers_seen.title: Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: It is challenging to perform lifelong language learning (LLL) on a stream of different tasks without any performance degradation comparing to the multi-task counterparts. To address this issue, we present Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation (L2KD), a simple but efficient method that can be easily applied to existing LLL architectures in order to mitigate the degradation. Specifically, when the LLL model is trained on a new task, we assign a teacher model to first learn the new task, and pass the knowledge to the LLL model via knowledge distillation. Therefore, the LLL model can better adapt to the new task while keeping the previously learned knowledge. Experiments show that the proposed L2KD consistently improves previous state-of-the-art models, and the degradation comparing to multi-task models in LLL tasks is well mitigated for both sequence generation and text classification tasks.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: Position: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Multipurpose Tool for Model Compression and Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is more than a compression trick: it is a principled, adaptable framework that can both reduce model size and provide transfer, robustness, and deployment advantages when combined with complementary techniques. A practical KD-centered strategy emphasizes transferring intermediate representations in addition to logits, leveraging multiple and domain-aware teachers, accommodating imperfect or heterogeneous teachers, and adapting to constraints such as privacy or federated settings. When KD is used alongside pruning, quantization, or architecture-aware design, it enables compact models that approach the performance of much larger teachers while meeting latency, memory, and hardware constraints.

papers_seen.author: Cook
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the primary tool for compressing large models into efficient students for deployment in deep learning and NLP. KD offers flexible mechanisms to transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from teachers to students, enabling substantial reductions in model size and latency while preserving much of the original performance. However, KD is not a one-size-fits-all recipe: its success depends on careful, task-aware design choices (e.g., which signals to transfer, teacher selection, data regimes, and complementary compression techniques) and on explicit strategies to detect and mitigate teacher error propagation. When applied thoughtfully and combined with other compression and deployment-aware methods, KD yields practical, high-fidelity compressed models across modalities and tasks.

papers_seen.author: Turner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become essential techniques for deploying large neural networks efficiently in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining predictive performance. Knowledge distillation addresses critical real-world deployment constraints including latency, memory consumption, privacy, and device heterogeneity, making it indispensable for practical applications across computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and specialized domains. The field has evolved from simple soft-label matching to a rich toolkit encompassing multiple complementary techniques that can be combined to achieve substantial efficiency gains while retaining most of the teacher model's performance.

papers_seen.author: Higgins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that enables the efficient deployment of large neural networks by training smaller student models to mimic the behavior of larger teacher models. This approach has become fundamental across computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains, addressing the critical challenge of reducing computational overhead and memory requirements while maintaining competitive performance. The technique encompasses diverse strategies ranging from soft label guidance to intermediate layer alignment and operates through the transfer of learned knowledge from teacher to student networks.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Releasing Graph Neural Networks with Differential Privacy Guarantees
papers_seen.abstract: With the increasing popularity of graph neural networks (GNNs) in several sensitive applications like healthcare and medicine, concerns have been raised over the privacy aspects of trained GNNs. More notably, GNNs are vulnerable to privacy attacks, such as membership inference attacks, even if only black-box access to the trained model is granted. We propose PrivGNN, a privacy-preserving framework for releasing GNN models in a centralized setting. Assuming an access to a public unlabeled graph, PrivGNN provides a framework to release GNN models trained explicitly on public data along with knowledge obtained from the private data in a privacy preserving manner. PrivGNN combines the knowledge-distillation framework with the two noise mechanisms, random subsampling, and noisy labeling, to ensure rigorous privacy guarantees. We theoretically analyze our approach in the Renyi differential privacy framework. Besides, we show the solid experimental performance of our method compared to several baselines adapted for graph-structured data. Our code is available at https://github.com/iyempissy/privGnn.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Linkless Link Prediction via Relational Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown exceptional performance in the task of link prediction. Despite their effectiveness, the high latency brought by non-trivial neighborhood data dependency limits GNNs in practical deployments. Conversely, the known efficient MLPs are much less effective than GNNs due to the lack of relational knowledge. In this work, to combine the advantages of GNNs and MLPs, we start with exploring direct knowledge distillation (KD) methods for link prediction, i.e., predicted logit-based matching and node representation-based matching. Upon observing direct KD analogs do not perform well for link prediction, we propose a relational KD framework, Linkless Link Prediction (LLP), to distill knowledge for link prediction with MLPs. Unlike simple KD methods that match independent link logits or node representations, LLP distills relational knowledge that is centered around each (anchor) node to the student MLP. Specifically, we propose rank-based matching and distribution-based matching strategies that complement each other. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LLP boosts the link prediction performance of MLPs with significant margins, and even outperforms the teacher GNNs on 7 out of 8 benchmarks. LLP also achieves a 70.68x speedup in link prediction inference compared to GNNs on the large-scale OGB dataset.

papers_seen.author: Walsh
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Core Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, KD enables the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP systems on resource-constrained devices without substantial accuracy loss. This approach addresses critical challenges in balancing model capacity with computational efficiency across diverse domains while supporting practical constraints such as privacy preservation and data scarcity. While KD is not a universal solution, when combined with complementary compression strategies and careful design choices, it represents the most practical and broadly applicable approach to achieving efficient neural networks suitable for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: A Multi-Strategy Prescription for Effective Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are most effective when treated as a multi-objective engineering problem rather than a single loss-matching task. Practical, robust compression for NLP and other deep models requires coordinated decisions about teacher construction, data and augmentation strategies, what to transfer (logits, features, or modules), and how to handle limited or absent training data. Combining dynamic multi-teacher selection, representation-level objectives, augmentation-aware distillation, and adversarial or meta-learned teacher paradigms yields students that retain more of the teacher's strengths while addressing common failure modes such as rare-token degradation and domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Morales
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Composable Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a versatile family of techniques that enable deployment of high-performing models in resource-constrained settings. By transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or synthesized data from a teacher to a student, KD reduces model size and inference cost while preserving much of a teacher’s functionality. KD is most effective when treated as a composable core operation—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, or task-specific alignment—and when its variants (data-free, online, teacher-free, or representation-based) are selected to match constraints such as data availability, privacy, or device heterogeneity. Despite strong empirical success, distillation has important failure modes arising from optimization difficulties and teacher–student misalignment; these warrant careful curriculum design, objective selection, and evaluation on task-specific failure cases. Overall, KD should be adopted as a foundational element of model-compression toolkits, used with explicit attention to its assumptions and limits.

papers_seen.author: Farrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for compressing large, complex neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from teacher to student models, this approach enables the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices and accelerates inference across diverse domains. Recent advances have expanded knowledge distillation beyond simple output matching to include intermediate representation alignment, data-free approaches, and integration with complementary compression methods, making it an essential methodology for practical machine learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: On Representation Knowledge Distillation for Graph Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a learning paradigm for boosting resource-efficient graph neural networks (GNNs) using more expressive yet cumbersome teacher models. Past work on distillation for GNNs proposed the Local Structure Preserving loss (LSP), which matches local structural relationships defined over edges across the student and teacher's node embeddings. This paper studies whether preserving the global topology of how the teacher embeds graph data can be a more effective distillation objective for GNNs, as real-world graphs often contain latent interactions and noisy edges. We propose Graph Contrastive Representation Distillation (G-CRD), which uses contrastive learning to implicitly preserve global topology by aligning the student node embeddings to those of the teacher in a shared representation space. Additionally, we introduce an expanded set of benchmarks on large-scale real-world datasets where the performance gap between teacher and student GNNs is non-negligible. Experiments across 4 datasets and 14 heterogeneous GNN architectures show that G-CRD consistently boosts the performance and robustness of lightweight GNNs, outperforming LSP (and a global structure preserving variant of LSP) as well as baselines from 2D computer vision. An analysis of the representational similarity among teacher and student embedding spaces reveals that G-CRD balances preserving local and global relationships, while structure preserving approaches are best at preserving one or the other. papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression and Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has matured from a single-purpose compression trick into a flexible framework that can compress models, transfer inductive biases, improve fairness and domain adaptability, and support continual learning across modalities. Its strengths come from multiple instantiations—logit matching, feature mimicking, contrastive representation alignment, module replacement, and automated search guided by distillation—which together make it broadly applicable for deploying high-performing models under resource constraints. At the same time, careful choice of distillation targets, mixture with hard labels, and awareness of teacher imperfections are key to realizing its benefits in practice.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical and Versatile Core Technique for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and essential technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, more deployable versions while maintaining task performance. By transferring knowledge from teacher models to student models through diverse mechanisms—including soft logits, intermediate representations, and feature-level alignment—KD enables efficient deployment across resource-constrained environments. When strategically combined with complementary techniques such as quantization, pruning, and data-free methods, KD provides robust solutions to real-world deployment challenges in both computer vision and natural language processing. However, KD is not universally applicable; optimization challenges and architectural mismatches require careful design and evaluation protocols to achieve consistent results.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: An Essential Strategy for Deploying Deep Learning and NLP Systems
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while transferring valuable learned knowledge. This approach enables the practical deployment of high-performing deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and machine translation. By transferring knowledge beyond simple class labels to encompass soft targets, intermediate representations, and structural behaviors, knowledge distillation addresses the critical challenge of balancing model capacity with computational efficiency while maintaining competitive performance.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context-Dependent Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated framework for producing compact models that preserve much of the performance of larger teachers. KD spans a range of mechanisms—from softened-output matching to intermediate-feature and layer-wise alignment—and can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. While KD often enables deployable students that approach teacher performance, success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to handle data availability or privacy constraints, and how to pair distillation with complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Zavala
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring task-relevant information. Across deep learning and NLP, KD encompasses output-level soft-label matching, feature- and layer-level supervision, architecture-aware procedures, and data-centric strategies (including pretraining and synthetic data). These techniques enable deployment in resource-constrained settings, often preserving much of a teacher’s performance while reducing latency, memory, and energy use. Practical success depends on choices about what teacher signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student components, whether to pretrain students, and how to handle limited or private data. Current advances broaden KD’s role beyond compression to include regularization, robustness, fairness-aware transfer, and privacy-preserving forms of model adaptation, while open challenges remain in principled selection of transfer targets, handling distribution shift, and automating task-adaptive compression.

papers_seen.author: Mckee
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable model-compression paradigm that transfers behavior from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce memory, latency, and compute while preserving task performance. Over the past decade KD has expanded beyond matching soft-output logits to include intermediate-feature and layer-level matching, multi-teacher and many-to-many mappings, data-free and privacy-aware approaches, and hybrid pipelines that combine distillation with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work shows distilled students can often approach teacher performance across vision, language, graph, and retrieval tasks, but practical success depends on choices about what is transferred, how teachers and students are matched, and how limited or private data are handled. Key open problems include principled teacher selection, coping with data heterogeneity or absence, robustness to rare phenomena and bias transfer, and tighter theoretical understanding of when distillation improves generalization.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as crucial techniques for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. These methods address the fundamental challenge of reducing model size, computational cost, and inference time while maintaining predictive performance. Across various domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and machine translation, researchers have developed diverse approaches to transfer knowledge from large teacher networks to smaller student networks, enabling efficient deployment without sacrificing quality.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Improved Accuracy in Spoken Question Answering
papers_seen.abstract: Spoken question answering (SQA) is a challenging task that requires the machine to fully understand the complex spoken documents. Automatic speech recognition (ASR) plays a significant role in the development of QA systems. However, the recent work shows that ASR systems generate highly noisy transcripts, which critically limit the capability of machine comprehension on the SQA task. To address the issue, we present a novel distillation framework. Specifically, we devise a training strategy to perform knowledge distillation (KD) from spoken documents and written counterparts. Our work makes a step towards distilling knowledge from the language model as a supervision signal to lead to better student accuracy by reducing the misalignment between automatic and manual transcriptions. Experiments demonstrate that our approach outperforms several state-of-the-art language models on the Spoken-SQuAD dataset.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Federated Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Distributed learning frameworks often rely on exchanging model parameters across workers, instead of revealing their raw data. A prime example is federated learning that exchanges the gradients or weights of each neural network model. Under limited communication resources, however, such a method becomes extremely costly particularly for modern deep neural networks having a huge number of model parameters. In this regard, federated distillation (FD) is a compelling distributed learning solution that only exchanges the model outputs whose dimensions are commonly much smaller than the model sizes (e.g., 10 labels in the MNIST dataset). The goal of this chapter is to provide a deep understanding of FD while demonstrating its communication efficiency and applicability to a variety of tasks. To this end, towards demystifying the operational principle of FD, the first part of this chapter provides a novel asymptotic analysis for two foundational algorithms of FD, namely knowledge distillation (KD) and co-distillation (CD), by exploiting the theory of neural tangent kernel (NTK). Next, the second part elaborates on a baseline implementation of FD for a classification task, and illustrates its performance in terms of accuracy and communication efficiency compared to FL. Lastly, to demonstrate the applicability of FD to various distributed learning tasks and environments, the third part presents two selected applications, namely FD over asymmetric uplink-and-downlink wireless channels and FD for reinforcement learning.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, enabling practical deployment of state-of-the-art neural networks in resource-constrained environments. This approach addresses critical challenges in deep learning and natural language processing by reducing computational costs, memory requirements, and latency while maintaining competitive performance. Beyond basic compression, knowledge distillation encompasses diverse strategies including soft-target matching, intermediate representation transfer, multi-teacher approaches, and task-aware adaptations that extend its applicability across vision, language processing, speech recognition, and other domains.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Tool for Compression, Generalization, and Responsible NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is more than a single recipe for shrinking models: it is a flexible framework that enables model compression, preserves or transfers useful behaviors (including inductive biases), supports domain adaptation and privacy-preserving deployment, and can be adapted to mitigate undesirable behaviors. Drawing on empirical and methodological work across NLP and other domains, KD should be considered a central technique for building smaller, faster models that retain or even improve important aspects of teacher behavior while meeting practical constraints.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and allied model-compression techniques provide practical ways to transfer predictive and representational knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models so compact systems can run under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. The literature shows a wide family of methods — matching softened logits, imitating intermediate features or attention, relational and task-specific mappings, self- and multi-teacher schemes, and data-side strategies such as augmentation, synthetic data, or pre-training compact architectures — that together enable strong trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy. Empirical successes span vision, speech, recommendation, and natural language tasks, but open issues remain, including teacher–student mismatch, robustness under distribution shift, limited or absent training data, and principled design of what to transfer for particular student capacities. Practical deployments benefit from combining complementary techniques (representation-level objectives, augmentation-aware distillation, pre-training of small models, and continual or task-adaptive strategies) and from careful tuning of teacher construction, data, and transfer objectives.

papers_seen.author: Chapman
papers_seen.title: Why Knowledge Distillation Should Be the Default Strategy for Deploying Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile strategy for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster models that retain most of the original performance. When combined with targeted techniques—multi-teacher distillation, feature- and attention-level objectives, domain-aware adaptation, self-distillation, and privacy- or federation-aware protocols—KD enables deployment under tight latency, memory, and privacy constraints while often improving robustness and generalization. Despite these successes, careful teacher-student design, data availability, and principled evaluation remain important open problems for reliable production use.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Versatile Core Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an adaptable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teacher performance. KD encompasses multiple families of techniques — soft-target matching, intermediate-representation matching, module replacement, online/peer distillation, and ensemble-to-single-model transfer — and has been applied successfully across NLP tasks (including large transformer compression and machine translation), graph and recommender systems, and large-scale distributed training. Realizing KD’s benefits in practice requires matching the distillation objective to student capacity and deployment constraints, choosing appropriate data or surrogate data strategies, and addressing interactions with training regularizers and teacher quality.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as crucial techniques for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. These methods address the fundamental challenge of reducing model size, computational cost, and inference time while maintaining predictive performance. Across various domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and machine translation, researchers have developed diverse approaches to transfer knowledge from large teacher networks to smaller student networks, enabling efficient deployment without sacrificing quality.

papers_seen.author: Mayo
papers_seen.title: Rethinking Soft Labels for Knowledge Distillation: A Bias-Variance Tradeoff Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective approach to leverage a well-trained network or an ensemble of them, named as the teacher, to guide the training of a student network. The outputs from the teacher network are used as soft labels for supervising the training of a new network. Recent studies \citep{muller2019does,yuan2020revisiting} revealed an intriguing property of the soft labels that making labels soft serves as a good regularization to the student network. From the perspective of statistical learning, regularization aims to reduce the variance, however how bias and variance change is not clear for training with soft labels. In this paper, we investigate the bias-variance tradeoff brought by distillation with soft labels. Specifically, we observe that during training the bias-variance tradeoff varies sample-wisely. Further, under the same distillation temperature setting, we observe that the distillation performance is negatively associated with the number of some specific samples, which are named as regularization samples since these samples lead to bias increasing and variance decreasing. Nevertheless, we empirically find that completely filtering out regularization samples also deteriorates distillation performance. Our discoveries inspired us to propose the novel weighted soft labels to help the network adaptively handle the sample-wise bias-variance tradeoff. Experiments on standard evaluation benchmarks validate the effectiveness of our method. Our code is available at \url{https://github.com/bellymonster/Weighted-Soft-Label-Distillation}.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lightweight student networks, KD enables practical deployment of sophisticated deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. The approach encompasses multiple methodologies including soft-target matching, feature-level imitation, and attention-based transfers, with applications spanning computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and specialized domains. While KD delivers substantial practical gains in model size, latency, and memory requirements, its effectiveness depends critically on careful design choices regarding what knowledge is transferred, data availability, teacher-student alignment, and task-specific optimization strategies.

papers_seen.author: Suarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Evidence, and Open Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses and adapts large teacher models into smaller, more deployable students by transferring predictive distributions, intermediate representations, or structural behavior. Across vision, language, speech, and graph domains, distillation variants enable latency- and memory-constrained deployment, improve transfer and robustness, and can be combined with architecture search or progressive module replacement to balance fidelity and efficiency. Practical success depends on choices about distillation targets, data availability (including data-free approaches), teacher–student capacity alignment, and task-aware training; these considerations frame ongoing research toward automated, privacy-aware, and domain-adaptive compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Compression, Transfer, and Robustification in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile technique that not only enables compressing large models into efficient students but also serves as a mechanism for domain adaptation, multi-task transfer, self-supervised representation transfer, and improved generalization. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can reproduce state-of-the-art performance with far fewer resources in NLP and vision, but success depends on design choices such as which teacher signals to transfer (logits, intermediate representations, or adversarial/support samples), how to align teacher and student layers, whether to select or weight training samples, and how to handle heterogeneous data sources. KD can be extended via multi-teacher, teacher-free, black-box, and adversarial formulations, yet practical limits remain under data heterogeneity and some optimization/regulatization interactions. Thoughtful integration of KD with layer mapping, sample selection, data augmentation, and domain-aware trust metrics yields the greatest practical benefit.

papers_seen.author: Pacheco
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Powerful Framework for Model Compression and Transfer Learning in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a highly effective approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This technique enables the transfer of knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, making it particularly valuable for deploying models in resource-constrained environments. The method has proven successful across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and multimodal learning. By leveraging various distillation strategies and loss functions, researchers have demonstrated that knowledge distillation can achieve substantial performance improvements and computational efficiency gains with minimal accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Walls
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and widely-adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while preserving much of the original performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, KD enables deployment on edge devices, addresses privacy and data-availability constraints, and facilitates knowledge transfer across architectures and modalities. This synthesis examines the core methods of knowledge distillation, key applications across domains, practical effectiveness, and important limitations and open challenges in the field.

papers_seen.author: Wise
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression methods create smaller, faster models by transferring useful information from large teacher networks to compact student networks. In practice, KD reduces inference latency and memory use while preserving much of teacher performance; it is implemented through a spectrum of techniques (soft-target matching, intermediate representation alignment, multi-teacher fusion, and data-side strategies) and is applied across domains from pretrained language models to domain adaptation and privacy-sensitive releases. Effectiveness depends on what signals are transferred, data available for distillation, alignment between teacher and student architectures, and deployment constraints; open challenges include robustness under distribution shift, few-shot or data-free distillation, principled teacher design for constrained students, and privacy-aware protocols.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Mitigating Gender Bias in Distilled Language Models via Counterfactual Role Reversal
papers_seen.abstract: Language models excel at generating coherent text, and model compression techniques such as knowledge distillation have enabled their use in resource-constrained settings. However, these models can be biased in multiple ways, including the unfounded association of male and female genders with gender-neutral professions. Therefore, knowledge distillation without any fairness constraints may preserve or exaggerate the teacher model's biases onto the distilled model. To this end, we present a novel approach to mitigate gender disparity in text generation by learning a fair model during knowledge distillation. We propose two modifications to the base knowledge distillation based on counterfactual role reversal$\unicode{x2014}$modifying teacher probabilities and augmenting the training set. We evaluate gender polarity across professions in open-ended text generated from the resulting distilled and finetuned GPT$\unicode{x2012}$2 models and demonstrate a substantial reduction in gender disparity with only a minor compromise in utility. Finally, we observe that language models that reduce gender polarity in language generation do not improve embedding fairness or downstream classification fairness.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: A Comprehensive Approach to Efficient Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for compressing deep neural networks and making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This approach transfers knowledge from larger, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, enabling significant reductions in model size and computational overhead while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation is particularly valuable across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and domain adaptation, where the trade-off between model complexity and practical deployment becomes increasingly important.

papers_seen.author: Waller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a model compression technique that enables the transfer of knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach has become increasingly essential for deploying state-of-the-art neural networks in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation encompasses a diverse set of theoretical and practical approaches, ranging from simple logit matching to sophisticated intermediate representation alignment and task-aware compression strategies. The technique has been successfully applied across multiple domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, speech recognition, and specialized applications such as recommendation systems and graph neural networks. By addressing critical deployment constraints such as latency, memory, computational cost, and privacy, knowledge distillation has emerged as a foundational technique in modern machine learning.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical and Necessary Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central framework for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from teachers to students. As deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy, heterogeneous devices) grow, KD’s flexibility — spanning soft-target matching, intermediate representation alignment, attention- and channel-wise transfer, multi-teacher schedules, and data-aware procedures — makes it uniquely suited to balance fidelity and efficiency. However, realizing KD’s promise in practice requires careful design choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student representations, and how to handle limited or private data. When combined with complementary compression techniques and representation-aware training practices, KD reliably produces compact models suitable for real-world NLP and multimodal systems.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: BAM! Born-Again Multi-Task Networks for Natural Language Understanding
papers_seen.abstract: It can be challenging to train multi-task neural networks that outperform or even match their single-task counterparts. To help address this, we propose using knowledge distillation where single-task models teach a multi-task model. We enhance this training with teacher annealing, a novel method that gradually transitions the model from distillation to supervised learning, helping the multi-task model surpass its single-task teachers. We evaluate our approach by multi-task fine-tuning BERT on the GLUE benchmark. Our method consistently improves over standard single-task and multi-task training.

papers_seen.author: Wheeler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Flexible Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a foundational technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while maintaining competitive performance. Rather than a single monolithic approach, KD functions best as a flexible, composable framework that can be adapted to specific task, data, and hardware constraints. When combined with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, and data-aware strategies, KD enables practical deployment of high-performing models on resource-constrained devices while addressing real-world challenges including privacy concerns, data unavailability, and computational limitations.

papers_seen.author: Silva
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Strategy for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and broadly applicable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while preserving predictive performance. By transferring knowledge from large teacher models to compact student networks, knowledge distillation enables efficient deployment across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and recommendation systems. This approach addresses critical practical constraints of modern machine learning by reducing storage requirements, computational costs, and inference latency, making sophisticated deep learning systems accessible for resource-constrained environments and real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Morales
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Composable Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a versatile family of techniques that enable deployment of high-performing models in resource-constrained settings. By transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or synthesized data from a teacher to a student, KD reduces model size and inference cost while preserving much of a teacher’s functionality. KD is most effective when treated as a composable core operation—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, or task-specific alignment—and when its variants (data-free, online, teacher-free, or representation-based) are selected to match constraints such as data availability, privacy, or device heterogeneity. Despite strong empirical success, distillation has important failure modes arising from optimization difficulties and teacher–student misalignment; these warrant careful curriculum design, objective selection, and evaluation on task-specific failure cases. Overall, KD should be adopted as a foundational element of model-compression toolkits, used with explicit attention to its assumptions and limits.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Collaborative Distillation for Ultra-Resolution Universal Style Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Universal style transfer methods typically leverage rich representations from deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models (e.g., VGG-19) pre-trained on large collections of images. Despite the effectiveness, its application is heavily constrained by the large model size to handle ultra-resolution images given limited memory. In this work, we present a new knowledge distillation method (named Collaborative Distillation) for encoder-decoder based neural style transfer to reduce the convolutional filters. The main idea is underpinned by a finding that the encoder-decoder pairs construct an exclusive collaborative relationship, which is regarded as a new kind of knowledge for style transfer models. Moreover, to overcome the feature size mismatch when applying collaborative distillation, a linear embedding loss is introduced to drive the student network to learn a linear embedding of the teacher's features. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness of our method when applied to different universal style transfer approaches (WCT and AdaIN), even if the model size is reduced by 15.5 times. Especially, on WCT with the compressed models, we achieve ultra-resolution (over 40 megapixels) universal style transfer on a 12GB GPU for the first time. Further experiments on optimization-based stylization scheme show the generality of our algorithm on different stylization paradigms. Our code and trained models are available at https://github.com/mingsun-tse/collaborative-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Explaining Knowledge Distillation by Quantifying the Knowledge
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a method to interpret the success of knowledge distillation by quantifying and analyzing task-relevant and task-irrelevant visual concepts that are encoded in intermediate layers of a deep neural network (DNN). More specifically, three hypotheses are proposed as follows. 1. Knowledge distillation makes the DNN learn more visual concepts than learning from raw data. 2. Knowledge distillation ensures that the DNN is prone to learning various visual concepts simultaneously. Whereas, in the scenario of learning from raw data, the DNN learns visual concepts sequentially. 3. Knowledge distillation yields more stable optimization directions than learning from raw data. Accordingly, we design three types of mathematical metrics to evaluate feature representations of the DNN. In experiments, we diagnosed various DNNs, and above hypotheses were verified.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: SEED: Self-supervised Distillation For Visual Representation
papers_seen.abstract: This paper is concerned with self-supervised learning for small models. The problem is motivated by our empirical studies that while the widely used contrastive self-supervised learning method has shown great progress on large model training, it does not work well for small models. To address this problem, we propose a new learning paradigm, named SElf-SupErvised Distillation (SEED), where we leverage a larger network (as Teacher) to transfer its representational knowledge into a smaller architecture (as Student) in a self-supervised fashion. Instead of directly learning from unlabeled data, we train a student encoder to mimic the similarity score distribution inferred by a teacher over a set of instances. We show that SEED dramatically boosts the performance of small networks on downstream tasks. Compared with self-supervised baselines, SEED improves the top-1 accuracy from 42.2% to 67.6% on EfficientNet-B0 and from 36.3% to 68.2% on MobileNet-v3-Large on the ImageNet-1k dataset.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical and Versatile Framework for Efficient Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a practical and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while preserving competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks, knowledge distillation enables the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. The technique encompasses multiple methodologies—including soft-target matching, feature mimicking, layer-wise alignment, and data-free synthesis—and has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and reinforcement learning. Recent research demonstrates that knowledge distillation is not merely a compression heuristic but a flexible toolkit that, when carefully designed and integrated with complementary techniques, can achieve student models that approach teacher performance while meeting practical deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: AutoGAN-Distiller: Searching to Compress Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: The compression of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has lately drawn attention, due to the increasing demand for deploying GANs into mobile devices for numerous applications such as image translation, enhancement and editing. However, compared to the substantial efforts to compressing other deep models, the research on compressing GANs (usually the generators) remains at its infancy stage. Existing GAN compression algorithms are limited to handling specific GAN architectures and losses. Inspired by the recent success of AutoML in deep compression, we introduce AutoML to GAN compression and develop an AutoGAN-Distiller (AGD) framework. Starting with a specifically designed efficient search space, AGD performs an end-to-end discovery for new efficient generators, given the target computational resource constraints. The search is guided by the original GAN model via knowledge distillation, therefore fulfilling the compression. AGD is fully automatic, standalone (i.e., needing no trained discriminators), and generically applicable to various GAN models. We evaluate AGD in two representative GAN tasks: image translation and super resolution. Without bells and whistles, AGD yields remarkably lightweight yet more competitive compressed models, that largely outperform existing alternatives. Our codes and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/TAMU-VITA/AGD.

papers_seen.author: Gaines
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression techniques enable the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning models in resource-constrained environments by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. These approaches have demonstrated significant success across diverse applications including natural language processing, computer vision, and speech processing, achieving substantial reductions in model size and computational cost while maintaining competitive accuracy levels. This synthesis explores the diverse methodologies, theoretical foundations, and practical applications of knowledge distillation and compression techniques in modern deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Alvarado
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while preserving performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to students, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices and reducing computational overhead. KD encompasses diverse methodologies including soft-target matching, feature-level mimicry, data-free approaches, and multi-teacher strategies, with applications spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks. The field continues to evolve with new insights into when and why distillation succeeds, addressing challenges such as data heterogeneity, privacy constraints, and the selection of appropriate student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Powell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Superior Approach to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile technique for compressing deep neural networks and transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models. Unlike traditional compression methods that simply reduce model parameters, knowledge distillation leverages teacher-student frameworks to transfer complex learned representations, enabling effective compression while maintaining or even improving model performance. This approach has been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks, making it essential for deploying high-performing models on resource-constrained devices.

papers_seen.author: Cherry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Task‑Aware Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable students while preserving predictive performance and enabling additional properties such as privacy, robustness, and fairness. When treated as a task-aware toolkit—combining soft-label matching, intermediate feature alignment, adversarial or generative data synthesis, and multi-teacher or curriculum strategies—KD can meet real-world deployment constraints (latency, memory, data access) across modalities. Practical success depends on explicit choices about what to transfer, how to generate or select distillation data, and how to align capacity and objectives between teacher and student; addressing these choices systematically enables KD to be both a compression engine and a mechanism for adapting models to constrained, private, or fairness-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer via Adversarial Belief Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Performing knowledge transfer from a large teacher network to a smaller student is a popular task in modern deep learning applications. However, due to growing dataset sizes and stricter privacy regulations, it is increasingly common not to have access to the data that was used to train the teacher. We propose a novel method which trains a student to match the predictions of its teacher without using any data or metadata. We achieve this by training an adversarial generator to search for images on which the student poorly matches the teacher, and then using them to train the student. Our resulting student closely approximates its teacher for simple datasets like SVHN, and on CIFAR10 we improve on the state-of-the-art for few-shot distillation (with 100 images per class), despite using no data. Finally, we also propose a metric to quantify the degree of belief matching between teacher and student in the vicinity of decision boundaries, and observe a significantly higher match between our zero-shot student and the teacher, than between a student distilled with real data and the teacher. Code available at: https://github.com/polo5/ZeroShotKnowledgeTransfer

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are essential techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models, enabling substantial reductions in model size, computational cost, and inference time while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and question answering. The techniques address fundamental practical challenges in making state-of-the-art models viable for real-world deployment with limited latency, memory, and energy budgets.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Critical Technique for Deep Learning Model Compression and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large deep learning models while maintaining performance. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student models, enabling efficient deployment across diverse applications. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents an essential strategy for addressing the trade-off between model complexity and practical deployment requirements in both computer vision and natural language processing domains.
