papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile but Context-Sensitive Tool for Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD has demonstrated practical value across vision, language, and other domains by reducing inference cost, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices, and supporting distributed or privacy-sensitive workflows. However, its effectiveness depends strongly on data availability, teacher–student capacity mismatch, domain and task specifics, and system constraints; thus KD should be applied as a composable element of a compression strategy rather than as a universal cure-all.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Unified Tool for Model Compression and Transfer in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is more than a single recipe for shrinking models: it is a flexible family of techniques that enables compression, privacy-preserving transfer, robustness under limited data, and improved task- or domain-specific performance. By transferring behavior or internal representations from high-capacity teachers to smaller students, KD enables deployment of performant models in constrained environments while enabling adaptations such as data-free distillation, task-adaptive compression, and architecture-aware transfers. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a primary engineering and research lever for model compression across modalities and tasks, and outlines practical variants that address common deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Adversarial Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) has made remarkable progress in the last few years and become a popular paradigm for model compression and knowledge transfer. However, almost all existing KD algorithms are data-driven, i.e., relying on a large amount of original training data or alternative data, which is usually unavailable in real-world scenarios. In this paper, we devote ourselves to this challenging problem and propose a novel adversarial distillation mechanism to craft a compact student model without any real-world data. We introduce a model discrepancy to quantificationally measure the difference between student and teacher models and construct an optimizable upper bound. In our work, the student and the teacher jointly act the role of the discriminator to reduce this discrepancy, when a generator adversarially produces some "hard samples" to enlarge it. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed data-free method yields comparable performance to existing data-driven methods. More strikingly, our approach can be directly extended to semantic segmentation, which is more complicated than classification, and our approach achieves state-of-the-art results. Code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/VainF/Data-Free-Adversarial-Distillation.

papers_seen.author: Bass
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Findings, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher networks into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations, enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. A rich set of techniques—logit/soft-target matching, feature and layer alignment, multi-teacher and online schemes, adversarial or decision-boundary guided samples, and data-free synthesis—has been developed to address different practical constraints. Empirical work shows substantial efficiency gains are possible, but success depends on choices of distilled targets, data availability, teacher quality, and training curricula; theoretical analyses provide partial explanations and suggest when soft or hard targets are preferable. Ongoing challenges include handling domain shift, low-frequency phenomena, distributed training, and principled student architecture selection.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Feature-map-level Online Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Feature maps contain rich information about image intensity and spatial correlation. However, previous online knowledge distillation methods only utilize the class probabilities. Thus in this paper, we propose an online knowledge distillation method that transfers not only the knowledge of the class probabilities but also that of the feature map using the adversarial training framework. We train multiple networks simultaneously by employing discriminators to distinguish the feature map distributions of different networks. Each network has its corresponding discriminator which discriminates the feature map from its own as fake while classifying that of the other network as real. By training a network to fool the corresponding discriminator, it can learn the other network's feature map distribution. We show that our method performs better than the conventional direct alignment method such as L1 and is more suitable for online distillation. Also, we propose a novel cyclic learning scheme for training more than two networks together. We have applied our method to various network architectures on the classification task and discovered a significant improvement of performance especially in the case of training a pair of a small network and a large one.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Comprehensive Framework for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and practical approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This technique enables the transfer of knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, making deployment in resource-constrained environments feasible without sacrificing accuracy. The method has proven successful across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and multimodal learning, offering substantial performance improvements and computational efficiency gains with minimal accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression methods form a broad set of techniques for transferring information from larger models (or ensembles) to smaller, faster, or more deployable models. Approaches range from using teacher soft labels to transfer logits, to aligning intermediate representations, to teacher-free and online schemes, and to task- or domain-aware compression for pretrained language models. Applications span image and object recognition, speech and spoken-language tasks, machine translation, continual/federated settings, and specialized domains where latency, memory, or privacy constraints are critical. Empirical work shows that carefully designed distillation—sometimes combined with data augmentation, representation alignment, or multi-teacher selection—can produce compact models that retain a large fraction of teacher performance while improving generalization, calibration, and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Distilling the Knowledge of BERT for Sequence-to-Sequence ASR
papers_seen.abstract: Attention-based sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) models have achieved promising results in automatic speech recognition (ASR). However, as these models decode in a left-to-right way, they do not have access to context on the right. We leverage both left and right context by applying BERT as an external language model to seq2seq ASR through knowledge distillation. In our proposed method, BERT generates soft labels to guide the training of seq2seq ASR. Furthermore, we leverage context beyond the current utterance as input to BERT. Experimental evaluations show that our method significantly improves the ASR performance from the seq2seq baseline on the Corpus of Spontaneous Japanese (CSJ). Knowledge distillation from BERT outperforms that from a transformer LM that only looks at left context. We also show the effectiveness of leveraging context beyond the current utterance. Our method outperforms other LM application approaches such as n-best rescoring and shallow fusion, while it does not require extra inference cost.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Cross-modal Knowledge Distillation for Vision-to-Sensor Action Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: Human activity recognition (HAR) based on multi-modal approach has been recently shown to improve the accuracy performance of HAR. However, restricted computational resources associated with wearable devices, i.e., smartwatch, failed to directly support such advanced methods. To tackle this issue, this study introduces an end-to-end Vision-to-Sensor Knowledge Distillation (VSKD) framework. In this VSKD framework, only time-series data, i.e., accelerometer data, is needed from wearable devices during the testing phase. Therefore, this framework will not only reduce the computational demands on edge devices, but also produce a learning model that closely matches the performance of the computational expensive multi-modal approach. In order to retain the local temporal relationship and facilitate visual deep learning models, we first convert time-series data to two-dimensional images by applying the Gramian Angular Field ( GAF) based encoding method. We adopted ResNet18 and multi-scale TRN with BN-Inception as teacher and student network in this study, respectively. A novel loss function, named Distance and Angle-wised Semantic Knowledge loss (DASK), is proposed to mitigate the modality variations between the vision and the sensor domain. Extensive experimental results on UTD-MHAD, MMAct, and Berkeley-MHAD datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and competitiveness of the proposed VSKD model which can deployed on wearable sensors.

papers_seen.author: Mayo
papers_seen.title: Rethinking Soft Labels for Knowledge Distillation: A Bias-Variance Tradeoff Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective approach to leverage a well-trained network or an ensemble of them, named as the teacher, to guide the training of a student network. The outputs from the teacher network are used as soft labels for supervising the training of a new network. Recent studies \citep{muller2019does,yuan2020revisiting} revealed an intriguing property of the soft labels that making labels soft serves as a good regularization to the student network. From the perspective of statistical learning, regularization aims to reduce the variance, however how bias and variance change is not clear for training with soft labels. In this paper, we investigate the bias-variance tradeoff brought by distillation with soft labels. Specifically, we observe that during training the bias-variance tradeoff varies sample-wisely. Further, under the same distillation temperature setting, we observe that the distillation performance is negatively associated with the number of some specific samples, which are named as regularization samples since these samples lead to bias increasing and variance decreasing. Nevertheless, we empirically find that completely filtering out regularization samples also deteriorates distillation performance. Our discoveries inspired us to propose the novel weighted soft labels to help the network adaptively handle the sample-wise bias-variance tradeoff. Experiments on standard evaluation benchmarks validate the effectiveness of our method. Our code is available at \url{https://github.com/bellymonster/Weighted-Soft-Label-Distillation}.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation in Deep Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation deals with the problem of training a smaller model (Student) from a high capacity source model (Teacher) so as to retain most of its performance. Existing approaches use either the training data or meta-data extracted from it in order to train the Student. However, accessing the dataset on which the Teacher has been trained may not always be feasible if the dataset is very large or it poses privacy or safety concerns (e.g., bio-metric or medical data). Hence, in this paper, we propose a novel data-free method to train the Student from the Teacher. Without even using any meta-data, we synthesize the Data Impressions from the complex Teacher model and utilize these as surrogates for the original training data samples to transfer its learning to Student via knowledge distillation. We, therefore, dub our method "Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation" and demonstrate that our framework results in competitive generalization performance as achieved by distillation using the actual training data samples on multiple benchmark datasets.

papers_seen.author: Kelley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Critical Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from complex teacher models to lightweight student networks, knowledge distillation addresses the critical challenge of deploying state-of-the-art deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices. This approach has proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications, enabling significant reductions in model size and computational cost with minimal accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Explaining Knowledge Distillation by Quantifying the Knowledge
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a method to interpret the success of knowledge distillation by quantifying and analyzing task-relevant and task-irrelevant visual concepts that are encoded in intermediate layers of a deep neural network (DNN). More specifically, three hypotheses are proposed as follows. 1. Knowledge distillation makes the DNN learn more visual concepts than learning from raw data. 2. Knowledge distillation ensures that the DNN is prone to learning various visual concepts simultaneously. Whereas, in the scenario of learning from raw data, the DNN learns visual concepts sequentially. 3. Knowledge distillation yields more stable optimization directions than learning from raw data. Accordingly, we design three types of mathematical metrics to evaluate feature representations of the DNN. In experiments, we diagnosed various DNNs, and above hypotheses were verified.

papers_seen.author: Allison
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large models into efficient students that retain much of the teacher’s performance. KD techniques—spanning logits-based soft-target transfer, intermediate feature alignment, and data-free synthesis—enable deployment of high-performing models on resource-constrained devices while also offering benefits in robustness and interpretability. When paired with task-aware design and careful teacher selection, distillation can produce compact models that meet real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints without large sacrifices in accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Shaffer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful paradigm for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and natural language processing. This survey synthesizes current approaches to distillation, covering compression of diverse architectures including transformers, vision models, and generative models. Key developments include data-free distillation methods, multi-teacher frameworks, and task-aware approaches. Applications span NLP tasks, computer vision, and specialized domains such as medical imaging and fake media detection. The field demonstrates that compact student models can achieve performance comparable to or exceeding their non-compressed counterparts while significantly reducing computational and memory requirements.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are fundamental techniques for enabling the deployment of large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, addressing the critical challenge of reducing model size while maintaining predictive performance. This review synthesizes recent advances in distillation techniques, compression methodologies, and their applications across various deep learning domains.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Does Knowledge Distillation Really Work?
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular technique for training a small student network to emulate a larger teacher model, such as an ensemble of networks. We show that while knowledge distillation can improve student generalization, it does not typically work as it is commonly understood: there often remains a surprisingly large discrepancy between the predictive distributions of the teacher and the student, even in cases when the student has the capacity to perfectly match the teacher. We identify difficulties in optimization as a key reason for why the student is unable to match the teacher. We also show how the details of the dataset used for distillation play a role in how closely the student matches the teacher -- and that more closely matching the teacher paradoxically does not always lead to better student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: Practical Strengths and Limits of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible framework for compressing large models into efficient students suitable for deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. When combined with complementary techniques—data augmentation, representation-level matching, online or collaborative training, and data-free strategies—KD yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance across vision and language tasks. However, achieving reliable gains requires task-aware choices about teacher signals, student capacity, and data availability; mismatches in inputs or internal structure and concerns about robustness and privacy remain important practical limitations.

papers_seen.author: Zuniga
papers_seen.title: Large scale distributed neural network training through online distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Techniques such as ensembling and distillation promise model quality improvements when paired with almost any base model. However, due to increased test-time cost (for ensembles) and increased complexity of the training pipeline (for distillation), these techniques are challenging to use in industrial settings. In this paper we explore a variant of distillation which is relatively straightforward to use as it does not require a complicated multi-stage setup or many new hyperparameters. Our first claim is that online distillation enables us to use extra parallelism to fit very large datasets about twice as fast. Crucially, we can still speed up training even after we have already reached the point at which additional parallelism provides no benefit for synchronous or asynchronous stochastic gradient descent. Two neural networks trained on disjoint subsets of the data can share knowledge by encouraging each model to agree with the predictions the other model would have made. These predictions can come from a stale version of the other model so they can be safely computed using weights that only rarely get transmitted. Our second claim is that online distillation is a cost-effective way to make the exact predictions of a model dramatically more reproducible. We support our claims using experiments on the Criteo Display Ad Challenge dataset, ImageNet, and the largest to-date dataset used for neural language modeling, containing $6\times 10^{11}$ tokens and based on the Common Crawl repository of web data.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Approaches
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques provide practical paths to deploy large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Recent work spans strategies that (1) compress by transferring softened outputs or intermediate representations from large teachers to smaller students, (2) pre-train compact architectures instead of only compressing post-hoc, (3) adapt distillation to task specifics (e.g., detection, generation, ranking), (4) enable distillation without access to original training data, and (5) combine KD with quantization, pruning, and data augmentation to improve robustness and efficiency. Empirical evidence shows that carefully designed distillation losses, data strategies, and teacher-student curricula can preserve much of teacher performance while greatly reducing model size, latency, and memory footprint. Practical trade-offs include the need for task-specific treatment (feature imitation, permutation-invariant alignment), sensitivity to the teacher’s training regime, and opportunities where teacher-free or self-distillation variants can match or exceed classic teacher-student pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge distillation from multi-modal to mono-modal segmentation networks
papers_seen.abstract: The joint use of multiple imaging modalities for medical image segmentation has been widely studied in recent years. The fusion of information from different modalities has demonstrated to improve the segmentation accuracy, with respect to mono-modal segmentations, in several applications. However, acquiring multiple modalities is usually not possible in a clinical setting due to a limited number of physicians and scanners, and to limit costs and scan time. Most of the time, only one modality is acquired. In this paper, we propose KD-Net, a framework to transfer knowledge from a trained multi-modal network (teacher) to a mono-modal one (student). The proposed method is an adaptation of the generalized distillation framework where the student network is trained on a subset (1 modality) of the teacher's inputs (n modalities). We illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in brain tumor segmentation with the BraTS 2018 dataset. Using different architectures, we show that the student network effectively learns from the teacher and always outperforms the baseline mono-modal network in terms of segmentation accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational, Multi-Strategy Approach for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most effective when treated not as a single algorithmic trick but as an engineering paradigm that integrates teacher design, student capacity, data strategy, representation objectives, and deployment constraints. When combined with complementary compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and deployment-aware practices (privacy, federated protocols, pre-training of small architectures), KD routinely enables compact models that meet latency, memory, and robustness requirements while preserving most of a teacher's performance. However, KD has limits: teacher–student mismatch, data heterogeneity in federated settings, and fairness or distribution-shift failures demand careful, task-aware design and evaluation. The practical position advocated here is that KD should be adopted as a core, configurable component of compression pipelines, with choice of techniques driven by operational constraints and empirical validation.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Techniques, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central and practical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while preserving performance across diverse applications. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments. KD encompasses multiple methodologies operating at different levels—from logits and feature maps to intermediate layer representations—and can be combined with complementary techniques such as quantization, pruning, and architecture search. While KD has proven effective across vision, language, and multimodal domains, successful implementation requires careful consideration of teacher-student alignment, data availability, optimization dynamics, and task-specific requirements.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers learned representations from complex teacher networks to simpler student networks, enabling efficient deployment of state-of-the-art models across diverse applications in deep learning and natural language processing. Beyond simple model compression, knowledge distillation facilitates knowledge transfer across different architectures, improves robustness, and supports learning from ensemble models. The technique has proven particularly valuable in addressing computational constraints that limit practical deployment while preserving the performance gains achieved through large-scale pre-training.

papers_seen.author: Mathis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression represent critical techniques for deploying state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, these approaches enable significant reductions in computational cost, memory requirements, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. This paper argues that knowledge distillation has evolved from a simple heuristic technique into a versatile, mature framework with diverse methodologies and broad applicability across computer vision, natural language processing, and multimodal learning domains. Success with knowledge distillation depends on careful matching of compression strategies to task-specific constraints and deployment requirements rather than reliance on a single universal approach.

papers_seen.author: Davidson
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large models into smaller, faster models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from a teacher to a student. Across vision, language, graph, generative, and neural-architecture-search settings, methods vary from matching soft labels to aligning intermediate features, using attention-based layer projection, contrastive alignment, and optimization-aware divergences. Practical adaptations address data availability, privacy, and efficiency constraints, while empirical and theoretical analyses reveal optimization limits, dataset and heterogeneity sensitivities, and opportunities from meta-learning teachers and task-specific design. Despite broad success, key open problems remain in reliably preserving teacher knowledge, designing data- and privacy-aware protocols, and tailoring distillation to domain-specific structures.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Practical and Principled Knowledge Distillation for Deep Models and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful family of techniques for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster, and often more interpretable models. When applied thoughtfully—matching architectures, choosing which teacher signals to transfer, and adapting to task- or data-specific properties—KD can preserve most of the teacher's performance while substantially reducing inference cost. However, indiscriminate application of distillation can harm performance (for example by overfitting to teacher errors or erasing useful data complexity); successful KD therefore combines algorithmic innovations (layer/feature matching, progressive replacement, adaptive search) with data-aware strategies (selective sample distillation, mixing raw and distilled data) and sometimes self-distillation to close remaining gaps.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Effectiveness, Methods, and Practical Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for training efficient student models by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models, with particular relevance to natural language processing and deep learning applications. This paper examines the evidence for the effectiveness of knowledge distillation approaches, explores various distillation methodologies including feature-based and adaptive approaches, and discusses practical applications in NLP tasks. While knowledge distillation consistently provides parameter reduction and computational efficiency, recent findings suggest the mechanism of improvement involves both direct knowledge transfer and regularization effects. The technique has proven effective across diverse domains including machine translation, neural language models, and transformer compression, though careful consideration of teacher selection, optimization strategies, and hyperparameter tuning remains essential for achieving optimal results.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: An Essential Strategy for Deploying Deep Learning and NLP Systems
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while transferring valuable learned knowledge. This approach enables the practical deployment of high-performing deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and machine translation. By transferring knowledge beyond simple class labels to encompass soft targets, intermediate representations, and structural behaviors, knowledge distillation addresses the critical challenge of balancing model capacity with computational efficiency while maintaining competitive performance.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and widely-adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, enabling practical deployment while maintaining competitive performance across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and machine translation. While knowledge distillation offers substantial practical benefits in reducing model size, computational cost, and inference latency, recent research reveals important limitations and nuances in how knowledge transfer occurs, and highlights the importance of careful design choices and methodical application rather than treating distillation as a universal solution.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models through various mechanisms, addressing the critical challenge of deploying state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices. The technique has proven effective across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and multimodal learning, making it an essential paradigm for practical deep learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Liu
papers_seen.title: Enabling Multimodal Generation on CLIP via Vision-Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The recent large-scale vision-language pre-training (VLP) of dual-stream architectures (e.g., CLIP) with a tremendous amount of image-text pair data, has shown its superiority on various multimodal alignment tasks. Despite its success, the resulting models are not capable of multimodal generative tasks due to the weak text encoder. To tackle this problem, we propose to augment the dual-stream VLP model with a textual pre-trained language model (PLM) via vision-language knowledge distillation (VLKD), enabling the capability for multimodal generation. VLKD is pretty data- and computation-efficient compared to the pre-training from scratch. Experimental results show that the resulting model has strong zero-shot performance on multimodal generation tasks, such as open-ended visual question answering and image captioning. For example, it achieves 44.5% zero-shot accuracy on the VQAv2 dataset, surpassing the previous state-of-the-art zero-shot model with $7\times$ fewer parameters. Furthermore, the original textual language understanding and generation ability of the PLM is maintained after VLKD, which makes our model versatile for both multimodal and unimodal tasks.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Efficient Transformer-based Large Scale Language Representations using Hardware-friendly Block Structured Pruning
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained large-scale language models have increasingly demonstrated high accuracy on many natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, the limited weight storage and computational speed on hardware platforms have impeded the popularity of pre-trained models, especially in the era of edge computing. In this work, we propose an efficient transformer-based large-scale language representation using hardware-friendly block structure pruning. We incorporate the reweighted group Lasso into block-structured pruning for optimization. Besides the significantly reduced weight storage and computation, the proposed approach achieves high compression rates. Experimental results on different models (BERT, RoBERTa, and DistilBERT) on the General Language Understanding Evaluation (GLUE) benchmark tasks show that we achieve up to 5.0x with zero or minor accuracy degradation on certain task(s). Our proposed method is also orthogonal to existing compact pre-trained language models such as DistilBERT using knowledge distillation, since a further 1.79x average compression rate can be achieved on top of DistilBERT with zero or minor accuracy degradation. It is suitable to deploy the final compressed model on resource-constrained edge devices.

papers_seen.author: Pham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are critical techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, these approaches enable significant reductions in model size and computational cost while maintaining competitive accuracy across diverse applications including computer vision, natural language processing, and machine translation. The field has evolved from basic teacher-student knowledge transfer to sophisticated multi-faceted approaches incorporating feature-level matching, data-free methods, and task-aware training protocols.

papers_seen.author: Mckay
papers_seen.title: MixKD: Towards Efficient Distillation of Large-scale Language Models
papers_seen.abstract: Large-scale language models have recently demonstrated impressive empirical performance. Nevertheless, the improved results are attained at the price of bigger models, more power consumption, and slower inference, which hinder their applicability to low-resource (both memory and computation) platforms. Knowledge distillation (KD) has been demonstrated as an effective framework for compressing such big models. However, large-scale neural network systems are prone to memorize training instances, and thus tend to make inconsistent predictions when the data distribution is altered slightly. Moreover, the student model has few opportunities to request useful information from the teacher model when there is limited task-specific data available. To address these issues, we propose MixKD, a data-agnostic distillation framework that leverages mixup, a simple yet efficient data augmentation approach, to endow the resulting model with stronger generalization ability. Concretely, in addition to the original training examples, the student model is encouraged to mimic the teacher's behavior on the linear interpolation of example pairs as well. We prove from a theoretical perspective that under reasonable conditions MixKD gives rise to a smaller gap between the generalization error and the empirical error. To verify its effectiveness, we conduct experiments on the GLUE benchmark, where MixKD consistently leads to significant gains over the standard KD training, and outperforms several competitive baselines. Experiments under a limited-data setting and ablation studies further demonstrate the advantages of the proposed approach.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression Across Modalities
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a flexible, domain-agnostic strategy that enables deployment of high-performing deep models in resource-constrained settings. By transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or distilled data between teacher and student, KD supports compression of generators, discriminative models, and multimodal systems, while enabling privacy-preserving and data-free workflows. When combined with careful pre-training, many-to-many layer alignment, or generative replay, KD allows compact architectures to approach the performance of large teachers and, in some cases, inherit desirable properties such as robustness or interpretability. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a foundational method in model compression toolkits and proposes practical emphases for future work: preserving internal representations, supporting data-free distillation, leveraging pre-training for small models, and distilling robustness.

papers_seen.author: Barnes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Extensions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques enable transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from large teacher models to smaller student models to meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, energy, privacy). Progress spans soft-target matching, representation- and layer-wise transfer, data-free and privacy-preserving approaches, and integration with pruning and architecture search. Effective distillation balances what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and whether or how to use original, augmented, or synthesized data; when combined with careful pre-training and hardware-aware compression, distilled students can approach teacher performance while meeting practical constraints.

papers_seen.author: Dudley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Strategy for Efficient Deep Learning: Enabling Practical Deployment of Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a crucial technique for model compression and efficient deployment of deep neural networks across diverse domains. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents a fundamentally important approach for reducing computational overhead and memory requirements of state-of-the-art neural models while maintaining competitive performance. Through systematic application in computer vision, natural language processing, and other domains, distillation has demonstrated remarkable effectiveness in creating compact student models that can operate within practical resource constraints. The technique's versatility, combined with its ability to achieve substantial efficiency gains with minimal accuracy loss, establishes it as an indispensable tool for the practical deployment of neural networks in resource-limited environments.

papers_seen.author: Jacobs
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational Technique for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a central and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from teacher models through various mechanisms—including soft logits, intermediate representations, and synthesized data—knowledge distillation addresses critical deployment challenges across deep learning and natural language processing. This technique represents a pragmatic solution for resource-constrained environments, offering substantial reductions in model size and inference latency without significant accuracy loss. However, realizing its full potential requires careful attention to optimization challenges, teacher-student alignment, and task-specific design considerations.

papers_seen.author: Higgins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that enables the efficient deployment of large neural networks by training smaller student models to mimic the behavior of larger teacher models. This approach has become fundamental across computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains, addressing the critical challenge of reducing computational overhead and memory requirements while maintaining competitive performance. The technique encompasses diverse strategies ranging from soft label guidance to intermediate layer alignment and operates through the transfer of learned knowledge from teacher to student networks.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: An Essential Strategy for Deploying Deep Learning and NLP Systems
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while transferring valuable learned knowledge. This approach enables the practical deployment of high-performing deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and machine translation. By transferring knowledge beyond simple class labels to encompass soft targets, intermediate representations, and structural behaviors, knowledge distillation addresses the critical challenge of balancing model capacity with computational efficiency while maintaining competitive performance.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Mitigating Gender Bias in Distilled Language Models via Counterfactual Role Reversal
papers_seen.abstract: Language models excel at generating coherent text, and model compression techniques such as knowledge distillation have enabled their use in resource-constrained settings. However, these models can be biased in multiple ways, including the unfounded association of male and female genders with gender-neutral professions. Therefore, knowledge distillation without any fairness constraints may preserve or exaggerate the teacher model's biases onto the distilled model. To this end, we present a novel approach to mitigate gender disparity in text generation by learning a fair model during knowledge distillation. We propose two modifications to the base knowledge distillation based on counterfactual role reversal$\unicode{x2014}$modifying teacher probabilities and augmenting the training set. We evaluate gender polarity across professions in open-ended text generated from the resulting distilled and finetuned GPT$\unicode{x2012}$2 models and demonstrate a substantial reduction in gender disparity with only a minor compromise in utility. Finally, we observe that language models that reduce gender polarity in language generation do not improve embedding fairness or downstream classification fairness.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: What Makes a "Good" Data Augmentation in Knowledge Distillation -- A Statistical Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a general neural network training approach that uses a teacher model to guide the student model. Existing works mainly study KD from the network output side (e.g., trying to design a better KD loss function), while few have attempted to understand it from the input side. Especially, its interplay with data augmentation (DA) has not been well understood. In this paper, we ask: Why do some DA schemes (e.g., CutMix) inherently perform much better than others in KD? What makes a "good" DA in KD? Our investigation from a statistical perspective suggests that a good DA scheme should reduce the covariance of the teacher-student cross-entropy. A practical metric, the stddev of teacher's mean probability (T. stddev), is further presented and well justified empirically. Besides the theoretical understanding, we also introduce a new entropy-based data-mixing DA scheme, CutMixPick, to further enhance CutMix. Extensive empirical studies support our claims and demonstrate how we can harvest considerable performance gains simply by using a better DA scheme in knowledge distillation.

papers_seen.author: Maddox
papers_seen.title: BERT-EMD: Many-to-Many Layer Mapping for BERT Compression with Earth Mover's Distance
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained language models (e.g., BERT) have achieved significant success in various natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, high storage and computational costs obstruct pre-trained language models to be effectively deployed on resource-constrained devices. In this paper, we propose a novel BERT distillation method based on many-to-many layer mapping, which allows each intermediate student layer to learn from any intermediate teacher layers. In this way, our model can learn from different teacher layers adaptively for various NLP tasks. %motivated by the intuition that different NLP tasks require different levels of linguistic knowledge contained in the intermediate layers of BERT. In addition, we leverage Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) to compute the minimum cumulative cost that must be paid to transform knowledge from teacher network to student network. EMD enables the effective matching for many-to-many layer mapping. %EMD can be applied to network layers with different sizes and effectively measures semantic distance between the teacher network and student network. Furthermore, we propose a cost attention mechanism to learn the layer weights used in EMD automatically, which is supposed to further improve the model's performance and accelerate convergence time. Extensive experiments on GLUE benchmark demonstrate that our model achieves competitive performance compared to strong competitors in terms of both accuracy and model compression.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Findings, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal knowledge from teacher networks. Across computer vision, NLP, speech, and generative modeling, distillation methods have evolved from matching soft logits to aligning intermediate representations and adapting layer mappings for heterogeneous architectures. Practical results show large reductions in parameter counts and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance, but challenges remain in robustness, student-friendly teacher design, and reliably transferring rarer or structural knowledge.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while preserving performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation encompasses multiple methodologies operating at different levels—from logits and feature maps to intermediate layer representations—and can be combined with complementary techniques such as quantization, pruning, and architecture search. The technique has proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and multimodal learning, with successful implementation requiring careful consideration of teacher-student alignment, data availability, optimization dynamics, and task-specific requirements.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers learned representations from complex teacher networks to simpler student networks, enabling efficient deployment of state-of-the-art models across diverse applications in deep learning and natural language processing. Beyond simple model compression, knowledge distillation facilitates knowledge transfer across different architectures, improves robustness, and supports learning from ensemble models. The technique has proven particularly valuable in addressing computational constraints that limit practical deployment while preserving the performance gains achieved through large-scale pre-training.

papers_seen.author: Larson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical Approach to Deploying Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Systems
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing. By transferring knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, knowledge distillation enables the deployment of sophisticated neural networks on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive performance. This approach has proven effective across multiple domains and has evolved beyond basic teacher-student frameworks to encompass diverse methodologies including feature-level distillation, multi-teacher selection, zero-shot learning, and adversarial sample selection. Despite challenges in optimization and teacher-student capacity mismatches, knowledge distillation remains essential for practical deployment scenarios requiring efficient inference without substantial accuracy degradation.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach enables the deployment of state-of-the-art neural networks in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. KD has evolved significantly beyond simple logit matching to encompass diverse techniques including intermediate representation matching, layer-wise alignment, multi-teacher training, data-free approaches, and task-adaptive architecture search. The technique is now widely applied across multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, graph neural networks, and generative tasks, addressing critical challenges in bridging the gap between model performance and practical deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Davenport
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Paradigm for Model Compression and Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to smaller student models, knowledge distillation addresses the critical challenge of deploying state-of-the-art deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains. This approach extends beyond basic model compression to enable practical deployment scenarios, privacy-preserving learning, and knowledge transfer across heterogeneous architectures. The technique has proven effective across natural language processing, computer vision, graph neural networks, and multimodal learning, establishing it as an indispensable tool for modern deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques have matured into a diverse set of theoretical and practical approaches for producing smaller, faster, or more specialized models from larger ones. Work in this area ranges from formal analyses of when and why distillation helps, to engineering advances that reduce runtime cost, enable training without original data, transfer across modalities, improve robustness and privacy, and tailor distilled models for downstream tasks or heterogeneous deployment environments. Practical methods include mimicking logits, matching intermediate representations or attention, progressively replacing modules, using student-focused filtering of teacher signals, and leveraging data augmentation or online collaboration between models. Emerging directions emphasize theoretical understanding, task-aware selection of distilled information, privacy-preserving or data-free pipelines, and retaining adversarial robustness while reducing model size.

papers_seen.author: Fletcher
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Composable, but Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. KD provides a flexible toolkit—matching logits, aligning features or intermediate layers, ensembling teachers, and integrating with pruning/quantization—that often yields strong accuracy/efficiency trade-offs for vision, NLP, and other domains. However, KD’s effectiveness depends on data availability, teacher-student capacity alignment, optimization dynamics, and the potential transfer of teacher biases; addressing these requires task-aware design, careful augmentation or data synthesis, and privacy-preserving or multi-teacher protocols when needed.

papers_seen.author: Valdez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has evolved from a single training recipe into a versatile set of techniques that enable deployment of large neural models under constraints of compute, latency, privacy, and heterogeneity. When combined with complementary strategies such as architecture search, progressive compression, and task-aware signal selection, distillation routinely produces compact models that retain much of teacher performance across modalities and tasks. Practical success depends on choosing distillation variants that match deployment needs and on designing teacher–student pairs and objectives that transfer the right internal and output signals.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are fundamental techniques for enabling the deployment of large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, addressing the critical challenge of reducing model size while maintaining predictive performance. This review synthesizes recent advances in distillation techniques, compression methodologies, and their applications across various deep learning domains.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from a larger teacher model to a smaller student model, enabling efficient deployment of neural networks while maintaining competitive performance. This technique has become increasingly important across various domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications. The approach addresses the critical challenge of deploying complex, high-performing deep learning models on resource-constrained devices by enabling smaller models to achieve comparable results to their larger counterparts.

papers_seen.author: Bass
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Findings, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher networks into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations, enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. A rich set of techniques—logit/soft-target matching, feature and layer alignment, multi-teacher and online schemes, adversarial or decision-boundary guided samples, and data-free synthesis—has been developed to address different practical constraints. Empirical work shows substantial efficiency gains are possible, but success depends on choices of distilled targets, data availability, teacher quality, and training curricula; theoretical analyses provide partial explanations and suggest when soft or hard targets are preferable. Ongoing challenges include handling domain shift, low-frequency phenomena, distributed training, and principled student architecture selection.

papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Object DGCNN: 3D Object Detection using Dynamic Graphs
papers_seen.abstract: 3D object detection often involves complicated training and testing pipelines, which require substantial domain knowledge about individual datasets. Inspired by recent non-maximum suppression-free 2D object detection models, we propose a 3D object detection architecture on point clouds. Our method models 3D object detection as message passing on a dynamic graph, generalizing the DGCNN framework to predict a set of objects. In our construction, we remove the necessity of post-processing via object confidence aggregation or non-maximum suppression. To facilitate object detection from sparse point clouds, we also propose a set-to-set distillation approach customized to 3D detection. This approach aligns the outputs of the teacher model and the student model in a permutation-invariant fashion, significantly simplifying knowledge distillation for the 3D detection task. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on autonomous driving benchmarks. We also provide abundant analysis of the detection model and distillation framework.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer via Adversarial Belief Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Performing knowledge transfer from a large teacher network to a smaller student is a popular task in modern deep learning applications. However, due to growing dataset sizes and stricter privacy regulations, it is increasingly common not to have access to the data that was used to train the teacher. We propose a novel method which trains a student to match the predictions of its teacher without using any data or metadata. We achieve this by training an adversarial generator to search for images on which the student poorly matches the teacher, and then using them to train the student. Our resulting student closely approximates its teacher for simple datasets like SVHN, and on CIFAR10 we improve on the state-of-the-art for few-shot distillation (with 100 images per class), despite using no data. Finally, we also propose a metric to quantify the degree of belief matching between teacher and student in the vicinity of decision boundaries, and observe a significantly higher match between our zero-shot student and the teacher, than between a student distilled with real data and the teacher. Code available at: https://github.com/polo5/ZeroShotKnowledgeTransfer

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Compression of Deep Learning Models for Text: A Survey
papers_seen.abstract: In recent years, the fields of natural language processing (NLP) and information retrieval (IR) have made tremendous progress thanksto deep learning models like Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTMs)networks, and Transformer [120] based models like Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) [24], GenerativePre-training Transformer (GPT-2) [94], Multi-task Deep Neural Network (MT-DNN) [73], Extra-Long Network (XLNet) [134], Text-to-text transfer transformer (T5) [95], T-NLG [98] and GShard [63]. But these models are humongous in size. On the other hand,real world applications demand small model size, low response times and low computational power wattage. In this survey, wediscuss six different types of methods (Pruning, Quantization, Knowledge Distillation, Parameter Sharing, Tensor Decomposition, andSub-quadratic Transformer based methods) for compression of such models to enable their deployment in real industry NLP projects.Given the critical need of building applications with efficient and small models, and the large amount of recently published work inthis area, we believe that this survey organizes the plethora of work done by the 'deep learning for NLP' community in the past fewyears and presents it as a coherent story.

papers_seen.author: Mayo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that trains a small student model to mimic a large teacher model, enabling efficient deployment without sacrificing performance. This approach has become increasingly important across various domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, offering significant speedup and reduced computational requirements while maintaining competitive accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Knowledge Distillation for CTR Prediction
papers_seen.abstract: Recently, deep learning-based models have been widely studied for click-through rate (CTR) prediction and lead to improved prediction accuracy in many industrial applications. However, current research focuses primarily on building complex network architectures to better capture sophisticated feature interactions and dynamic user behaviors. The increased model complexity may slow down online inference and hinder its adoption in real-time applications. Instead, our work targets at a new model training strategy based on knowledge distillation (KD). KD is a teacher-student learning framework to transfer knowledge learned from a teacher model to a student model. The KD strategy not only allows us to simplify the student model as a vanilla DNN model but also achieves significant accuracy improvements over the state-of-the-art teacher models. The benefits thus motivate us to further explore the use of a powerful ensemble of teachers for more accurate student model training. We also propose some novel techniques to facilitate ensembled CTR prediction, including teacher gating and early stopping by distillation loss. We conduct comprehensive experiments against 12 existing models and across three industrial datasets. Both offline and online A/B testing results show the effectiveness of our KD-based training strategy.

papers_seen.author: Mcclain
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation from Internal Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is typically conducted by training a small model (the student) to mimic a large and cumbersome model (the teacher). The idea is to compress the knowledge from the teacher by using its output probabilities as soft-labels to optimize the student. However, when the teacher is considerably large, there is no guarantee that the internal knowledge of the teacher will be transferred into the student; even if the student closely matches the soft-labels, its internal representations may be considerably different. This internal mismatch can undermine the generalization capabilities originally intended to be transferred from the teacher to the student. In this paper, we propose to distill the internal representations of a large model such as BERT into a simplified version of it. We formulate two ways to distill such representations and various algorithms to conduct the distillation. We experiment with datasets from the GLUE benchmark and consistently show that adding knowledge distillation from internal representations is a more powerful method than only using soft-label distillation.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: A Multi-Strategy Prescription for Effective Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are most effective when treated as a multi-objective engineering problem rather than a single loss-matching task. Practical, robust compression for NLP and other deep models requires coordinated decisions about teacher construction, data and augmentation strategies, what to transfer (logits, features, or modules), and how to handle limited or absent training data. Combining dynamic multi-teacher selection, representation-level objectives, augmentation-aware distillation, and adversarial or meta-learned teacher paradigms yields students that retain more of the teacher's strengths while addressing common failure modes such as rare-token degradation and domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a practical, flexible set of techniques that enable deploying compact models while retaining much of the performance of larger teachers. When applied with attention to what is distilled (logits versus internal representations), how teachers and students are matched, and how scarce or private data are handled, KD routinely produces deployable models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a universal remedy: teacher–student capacity mismatches, data limitations, optimization dynamics, and task-specific phenomena (e.g., low-frequency tokens) can limit or bias results. A principled KD pipeline—layer-aware representation transfer, data-aware augmentation or synthesis, multi-source supervision, and careful evaluation on rare phenomena and fairness—yields the best practical outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Transferring Knowledge for Efficient Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining performance. This approach transfers knowledge from a larger teacher model to a smaller student model, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices. Model compression through distillation has proven effective across diverse applications including natural language processing, computer vision, and multimodal learning. This paper surveys the principles, methods, and applications of knowledge distillation and related compression techniques in deep learning.
