papers_seen.author: Figueroa
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a set of methods that compress large, high-performing neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. Across modalities and tasks, distillation operates as a flexible toolkit—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations or attentions, and adapting training data or objectives—to achieve favorable tradeoffs between model size, latency, and performance. Practical deployments combine KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture changes) and task-aware design choices. While KD routinely yields strong size–performance gains, its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, the choice of distilled targets, data and augmentation strategies, and attention to distributional and low-frequency phenomena; these factors also expose open problems in representation alignment, robustness, and principled teacher design.

papers_seen.author: Silva
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Strategy for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and broadly applicable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while preserving predictive performance. By transferring knowledge from large teacher models to compact student networks, knowledge distillation enables efficient deployment across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and recommendation systems. This approach addresses critical practical constraints of modern machine learning by reducing storage requirements, computational costs, and inference latency, making sophisticated deep learning systems accessible for resource-constrained environments and real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation in Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Since deep learning became a key player in natural language processing (NLP), many deep learning models have been showing remarkable performances in a variety of NLP tasks, and in some cases, they are even outperforming humans. Such high performance can be explained by efficient knowledge representation of deep learning models. While many methods have been proposed to learn more efficient representation, knowledge distillation from pretrained deep networks suggest that we can use more information from the soft target probability to train other neural networks. In this paper, we propose a new knowledge distillation method self-knowledge distillation, based on the soft target probabilities of the training model itself, where multimode information is distilled from the word embedding space right below the softmax layer. Due to the time complexity, our method approximates the soft target probabilities. In experiments, we applied the proposed method to two different and fundamental NLP tasks: language model and neural machine translation. The experiment results show that our proposed method improves performance on the tasks.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Rejuvenating Low-Frequency Words: Making the Most of Parallel Data in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly used to construct synthetic data for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models. However, there exists a discrepancy on low-frequency words between the distilled and the original data, leading to more errors on predicting low-frequency words. To alleviate the problem, we directly expose the raw data into NAT by leveraging pretraining. By analyzing directed alignments, we found that KD makes low-frequency source words aligned with targets more deterministically but fails to align sufficient low-frequency words from target to source. Accordingly, we propose reverse KD to rejuvenate more alignments for low-frequency target words. To make the most of authentic and synthetic data, we combine these complementary approaches as a new training strategy for further boosting NAT performance. We conduct experiments on five translation benchmarks over two advanced architectures. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach can significantly and universally improve translation quality by reducing translation errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach achieves 28.2 and 33.9 BLEU points on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets, respectively. Our code, data, and trained models are available at \url{https://github.com/alphadl/RLFW-NAT}.

papers_seen.author: Mckay
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-adopted model compression technique that trains a smaller student model to mimic the behavior of a larger teacher model. This approach enables the deployment of high-performing deep learning models on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive accuracy. Knowledge distillation has been applied across multiple domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and speech recognition, with variants adapted to different architectures and specific tasks.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical and Necessary Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central framework for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from teachers to students. As deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy, heterogeneous devices) grow, KD’s flexibility — spanning soft-target matching, intermediate representation alignment, attention- and channel-wise transfer, multi-teacher schedules, and data-aware procedures — makes it uniquely suited to balance fidelity and efficiency. However, realizing KD’s promise in practice requires careful design choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student representations, and how to handle limited or private data. When combined with complementary compression techniques and representation-aware training practices, KD reliably produces compact models suitable for real-world NLP and multimodal systems.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Cross-modal Knowledge Distillation for Vision-to-Sensor Action Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: Human activity recognition (HAR) based on multi-modal approach has been recently shown to improve the accuracy performance of HAR. However, restricted computational resources associated with wearable devices, i.e., smartwatch, failed to directly support such advanced methods. To tackle this issue, this study introduces an end-to-end Vision-to-Sensor Knowledge Distillation (VSKD) framework. In this VSKD framework, only time-series data, i.e., accelerometer data, is needed from wearable devices during the testing phase. Therefore, this framework will not only reduce the computational demands on edge devices, but also produce a learning model that closely matches the performance of the computational expensive multi-modal approach. In order to retain the local temporal relationship and facilitate visual deep learning models, we first convert time-series data to two-dimensional images by applying the Gramian Angular Field ( GAF) based encoding method. We adopted ResNet18 and multi-scale TRN with BN-Inception as teacher and student network in this study, respectively. A novel loss function, named Distance and Angle-wised Semantic Knowledge loss (DASK), is proposed to mitigate the modality variations between the vision and the sensor domain. Extensive experimental results on UTD-MHAD, MMAct, and Berkeley-MHAD datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and competitiveness of the proposed VSKD model which can deployed on wearable sensors.

papers_seen.author: Walton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Imperfect Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely adopted approach to compress high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students for deployment in resource-constrained settings. Empirical results show KD can preserve much of a teacher's performance across vision, speech, and language tasks and supports many variants (e.g., feature matching, ensemble transfer, self-distillation, and data-free strategies). At the same time, KD is not a panacea: optimization difficulties, teacher–student mismatch, and data availability introduce limits that require methodical choices (what to transfer, how to train, and when to synthesize or curate data). Careful design—combining representation-level objectives, architecture-aware mapping, multi-teacher or adversarial schemes, and federated or zero-shot adaptations—yields the best practical trade-offs for accuracy, cost, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Knowledge Distillation for CTR Prediction
papers_seen.abstract: Recently, deep learning-based models have been widely studied for click-through rate (CTR) prediction and lead to improved prediction accuracy in many industrial applications. However, current research focuses primarily on building complex network architectures to better capture sophisticated feature interactions and dynamic user behaviors. The increased model complexity may slow down online inference and hinder its adoption in real-time applications. Instead, our work targets at a new model training strategy based on knowledge distillation (KD). KD is a teacher-student learning framework to transfer knowledge learned from a teacher model to a student model. The KD strategy not only allows us to simplify the student model as a vanilla DNN model but also achieves significant accuracy improvements over the state-of-the-art teacher models. The benefits thus motivate us to further explore the use of a powerful ensemble of teachers for more accurate student model training. We also propose some novel techniques to facilitate ensembled CTR prediction, including teacher gating and early stopping by distillation loss. We conduct comprehensive experiments against 12 existing models and across three industrial datasets. Both offline and online A/B testing results show the effectiveness of our KD-based training strategy.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Current Approaches and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and natural language processing. By training smaller student models to learn from larger teacher models, distillation enables the development of efficient yet accurate neural networks suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices. This synthesis examines the current landscape of knowledge distillation methods, their theoretical foundations, and diverse applications across computer vision, NLP, and specialized domains.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from teacher models. Across vision, language, graph, and generative settings, distillation methods range from matching softened logits to aligning intermediate features, using data-centric strategies (e.g., synthetic data or teacher-generated targets), selective sample weighting, and meta-learning of teacher behaviors. Distillation functions both as a compression tool and as a mechanism for regularization, domain adaptation, and privacy-aware transfer; however, practical success depends on teacher quality, data availability and complexity, optimization dynamics, and careful choice of distillation targets and sample selection. Domain-specific adaptations (e.g., for non-autoregressive translation, machine reading comprehension, and graph neural networks) show significant gains but highlight open problems in reliably preserving rare/low-frequency phenomena and in formalizing when distillation is most effective.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Towards Understanding Ensemble, Knowledge Distillation and Self-Distillation in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We formally study how ensemble of deep learning models can improve test accuracy, and how the superior performance of ensemble can be distilled into a single model using knowledge distillation. We consider the challenging case where the ensemble is simply an average of the outputs of a few independently trained neural networks with the SAME architecture, trained using the SAME algorithm on the SAME data set, and they only differ by the random seeds used in the initialization.   We show that ensemble/knowledge distillation in Deep Learning works very differently from traditional learning theory (such as boosting or NTKs, neural tangent kernels). To properly understand them, we develop a theory showing that when data has a structure we refer to as ``multi-view'', then ensemble of independently trained neural networks can provably improve test accuracy, and such superior test accuracy can also be provably distilled into a single model by training a single model to match the output of the ensemble instead of the true label. Our result sheds light on how ensemble works in deep learning in a way that is completely different from traditional theorems, and how the ``dark knowledge'' is hidden in the outputs of the ensemble and can be used in distillation. In the end, we prove that self-distillation can also be viewed as implicitly combining ensemble and knowledge distillation to improve test accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Mcclain
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: Powerful, Practical, but Not a Panacea
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a core technique for compressing large models, transferring knowledge across architectures, enabling private or federated workflows, and improving efficiency for deployment in resource-constrained settings. While KD often yields substantial practical gains—reducing model size and inference cost with limited loss in performance—it has important theoretical and empirical limitations related to optimization, data dependence, model and domain heterogeneity, and teacher–student mismatch. A pragmatic stance recognizes KD as a versatile toolset whose effectiveness depends on how it is applied: the choice of distilled targets (logits, features, or relations), the availability or synthesis of data, the use of multiple teachers or staged procedures, and awareness of when distillation can harm or help generalization. This paper argues that KD should be used as part of a broader compression and adaptation strategy guided by empirical diagnostics and appropriate extensions (multi-teacher, zero-shot/data-free, federated/distilled protocols, or self-supervised distillation) rather than as an off-the-shelf cure-all.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central strategy for compressing large neural models into compact students that retain much of the teachers' performance. KD encompasses a family of techniques—matching softened logits, intermediate representations, attention maps, or synthesized data—that are applicable across modalities (vision, language, multimodal, graphs, and generative models). Practical KD workflows combine careful teacher selection, layer or token alignment, pre-training for the student, and complementary compression techniques (e.g., pruning or structured sparsity). While KD routinely yields favorable size–performance tradeoffs in production settings, its effectiveness depends on optimization choices, data availability, and mitigation of undesirable transferred behavior (bias, overconfidence, low-frequency errors). Current directions emphasize preserving internal representations, enabling data-free or privacy-preserving distillation, and carrying forward robustness and interpretability from teachers to students.

papers_seen.author: Aguilar
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical and Versatile Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential and widely-adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while preserving much of their performance. The approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students through multiple complementary mechanisms, enabling efficient inference and reduced computational requirements across diverse domains. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents a core practical strategy for model compression, supported by diverse methodologies, empirical validation across multiple applications, and a growing body of research addressing both effectiveness and limitations.

papers_seen.author: Alvarado
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while preserving performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to students, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices and reducing computational overhead. KD encompasses diverse methodologies including soft-target matching, feature-level mimicry, data-free approaches, and multi-teacher strategies, with applications spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks. The field continues to evolve with new insights into when and why distillation succeeds, addressing challenges such as data heterogeneity, privacy constraints, and the selection of appropriate student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Farmer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Advancing Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Systems
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining or even improving performance. This approach involves transferring knowledge from a large teacher model to a compact student model, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices without sacrificing accuracy. While the foundational concept has been widely applied across computer vision, recommender systems, and natural language processing, recent advances have introduced sophisticated variations and domain-specific adaptations. This paper provides a comprehensive overview of knowledge distillation methodologies, including selective distillation approaches, cross-modal knowledge transfer, adversarial learning frameworks, and specialized applications to transformer-based architectures and sequential tasks.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Efficient and Robust Deep Models in NLP and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a heuristic into a versatile, practical toolkit for compressing and adapting large deep models. Properly applied, KD preserves or even improves predictive quality while reducing model size, latency, and communication cost, and it can be extended to meet constraints such as limited data, device precision, and privacy. However, the benefits depend critically on what is distilled (outputs versus internal representations), how teachers and students are matched, and which training samples or modalities are used. I argue KD should be a core method in any deployment-oriented deep learning pipeline, combined with representation-level objectives, selective example strategies, and privacy- or communication-aware protocols.

papers_seen.author: Liu
papers_seen.title: Enabling Multimodal Generation on CLIP via Vision-Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The recent large-scale vision-language pre-training (VLP) of dual-stream architectures (e.g., CLIP) with a tremendous amount of image-text pair data, has shown its superiority on various multimodal alignment tasks. Despite its success, the resulting models are not capable of multimodal generative tasks due to the weak text encoder. To tackle this problem, we propose to augment the dual-stream VLP model with a textual pre-trained language model (PLM) via vision-language knowledge distillation (VLKD), enabling the capability for multimodal generation. VLKD is pretty data- and computation-efficient compared to the pre-training from scratch. Experimental results show that the resulting model has strong zero-shot performance on multimodal generation tasks, such as open-ended visual question answering and image captioning. For example, it achieves 44.5% zero-shot accuracy on the VQAv2 dataset, surpassing the previous state-of-the-art zero-shot model with $7\times$ fewer parameters. Furthermore, the original textual language understanding and generation ability of the PLM is maintained after VLKD, which makes our model versatile for both multimodal and unimodal tasks.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical and Versatile Framework for Efficient Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a practical and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while preserving competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks, knowledge distillation enables the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. The technique encompasses multiple methodologies—including soft-target matching, feature mimicking, layer-wise alignment, and data-free synthesis—and has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and reinforcement learning. Recent research demonstrates that knowledge distillation is not merely a compression heuristic but a flexible toolkit that, when carefully designed and integrated with complementary techniques, can achieve student models that approach teacher performance while meeting practical deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation with Progressive Refinement of Targets
papers_seen.abstract: The generalization capability of deep neural networks has been substantially improved by applying a wide spectrum of regularization methods, e.g., restricting function space, injecting randomness during training, augmenting data, etc. In this work, we propose a simple yet effective regularization method named progressive self-knowledge distillation (PS-KD), which progressively distills a model's own knowledge to soften hard targets (i.e., one-hot vectors) during training. Hence, it can be interpreted within a framework of knowledge distillation as a student becomes a teacher itself. Specifically, targets are adjusted adaptively by combining the ground-truth and past predictions from the model itself. We show that PS-KD provides an effect of hard example mining by rescaling gradients according to difficulty in classifying examples. The proposed method is applicable to any supervised learning tasks with hard targets and can be easily combined with existing regularization methods to further enhance the generalization performance. Furthermore, it is confirmed that PS-KD achieves not only better accuracy, but also provides high quality of confidence estimates in terms of calibration as well as ordinal ranking. Extensive experimental results on three different tasks, image classification, object detection, and machine translation, demonstrate that our method consistently improves the performance of the state-of-the-art baselines. The code is available at https://github.com/lgcnsai/PS-KD-Pytorch.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Compressing GANs using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been used in several machine learning tasks such as domain transfer, super resolution, and synthetic data generation. State-of-the-art GANs often use tens of millions of parameters, making them expensive to deploy for applications in low SWAP (size, weight, and power) hardware, such as mobile devices, and for applications with real time capabilities. There has been no work found to reduce the number of parameters used in GANs. Therefore, we propose a method to compress GANs using knowledge distillation techniques, in which a smaller "student" GAN learns to mimic a larger "teacher" GAN. We show that the distillation methods used on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Celeb-A datasets can compress teacher GANs at ratios of 1669:1, 58:1, and 87:1, respectively, while retaining the quality of the generated image. From our experiments, we observe a qualitative limit for GAN's compression. Moreover, we observe that, with a fixed parameter budget, compressed GANs outperform GANs trained using standard training methods. We conjecture that this is partially owing to the optimization landscape of over-parameterized GANs which allows efficient training using alternating gradient descent. Thus, training an over-parameterized GAN followed by our proposed compression scheme provides a high quality generative model with a small number of parameters.

papers_seen.author: Schultz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Methods, Applications, and Practical Constraints
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger teacher models into smaller student models to reduce model size, latency, and resource use while preserving task performance. Distillation mechanisms include transferring softened output distributions, matching intermediate representations, ensembling or online teacher strategies, and data- or task-aware adaptations. KD has been applied across domains — from recommendation and ranking to object detection, non-autoregressive machine translation, and federated settings — and is often combined with complementary compression methods. Its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, the choice of distilled targets, student capacity, and the match between training data and deployment conditions; these dependencies motivate pragmatic design choices and ongoing research into robust, data-efficient, and privacy-aware distillation pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Critical Technique for Deep Learning Model Compression and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large deep learning models while maintaining performance. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student models, enabling efficient deployment across diverse applications. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents an essential strategy for addressing the trade-off between model complexity and practical deployment requirements in both computer vision and natural language processing domains.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Adversarial Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) has made remarkable progress in the last few years and become a popular paradigm for model compression and knowledge transfer. However, almost all existing KD algorithms are data-driven, i.e., relying on a large amount of original training data or alternative data, which is usually unavailable in real-world scenarios. In this paper, we devote ourselves to this challenging problem and propose a novel adversarial distillation mechanism to craft a compact student model without any real-world data. We introduce a model discrepancy to quantificationally measure the difference between student and teacher models and construct an optimizable upper bound. In our work, the student and the teacher jointly act the role of the discriminator to reduce this discrepancy, when a generator adversarially produces some "hard samples" to enlarge it. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed data-free method yields comparable performance to existing data-driven methods. More strikingly, our approach can be directly extended to semantic segmentation, which is more complicated than classification, and our approach achieves state-of-the-art results. Code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/VainF/Data-Free-Adversarial-Distillation.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Deploying Deep Learning Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for enabling the deployment of large, powerful deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, these methods address the fundamental challenge of making state-of-the-art models practical for real-world applications that require fast inference and limited computational resources.

papers_seen.author: Mitchell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, Applications, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models by transferring information beyond hard labels. A mature toolkit now includes soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, multi-stage and multi-teacher pipelines, data-free or synthesized-data strategies, and privacy-aware variants. Distillation has been applied to vision, language, graphs, generative models, and healthcare, producing substantial inference and deployment gains while exposing limits arising from optimization, teacher–student mismatch, and data constraints. Progress requires carefully matching the distilled signals to student capacity, combining distillation with complementary compression methods, and addressing theoretical and practical failure modes to ensure robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Flynn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Critical Strategy for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential technique for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments by transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach enables substantial reductions in model size, computational cost, and inference latency while maintaining competitive predictive performance. While knowledge distillation is not a universal solution, when carefully combined with complementary strategies such as representation-level transfer, task-specific optimization, and data-aware techniques, it becomes an indispensable tool for bringing state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP models into practical systems across diverse domains.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: A Comprehensive Approach to Efficient Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for compressing deep neural networks and making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This approach transfers knowledge from larger, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, enabling significant reductions in model size and computational overhead while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation is particularly valuable across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and domain adaptation, where the trade-off between model complexity and practical deployment becomes increasingly important.

papers_seen.author: Ortiz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, enabling deployment across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and graph neural networks. Beyond basic model compression, knowledge distillation encompasses multiple methodologies including soft target matching, feature-level mimicking, intermediate representation alignment, and multi-teacher pipelines. While the technique addresses critical practical challenges such as reducing computational cost, latency, memory consumption, and enabling privacy-preserving deployment, significant challenges remain in principled teacher-student design, handling data scarcity, and understanding when distillation enhances generalization.

papers_seen.author: Mueller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Effective Strategies for Deploying Deep Learning Models in Resource-Constrained Environments
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and practical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices and edge computing systems. By leveraging various distillation methodologies—from soft target matching to feature-level alignment—this technique addresses fundamental challenges in deep learning deployment without sacrificing model capability. Knowledge distillation has proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and graph neural networks, making it a foundational technique in modern machine learning.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Graph-less Neural Networks: Teaching Old MLPs New Tricks via Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are popular for graph machine learning and have shown great results on wide node classification tasks. Yet, they are less popular for practical deployments in the industry owing to their scalability challenges incurred by data dependency. Namely, GNN inference depends on neighbor nodes multiple hops away from the target, and fetching them burdens latency-constrained applications. Existing inference acceleration methods like pruning and quantization can speed up GNNs by reducing Multiplication-and-ACcumulation (MAC) operations, but the improvements are limited given the data dependency is not resolved. Conversely, multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) have no graph dependency and infer much faster than GNNs, even though they are less accurate than GNNs for node classification in general. Motivated by these complementary strengths and weaknesses, we bring GNNs and MLPs together via knowledge distillation (KD). Our work shows that the performance of MLPs can be improved by large margins with GNN KD. We call the distilled MLPs Graph-less Neural Networks (GLNNs) as they have no inference graph dependency. We show that GLNNs with competitive accuracy infer faster than GNNs by 146X-273X and faster than other acceleration methods by 14X-27X. Under a production setting involving both transductive and inductive predictions across 7 datasets, GLNN accuracies improve over stand-alone MLPs by 12.36% on average and match GNNs on 6/7 datasets. Comprehensive analysis shows when and why GLNNs can achieve competitive accuracies to GNNs and suggests GLNN as a handy choice for latency-constrained applications.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Comprehensive Framework for Efficient Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying deep neural networks efficiently across diverse applications. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student networks while maintaining performance. This survey examines the fundamental principles, applications, and recent advances in knowledge distillation across multiple domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized tasks. The techniques address critical challenges in model deployment including computational efficiency, memory constraints, and privacy preservation while maintaining state-of-the-art performance levels.

papers_seen.author: Santana
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from large teacher models to compact student models, addressing the critical challenge of deploying state-of-the-art deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices. The technique encompasses diverse methodologies spanning logits-based distillation, feature and intermediate-layer matching, data-free approaches, multi-teacher strategies, and task-aware compression methods. Knowledge distillation has proven effective across multiple domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and specialized applications, making it an essential methodology for practical deep learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from larger, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, efficient student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. The literature frames KD as a flexible toolbox rather than a single recipe: approaches include transferring output soft-labels, aligning intermediate representations or attention, using multi-teacher schedules, and combining distillation with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical work shows these choices — what to transfer, how to align student and teacher, and which data or augmentations to use — substantially affect whether a student approaches teacher performance. KD has been adapted across classification, sequence modeling, translation, retrieval, recommender systems, generative models, and many NLP tasks, with ongoing challenges around data-free distillation, representation alignment, and robustness in low-resource or privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Practical Paths and Limits for Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) remains a central technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while preserving performance. KD has evolved from simple logit matching to diverse strategies that address data availability, task specificity, representation-level transfer, and architectural mismatches. However, fundamental limits—especially under heterogeneous data or federated settings—and practical challenges such as selecting useful teacher signal and coping with student capacity remain. A pragmatic approach combines data-aware or data-free sample generation, representation- and layer-level objectives, and task-aware filtering to maximize transfer while respecting privacy, compute, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Byrd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical Tool for Model Compression: Strengths, Mechanisms, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. KD methods—ranging from soft-target matching to representation-level imitation, self-distillation, and adversarial teacher–student games—enable substantial efficiency gains while often improving generalization. However, distillation's benefits depend on careful design choices (what signals to transfer, how to align layers, and how to handle data or privacy constraints) and it is not a universal panacea: issues such as teacher–student mismatch, scarce or unavailable data, and task-specific optimization barriers require specialized strategies and evaluation. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a flexible, composable framework that is essential for practical compression but must be applied with task-aware techniques and awareness of its limitations.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity models into smaller, faster students by transferring information from a teacher model. Across vision, speech, and language tasks, distillation techniques reduce inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance, enable deployment on resource-constrained devices, and can address privacy or data-sharing constraints. Approaches vary from matching teacher soft outputs to imitating internal representations, to multi-teacher schemes and data-free synthesis. Recent work also investigates the theory of when and why distillation helps and how to combine distillation with complementary compression methods such as pruning. Practical guidelines emphasize handling imperfect teachers, balancing hard and soft labels, and adapting algorithms to the application domain (e.g., non-autoregressive translation or question answering). Open challenges remain in data-free distillation, robust multi-teacher fusion, and principled trade-offs between bias and variance introduced by softened supervision.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Practical and Principled Knowledge Distillation for Deep Models and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful family of techniques for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster, and often more interpretable models. When applied thoughtfully—matching architectures, choosing which teacher signals to transfer, and adapting to task- or data-specific properties—KD can preserve most of the teacher's performance while substantially reducing inference cost. However, indiscriminate application of distillation can harm performance (for example by overfitting to teacher errors or erasing useful data complexity); successful KD therefore combines algorithmic innovations (layer/feature matching, progressive replacement, adaptive search) with data-aware strategies (selective sample distillation, mixing raw and distilled data) and sometimes self-distillation to close remaining gaps.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential, Practical, and Context-Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practically effective technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. KD methods—ranging from logit-level supervision and feature/attention imitation to ensemble, multi-teacher, and data-free variants—have enabled real-world gains in latency, memory, and cross-device applicability across NLP, vision, speech, and graph tasks. At the same time, KD’s benefits depend on careful design choices (what to transfer, how to generate or select data, and how to match teacher and student capacity), and there are empirical and theoretical limitations that counsel a measured, diagnostic-driven application rather than blind deployment. This paper argues that KD is an essential component of modern model-compression toolkits but not a panacea: its success requires method selection, data or metadata strategies, and complementary techniques to manage trade-offs in accuracy, robustness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Mason
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Empirical Findings, and Practical Tradeoffs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques have become central to making large deep models—especially pretrained language models—practical for resource-constrained deployment and domain-specific use. Work in this area spans teacher-student soft-label distillation, architectural compression and replacement, layer-mapping strategies, data-free and robustness-aware procedures, and combinations with low-precision arithmetic. Empirical results demonstrate substantial reductions in size and latency while often preserving most task performance, but practical challenges remain around teacher–student mismatch, domain shift, access to original training data, adversarial robustness, and choosing task-specific compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Approaches
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques provide practical paths to deploy large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Recent work spans strategies that (1) compress by transferring softened outputs or intermediate representations from large teachers to smaller students, (2) pre-train compact architectures instead of only compressing post-hoc, (3) adapt distillation to task specifics (e.g., detection, generation, ranking), (4) enable distillation without access to original training data, and (5) combine KD with quantization, pruning, and data augmentation to improve robustness and efficiency. Empirical evidence shows that carefully designed distillation losses, data strategies, and teacher-student curricula can preserve much of teacher performance while greatly reducing model size, latency, and memory footprint. Practical trade-offs include the need for task-specific treatment (feature imitation, permutation-invariant alignment), sensitivity to the teacher’s training regime, and opportunities where teacher-free or self-distillation variants can match or exceed classic teacher-student pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and NLP. By training a lightweight student network to mimic a larger, well-trained teacher network, this approach enables the deployment of high-performance models on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive accuracy. Knowledge distillation operates through the transfer of soft targets and intermediate representations from teacher to student networks, providing implicit regularization and accelerating convergence. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, machine translation, information retrieval, and speech processing, offering substantial reductions in model size and computational cost with minimal performance degradation.

papers_seen.author: Le
papers_seen.title: VPN++: Rethinking Video-Pose embeddings for understanding Activities of Daily Living
papers_seen.abstract: Many attempts have been made towards combining RGB and 3D poses for the recognition of Activities of Daily Living (ADL). ADL may look very similar and often necessitate to model fine-grained details to distinguish them. Because the recent 3D ConvNets are too rigid to capture the subtle visual patterns across an action, this research direction is dominated by methods combining RGB and 3D Poses. But the cost of computing 3D poses from RGB stream is high in the absence of appropriate sensors. This limits the usage of aforementioned approaches in real-world applications requiring low latency. Then, how to best take advantage of 3D Poses for recognizing ADL? To this end, we propose an extension of a pose driven attention mechanism: Video-Pose Network (VPN), exploring two distinct directions. One is to transfer the Pose knowledge into RGB through a feature-level distillation and the other towards mimicking pose driven attention through an attention-level distillation. Finally, these two approaches are integrated into a single model, we call VPN++. We show that VPN++ is not only effective but also provides a high speed up and high resilience to noisy Poses. VPN++, with or without 3D Poses, outperforms the representative baselines on 4 public datasets. Code is available at https://github.com/srijandas07/vpnplusplus.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Understanding Knowledge Distillation in Non-autoregressive Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Non-autoregressive machine translation (NAT) systems predict a sequence of output tokens in parallel, achieving substantial improvements in generation speed compared to autoregressive models. Existing NAT models usually rely on the technique of knowledge distillation, which creates the training data from a pretrained autoregressive model for better performance. Knowledge distillation is empirically useful, leading to large gains in accuracy for NAT models, but the reason for this success has, as of yet, been unclear. In this paper, we first design systematic experiments to investigate why knowledge distillation is crucial to NAT training. We find that knowledge distillation can reduce the complexity of data sets and help NAT to model the variations in the output data. Furthermore, a strong correlation is observed between the capacity of an NAT model and the optimal complexity of the distilled data for the best translation quality. Based on these findings, we further propose several approaches that can alter the complexity of data sets to improve the performance of NAT models. We achieve the state-of-the-art performance for the NAT-based models, and close the gap with the autoregressive baseline on WMT14 En-De benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Morales
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Composable Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a versatile family of techniques that enable deployment of high-performing models in resource-constrained settings. By transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or synthesized data from a teacher to a student, KD reduces model size and inference cost while preserving much of a teacher’s functionality. KD is most effective when treated as a composable core operation—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, or task-specific alignment—and when its variants (data-free, online, teacher-free, or representation-based) are selected to match constraints such as data availability, privacy, or device heterogeneity. Despite strong empirical success, distillation has important failure modes arising from optimization difficulties and teacher–student misalignment; these warrant careful curriculum design, objective selection, and evaluation on task-specific failure cases. Overall, KD should be adopted as a foundational element of model-compression toolkits, used with explicit attention to its assumptions and limits.

papers_seen.author: Walls
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and widely-adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while preserving much of the original performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, KD enables deployment on edge devices, addresses privacy and data-availability constraints, and facilitates knowledge transfer across architectures and modalities. This synthesis examines the core methods of knowledge distillation, key applications across domains, practical effectiveness, and important limitations and open challenges in the field.

papers_seen.author: Tran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Theory, and Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for compressing large neural networks into smaller models that preserve predictive performance and desirable properties of the teacher. KD encompasses soft-label supervision, intermediate-feature matching, layer-wise alignment, multi-teacher fusion, online co-training, and teacher-free/self-distillation, and it is applied across modalities (vision, language, generation, recommendation) to meet deployment constraints such as latency, memory, low-precision arithmetic, privacy, and domain shift. Successful distillation requires task-aware choices of what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, how to generate or select data for transfer, and how to combine objectives to trade off fidelity and generalization. Remaining challenges include principled selection of distilled signals, data-free and privacy-preserving workflows, robustness under domain shift, and automated, task-adaptive compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-adopted technique for compressing neural networks by transferring knowledge from a larger teacher model to a smaller student model. This approach enables the development of efficient models with reduced parameters and computational requirements while maintaining high performance across various domains including computer vision and natural language processing. The field has evolved to encompass diverse methodologies, from basic logit matching to advanced layer-wise and feature-level distillation approaches, with applications spanning machine translation, question answering, sentiment analysis, and multi-modal learning.

papers_seen.author: Estes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical, Task-Aware Imperative for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques are indispensable for deploying modern deep learning models in resource-constrained settings. By transferring soft-targets, intermediate representations, or other distilled signals from larger teacher models to compact students, KD preserves much of the teacher’s performance while reducing inference cost, memory footprint, and latency. Effective distillation is not a single algorithm but a family of methods that must be chosen and tuned with respect to task requirements, student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints; when combined with complementary compression strategies, KD enables real-world use of powerful models across vision, language, and multimodal domains.

papers_seen.author: Silva
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as fundamental techniques for deploying large neural networks on resource-constrained devices while maintaining predictive performance. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, these approaches address critical challenges in inference speed, memory consumption, and computational resource requirements. The techniques have been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, and specialized applications, enabling practical deployment of sophisticated deep learning systems in real-world environments with limited computational resources.

papers_seen.author: Cameron
papers_seen.title: Well-Read Students Learn Better: On the Importance of Pre-training Compact Models
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in natural language representations have been accompanied by large and expensive models that leverage vast amounts of general-domain text through self-supervised pre-training. Due to the cost of applying such models to down-stream tasks, several model compression techniques on pre-trained language representations have been proposed (Sun et al., 2019; Sanh, 2019). However, surprisingly, the simple baseline of just pre-training and fine-tuning compact models has been overlooked. In this paper, we first show that pre-training remains important in the context of smaller architectures, and fine-tuning pre-trained compact models can be competitive to more elaborate methods proposed in concurrent work. Starting with pre-trained compact models, we then explore transferring task knowledge from large fine-tuned models through standard knowledge distillation. The resulting simple, yet effective and general algorithm, Pre-trained Distillation, brings further improvements. Through extensive experiments, we more generally explore the interaction between pre-training and distillation under two variables that have been under-studied: model size and properties of unlabeled task data. One surprising observation is that they have a compound effect even when sequentially applied on the same data. To accelerate future research, we will make our 24 pre-trained miniature BERT models publicly available.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Unified Tool for Model Compression and Transfer in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is more than a single recipe for shrinking models: it is a flexible family of techniques that enables compression, privacy-preserving transfer, robustness under limited data, and improved task- or domain-specific performance. By transferring behavior or internal representations from high-capacity teachers to smaller students, KD enables deployment of performant models in constrained environments while enabling adaptations such as data-free distillation, task-adaptive compression, and architecture-aware transfers. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a primary engineering and research lever for model compression across modalities and tasks, and outlines practical variants that address common deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while maintaining competitive performance. Rather than a monolithic approach, knowledge distillation represents a flexible family of methods that transfer various forms of knowledge—from output distributions to intermediate representations—from teacher to student models. This technique enables the deployment of state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices and addresses critical challenges in reducing computational costs, latency, and memory requirements without significant accuracy loss. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, speech recognition, and federated learning settings.

papers_seen.author: Humphrey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Deploying Deep Learning Models in Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile technique for compressing deep neural networks and improving their practical deployability. By enabling smaller "student" networks to learn from larger "teacher" models, knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in deploying deep learning systems across diverse domains and hardware constraints. This approach achieves significant model compression ratios while maintaining or even improving performance, making it invaluable for applications requiring efficient inference, interpretability, and resource-constrained deployment. The technique extends beyond simple model compression to encompass diverse applications including natural language processing, computer vision, reinforcement learning, and federated learning, demonstrating its fundamental importance in modern machine learning practice.

papers_seen.author: Kidd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential, Task-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, efficient students suitable for deployment in resource-constrained settings. When applied thoughtfully—selecting which teacher signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student representations, and adapting procedures to task and data constraints—KD can preserve most of a teacher's performance while dramatically reducing model size and inference cost. However, its effectiveness depends on design choices (targets, intermediate supervision, data selection) and on awareness of task-specific failure modes; KD is powerful but not universally automatic, and it should be integrated with complementary compression and adaptation techniques to achieve reliable, production-ready results.
