papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Findings, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal knowledge from teacher networks. Across computer vision, NLP, speech, and generative modeling, distillation methods have evolved from matching soft logits to aligning intermediate representations and adapting layer mappings for heterogeneous architectures. Practical results show large reductions in parameter counts and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance, but challenges remain in robustness, student-friendly teacher design, and reliably transferring rarer or structural knowledge.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Distilling portable Generative Adversarial Networks for Image Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been widely used in various image-to-image translation tasks, they can be hardly applied on mobile devices due to their heavy computation and storage cost. Traditional network compression methods focus on visually recognition tasks, but never deal with generation tasks. Inspired by knowledge distillation, a student generator of fewer parameters is trained by inheriting the low-level and high-level information from the original heavy teacher generator. To promote the capability of student generator, we include a student discriminator to measure the distances between real images, and images generated by student and teacher generators. An adversarial learning process is therefore established to optimize student generator and student discriminator. Qualitative and quantitative analysis by conducting experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method can learn portable generative models with strong performance.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Practical Paths and Limits for Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) remains a central technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while preserving performance. KD has evolved from simple logit matching to diverse strategies that address data availability, task specificity, representation-level transfer, and architectural mismatches. However, fundamental limits—especially under heterogeneous data or federated settings—and practical challenges such as selecting useful teacher signal and coping with student capacity remain. A pragmatic approach combines data-aware or data-free sample generation, representation- and layer-level objectives, and task-aware filtering to maximize transfer while respecting privacy, compute, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Pena
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practical family of methods for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information from a high-capacity teacher to a compact student using a range of signals (soft logits, intermediate representations, layer-wise supervision, or synthesized data). Across vision and language tasks, KD enables substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance, and it composes effectively with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical success requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to handle limited or private data, and how to evaluate robustness and rare-case behavior.

papers_seen.author: Jacobs
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational Technique for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a central and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from teacher models through various mechanisms—including soft logits, intermediate representations, and synthesized data—knowledge distillation addresses critical deployment challenges across deep learning and natural language processing. This technique represents a pragmatic solution for resource-constrained environments, offering substantial reductions in model size and inference latency without significant accuracy loss. However, realizing its full potential requires careful attention to optimization challenges, teacher-student alignment, and task-specific design considerations.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: The Case for Responsible, Task-Adaptive Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an indispensable tool for compressing large neural models into compact, deployable students. When combined with representation transfer, architecture search, and data-aware synthesis, KD enables substantial reductions in latency and memory while retaining much of the teacher's performance. However, distillation must be applied carefully: mismatches between teacher and student internals, scarce or private training data, and distributional or low-frequency phenomena can limit gains or introduce undesirable artifacts. I argue that KD should be treated as a system-level design choice that pairs multi-objective distillation objectives with task-adaptive student architectures and privacy- or robustness-aware synthesis methods to realize reliable, production-ready compression.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and NLP. This approach involves training a lightweight student network to mimic a more powerful teacher network, enabling the creation of efficient models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and multimodal learning, addressing the challenge of maintaining high performance while significantly reducing computational requirements and model size.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) trains compact student models to mimic larger teacher models to reduce size, latency, and resource use while retaining much of the teacher's performance. KD encompasses several transfer mechanisms (soft-target/logit transfer, intermediate feature and layer matching, attention-based mapping, and data- or model-aware curricula) and extensions (ensemble distillation, data-free or privacy-preserving workflows, and adversarial sample selection). Applied widely in NLP (including compressing large pretrained transformers), computer vision, and multimodal systems, KD is most effective when combined with complementary techniques—task-aware layer alignment, careful teacher selection or ensembling, and data strategies—to meet deployment constraints. Remaining open problems include principled choices of transfer targets, robustness under domain and data heterogeneity, and automated, task-adaptive compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: BERT-of-Theseus: Compressing BERT by Progressive Module Replacing
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel model compression approach to effectively compress BERT by progressive module replacing. Our approach first divides the original BERT into several modules and builds their compact substitutes. Then, we randomly replace the original modules with their substitutes to train the compact modules to mimic the behavior of the original modules. We progressively increase the probability of replacement through the training. In this way, our approach brings a deeper level of interaction between the original and compact models. Compared to the previous knowledge distillation approaches for BERT compression, our approach does not introduce any additional loss function. Our approach outperforms existing knowledge distillation approaches on GLUE benchmark, showing a new perspective of model compression.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Graph-less Neural Networks: Teaching Old MLPs New Tricks via Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are popular for graph machine learning and have shown great results on wide node classification tasks. Yet, they are less popular for practical deployments in the industry owing to their scalability challenges incurred by data dependency. Namely, GNN inference depends on neighbor nodes multiple hops away from the target, and fetching them burdens latency-constrained applications. Existing inference acceleration methods like pruning and quantization can speed up GNNs by reducing Multiplication-and-ACcumulation (MAC) operations, but the improvements are limited given the data dependency is not resolved. Conversely, multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) have no graph dependency and infer much faster than GNNs, even though they are less accurate than GNNs for node classification in general. Motivated by these complementary strengths and weaknesses, we bring GNNs and MLPs together via knowledge distillation (KD). Our work shows that the performance of MLPs can be improved by large margins with GNN KD. We call the distilled MLPs Graph-less Neural Networks (GLNNs) as they have no inference graph dependency. We show that GLNNs with competitive accuracy infer faster than GNNs by 146X-273X and faster than other acceleration methods by 14X-27X. Under a production setting involving both transductive and inductive predictions across 7 datasets, GLNN accuracies improve over stand-alone MLPs by 12.36% on average and match GNNs on 6/7 datasets. Comprehensive analysis shows when and why GLNNs can achieve competitive accuracies to GNNs and suggests GLNN as a handy choice for latency-constrained applications.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Evidence, and Practical Guidelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring information beyond hard labels. KD encompasses multiple mechanisms (soft targets, feature imitation, contrastive alignment, multi-teacher pipelines, and data distillation) and is effective across domains including NLP, machine translation, recommendation, and graph and multimodal models. When combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture replacement), KD enables deployment on resource-constrained hardware while largely preserving performance. Success hinges on choices of distillation targets, teacher quality, data and augmentation strategies, and student capacity.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Federated Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Distributed learning frameworks often rely on exchanging model parameters across workers, instead of revealing their raw data. A prime example is federated learning that exchanges the gradients or weights of each neural network model. Under limited communication resources, however, such a method becomes extremely costly particularly for modern deep neural networks having a huge number of model parameters. In this regard, federated distillation (FD) is a compelling distributed learning solution that only exchanges the model outputs whose dimensions are commonly much smaller than the model sizes (e.g., 10 labels in the MNIST dataset). The goal of this chapter is to provide a deep understanding of FD while demonstrating its communication efficiency and applicability to a variety of tasks. To this end, towards demystifying the operational principle of FD, the first part of this chapter provides a novel asymptotic analysis for two foundational algorithms of FD, namely knowledge distillation (KD) and co-distillation (CD), by exploiting the theory of neural tangent kernel (NTK). Next, the second part elaborates on a baseline implementation of FD for a classification task, and illustrates its performance in terms of accuracy and communication efficiency compared to FL. Lastly, to demonstrate the applicability of FD to various distributed learning tasks and environments, the third part presents two selected applications, namely FD over asymmetric uplink-and-downlink wireless channels and FD for reinforcement learning.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a prominent technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and natural language processing. This approach involves training a smaller student network to mimic the output of a larger, more capable teacher network. The method addresses critical challenges in deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments while maintaining performance quality. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, machine translation, and information retrieval systems.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a simple technique for matching teacher logits into a broad, practical framework for compressing large models and adapting them to deployment constraints. Contemporary KD encompasses soft-output matching, intermediate feature and layer imitation, online mutual distillation, data-free and zero-shot procedures, and combinations with pruning or low-precision quantization. Empirical evidence shows that when distillation choices (targets, data, teacher selection, and training curriculum) are matched to operational constraints, student models can retain much of teacher performance while achieving significant reductions in size, latency, and memory. Remaining challenges include teacher–student capacity mismatch, distilling robustness and rare phenomena, privacy-preserving distillation, and automating design choices across heterogeneous hardware and tasks. Practical success typically arises from integrated pipelines that combine multiple distillation signals with complementary compression techniques and data strategies.

papers_seen.author: Callahan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring useful information from teacher models. Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple soft-label matching to a rich toolkit that includes representation- and layer-level transfer, architecture-aware transformations, data- and teacher-selection strategies, and domain-adaptive procedures. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can yield large efficiency gains while retaining most teacher performance, but practical success depends on careful choices about what is distilled, how teachers and students are prepared, and how data or synthetic examples are used.

papers_seen.author: Cohen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Powerful Tool for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for training efficient student models by transferring knowledge from larger teacher networks. This paper argues that knowledge distillation is uniquely valuable not only for model compression and deployment on resource-constrained devices, but also for enabling knowledge transfer across diverse model architectures, improving model robustness, and facilitating collaborative learning in distributed and federated settings. The evidence demonstrates that distillation succeeds through multiple mechanisms beyond traditional soft label matching, making it an indispensable method for practical deep learning applications.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Practical Principles for Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are practical, broadly applicable strategies for deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Across tasks from retrieval and reading comprehension to multimodal generation and federated learning, distillation can preserve much of a teacher model's performance while cutting inference cost, enabling new real-time and on-device applications. Success depends less on a single canonical recipe and more on matching the distillation strategy to the deployment constraints and task: progressive structural compression, task-adaptive architecture search, layer- and feature-aware matching, careful treatment of soft targets and data, and privacy- or communication-aware protocols each address common real-world failure modes. Combining these complementary techniques yields compact students that are both efficient and robust for NLP and other domains.

papers_seen.author: Mathis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression represent critical techniques for deploying state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, these approaches enable significant reductions in computational cost, memory requirements, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. This paper argues that knowledge distillation has evolved from a simple heuristic technique into a versatile, mature framework with diverse methodologies and broad applicability across computer vision, natural language processing, and multimodal learning domains. Success with knowledge distillation depends on careful matching of compression strategies to task-specific constraints and deployment requirements rather than reliance on a single universal approach.

papers_seen.author: Ball
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical Framework for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, faster models suitable for resource-constrained deployment. By transferring knowledge from teacher models to student models, distillation enables practitioners to reduce inference latency and memory requirements while maintaining competitive performance. The approach spans diverse applications across computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and specialized domains, making it essential for practical deployment of state-of-the-art models.

papers_seen.author: Pham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are critical techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, these approaches enable significant reductions in model size and computational cost while maintaining competitive accuracy across diverse applications including computer vision, natural language processing, and machine translation. The field has evolved from basic teacher-student knowledge transfer to sophisticated multi-faceted approaches incorporating feature-level matching, data-free methods, and task-aware training protocols.

papers_seen.author: Rios
papers_seen.title: Improving Neural Topic Models using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Topic models are often used to identify human-interpretable topics to help make sense of large document collections. We use knowledge distillation to combine the best attributes of probabilistic topic models and pretrained transformers. Our modular method can be straightforwardly applied with any neural topic model to improve topic quality, which we demonstrate using two models having disparate architectures, obtaining state-of-the-art topic coherence. We show that our adaptable framework not only improves performance in the aggregate over all estimated topics, as is commonly reported, but also in head-to-head comparisons of aligned topics.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression approaches transfer information from larger or differently-abled models to smaller, faster, or modality-restricted models. Methods vary from matching final soft logits to mimicking intermediate representations, mapping layers across architectures, adversarially synthesizing training data, and adapting distillation to distributed or heterogeneous-device settings. Empirical and theoretical work highlights trade-offs between simplicity, effectiveness, data availability, and task-specificity, and suggests design patterns for effective compression across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks.

papers_seen.author: Galvan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Practice and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This synthesis examines knowledge distillation as a versatile approach for model compression that operates through multiple mechanisms, from transferring soft output distributions to aligning intermediate representations. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and speech processing, enabling the deployment of sophisticated models on resource-constrained devices.

papers_seen.author: Henson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Versatile Framework for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to constrained student networks, knowledge distillation enables practical deployment of sophisticated deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and multimodal applications. The approach encompasses multiple complementary strategies ranging from soft-label matching and feature-level transfer to data-free variants and integration with other compression techniques, establishing itself as a core practical framework for modern machine learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Walton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Imperfect Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely adopted approach to compress high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students for deployment in resource-constrained settings. Empirical results show KD can preserve much of a teacher's performance across vision, speech, and language tasks and supports many variants (e.g., feature matching, ensemble transfer, self-distillation, and data-free strategies). At the same time, KD is not a panacea: optimization difficulties, teacher–student mismatch, and data availability introduce limits that require methodical choices (what to transfer, how to train, and when to synthesize or curate data). Careful design—combining representation-level objectives, architecture-aware mapping, multi-teacher or adversarial schemes, and federated or zero-shot adaptations—yields the best practical trade-offs for accuracy, cost, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Unifying Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, flexible toolkit for compressing large neural models while preserving task performance. Across NLP and other domains, KD enables trade-offs among model size, latency, privacy, interpretability, and cross-device heterogeneity. Effective application requires choosing or designing KD variants that match the deployment constraint (e.g., layer matching for transformers, meta-learning teachers, data-free generation, or federated output sharing). When combined with complementary compression practices (progressive replacement, architectural search, or attention-based feature matching), KD routinely yields compact models suitable for real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis from Provided Studies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) trains compact student models to capture the predictive behavior or internal representations of larger teacher networks, enabling deployment under latency, memory, and compute constraints. Across domains, KD strategies range from matching softened output distributions to transferring intermediate features or relational structure, and they are commonly combined with complementary compression techniques such as quantization or architecture search. Empirical evidence shows KD can substantially reduce model size and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance, but effectiveness depends on choices about distillation targets, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability, and task-aware training protocols. Practical pipelines emphasize careful design of objectives, selective use of training examples, and efficiency-aware engineering to make KD viable in production systems.

papers_seen.author: Calderon
papers_seen.title: Learning Generalizable Models for Vehicle Routing Problems via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent neural methods for vehicle routing problems always train and test the deep models on the same instance distribution (i.e., uniform). To tackle the consequent cross-distribution generalization concerns, we bring the knowledge distillation to this field and propose an Adaptive Multi-Distribution Knowledge Distillation (AMDKD) scheme for learning more generalizable deep models. Particularly, our AMDKD leverages various knowledge from multiple teachers trained on exemplar distributions to yield a light-weight yet generalist student model. Meanwhile, we equip AMDKD with an adaptive strategy that allows the student to concentrate on difficult distributions, so as to absorb hard-to-master knowledge more effectively. Extensive experimental results show that, compared with the baseline neural methods, our AMDKD is able to achieve competitive results on both unseen in-distribution and out-of-distribution instances, which are either randomly synthesized or adopted from benchmark datasets (i.e., TSPLIB and CVRPLIB). Notably, our AMDKD is generic, and consumes less computational resources for inference.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Essential for Practical Compression, but Not a Panacea
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large deep learning and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD enables substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance through a variety of targets and training protocols. However, its effectiveness depends on choices of distillation signals, data availability, teacher–student design, and optimization; KD therefore works best as part of hybrid compression pipelines and with careful empirical diagnostics.

papers_seen.author: Chandler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Multifaceted Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, adaptable approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while often preserving or even improving generalization. KD operates at multiple levels—soft logits, intermediate representations, relational signals, and architectural guidance—and can be combined with data, augmentation, and architecture-design techniques to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. While KD delivers strong empirical gains across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks, its success depends on careful matching of teacher signals, student capacity, data strategies, and task-specific objectives; outstanding problems include robustness transfer, teacher imperfections, heterogeneous architecture alignment, and data-free distillation strategies.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Comprehensive Framework for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and practical approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This technique enables the transfer of knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, making deployment in resource-constrained environments feasible without sacrificing accuracy. The method has proven successful across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and multimodal learning, offering substantial performance improvements and computational efficiency gains with minimal accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Principles, Methods, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and model compression represent a broad set of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger, more complex neural networks to smaller, more efficient models. These approaches enable deployment of high-performing deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive accuracy. Applications span diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, speech recognition, and graph neural networks. Knowledge distillation has evolved from a heuristic compression technique to a versatile, modality-agnostic toolkit that addresses critical challenges in model efficiency, latency reduction, privacy preservation, and task-specific performance optimization.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Methods, Adaptations, and Practical Insights
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques have become standard tools to transfer knowledge from large, high-capacity models to smaller, efficient models suitable for deployment. Research across modalities and tasks has developed variants that go beyond matching output logits, including feature mimicking, attention- and channel-wise transfers, layer alignment strategies, and task-adaptive or domain-aware schemes. These approaches aim to preserve predictive accuracy and representational structure while reducing storage, computation, and latency. Practical advances demonstrate that carefully designed distillation objectives and mapping strategies can yield compact models that approach teacher performance on classification, ranking, language, speech, graph, and generative tasks, and that adapting distillation to task or domain specifics improves real-world applicability.

papers_seen.author: Brennan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Critical Technique for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the practical deployment of state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices and environments where latency, memory, and computational efficiency are critical constraints. Spanning applications across computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains including graph neural networks and non-autoregressive machine translation, knowledge distillation represents a pragmatic and core method in any deployment-oriented deep learning pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Daniels
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a single compression trick into a broad, practical toolkit that enables deployment of high-performing models under real-world constraints. KD techniques transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller students, and they can be adapted to address deployment constraints such as device heterogeneity, privacy, domain shift, fairness, and limited or missing training data. When combined with task-aware design choices and complementary compression methods, KD routinely produces compact models suitable for latency-, memory-, and privacy-constrained applications across vision, speech, and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Walton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Imperfect Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely adopted approach to compress high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students for deployment in resource-constrained settings. Empirical results show KD can preserve much of a teacher's performance across vision, speech, and language tasks and supports many variants (e.g., feature matching, ensemble transfer, self-distillation, and data-free strategies). At the same time, KD is not a panacea: optimization difficulties, teacher–student mismatch, and data availability introduce limits that require methodical choices (what to transfer, how to train, and when to synthesize or curate data). Careful design—combining representation-level objectives, architecture-aware mapping, multi-teacher or adversarial schemes, and federated or zero-shot adaptations—yields the best practical trade-offs for accuracy, cost, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: AlphaNet: Improved Training of Supernets with Alpha-Divergence
papers_seen.abstract: Weight-sharing neural architecture search (NAS) is an effective technique for automating efficient neural architecture design. Weight-sharing NAS builds a supernet that assembles all the architectures as its sub-networks and jointly trains the supernet with the sub-networks. The success of weight-sharing NAS heavily relies on distilling the knowledge of the supernet to the sub-networks. However, we find that the widely used distillation divergence, i.e., KL divergence, may lead to student sub-networks that over-estimate or under-estimate the uncertainty of the teacher supernet, leading to inferior performance of the sub-networks. In this work, we propose to improve the supernet training with a more generalized alpha-divergence. By adaptively selecting the alpha-divergence, we simultaneously prevent the over-estimation or under-estimation of the uncertainty of the teacher model. We apply the proposed alpha-divergence based supernets training to both slimmable neural networks and weight-sharing NAS, and demonstrate significant improvements. Specifically, our discovered model family, AlphaNet, outperforms prior-art models on a wide range of FLOPs regimes, including BigNAS, Once-for-All networks, and AttentiveNAS. We achieve ImageNet top-1 accuracy of 80.0% with only 444M FLOPs. Our code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/facebookresearch/AlphaNet.

papers_seen.author: Allison
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large models into efficient students that retain much of the teacher’s performance. KD techniques—spanning logits-based soft-target transfer, intermediate feature alignment, and data-free synthesis—enable deployment of high-performing models on resource-constrained devices while also offering benefits in robustness and interpretability. When paired with task-aware design and careful teacher selection, distillation can produce compact models that meet real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints without large sacrifices in accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Robbins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques transfer information from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory, and latency while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. The toolkit includes soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate feature and layer mimicry, layer-wise or task-aware filtering, multi- and online-teacher schemes, data-free and synthetic-data approaches, and combinations with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Practical success depends on aligning what is distilled to student capacity and task needs, designing efficient training protocols, and mitigating limits such as teacher–student mismatch, optimization barriers, and degraded performance on low-frequency phenomena. This synthesis summarizes core mechanisms, empirical patterns, practical design choices, domain adaptations (including NLP and generative models), and open challenges for robust, deployment-ready compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Potter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Default for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP (with Caveats and Design Guidelines)
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically proven framework for compressing large teacher models into smaller student models that retain much of the teacher’s capabilities while meeting deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy). When combined with careful teacher–student alignment, multi-source supervision, privacy-preserving mechanisms, and task-aware data strategies, KD routinely produces favorable size–performance tradeoffs across vision, language, generative, and recommendation tasks. However, its practical success depends on matching distillation objectives to student capacity, addressing data availability and domain shift, and mitigating transferred errors or undesirable behaviors. KD should therefore be the default tool for model compression in production, used alongside complementary techniques and principled evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Whitehead
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practice, and Open Issues
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, faster models by transferring information from a teacher to a student. KD techniques operate at multiple levels — soft targets, intermediate features, attention/relations, or via self- and online-distillation — and are widely used to enable deployment in resource- and latency-constrained settings across NLP, speech, vision, and multimodal tasks. Empirical work shows that carefully designed distillation pipelines can preserve most teacher performance while substantially reducing model size and inference cost, but effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data used for distillation, and matching between teacher and student objectives.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or other internal signals. Across vision and language, practitioners use a toolbox of techniques—soft-target/logit matching, feature- and attention-level alignment, layer-wise mapping or progressive replacement, multi/online-teacher schedules, and data-free synthesis—to reduce parameter counts and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. Empirical work shows substantial efficiency gains are possible when distillation is combined with complementary methods (pre-training, pruning, quantization, architecture design), but open problems remain in robustness transfer, domain shift, low-frequency and structural knowledge, and principled teacher-student selection for varied deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Mueller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Effective Strategies for Deploying Deep Learning Models in Resource-Constrained Environments
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and practical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices and edge computing systems. By leveraging various distillation methodologies—from soft target matching to feature-level alignment—this technique addresses fundamental challenges in deep learning deployment without sacrificing model capability. Knowledge distillation has proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and graph neural networks, making it a foundational technique in modern machine learning.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Effective Practices and Limits of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students. When combined with complementary strategies—such as pre-training compact architectures, layer-wise or representation-level transfer, task-aware selection of distilled signals, quantization, and federated or data-free techniques—KD can preserve much of teacher performance while meeting resource constraints. However, distillation is not a silver bullet: optimization challenges, mismatch between teacher and student internals, and mismatches between teacher predictions and task needs can limit gains. Careful design choices and evaluation protocols are therefore necessary to obtain robust, privacy-preserving, and task-appropriate compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Is Label Smoothing Truly Incompatible with Knowledge Distillation: An Empirical Study
papers_seen.abstract: This work aims to empirically clarify a recently discovered perspective that label smoothing is incompatible with knowledge distillation. We begin by introducing the motivation behind on how this incompatibility is raised, i.e., label smoothing erases relative information between teacher logits. We provide a novel connection on how label smoothing affects distributions of semantically similar and dissimilar classes. Then we propose a metric to quantitatively measure the degree of erased information in sample's representation. After that, we study its one-sidedness and imperfection of the incompatibility view through massive analyses, visualizations and comprehensive experiments on Image Classification, Binary Networks, and Neural Machine Translation. Finally, we broadly discuss several circumstances wherein label smoothing will indeed lose its effectiveness. Project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/LS_and_KD/index.html.

papers_seen.author: Mcmillan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression transfer predictive behavior or internal structure from large teacher models to smaller student models so that compact models can run under latency, memory, and privacy constraints while retaining much of the original performance. A spectrum of techniques—matching teacher output distributions, aligning intermediate representations, attention- or correlation-based feature imitation, task-adaptive architecture search, and data-side methods such as augmentation or synthetic example generation—have been developed and combined in practice. Success depends on choices about what signal to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to prepare or augment the data used for distillation; open problems include robust transfer under distribution shift, privacy-preserving and data-free distillation, and principled teacher design for specific student architectures and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression and Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has matured from a single-purpose compression trick into a flexible framework that can compress models, transfer inductive biases, improve fairness and domain adaptability, and support continual learning across modalities. Its strengths come from multiple instantiations—logit matching, feature mimicking, contrastive representation alignment, module replacement, and automated search guided by distillation—which together make it broadly applicable for deploying high-performing models under resource constraints. At the same time, careful choice of distillation targets, mixture with hard labels, and awareness of teacher imperfections are key to realizing its benefits in practice.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential, Practical, and Context-Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practically effective technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. KD methods—ranging from logit-level supervision and feature/attention imitation to ensemble, multi-teacher, and data-free variants—have enabled real-world gains in latency, memory, and cross-device applicability across NLP, vision, speech, and graph tasks. At the same time, KD’s benefits depend on careful design choices (what to transfer, how to generate or select data, and how to match teacher and student capacity), and there are empirical and theoretical limitations that counsel a measured, diagnostic-driven application rather than blind deployment. This paper argues that KD is an essential component of modern model-compression toolkits but not a panacea: its success requires method selection, data or metadata strategies, and complementary techniques to manage trade-offs in accuracy, robustness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Brown

Recent advances address practical challenges such as data scarcity, privacy constraints, and robustness transfer, while open problems remain in principled teacher-student design and understanding when distillation enhances generalization versus propagating undesirable biases.

papers_seen.author: Adams

However, fundamental limits—especially under heterogeneous data or federated settings—and practical challenges such as selecting useful teacher signal and coping with student capacity remain. A pragmatic approach combines data-aware or data-free sample generation, representation- and layer-level objectives, and task-aware filtering to maximize transfer while respecting privacy, compute, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Yu

papers_seen.author: Crosby

The field encompasses diverse approaches including logit-level distillation, feature-based imitation, data-free methods, and multi-teacher frameworks, with successful applications across computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and recommendation systems.

papers_seen.author: Adams

This paper argues that knowledge distillation is indispensable for modern machine learning applications, particularly in NLP and computer vision, where the trade-off between model complexity and efficiency remains critical for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Reinforced Multi-Teacher Selection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In natural language processing (NLP) tasks, slow inference speed and huge footprints in GPU usage remain the bottleneck of applying pre-trained deep models in production. As a popular method for model compression, knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from one or multiple large (teacher) models to a small (student) model. When multiple teacher models are available in distillation, the state-of-the-art methods assign a fixed weight to a teacher model in the whole distillation. Furthermore, most of the existing methods allocate an equal weight to every teacher model. In this paper, we observe that, due to the complexity of training examples and the differences in student model capability, learning differentially from teacher models can lead to better performance of student models distilled. We systematically develop a reinforced method to dynamically assign weights to teacher models for different training instances and optimize the performance of student model. Our extensive experimental results on several NLP tasks clearly verify the feasibility and effectiveness of our approach.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Towards Understanding Ensemble, Knowledge Distillation and Self-Distillation in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We formally study how ensemble of deep learning models can improve test accuracy, and how the superior performance of ensemble can be distilled into a single model using knowledge distillation. We consider the challenging case where the ensemble is simply an average of the outputs of a few independently trained neural networks with the SAME architecture, trained using the SAME algorithm on the SAME data set, and they only differ by the random seeds used in the initialization.   We show that ensemble/knowledge distillation in Deep Learning works very differently from traditional learning theory (such as boosting or NTKs, neural tangent kernels). To properly understand them, we develop a theory showing that when data has a structure we refer to as ``multi-view'', then ensemble of independently trained neural networks can provably improve test accuracy, and such superior test accuracy can also be provably distilled into a single model by training a single model to match the output of the ensemble instead of the true label. Our result sheds light on how ensemble works in deep learning in a way that is completely different from traditional theorems, and how the ``dark knowledge'' is hidden in the outputs of the ensemble and can be used in distillation. In the end, we prove that self-distillation can also be viewed as implicitly combining ensemble and knowledge distillation to improve test accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Fletcher
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Composable, but Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. KD provides a flexible toolkit—matching logits, aligning features or intermediate layers, ensembling teachers, and integrating with pruning/quantization—that often yields strong accuracy/efficiency trade-offs for vision, NLP, and other domains. However, KD’s effectiveness depends on data availability, teacher-student capacity alignment, optimization dynamics, and the potential transfer of teacher biases; addressing these requires task-aware design, careful augmentation or data synthesis, and privacy-preserving or multi-teacher protocols when needed.
