papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Techniques, Applications, and Advances
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are critical techniques for deploying deep neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, reducing computational requirements while maintaining performance. This paper surveys key approaches to knowledge distillation and model compression across various domains including NLP, computer vision, and graph neural networks, examining theoretical foundations, practical implementations, and recent advances that enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of neural network deployment.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical, Multi-Domain Imperative
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and widely applicable strategy for compressing deep models and enabling their deployment in resource-constrained settings. By transferring predictive and representational knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller students, KD reduces inference costs while often preserving — and sometimes improving — accuracy and robustness. Across computer vision, speech, NLP, and large-scale distributed training, KD enables designers to balance performance and efficiency, but realizing its full potential requires careful choices about what is distilled (logits, features, relations), which data or surrogates are used, and how multi-teacher or online protocols are organized.

papers_seen.author: Ray
papers_seen.title: Transferring Inductive Biases through Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Having the right inductive biases can be crucial in many tasks or scenarios where data or computing resources are a limiting factor, or where training data is not perfectly representative of the conditions at test time. However, defining, designing and efficiently adapting inductive biases is not necessarily straightforward. In this paper, we explore the power of knowledge distillation for transferring the effect of inductive biases from one model to another. We consider families of models with different inductive biases, LSTMs vs. Transformers and CNNs vs. MLPs, in the context of tasks and scenarios where having the right inductive biases is critical. We study the effect of inductive biases on the solutions the models converge to and investigate how and to what extent the effect of inductive biases is transferred through knowledge distillation, in terms of not only performance but also different aspects of converged solutions.

papers_seen.author: Torres
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Necessary but Context-Dependent Tool for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has become a central technique for compressing large neural networks into efficient student models deployable on resource-constrained devices. While knowledge distillation successfully transfers knowledge from teacher to student across diverse domains including NLP and computer vision, its effectiveness is neither universal nor automatic. Careful attention to data characteristics, teacher-student capacity relationships, and task-specific design choices is essential for reliable compression performance. This position argues that knowledge distillation is a necessary component of any practical compression toolbox, but must be combined with thoughtful method selection, multiple transfer mechanisms, and domain-aware adaptation to achieve production-ready results.

papers_seen.author: Callahan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring useful information from teacher models. Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple soft-label matching to a rich toolkit that includes representation- and layer-level transfer, architecture-aware transformations, data- and teacher-selection strategies, and domain-adaptive procedures. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can yield large efficiency gains while retaining most teacher performance, but practical success depends on careful choices about what is distilled, how teachers and students are prepared, and how data or synthetic examples are used.

papers_seen.author: Marshall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student models, enabling efficient deployment in resource-constrained environments across computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and speech recognition. Knowledge distillation encompasses diverse methodologies including soft-label matching, intermediate representation transfer, feature-level distillation, and multi-teacher ensemble strategies. While knowledge distillation frequently yields substantial gains in model size, latency, and memory with modest performance loss, its effectiveness depends on critical factors including teacher quality, student capacity, data characteristics, and the specific form of knowledge transferred. Current research advances include theoretical understanding of when and why distillation works, task-aware student design, robustness considerations, and adaptation to privacy-sensitive and distributed training scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Necessity for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Best Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and often indispensable strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students that retain much of the teachers' capabilities. Across computer vision, NLP, graph learning and other modalities, KD enables dramatic reductions in model size and inference cost while preserving or sometimes improving generalization. Success depends on design choices — what form of knowledge to transfer, how teacher and student layers are aligned, how multiple teachers are weighed, and how distillation interacts with domain shift and privacy constraints — and these choices determine whether a distilled student meets the performance and robustness needs of real deployments.

papers_seen.author: Tran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Theory, and Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for compressing large neural networks into smaller models that preserve predictive performance and desirable properties of the teacher. KD encompasses soft-label supervision, intermediate-feature matching, layer-wise alignment, multi-teacher fusion, online co-training, and teacher-free/self-distillation, and it is applied across modalities (vision, language, generation, recommendation) to meet deployment constraints such as latency, memory, low-precision arithmetic, privacy, and domain shift. Successful distillation requires task-aware choices of what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, how to generate or select data for transfer, and how to combine objectives to trade off fidelity and generalization. Remaining challenges include principled selection of distilled signals, data-free and privacy-preserving workflows, robustness under domain shift, and automated, task-adaptive compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Estes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical, Task-Aware Imperative for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques are indispensable for deploying modern deep learning models in resource-constrained settings. By transferring soft-targets, intermediate representations, or other distilled signals from larger teacher models to compact students, KD preserves much of the teacher’s performance while reducing inference cost, memory footprint, and latency. Effective distillation is not a single algorithm but a family of methods that must be chosen and tuned with respect to task requirements, student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints; when combined with complementary compression strategies, KD enables real-world use of powerful models across vision, language, and multimodal domains.

papers_seen.author: Russell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Composable Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a foundational, composable technique for compressing deep and NLP models: it reliably transfers predictive behavior and representations from high-capacity teachers into smaller students, and when combined with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search, data synthesis or adversarial training) it enables practical deployment on resource-constrained hardware. Realizing KD's benefits requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to handle data and teacher quality, and how to integrate KD into an end-to-end compression pipeline; when used with these considerations it yields compact, robust models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, size, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Pope
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a compact, flexible, and empirically effective route to compress large neural models into deployable students. When treated as a design-first tool rather than a single loss term, KD can be combined with pre-training of compact architectures, representation-level objectives, data-efficient and data-free techniques, and architecture- or task-aware adjustments to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Adopting KD as the default strategy requires engineering practices that explicitly address teacher–student alignment, domain shift, rare-token behavior, and evaluation protocols, but doing so yields a practical, composable pipeline for converting research-scale models into production-ready systems.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Explaining Knowledge Distillation by Quantifying the Knowledge
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a method to interpret the success of knowledge distillation by quantifying and analyzing task-relevant and task-irrelevant visual concepts that are encoded in intermediate layers of a deep neural network (DNN). More specifically, three hypotheses are proposed as follows. 1. Knowledge distillation makes the DNN learn more visual concepts than learning from raw data. 2. Knowledge distillation ensures that the DNN is prone to learning various visual concepts simultaneously. Whereas, in the scenario of learning from raw data, the DNN learns visual concepts sequentially. 3. Knowledge distillation yields more stable optimization directions than learning from raw data. Accordingly, we design three types of mathematical metrics to evaluate feature representations of the DNN. In experiments, we diagnosed various DNNs, and above hypotheses were verified.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression Across Modalities
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a flexible, domain-agnostic strategy that enables deployment of high-performing deep models in resource-constrained settings. By transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or distilled data between teacher and student, KD supports compression of generators, discriminative models, and multimodal systems, while enabling privacy-preserving and data-free workflows. When combined with careful pre-training, many-to-many layer alignment, or generative replay, KD allows compact architectures to approach the performance of large teachers and, in some cases, inherit desirable properties such as robustness or interpretability. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a foundational method in model compression toolkits and proposes practical emphases for future work: preserving internal representations, supporting data-free distillation, leveraging pre-training for small models, and distilling robustness.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Apprentice: Using Knowledge Distillation Techniques To Improve Low-Precision Network Accuracy
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning networks have achieved state-of-the-art accuracies on computer vision workloads like image classification and object detection. The performant systems, however, typically involve big models with numerous parameters. Once trained, a challenging aspect for such top performing models is deployment on resource constrained inference systems - the models (often deep networks or wide networks or both) are compute and memory intensive. Low-precision numerics and model compression using knowledge distillation are popular techniques to lower both the compute requirements and memory footprint of these deployed models. In this paper, we study the combination of these two techniques and show that the performance of low-precision networks can be significantly improved by using knowledge distillation techniques. Our approach, Apprentice, achieves state-of-the-art accuracies using ternary precision and 4-bit precision for variants of ResNet architecture on ImageNet dataset. We present three schemes using which one can apply knowledge distillation techniques to various stages of the train-and-deploy pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Mason
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Empirical Findings, and Practical Tradeoffs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques have become central to making large deep models—especially pretrained language models—practical for resource-constrained deployment and domain-specific use. Work in this area spans teacher-student soft-label distillation, architectural compression and replacement, layer-mapping strategies, data-free and robustness-aware procedures, and combinations with low-precision arithmetic. Empirical results demonstrate substantial reductions in size and latency while often preserving most task performance, but practical challenges remain around teacher–student mismatch, domain shift, access to original training data, adversarial robustness, and choosing task-specific compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) reduces the cost of large neural models by training smaller students to imitate higher-capacity teachers. The field has matured into a diverse toolkit that includes soft-label matching, feature- and layer-level imitation, data-free and federated variants, multi-teacher and ensemble strategies, and task-aware architecture design. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can recover much of a teacher's performance across vision, language, speech, and graph tasks while enabling deployment under compute, privacy, and device constraints; remaining challenges center on data absence, inductive-bias mismatch, automated student design, and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Davenport
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Paradigm for Model Compression and Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to smaller student models, knowledge distillation addresses the critical challenge of deploying state-of-the-art deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains. This approach extends beyond basic model compression to enable practical deployment scenarios, privacy-preserving learning, and knowledge transfer across heterogeneous architectures. The technique has proven effective across natural language processing, computer vision, graph neural networks, and multimodal learning, establishing it as an indispensable tool for modern deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Silva
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as fundamental techniques for deploying large neural networks on resource-constrained devices while maintaining predictive performance. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, these approaches address critical challenges in inference speed, memory consumption, and computational resource requirements. The techniques have been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, and specialized applications, enabling practical deployment of sophisticated deep learning systems in real-world environments with limited computational resources.

papers_seen.author: Chambers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a versatile and practical family of techniques for compressing large deep neural models into smaller, deployable ones without substantial loss of performance. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks, addressing critical deployment constraints including computational cost, memory requirements, inference latency, and privacy concerns. KD has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and specialized applications, with continuous methodological innovations expanding its scope and effectiveness.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Improving the Interpretability of Deep Neural Networks with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep Neural Networks have achieved huge success at a wide spectrum of applications from language modeling, computer vision to speech recognition. However, nowadays, good performance alone is not sufficient to satisfy the needs of practical deployment where interpretability is demanded for cases involving ethics and mission critical applications. The complex models of Deep Neural Networks make it hard to understand and reason the predictions, which hinders its further progress. To tackle this problem, we apply the Knowledge Distillation technique to distill Deep Neural Networks into decision trees in order to attain good performance and interpretability simultaneously. We formulate the problem at hand as a multi-output regression problem and the experiments demonstrate that the student model achieves significantly better accuracy performance (about 1\% to 5\%) than vanilla decision trees at the same level of tree depth. The experiments are implemented on the TensorFlow platform to make it scalable to big datasets. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to distill Deep Neural Networks into vanilla decision trees on multi-class datasets.

papers_seen.author: Byrd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical Tool for Model Compression: Strengths, Mechanisms, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. KD methods—ranging from soft-target matching to representation-level imitation, self-distillation, and adversarial teacher–student games—enable substantial efficiency gains while often improving generalization. However, distillation's benefits depend on careful design choices (what signals to transfer, how to align layers, and how to handle data or privacy constraints) and it is not a universal panacea: issues such as teacher–student mismatch, scarce or unavailable data, and task-specific optimization barriers require specialized strategies and evaluation. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a flexible, composable framework that is essential for practical compression but must be applied with task-aware techniques and awareness of its limitations.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-adopted model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large, complex teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach enables the deployment of high-performing deep learning models on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive accuracy. Knowledge distillation has been applied across multiple domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, graph neural networks, and recommendation systems, with variants adapted to different architectures and task-specific requirements. The technique addresses the critical challenge of deploying sophisticated neural models in resource-constrained environments while managing computational efficiency, latency, and storage constraints.

papers_seen.author: Blair
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful, flexible approach for turning large models into compact, deployable students. KD techniques range from simple soft-label matching to sophisticated intermediate-representation alignment, meta-learned teachers, and self-supervised or adversarially aware objectives. These methods have been shown to preserve much of teacher performance across vision and language tasks while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. At the same time, practical success depends on choices about what information to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to handle limited or private data—areas where principled guidelines and automated strategies remain active opportunities for research and engineering.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Is Label Smoothing Truly Incompatible with Knowledge Distillation: An Empirical Study
papers_seen.abstract: This work aims to empirically clarify a recently discovered perspective that label smoothing is incompatible with knowledge distillation. We begin by introducing the motivation behind on how this incompatibility is raised, i.e., label smoothing erases relative information between teacher logits. We provide a novel connection on how label smoothing affects distributions of semantically similar and dissimilar classes. Then we propose a metric to quantitatively measure the degree of erased information in sample's representation. After that, we study its one-sidedness and imperfection of the incompatibility view through massive analyses, visualizations and comprehensive experiments on Image Classification, Binary Networks, and Neural Machine Translation. Finally, we broadly discuss several circumstances wherein label smoothing will indeed lose its effectiveness. Project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/LS_and_KD/index.html.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Settings, and Insights
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving task performance. Research over the past decade has extended the basic KD idea (teacher soft targets guiding a student) into a diverse set of methods and problem settings: data-free and zero-shot distillation when original data are unavailable, privacy- and communication-aware distillation for on-device or federated deployments, architecture-aware and layer-mapping strategies for large pretrained models, self-distillation and task-adaptive compression, and representational or contrastive objectives tailored for structured domains. Empirical work shows KD enables large speedups and size reductions across vision, speech, graph, and NLP tasks; theoretical and empirical analyses clarify when soft labels help, how dataset complexity interacts with student capacity, and how distillation objectives should be chosen for different architectures and downstream constraints.

papers_seen.author: Walsh
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Core Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, KD enables the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP systems on resource-constrained devices without substantial accuracy loss. This approach addresses critical challenges in balancing model capacity with computational efficiency across diverse domains while supporting practical constraints such as privacy preservation and data scarcity. While KD is not a universal solution, when combined with complementary compression strategies and careful design choices, it represents the most practical and broadly applicable approach to achieving efficient neural networks suitable for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Understanding Knowledge Distillation in Non-autoregressive Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Non-autoregressive machine translation (NAT) systems predict a sequence of output tokens in parallel, achieving substantial improvements in generation speed compared to autoregressive models. Existing NAT models usually rely on the technique of knowledge distillation, which creates the training data from a pretrained autoregressive model for better performance. Knowledge distillation is empirically useful, leading to large gains in accuracy for NAT models, but the reason for this success has, as of yet, been unclear. In this paper, we first design systematic experiments to investigate why knowledge distillation is crucial to NAT training. We find that knowledge distillation can reduce the complexity of data sets and help NAT to model the variations in the output data. Furthermore, a strong correlation is observed between the capacity of an NAT model and the optimal complexity of the distilled data for the best translation quality. Based on these findings, we further propose several approaches that can alter the complexity of data sets to improve the performance of NAT models. We achieve the state-of-the-art performance for the NAT-based models, and close the gap with the autoregressive baseline on WMT14 En-De benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Revisiting Knowledge Distillation via Label Smoothing Regularization
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to distill the knowledge of a cumbersome teacher model into a lightweight student model. Its success is generally attributed to the privileged information on similarities among categories provided by the teacher model, and in this sense, only strong teacher models are deployed to teach weaker students in practice. In this work, we challenge this common belief by following experimental observations: 1) beyond the acknowledgment that the teacher can improve the student, the student can also enhance the teacher significantly by reversing the KD procedure; 2) a poorly-trained teacher with much lower accuracy than the student can still improve the latter significantly. To explain these observations, we provide a theoretical analysis of the relationships between KD and label smoothing regularization. We prove that 1) KD is a type of learned label smoothing regularization and 2) label smoothing regularization provides a virtual teacher model for KD. From these results, we argue that the success of KD is not fully due to the similarity information between categories from teachers, but also to the regularization of soft targets, which is equally or even more important.   Based on these analyses, we further propose a novel Teacher-free Knowledge Distillation (Tf-KD) framework, where a student model learns from itself or manuallydesigned regularization distribution. The Tf-KD achieves comparable performance with normal KD from a superior teacher, which is well applied when a stronger teacher model is unavailable. Meanwhile, Tf-KD is generic and can be directly deployed for training deep neural networks. Without any extra computation cost, Tf-KD achieves up to 0.65\% improvement on ImageNet over well-established baseline models, which is superior to label smoothing regularization.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from teacher models. Across vision, language, graph, and generative settings, distillation methods range from matching softened logits to aligning intermediate features, using data-centric strategies (e.g., synthetic data or teacher-generated targets), selective sample weighting, and meta-learning of teacher behaviors. Distillation functions both as a compression tool and as a mechanism for regularization, domain adaptation, and privacy-aware transfer; however, practical success depends on teacher quality, data availability and complexity, optimization dynamics, and careful choice of distillation targets and sample selection. Domain-specific adaptations (e.g., for non-autoregressive translation, machine reading comprehension, and graph neural networks) show significant gains but highlight open problems in reliably preserving rare/low-frequency phenomena and in formalizing when distillation is most effective.

papers_seen.author: Whitehead
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practice, and Open Issues
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, faster models by transferring information from a teacher to a student. KD techniques operate at multiple levels — soft targets, intermediate features, attention/relations, or via self- and online-distillation — and are widely used to enable deployment in resource- and latency-constrained settings across NLP, speech, vision, and multimodal tasks. Empirical work shows that carefully designed distillation pipelines can preserve most teacher performance while substantially reducing model size and inference cost, but effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data used for distillation, and matching between teacher and student objectives.

papers_seen.author: Allen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Critical Technology for Efficient Neural Network Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has become an indispensable technique for deploying high-performing deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to compact student models, distillation enables significant reductions in computational requirements and model size while maintaining competitive performance. This position argues that knowledge distillation, when properly designed and combined with complementary compression strategies, represents the most practical and versatile approach to achieving efficient neural networks across diverse applications in computer vision, natural language processing, and beyond.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transform large, expensive models into smaller, faster, or otherwise more deployable models by transferring knowledge from one model (teacher) to another (student). Research over the past decade has produced a spectrum of methods: representation- and layer-matching, soft-target regularization and teacher-free variants, data-free and adversarial sample synthesis, many-to-many layer alignment for transformer compression, and task-adaptive architecture search with distillation objectives. These approaches address practical constraints—limited compute, privacy of training data, heterogeneous devices, and task-specific requirements—while revealing theoretical connections between KD and regularization. Empirical work shows KD is effective across vision and language tasks, can enable competitive small models for NLP, and remains central to specialized pipelines such as non-autoregressive translation and transformer pruning. Open directions include better matching of inductive biases between teacher and student, principled handling of data absence or privacy, and automated, task-aware compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Farmer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Advancing Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Systems
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining or even improving performance. This approach involves transferring knowledge from a large teacher model to a compact student model, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices without sacrificing accuracy. While the foundational concept has been widely applied across computer vision, recommender systems, and natural language processing, recent advances have introduced sophisticated variations and domain-specific adaptations. This paper provides a comprehensive overview of knowledge distillation methodologies, including selective distillation approaches, cross-modal knowledge transfer, adversarial learning frameworks, and specialized applications to transformer-based architectures and sequential tasks.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach enables the deployment of state-of-the-art neural networks in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. KD has evolved significantly beyond simple logit matching to encompass diverse techniques including intermediate representation matching, layer-wise alignment, multi-teacher training, data-free approaches, and task-adaptive architecture search. The technique is now widely applied across multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, graph neural networks, and generative tasks, addressing critical challenges in bridging the gap between model performance and practical deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Unifying Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, flexible toolkit for compressing large neural models while preserving task performance. Across NLP and other domains, KD enables trade-offs among model size, latency, privacy, interpretability, and cross-device heterogeneity. Effective application requires choosing or designing KD variants that match the deployment constraint (e.g., layer matching for transformers, meta-learning teachers, data-free generation, or federated output sharing). When combined with complementary compression practices (progressive replacement, architectural search, or attention-based feature matching), KD routinely yields compact models suitable for real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Cook
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the primary tool for compressing large models into efficient students for deployment in deep learning and NLP. KD offers flexible mechanisms to transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from teachers to students, enabling substantial reductions in model size and latency while preserving much of the original performance. However, KD is not a one-size-fits-all recipe: its success depends on careful, task-aware design choices (e.g., which signals to transfer, teacher selection, data regimes, and complementary compression techniques) and on explicit strategies to detect and mitigate teacher error propagation. When applied thoughtfully and combined with other compression and deployment-aware methods, KD yields practical, high-fidelity compressed models across modalities and tasks.

papers_seen.author: Scott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Provided Works
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) reduces model size and inference cost by transferring behavior from large teacher models to smaller student models. Across deep learning and NLP, KD has evolved from simple soft-target matching to a diverse set of practices including intermediate-feature matching, layer-wise alignment, multi-teacher curricula, architecture-aware transformations, and data- or privacy-aware variants. These approaches enable deployment under latency, memory, and regulatory constraints while raising practical questions about teacher–student design, data availability, and robustness under distribution shift. This synthesis summarizes common mechanisms, practical strategies, empirical outcomes, and open challenges reported in the provided literature.

papers_seen.author: Ortiz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, enabling deployment across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and graph neural networks. Beyond basic model compression, knowledge distillation encompasses multiple methodologies including soft target matching, feature-level mimicking, intermediate representation alignment, and multi-teacher pipelines. While the technique addresses critical practical challenges such as reducing computational cost, latency, memory consumption, and enabling privacy-preserving deployment, significant challenges remain in principled teacher-student design, handling data scarcity, and understanding when distillation enhances generalization.

papers_seen.author: Osborne
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge from Deep Networks with Applications to Healthcare Domain
papers_seen.abstract: Exponential growth in Electronic Healthcare Records (EHR) has resulted in new opportunities and urgent needs for discovery of meaningful data-driven representations and patterns of diseases in Computational Phenotyping research. Deep Learning models have shown superior performance for robust prediction in computational phenotyping tasks, but suffer from the issue of model interpretability which is crucial for clinicians involved in decision-making. In this paper, we introduce a novel knowledge-distillation approach called Interpretable Mimic Learning, to learn interpretable phenotype features for making robust prediction while mimicking the performance of deep learning models. Our framework uses Gradient Boosting Trees to learn interpretable features from deep learning models such as Stacked Denoising Autoencoder and Long Short-Term Memory. Exhaustive experiments on a real-world clinical time-series dataset show that our method obtains similar or better performance than the deep learning models, and it provides interpretable phenotypes for clinical decision making.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation in Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Since deep learning became a key player in natural language processing (NLP), many deep learning models have been showing remarkable performances in a variety of NLP tasks, and in some cases, they are even outperforming humans. Such high performance can be explained by efficient knowledge representation of deep learning models. While many methods have been proposed to learn more efficient representation, knowledge distillation from pretrained deep networks suggest that we can use more information from the soft target probability to train other neural networks. In this paper, we propose a new knowledge distillation method self-knowledge distillation, based on the soft target probabilities of the training model itself, where multimode information is distilled from the word embedding space right below the softmax layer. Due to the time complexity, our method approximates the soft target probabilities. In experiments, we applied the proposed method to two different and fundamental NLP tasks: language model and neural machine translation. The experiment results show that our proposed method improves performance on the tasks.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Effective yet Context-Dependent Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and widely-adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while preserving performance. By enabling knowledge transfer through soft targets and intermediate representations, distillation addresses the critical challenge of deploying sophisticated deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices. However, distillation is not universally applicable and requires careful design choices regarding teacher-student alignment, data availability, and task-specific constraints to realize optimal compression benefits.

papers_seen.author: Roman
papers_seen.title: Fair Feature Distillation for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: Fairness is becoming an increasingly crucial issue for computer vision, especially in the human-related decision systems. However, achieving algorithmic fairness, which makes a model produce indiscriminative outcomes against protected groups, is still an unresolved problem. In this paper, we devise a systematic approach which reduces algorithmic biases via feature distillation for visual recognition tasks, dubbed as MMD-based Fair Distillation (MFD). While the distillation technique has been widely used in general to improve the prediction accuracy, to the best of our knowledge, there has been no explicit work that also tries to improve fairness via distillation. Furthermore, We give a theoretical justification of our MFD on the effect of knowledge distillation and fairness. Throughout the extensive experiments, we show our MFD significantly mitigates the bias against specific minorities without any loss of the accuracy on both synthetic and real-world face datasets.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Channel Distillation: Channel-Wise Attention for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is to transfer the knowledge from the data learned by the teacher network to the student network, so that the student has the advantage of less parameters and less calculations, and the accuracy is close to the teacher. In this paper, we propose a new distillation method, which contains two transfer distillation strategies and a loss decay strategy. The first transfer strategy is based on channel-wise attention, called Channel Distillation (CD). CD transfers the channel information from the teacher to the student. The second is Guided Knowledge Distillation (GKD). Unlike Knowledge Distillation (KD), which allows the student to mimic each sample's prediction distribution of the teacher, GKD only enables the student to mimic the correct output of the teacher. The last part is Early Decay Teacher (EDT). During the training process, we gradually decay the weight of the distillation loss. The purpose is to enable the student to gradually control the optimization rather than the teacher. Our proposed method is evaluated on ImageNet and CIFAR100. On ImageNet, we achieve 27.68% of top-1 error with ResNet18, which outperforms state-of-the-art methods. On CIFAR100, we achieve surprising result that the student outperforms the teacher. Code is available at https://github.com/zhouzaida/channel-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Cherry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Task‑Aware Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable students while preserving predictive performance and enabling additional properties such as privacy, robustness, and fairness. When treated as a task-aware toolkit—combining soft-label matching, intermediate feature alignment, adversarial or generative data synthesis, and multi-teacher or curriculum strategies—KD can meet real-world deployment constraints (latency, memory, data access) across modalities. Practical success depends on explicit choices about what to transfer, how to generate or select distillation data, and how to align capacity and objectives between teacher and student; addressing these choices systematically enables KD to be both a compression engine and a mechanism for adapting models to constrained, private, or fairness-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels—commonly via softened outputs, intermediate feature targets, or structural behavior. Across computer vision, NLP, speech, and recommendation systems, KD variants enable substantial reductions in parameters, memory, and latency while preserving much of teacher performance. Practical application requires tailoring what is transferred (logits, features, attention, or decisions), how teachers and students are aligned architecturally, and how data is used or synthesized; addressing teacher–student mismatch, limited or private data, and task-specific constraints is critical to robust, deployable compression pipelines. Recent work moves toward combined pipelines that jointly search or prune student structure while distilling appropriate signals, and toward adaptations for heterogeneous teachers, sequence tasks, and resource- or privacy-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Davidson
papers_seen.title: Robust Re-Identification by Multiple Views Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: To achieve robustness in Re-Identification, standard methods leverage tracking information in a Video-To-Video fashion. However, these solutions face a large drop in performance for single image queries (e.g., Image-To-Video setting). Recent works address this severe degradation by transferring temporal information from a Video-based network to an Image-based one. In this work, we devise a training strategy that allows the transfer of a superior knowledge, arising from a set of views depicting the target object. Our proposal - Views Knowledge Distillation (VKD) - pins this visual variety as a supervision signal within a teacher-student framework, where the teacher educates a student who observes fewer views. As a result, the student outperforms not only its teacher but also the current state-of-the-art in Image-To-Video by a wide margin (6.3% mAP on MARS, 8.6% on Duke-Video-ReId and 5% on VeRi-776). A thorough analysis - on Person, Vehicle and Animal Re-ID - investigates the properties of VKD from a qualitatively and quantitatively perspective. Code is available at https://github.com/aimagelab/VKD.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying large deep neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while preserving predictive performance. Applications span computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and other domains, with diverse approaches adapted to specific task requirements and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression represent critical techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, these approaches enable significant reductions in model size and computational cost while maintaining competitive accuracy across diverse applications including computer vision, natural language processing, and machine translation. The field has evolved from basic teacher-student knowledge transfer to sophisticated multi-faceted approaches incorporating feature-level matching, data-free methods, sample selection strategies, and robustness-aware training protocols.

papers_seen.author: Harmon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Composable Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques that enables high-performing models to be deployed under resource constraints by transferring behavior, representations, or synthesized signals from larger teachers to smaller students. When treated as a composable, task-aware component of compression toolkits—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, or data synthesis—KD routinely yields practical size–performance tradeoffs. However, realizing reliable outcomes requires careful teacher selection, objective design, curriculum and data strategies, and explicit attention to failure modes such as optimization gaps, capacity mismatch, and the transfer of undesirable behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and NLP applications. By enabling the transfer of knowledge from large teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges of inference speed, memory consumption, and computational resource requirements. This approach has been successfully applied across diverse domains including NLP tasks, computer vision, federated learning, and various specialized applications, offering practical solutions for deploying complex models in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Warner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Strategies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that trains a smaller student network to transfer knowledge from a larger teacher model, enabling efficient deployment of complex neural networks on resource-constrained devices. This approach has become essential for making state-of-the-art models practical while maintaining competitive performance across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and speech recognition. Knowledge distillation addresses fundamental challenges in model efficiency by enabling reductions in size and latency without substantial loss in task performance.

papers_seen.author: Carr
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Composable, Practical Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models by transferring useful behavior from teacher models to students. Across vision, speech, and NLP, KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while often preserving much of the teacher's performance. The technique encompasses multiple operational modalities — logits matching, feature mimicking, multi-teacher fusion, data-free synthesis, and distributed/federated protocols — and is best applied as an adaptable toolkit whose components are selected to match data availability, privacy constraints, robustness needs, and target hardware.

papers_seen.author: Mckee
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable model-compression paradigm that transfers behavior from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce memory, latency, and compute while preserving task performance. Over the past decade KD has expanded beyond matching soft-output logits to include intermediate-feature and layer-level matching, multi-teacher and many-to-many mappings, data-free and privacy-aware approaches, and hybrid pipelines that combine distillation with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work shows distilled students can often approach teacher performance across vision, language, graph, and retrieval tasks, but practical success depends on choices about what is transferred, how teachers and students are matched, and how limited or private data are handled. Key open problems include principled teacher selection, coping with data heterogeneity or absence, robustness to rare phenomena and bias transfer, and tighter theoretical understanding of when distillation improves generalization.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Learning Student-Friendly Teacher Networks for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel knowledge distillation approach to facilitate the transfer of dark knowledge from a teacher to a student. Contrary to most of the existing methods that rely on effective training of student models given pretrained teachers, we aim to learn the teacher models that are friendly to students and, consequently, more appropriate for knowledge transfer. In other words, at the time of optimizing a teacher model, the proposed algorithm learns the student branches jointly to obtain student-friendly representations. Since the main goal of our approach lies in training teacher models and the subsequent knowledge distillation procedure is straightforward, most of the existing knowledge distillation methods can adopt this technique to improve the performance of diverse student models in terms of accuracy and convergence speed. The proposed algorithm demonstrates outstanding accuracy in several well-known knowledge distillation techniques with various combinations of teacher and student models even in the case that their architectures are heterogeneous and there is no prior knowledge about student models at the time of training teacher networks.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-adopted model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large, complex teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach enables the deployment of high-performing deep learning models on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive accuracy. Knowledge distillation has been applied across multiple domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, graph neural networks, and recommendation systems, with variants adapted to different architectures and task-specific requirements. The technique addresses the critical challenge of deploying sophisticated neural models in resource-constrained environments while managing computational efficiency, latency, and storage constraints.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical Strategy for Deploying Deep Learning and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a powerful and practical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, KD enables the deployment of state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices. While KD is not a universal solution and requires careful design choices, when combined with complementary strategies such as representation-level transfer, data-aware techniques, and task-specific optimization, it can preserve much of the teacher's performance while substantially reducing inference costs and memory requirements. This makes KD an essential strategy for practical deep learning deployment across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: Compressing Deep Graph Neural Networks via Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep graph neural networks (GNNs) have been shown to be expressive for modeling graph-structured data. Nevertheless, the over-stacked architecture of deep graph models makes it difficult to deploy and rapidly test on mobile or embedded systems. To compress over-stacked GNNs, knowledge distillation via a teacher-student architecture turns out to be an effective technique, where the key step is to measure the discrepancy between teacher and student networks with predefined distance functions. However, using the same distance for graphs of various structures may be unfit, and the optimal distance formulation is hard to determine. To tackle these problems, we propose a novel Adversarial Knowledge Distillation framework for graph models named GraphAKD, which adversarially trains a discriminator and a generator to adaptively detect and decrease the discrepancy. Specifically, noticing that the well-captured inter-node and inter-class correlations favor the success of deep GNNs, we propose to criticize the inherited knowledge from node-level and class-level views with a trainable discriminator. The discriminator distinguishes between teacher knowledge and what the student inherits, while the student GNN works as a generator and aims to fool the discriminator. To our best knowledge, GraphAKD is the first to introduce adversarial training to knowledge distillation in graph domains. Experiments on node-level and graph-level classification benchmarks demonstrate that GraphAKD improves the student performance by a large margin. The results imply that GraphAKD can precisely transfer knowledge from a complicated teacher GNN to a compact student GNN.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Research in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques enable deployment of large deep models in resource-constrained settings by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations from larger ‘‘teacher’’ models to smaller ‘‘student’’ models. Research over the past decade has developed multiple complementary approaches — logit-level distillation, feature- and attention-based imitation, architecture-aware compression, data-free and privacy-preserving variants, and teacher-training strategies — each addressing different practical constraints such as limited data, heterogeneous devices, latency, or privacy. Empirical work shows that careful design choices (what to transfer, when to transfer, and how to adapt student architectures) often determine whether a distilled student approaches teacher-level performance; theoretical and empirical analyses clarify when distillation helps, how ensemble and ‘‘dark knowledge’’ contribute, and why mixing hard and soft targets can be beneficial. Continued progress connects distillation with neural architecture search, meta-learning of teachers, and robust data synthesis to broaden applicability across vision, speech, retrieval, graph, and NLP tasks.

papers_seen.author: Oliver
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Practical, Responsible Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core technique for reducing the size and inference cost of high‑capacity models while retaining much of their predictive power. KD extends beyond simple teacher→student soft‑label matching to include representation‑level transfer, contrastive alignment, data‑free synthesis, and privacy‑aware schemes that make compression feasible when original training data are unavailable or sensitive. When combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and guided by task‑aware choices about what and when to transfer, KD enables deployable models for resource‑constrained and safety‑sensitive settings. However, realizing these benefits requires attention to teacher–student capacity gaps, the form of transferred knowledge, and domain or token‑frequency effects; principled design and evaluation are therefore essential for reliable compression in practice.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Critical Technique for Deep Learning Model Compression and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large deep learning models while maintaining performance. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student models, enabling efficient deployment across diverse applications. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents an essential strategy for addressing the trade-off between model complexity and practical deployment requirements in both computer vision and natural language processing domains.
