papers_seen.author: Farmer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Advancing Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Systems
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining or even improving performance. This approach involves transferring knowledge from a large teacher model to a compact student model, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices without sacrificing accuracy. While the foundational concept has been widely applied across computer vision, recommender systems, and natural language processing, recent advances have introduced sophisticated variations and domain-specific adaptations. This paper provides a comprehensive overview of knowledge distillation methodologies, including selective distillation approaches, cross-modal knowledge transfer, adversarial learning frameworks, and specialized applications to transformer-based architectures and sequential tasks.

papers_seen.author: Tran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Theory, and Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for compressing large neural networks into smaller models that preserve predictive performance and desirable properties of the teacher. KD encompasses soft-label supervision, intermediate-feature matching, layer-wise alignment, multi-teacher fusion, online co-training, and teacher-free/self-distillation, and it is applied across modalities (vision, language, generation, recommendation) to meet deployment constraints such as latency, memory, low-precision arithmetic, privacy, and domain shift. Successful distillation requires task-aware choices of what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, how to generate or select data for transfer, and how to combine objectives to trade off fidelity and generalization. Remaining challenges include principled selection of distilled signals, data-free and privacy-preserving workflows, robustness under domain shift, and automated, task-adaptive compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Approaches
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, more efficient students while retaining much of the teachers' performance. Recent work expands the KD toolkit beyond matching soft logits to include feature- and layer-level mimicry, task-aware selection of teacher knowledge, data-free and multi-teacher strategies, and augmentation-driven improvements. Practical advances target domain-specific challenges in language models and cross-modal systems, emphasize efficient training and deployment on heterogeneous hardware, and reinterpret KD as a form of regularization that can sometimes be partially replaced or simulated. This review synthesizes these directions and highlights recurring design principles for effective distillation in both NLP and general deep learning settings.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become fundamental techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, enabling practical deployment while maintaining competitive performance. The techniques address critical challenges in modern deep learning, including reducing inference latency, memory requirements, and computational costs across diverse domains including computer vision and natural language processing.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Preserving Privacy in Federated Learning with Ensemble Cross-Domain Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is a machine learning paradigm where local nodes collaboratively train a central model while the training data remains decentralized. Existing FL methods typically share model parameters or employ co-distillation to address the issue of unbalanced data distribution. However, they suffer from communication bottlenecks. More importantly, they risk privacy leakage. In this work, we develop a privacy preserving and communication efficient method in a FL framework with one-shot offline knowledge distillation using unlabeled, cross-domain public data. We propose a quantized and noisy ensemble of local predictions from completely trained local models for stronger privacy guarantees without sacrificing accuracy. Based on extensive experiments on image classification and text classification tasks, we show that our privacy-preserving method outperforms baseline FL algorithms with superior performance in both accuracy and communication efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Bowman
papers_seen.title: TRILLsson: Distilled Universal Paralinguistic Speech Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in self-supervision have dramatically improved the quality of speech representations. However, deployment of state-of-the-art embedding models on devices has been restricted due to their limited public availability and large resource footprint. Our work addresses these issues by publicly releasing a collection of paralinguistic speech models that are small and near state-of-the-art performance. Our approach is based on knowledge distillation, and our models are distilled on public data only. We explore different architectures and thoroughly evaluate our models on the Non-Semantic Speech (NOSS) benchmark. Our largest distilled model is less than 15% the size of the original model (314MB vs 2.2GB), achieves over 96% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks, and is trained on 6.5% the data. The smallest model is 1% in size (22MB) and achieves over 90% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks. Our models outperform the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 model on 6 of 7 tasks, and our smallest model outperforms the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 on both emotion recognition tasks despite being 7% the size.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Layer-aware, Multi-source, and Data-efficient Knowledge Distillation for Compressing Pretrained NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a central tool for compressing large pre-trained language models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Effective compression requires going beyond matching final logits: it benefits from transferring intermediate representations, adapting to domain shifts, leveraging multiple reliable supervision sources, and handling cases where original training data cannot be shared. I argue that a practical, high-performing distillation pipeline for NLP should (1) align teacher and student internal representations with flexible many-to-many mappings, (2) weight and fuse signals from multiple teachers by confidence, (3) include domain-aware adaptation before distillation, and (4) incorporate data-free or privacy-preserving distillation options when necessary. Combining these elements yields compact models that retain much of the teacher’s capabilities while meeting deployment and privacy goals.

papers_seen.author: Hawkins
papers_seen.title: A Fast Knowledge Distillation Framework for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: While Knowledge Distillation (KD) has been recognized as a useful tool in many visual tasks, such as supervised classification and self-supervised representation learning, the main drawback of a vanilla KD framework is its mechanism, which consumes the majority of the computational overhead on forwarding through the giant teacher networks, making the entire learning procedure inefficient and costly. ReLabel, a recently proposed solution, suggests creating a label map for the entire image. During training, it receives the cropped region-level label by RoI aligning on a pre-generated entire label map, allowing for efficient supervision generation without having to pass through the teachers many times. However, as the KD teachers are from conventional multi-crop training, there are various mismatches between the global label-map and region-level label in this technique, resulting in performance deterioration. In this study, we present a Fast Knowledge Distillation (FKD) framework that replicates the distillation training phase and generates soft labels using the multi-crop KD approach, while training faster than ReLabel since no post-processes such as RoI align and softmax operations are used. When conducting multi-crop in the same image for data loading, our FKD is even more efficient than the traditional image classification framework. On ImageNet-1K, we obtain 79.8% with ResNet-50, outperforming ReLabel by ~1.0% while being faster. On the self-supervised learning task, we also show that FKD has an efficiency advantage. Our project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/FKD/index.html, source code and models are available at: https://github.com/szq0214/FKD.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, enabling practical deployment of state-of-the-art neural networks in resource-constrained environments. This approach addresses critical challenges in deep learning and natural language processing by reducing computational costs, memory requirements, and latency while maintaining competitive performance. Beyond basic compression, knowledge distillation encompasses diverse strategies including soft-target matching, intermediate representation transfer, multi-teacher approaches, and task-aware adaptations that extend its applicability across vision, language processing, speech recognition, and other domains.

papers_seen.author: Farrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for compressing large, complex neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from teacher to student models, this approach enables the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices and accelerates inference across diverse domains. Recent advances have expanded knowledge distillation beyond simple output matching to include intermediate representation alignment, data-free approaches, and integration with complementary compression methods, making it an essential methodology for practical machine learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Pena
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practical family of methods for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information from a high-capacity teacher to a compact student using a range of signals (soft logits, intermediate representations, layer-wise supervision, or synthesized data). Across vision and language tasks, KD enables substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance, and it composes effectively with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical success requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to handle limited or private data, and how to evaluate robustness and rare-case behavior.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning, enabling the training of smaller, more efficient student models to mimic the behavior of larger teacher models. This approach has become increasingly important for deploying neural networks on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive accuracy. The technique has been extensively studied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, federated learning, and generative models, with various architectural innovations and theoretical frameworks developed to improve its effectiveness and applicability.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a prominent technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and natural language processing. This approach involves training a smaller student network to mimic the output of a larger, more capable teacher network. The method addresses critical challenges in deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments while maintaining performance quality. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, machine translation, and information retrieval systems.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Compressing GANs using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been used in several machine learning tasks such as domain transfer, super resolution, and synthetic data generation. State-of-the-art GANs often use tens of millions of parameters, making them expensive to deploy for applications in low SWAP (size, weight, and power) hardware, such as mobile devices, and for applications with real time capabilities. There has been no work found to reduce the number of parameters used in GANs. Therefore, we propose a method to compress GANs using knowledge distillation techniques, in which a smaller "student" GAN learns to mimic a larger "teacher" GAN. We show that the distillation methods used on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Celeb-A datasets can compress teacher GANs at ratios of 1669:1, 58:1, and 87:1, respectively, while retaining the quality of the generated image. From our experiments, we observe a qualitative limit for GAN's compression. Moreover, we observe that, with a fixed parameter budget, compressed GANs outperform GANs trained using standard training methods. We conjecture that this is partially owing to the optimization landscape of over-parameterized GANs which allows efficient training using alternating gradient descent. Thus, training an over-parameterized GAN followed by our proposed compression scheme provides a high quality generative model with a small number of parameters.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-adopted technique for compressing neural networks by transferring knowledge from a larger teacher model to a smaller student model. This approach enables the development of efficient models with reduced parameters and computational requirements while maintaining high performance across various domains including computer vision and natural language processing. The field has evolved to encompass diverse methodologies, from basic logit matching to advanced layer-wise and feature-level distillation approaches, with applications spanning machine translation, question answering, sentiment analysis, and multi-modal learning.

papers_seen.author: Moreno
papers_seen.title: Promises and Practicalities of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable strategy for compressing large models into smaller, faster students while preserving performance. Empirical successes span vision, language, graph, and retrieval tasks, and variants include multi-teacher, self-distillation, feature-level and adversarial formulations. However, distillation is not a panacea: its benefits depend on how knowledge is represented (soft targets vs. internal features), on the student–teacher interaction mechanisms, and on data- and deployment-specific constraints (e.g., heterogeneous clients or low-frequency tokens). This article argues that KD is a powerful and flexible tool when combined with principled modifications — such as internal-representation distillation, projector ensembles, multi-teacher curricula, improved data augmentation, and task-aware distillation losses — but that practitioners must attend to these factors to realize reliable compression and generalization gains.

papers_seen.author: Robertson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and practical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and speech recognition. Through various mechanisms and strategic design choices, knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in balancing model capacity with computational efficiency without substantial accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Blair
papers_seen.title: Distilling Policy Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The transfer of knowledge from one policy to another is an important tool in Deep Reinforcement Learning. This process, referred to as distillation, has been used to great success, for example, by enhancing the optimisation of agents, leading to stronger performance faster, on harder domains [26, 32, 5, 8]. Despite the widespread use and conceptual simplicity of distillation, many different formulations are used in practice, and the subtle variations between them can often drastically change the performance and the resulting objective that is being optimised. In this work, we rigorously explore the entire landscape of policy distillation, comparing the motivations and strengths of each variant through theoretical and empirical analysis. Our results point to three distillation techniques, that are preferred depending on specifics of the task. Specifically a newly proposed expected entropy regularised distillation allows for quicker learning in a wide range of situations, while still guaranteeing convergence.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Methods and Practices for Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible set of techniques to transfer knowledge from a high-capacity teacher model to a smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student. Work across modalities and tasks has shown KD can yield compact models that approach teacher performance, enable deployment on resource-limited devices, help mitigate data-availability or privacy constraints, and act as a vehicle for transferring ensemble or multi-teacher knowledge into a single model. Practical KD methods vary in what they transfer (logits, intermediate features, or rankings), whether they require original training data, and how they structure training (offline, online, adversarial, or curriculum-based). Empirical and methodological work highlights (1) the effectiveness of feature-level supervision in many settings, (2) the value of synthetic or replayed data when real data are unavailable, (3) that ensemble and online schemes can speed training and improve robustness, and (4) that augmentation, sample selection, and task-specific losses materially affect distilled-student outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Adapt-and-Distill: Developing Small, Fast and Effective Pretrained Language Models for Domains
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained models have achieved great success in many natural language processing tasks. However, when they are applied in specific domains, these models suffer from domain shift and bring challenges in fine-tuning and online serving for latency and capacity constraints. In this paper, we present a general approach to developing small, fast and effective pre-trained models for specific domains. This is achieved by adapting the off-the-shelf general pre-trained models and performing task-agnostic knowledge distillation in target domains. Specifically, we propose domain-specific vocabulary expansion in the adaptation stage and employ corpus level occurrence probability to choose the size of incremental vocabulary automatically. Then we systematically explore different strategies to compress the large pre-trained models for specific domains. We conduct our experiments in the biomedical and computer science domain. The experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves better performance over the BERT BASE model in domain-specific tasks while 3.3x smaller and 5.1x faster than BERT BASE. The code and pre-trained models are available at https://aka.ms/adalm.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Model Compression with Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation for Web Question Answering System
papers_seen.abstract: Deep pre-training and fine-tuning models (such as BERT and OpenAI GPT) have demonstrated excellent results in question answering areas. However, due to the sheer amount of model parameters, the inference speed of these models is very slow. How to apply these complex models to real business scenarios becomes a challenging but practical problem. Previous model compression methods usually suffer from information loss during the model compression procedure, leading to inferior models compared with the original one. To tackle this challenge, we propose a Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (TMKD for short) method for web Question Answering system. We first develop a general Q\&A distillation task for student model pre-training, and further fine-tune this pre-trained student model with multi-teacher knowledge distillation on downstream tasks (like Web Q\&A task, MNLI, SNLI, RTE tasks from GLUE), which effectively reduces the overfitting bias in individual teacher models, and transfers more general knowledge to the student model. The experiment results show that our method can significantly outperform the baseline methods and even achieve comparable results with the original teacher models, along with substantial speedup of model inference.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential, Practical, and Context-Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practically effective technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. KD methods—ranging from logit-level supervision and feature/attention imitation to ensemble, multi-teacher, and data-free variants—have enabled real-world gains in latency, memory, and cross-device applicability across NLP, vision, speech, and graph tasks. At the same time, KD’s benefits depend on careful design choices (what to transfer, how to generate or select data, and how to match teacher and student capacity), and there are empirical and theoretical limitations that counsel a measured, diagnostic-driven application rather than blind deployment. This paper argues that KD is an essential component of modern model-compression toolkits but not a panacea: its success requires method selection, data or metadata strategies, and complementary techniques to manage trade-offs in accuracy, robustness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Rhodes
papers_seen.title: Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: It is challenging to perform lifelong language learning (LLL) on a stream of different tasks without any performance degradation comparing to the multi-task counterparts. To address this issue, we present Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation (L2KD), a simple but efficient method that can be easily applied to existing LLL architectures in order to mitigate the degradation. Specifically, when the LLL model is trained on a new task, we assign a teacher model to first learn the new task, and pass the knowledge to the LLL model via knowledge distillation. Therefore, the LLL model can better adapt to the new task while keeping the previously learned knowledge. Experiments show that the proposed L2KD consistently improves previous state-of-the-art models, and the degradation comparing to multi-task models in LLL tasks is well mitigated for both sequence generation and text classification tasks.

papers_seen.author: Osborne
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge from Deep Networks with Applications to Healthcare Domain
papers_seen.abstract: Exponential growth in Electronic Healthcare Records (EHR) has resulted in new opportunities and urgent needs for discovery of meaningful data-driven representations and patterns of diseases in Computational Phenotyping research. Deep Learning models have shown superior performance for robust prediction in computational phenotyping tasks, but suffer from the issue of model interpretability which is crucial for clinicians involved in decision-making. In this paper, we introduce a novel knowledge-distillation approach called Interpretable Mimic Learning, to learn interpretable phenotype features for making robust prediction while mimicking the performance of deep learning models. Our framework uses Gradient Boosting Trees to learn interpretable features from deep learning models such as Stacked Denoising Autoencoder and Long Short-Term Memory. Exhaustive experiments on a real-world clinical time-series dataset show that our method obtains similar or better performance than the deep learning models, and it provides interpretable phenotypes for clinical decision making.

papers_seen.author: Liu
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Bridging Performance and Efficiency
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression in deep learning, enabling the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive models to smaller, more efficient ones. This approach addresses the critical challenge of deploying neural networks on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive performance. The technique applies across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and machine translation, demonstrating its versatility as a general-purpose compression method. By training smaller student models to mimic larger teacher models, knowledge distillation achieves significant reductions in model size and computational cost without substantial accuracy degradation, making it essential for practical deployment scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models. When combined with careful design of student capacity, layer alignment, and complementary compression methods, KD enables substantial reductions in memory and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. However, distillation is not a universal remedy: its effectiveness depends on choices about what is transferred, available data, and how student and teacher internals align. Practical deployments benefit from treating KD as a multi-strategy engineering problem—selecting appropriate distillation targets, leveraging multi-teacher or data-free options when necessary, and addressing optimization gaps and low-frequency phenomena through task-aware interventions.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression: Capabilities, Complementary Techniques, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central, practical approach for compressing large deep models into efficient students suitable for deployment. KD is versatile: it transfers logits, intermediate representations, and relational knowledge, can operate with or without original training data, and can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet real-world constraints. However, distilled models can inherit optimization difficulties, dataset artifacts, and biases from teachers, so reliable deployment requires task-adaptive method design, student-aware objectives, and privacy- or resource-aware protocols. When treated as a toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD enables production-ready compression across vision and NLP settings.

papers_seen.author: Byrd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical Tool for Model Compression: Strengths, Mechanisms, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. KD methods—ranging from soft-target matching to representation-level imitation, self-distillation, and adversarial teacher–student games—enable substantial efficiency gains while often improving generalization. However, distillation's benefits depend on careful design choices (what signals to transfer, how to align layers, and how to handle data or privacy constraints) and it is not a universal panacea: issues such as teacher–student mismatch, scarce or unavailable data, and task-specific optimization barriers require specialized strategies and evaluation. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a flexible, composable framework that is essential for practical compression but must be applied with task-aware techniques and awareness of its limitations.

papers_seen.author: Pope
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a compact, flexible, and empirically effective route to compress large neural models into deployable students. When treated as a design-first tool rather than a single loss term, KD can be combined with pre-training of compact architectures, representation-level objectives, data-efficient and data-free techniques, and architecture- or task-aware adjustments to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Adopting KD as the default strategy requires engineering practices that explicitly address teacher–student alignment, domain shift, rare-token behavior, and evaluation protocols, but doing so yields a practical, composable pipeline for converting research-scale models into production-ready systems.

papers_seen.author: Cobb
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from teacher models. When combined with task-aware design choices—choice of distilled signals, teacher selection, data strategies, and architecture co-design—KD routinely yields compact models that approach teacher performance while satisfying deployment constraints such as latency, memory, and privacy. To be reliable in production, KD must be applied as part of an integrated pipeline that addresses data availability, teacher–student capacity mismatch, and potential transfer of biases.
